declarations.name: is_condorcet_winning_set
declarations.informal: With n voters holding strict rankings of m candidates, S is a Condorcet winning set if for every candidate a ∉ S, strictly fewer than n/2 voters rank a above every member of S (equivalently, a strict majority prefers some member of S to a).
declarations.statement:
def is_condorcet_winning_set {n m : ℕ} (P : Fin n → Equiv.Perm (Fin m)) (S : Finset (Fin m)) :
    Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A Condorcet winning set in the election where voter `v` ranks candidate `c` at position `P v c` (position 0 is the top): for every candidate `a` outside `S`, strictly fewer than half of the voters rank `a` above every member of `S`. -/
def is_condorcet_winning_set {n m : ℕ} (P : Fin n → Equiv.Perm (Fin m)) (S : Finset (Fin m)) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ a, a ∉ S → 2 * (Finset.univ.filter fun v => ∀ b ∈ S, P v a < P v b).card < n
declarations.citation: Condorcet winning sets (Social Choice and Welfare 44(3):493-517, 2015), definition of Condorcet winning sets and Condorcet dimension

declarations.name: condorcet_winning_set_univ
declarations.informal: The set of all candidates is a Condorcet winning set.
declarations.statement:
theorem condorcet_winning_set_univ {n m : ℕ} (P : Fin n → Equiv.Perm (Fin m)) :
    is_condorcet_winning_set P Finset.univ
declarations.source:
theorem condorcet_winning_set_univ {n m : ℕ} (P : Fin n → Equiv.Perm (Fin m)) :
    is_condorcet_winning_set P Finset.univ := by
  intro a ha; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ a) ha

explanation.summary: To show that the universal set of all candidates is a Condorcet winning set, we must show that any candidate outside it satisfies a pairwise condition against the set. However, every candidate belongs to the universal set by definition. Thus, the condition that a candidate lies outside the set is impossible, and the theorem holds vacuously.

steps.claim: The universal set of candidates satisfies the Condorcet winning set condition.
steps.explanation: By definition, a set of candidates $S$ is a Condorcet winning set if every candidate $a \\notin S$ satisfies a certain pairwise majority condition. Supposing there were a candidate $a$ outside the universal set (the hypothesis $ha : a \\notin \\mathrm{univ}$), this directly contradicts the fact that every candidate belongs to the universal set by `Finset.mem_univ`. The claim therefore holds vacuously.
steps.code: intro a ha; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ a) ha

glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to the universal set `Finset.univ`.

declarations.name: condorcet_dimension_le_three_of_le_four
declarations.informal: Every election with at most four candidates (and at least one voter) has a Condorcet winning set of at most three candidates: drop a candidate ranked first by fewer than half of the voters.
declarations.statement:
theorem condorcet_dimension_le_three_of_le_four (n m : ℕ) (P : Fin n → Equiv.Perm (Fin m))
    (hn : 0 < n) (hm : m ≤ 4) :
    ∃ S : Finset (Fin m), S.card ≤ 3 ∧ is_condorcet_winning_set P S
declarations.source:
theorem condorcet_dimension_le_three_of_le_four (n m : ℕ) (P : Fin n → Equiv.Perm (Fin m))
    (hn : 0 < n) (hm : m ≤ 4) :
    ∃ S : Finset (Fin m), S.card ≤ 3 ∧ is_condorcet_winning_set P S := by
  classical
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge m 4 with hm3 | hm4
  · exact ⟨Finset.univ, by simp; omega, condorcet_winning_set_univ P⟩
  obtain rfl : m = 4 := by omega
  let top : Fin 4 → Finset (Fin n) := fun a =>
    Finset.univ.filter fun v => ∀ b ∈ Finset.univ.erase a, P v a < P v b
  have hdisj : (↑(Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 4)) : Set (Fin 4)).PairwiseDisjoint top := by
    intro a _ b _ hab
    rw [Function.onFun, Finset.disjoint_left]
    intro v hva hvb
    simp only [top, Finset.mem_filter] at hva hvb
    have h1 := hva.2 b (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨Ne.symm hab, Finset.mem_univ _⟩)
    have h2 := hvb.2 a (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hab, Finset.mem_univ _⟩)
    exact absurd (h1.trans h2) (lt_irrefl _)
  have hsum : ∑ a, (top a).card ≤ n := by
    rw [← Finset.card_biUnion hdisj]
    exact (Finset.card_le_univ _).trans (by simp)
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ : ∃ a, 2 * (top a).card < n := by
    by_contra h
    push Not at h
    have h4 : ∑ _a : Fin 4, n ≤ ∑ a, 2 * (top a).card := Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => h a
    rw [← Finset.mul_sum] at h4
    simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul] at h4
    omega
  refine ⟨Finset.univ.erase a, by simp, fun x hx => ?_⟩
  have : x = a := by simpa using hx
  subst this
  exact ha
declarations.citation: smallest nontrivial case of the question whether the Condorcet dimension is always at most 3 (Condorcet winning sets (Social Choice and Welfare 44(3):493-517, 2015); arXiv:2604.19851 states the gap 3 ≤ dim ≤ 5 as open)

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by case analysis on the number of candidates m ≤ 4. If m < 4, taking all candidates gives a winning set of size at most three. When m = 4, the sets of voters ranking each candidate first are pairwise disjoint, so their sizes sum to at most n. Since n > 0, an averaging argument guarantees some candidate a is ranked first by strictly fewer than n/2 voters. Dropping candidate a leaves three candidates, and because a cannot defeat all three simultaneously by a majority, the remaining three form a Condorcet winning set.

steps.claim: If there are strictly fewer than four candidates (m < 4), the full set of candidates is a Condorcet winning set of size at most three.
steps.explanation: We split into cases using `Nat.lt_or_ge` on whether m < 4 or m ≥ 4. If m < 4, the full set of candidates Finset.univ has size m ≤ 3. By `condorcet_winning_set_univ`, the full candidate set is always a Condorcet winning set because no candidate is left outside the set, which closes this case.
steps.code:
classical
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge m 4 with hm3 | hm4
  · exact ⟨Finset.univ, by simp; omega, condorcet_winning_set_univ P⟩

steps.claim: In the remaining case, the number of candidates is exactly four (m = 4).
steps.explanation: Since m ≤ 4 by hypothesis and m ≥ 4 from the case split, linear integer arithmetic (`omega`) determines that m = 4.
steps.code: obtain rfl : m = 4 := by omega

steps.claim: For each candidate a, the set top(a) of voters who rank a strictly ahead of all other candidates is well-defined, and these sets are pairwise disjoint across all four candidates.
steps.explanation: For each candidate a, top(a) is defined as the set of voters v who rank a strictly ahead of every other candidate b ≠ a (using `Finset.mem_filter`). To prove pairwise disjointness (`Function.onFun`, `Finset.disjoint_left`), suppose for contradiction that some voter v belongs to both top(a) and top(b) with a ≠ b (`Ne.symm`, `Finset.mem_univ`). Then v ranks a ahead of b and b ahead of a, so P(v)(a) < P(v)(b) < P(v)(a). By transitivity this gives P(v)(a) < P(v)(a), contradicting the irreflexivity of strict inequality (`lt_irrefl`).
steps.code:
let top : Fin 4 → Finset (Fin n) := fun a =>
    Finset.univ.filter fun v => ∀ b ∈ Finset.univ.erase a, P v a < P v b
  have hdisj : (↑(Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 4)) : Set (Fin 4)).PairwiseDisjoint top := by
    intro a _ b _ hab
    rw [Function.onFun, Finset.disjoint_left]
    intro v hva hvb
    simp only [top, Finset.mem_filter] at hva hvb
    have h1 := hva.2 b (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨Ne.symm hab, Finset.mem_univ _⟩)
    have h2 := hvb.2 a (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hab, Finset.mem_univ _⟩)
    exact absurd (h1.trans h2) (lt_irrefl _)

steps.claim: The sum of the numbers of voters ranking each candidate first is at most the total number of voters n.
steps.explanation: Because the sets top(a) are pairwise disjoint, the sum of their cardinalities equals the size of their union (`Finset.card_biUnion`). This union is a subset of all n voters, so its cardinality is bounded by n (`Finset.card_le_univ`).
steps.code:
have hsum : ∑ a, (top a).card ≤ n := by
    rw [← Finset.card_biUnion hdisj]
    exact (Finset.card_le_univ _).trans (by simp)

steps.claim: There exists a candidate a ranked first by strictly fewer than n / 2 voters, that is, 2 * |top(a)| < n.
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that every candidate a satisfies 2 * |top(a)| ≥ n. Summing over all four candidates (`Finset.sum_le_sum`) and distributing the multiplication (`Finset.mul_sum`, `Finset.sum_const`, `Finset.card_univ`, `Fintype.card_fin`, `smul_eq_mul`) gives 4n ≤ 2 ∑_a |top(a)|. Since the sum of cardinalities is at most n, this yields 4n ≤ 2n. Because n > 0, this is impossible (`omega`).
steps.code:
obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ : ∃ a, 2 * (top a).card < n := by
    by_contra h
    push Not at h
    have h4 : ∑ _a : Fin 4, n ≤ ∑ a, 2 * (top a).card := Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => h a
    rw [← Finset.mul_sum] at h4
    simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul] at h4
    omega

steps.claim: Removing candidate a leaves a set of at most three candidates that forms a Condorcet winning set.
steps.explanation: We choose S to be all candidates except a, namely Finset.univ.erase a. Its size is 4 - 1 = 3 ≤ 3. By definition, S is a Condorcet winning set if no candidate outside S is preferred to every member of S by at least half the voters. The only candidate not in S is x = a. The voters preferring a to all candidates in S are precisely those who rank a first, namely top(a). Since 2 * |top(a)| < n by choice of a, strictly fewer than half the voters prefer a to all of S, so S is a Condorcet winning set.
steps.code:
refine ⟨Finset.univ.erase a, by simp, fun x hx => ?_⟩
  have : x = a := by simpa using hx
  subst this
  exact ha

glossary.Nat.lt_or_ge: For any natural numbers n and m, either n < m or n ≥ m.
glossary.condorcet_winning_set_univ: The set of all candidates is always a Condorcet winning set.
glossary.Function.onFun: Applies a binary relation to the results of a function on two arguments: Function.onFun R f x y = R (f x) (f y).
glossary.Finset.disjoint_left: Two finite sets are disjoint if and only if no element of the first belongs to the second.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to a filtered finset s.filter p if and only if it belongs to s and satisfies predicate p.
glossary.Ne.symm: Inequality is symmetric: if a ≠ b, then b ≠ a.
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to its universe finset Finset.univ.
glossary.lt_irrefl: Strict inequality is irreflexive: for any element a, ¬(a < a).
glossary.Finset.card_biUnion: The cardinality of a union of pairwise disjoint finite sets indexed by a finset equals the sum of their cardinalities.
glossary.Finset.card_le_univ: The cardinality of any sub-finset of a finite type is at most the total cardinality of that type.
glossary.Finset.sum_le_sum: If f(i) ≤ g(i) for all elements i in a finset s, then ∑ i ∈ s, f(i) ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, g(i).
glossary.Finset.mul_sum: Multiplication distributes over finite summation: a * ∑ i ∈ s, f(i) = ∑ i ∈ s, a * f(i).
glossary.Finset.sum_const: The sum of a constant value b over a finset s equals |s| • b.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universe finset of a finite type equals the cardinality of the type.
glossary.Fintype.card_fin: The cardinality of Fin n is n.
glossary.smul_eq_mul: Scalar multiplication of natural numbers coincides with ordinary multiplication.

caveats: In this formalization, a voter v's preference is represented by a permutation P(v) of candidates where a smaller numerical value indicates a higher preference rank; thus P(v)(a) < P(v)(b) means voter v prefers candidate a over candidate b.

declarations.name: is_ejr_cohesive_group
declarations.informal: For committee size k, a group G of the n voters is ℓ-cohesive if |G| ≥ ℓ·n/k and |∩_{i∈G} A_i| ≥ ℓ.
declarations.statement:
def is_ejr_cohesive_group {n m : ℕ} (A : Fin n → Finset (Fin m)) (k ℓ : ℕ)
    (G : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A group `G` of voters is `ℓ`-cohesive for committee size `k` in the approval profile `A` (voters `Fin n`, candidates `Fin m`): `|G| ≥ ℓ n / k` and the members of `G` jointly approve at least `ℓ` candidates. -/
def is_ejr_cohesive_group {n m : ℕ} (A : Fin n → Finset (Fin m)) (k ℓ : ℕ)
    (G : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ℓ * n ≤ G.card * k ∧ ℓ ≤ (Finset.univ.filter fun c => ∀ i ∈ G, c ∈ A i).card
declarations.citation: arXiv:2007.01795 (Multi-Winner Voting with Approval Preferences), definition of ℓ-cohesive groups (Sec. on proportionality axioms); division cleared as ℓ·n ≤ |G|·k

declarations.name: is_ejr_committee
declarations.informal: A committee W with |W| = k satisfies EJR if for every ℓ ≥ 1 and every ℓ-cohesive group G some voter i ∈ G has |A_i ∩ W| ≥ ℓ.
declarations.statement:
def is_ejr_committee {n m : ℕ} (A : Fin n → Finset (Fin m)) (k : ℕ) (W : Finset (Fin m)) :
    Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Extended justified representation of a committee `W` of size `k`: for every `ℓ ≥ 1`, every `ℓ`-cohesive group has a member who approves at least `ℓ` members of `W`. -/
def is_ejr_committee {n m : ℕ} (A : Fin n → Finset (Fin m)) (k : ℕ) (W : Finset (Fin m)) :
    Prop :=
  W.card = k ∧ ∀ ℓ, 1 ≤ ℓ → ∀ G : Finset (Fin n), is_ejr_cohesive_group A k ℓ G →
    ∃ i ∈ G, ℓ ≤ (A i ∩ W).card
declarations.citation: arXiv:2007.01795 (Multi-Winner Voting with Approval Preferences), definition of EJR

explanation.summary: To show that the path graph on three vertices is a spanning path graph, we provide the identity permutation on its vertices as the witness. Under the identity permutation, the required condition is that two vertices are adjacent if and only if their indices differ by one, which is the definition of adjacency in a path graph.

steps.claim: The identity permutation witnesses that the path graph on three vertices is a spanning path.
steps.explanation: We instantiate the existential quantifier in the definition of a spanning path graph with the identity permutation on $\operatorname{Fin} 3$. For any vertices $a$ and $b$, the identity permutation satisfies $1(a) = a$ and $1(b) = b$, so the condition reduces to the definition of adjacency in the path graph given by `SimpleGraph.pathGraph_adj`, closing the equivalence.
steps.code: ⟨1, fun a b => by simp [SimpleGraph.pathGraph_adj]⟩

glossary.SimpleGraph.pathGraph_adj: In a path graph on $n$ vertices, two vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent if and only if their integer values differ by $1$ ($u + 1 = v$ or $v + 1 = u$).

declarations.name: temporal_connected_explore_sq
declarations.informal: Every temporal graph on n vertices all of whose snapshots are connected can be explored from any start vertex within (n − 1)² time steps.
declarations.statement:
theorem temporal_connected_explore_sq :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : ℕ → SimpleGraph (Fin n)), (∀ t, (G t).Connected) →
      ∀ s : Fin n, ∃ w : ℕ → Fin n, w 0 = s ∧ is_temporal_walk G w ∧
        temporal_walk_explores_by w ((n - 1) ^ 2)
declarations.source:
theorem temporal_connected_reach_within {n : ℕ} (G : ℕ → SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (hG : ∀ t, (G t).Connected) (t0 : ℕ) (v u : Fin n) :
    ∃ w : ℕ → Fin n, w 0 = v ∧ (∀ i, w (i + 1) = w i ∨ (G (t0 + i)).Adj (w i) (w (i + 1))) ∧
      ∃ j ≤ n - 1, w j = u := by
  classical
  let R : ℕ → Finset (Fin n) := fun j => Finset.univ.filter fun y =>
    ∃ p : ℕ → Fin n, p 0 = v ∧ (∀ i < j, p (i + 1) = p i ∨ (G (t0 + i)).Adj (p i) (p (i + 1))) ∧
      p j = y
  have hmono : ∀ j, R j ⊆ R (j + 1) := by
    intro j y hy
    simp only [R, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hy ⊢
    obtain ⟨p, hp0, hp, hpj⟩ := hy
    refine ⟨fun i => if i ≤ j then p i else y, by simp [hp0], fun i hi => ?_, by simp⟩
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge i j with h | h
    · have := hp i h
      simp only [show i ≤ j from h.le, show i + 1 ≤ j from h, if_true]
      exact this
    · obtain rfl : i = j := by omega
      left; simp [hpj]
  have hv : v ∈ R 0 := by
    simp only [R, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
    exact ⟨fun _ => v, rfl, fun i hi => absurd hi (Nat.not_lt_zero _), rfl⟩
  have hgrow : ∀ j, R j ≠ Finset.univ → (R j).card < (R (j + 1)).card := by
    intro j hj
    obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ : ∃ z, z ∉ R j := by
      by_contra h; push Not at h; exact hj (Finset.eq_univ_iff_forall.2 h)
    have hvj : v ∈ R j := by
      clear hz hj
      induction j with
      | zero => exact hv
      | succ j ih => exact hmono j ih
    obtain ⟨wk⟩ := (hG (t0 + j)).preconnected v z
    obtain ⟨d, -, hd1, hd2⟩ := wk.exists_boundary_dart (↑(R j) : Set (Fin n)) hvj hz
    refine Finset.card_lt_card ((hmono j).ssubset_of_not_subset fun hsub => hd2 ?_)
    have hy : d.snd ∈ R (j + 1) := by
      have h1 : d.fst ∈ R j := hd1
      simp only [R, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at h1 ⊢
      obtain ⟨p, hp0, hp, hpj⟩ := h1
      refine ⟨fun i => if i ≤ j then p i else d.snd, by simp [hp0], fun i hi => ?_, by simp⟩
      rcases Nat.lt_or_ge i j with h | h
      · simp only [show i ≤ j from h.le, show i + 1 ≤ j from h, if_true]
        exact hp i h
      · obtain rfl : i = j := by omega
        right; simpa [hpj] using d.adj
    exact hsub hy
  have hcard : ∀ j, min (j + 1) n ≤ (R j).card := by
    intro j
    induction j with
    | zero =>
      have := Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨v, hv⟩
      omega
    | succ j ih =>
      by_cases hj : R j = Finset.univ
      · have : R (j + 1) = Finset.univ := Finset.eq_univ_of_forall fun y =>
          hmono j (by rw [hj]; exact Finset.mem_univ y)
        rw [this, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]; omega
      · have := hgrow j hj; omega
  have hn : 1 ≤ n := Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.2 fun h => by subst h; exact v.elim0
  have hfull : R (n - 1) = Finset.univ := by
    apply Finset.eq_univ_of_card
    have := hcard (n - 1)
    have hle := Finset.card_le_univ (R (n - 1))
    simp only [Fintype.card_fin] at hle ⊢
    omega
  have hu : u ∈ R (n - 1) := by rw [hfull]; exact Finset.mem_univ u
  simp only [R, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hu
  obtain ⟨p, hp0, hp, hpj⟩ := hu
  refine ⟨fun i => if i ≤ n - 1 then p i else u, by simp [hp0], fun i => ?_,
    ⟨n - 1, le_rfl, by simp [hpj]⟩⟩
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge i (n - 1) with h | h
  · simp only [show i ≤ n - 1 from h.le, show i + 1 ≤ n - 1 from h, if_true]
    exact hp i h
  · left
    have h1 : ¬ (i + 1 ≤ n - 1) := by omega
    simp only [h1, if_false]
    by_cases h2 : i ≤ n - 1
    · obtain rfl : i = n - 1 := by omega
      simp [hpj]
    · simp [h2]

theorem temporal_connected_visit_list {n : ℕ} (G : ℕ → SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (hG : ∀ t, (G t).Connected) (L : List (Fin n)) :
    ∀ (t0 : ℕ) (v : Fin n), ∃ w : ℕ → Fin n, w 0 = v ∧
      (∀ i, w (i + 1) = w i ∨ (G (t0 + i)).Adj (w i) (w (i + 1))) ∧
      ∀ u ∈ L, ∃ j ≤ L.length * (n - 1), w j = u := by
  induction L with
  | nil =>
    intro t0 v
    exact ⟨fun _ => v, rfl, fun _ => Or.inl rfl, fun u hu => absurd hu List.not_mem_nil⟩
  | cons a L ih =>
    intro t0 v
    obtain ⟨q, hq0, hq, j, hj, hqj⟩ := temporal_connected_reach_within G hG t0 v a
    obtain ⟨p, hp0, hp, hpL⟩ := ih (t0 + j) a
    refine ⟨fun i => if i ≤ j then q i else p (i - j), by simp [hq0], fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
    · rcases Nat.lt_or_ge i j with h | h
      · simp only [show i ≤ j from h.le, show i + 1 ≤ j from h, if_true]
        exact hq i
      · have h1 : ¬ (i + 1 ≤ j) := by omega
        simp only [h1, if_false]
        have hpi := hp (i - j)
        have e1 : i - j + 1 = i + 1 - j := by omega
        have e2 : t0 + j + (i - j) = t0 + i := by omega
        rw [e1, e2] at hpi
        by_cases h2 : i ≤ j
        · obtain rfl : i = j := by omega
          simp only [le_refl, if_true, hqj]
          simpa [hp0] using hpi
        · simp only [h2, if_false]
          exact hpi
    · intro u hu
      rcases List.mem_cons.1 hu with rfl | hu
      · refine ⟨j, ?_, by simp [hqj]⟩
        rw [List.length_cons]
        exact le_trans hj (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left (n - 1) (Nat.succ_pos _))
      · obtain ⟨k, hk, hpk⟩ := hpL u hu
        refine ⟨j + k, by rw [List.length_cons, add_mul, one_mul]; omega, ?_⟩
        by_cases hk0 : k = 0
        · subst hk0
          simp only [Nat.add_zero, le_refl, if_true]
          rw [hqj, ← hpk, hp0]
        · have : ¬ (j + k ≤ j) := by omega
          simp only [this, if_false, Nat.add_sub_cancel_left, hpk]

theorem temporal_connected_explore_sq :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : ℕ → SimpleGraph (Fin n)), (∀ t, (G t).Connected) →
      ∀ s : Fin n, ∃ w : ℕ → Fin n, w 0 = s ∧ is_temporal_walk G w ∧
        temporal_walk_explores_by w ((n - 1) ^ 2) := by
  classical
  intro n G hG s
  obtain ⟨w, hw0, hw, hL⟩ := temporal_connected_visit_list G hG (Finset.univ.erase s).toList 0 s
  refine ⟨w, hw0, fun t => by simpa using hw t, fun u => ?_⟩
  by_cases hu : u = s
  · exact ⟨0, Nat.zero_le _, hu ▸ hw0⟩
  · obtain ⟨j, hj, hwj⟩ := hL u (by simp [hu])
    refine ⟨j, le_trans hj ?_, hwj⟩
    simp only [Finset.length_toList, Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ s),
      Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
    rw [sq]
declarations.citation: On Temporal Graph Exploration (ICALP 2015), the O(n²) upper bound for always-connected temporal graphs, recalled as [24] in arXiv:2610.06228, Sec. 1; the Lean states the explicit bound (n − 1)² from the standard reachability argument

explanation.summary: Every temporal graph with connected snapshots can be explored within (n − 1)² time steps by visiting vertices sequentially. First, snapshot connectedness guarantees that the reachable set from any vertex grows by at least one at each step until it covers the entire graph, so any single target vertex can be reached within n − 1 steps. By induction on list length, concatenating these single-target walks produces a temporal walk visiting any list of vertices within length times n − 1 steps. Finally, applying this to the list of all n − 1 vertices other than the starting vertex yields a complete exploration within (n − 1)² steps.

steps.claim: Define R(j) as the set of vertices reachable from v at time t0 + j via a temporal walk of length j
steps.explanation: We define R(j) ⊆ Fin n to be the finset of all vertices y for which there exists a temporal walk p starting at v at time t0 such that p(j) = y.
steps.code:
classical
  let R : ℕ → Finset (Fin n) := fun j => Finset.univ.filter fun y =>
    ∃ p : ℕ → Fin n, p 0 = v ∧ (∀ i < j, p (i + 1) = p i ∨ (G (t0 + i)).Adj (p i) (p (i + 1))) ∧
      p j = y

steps.claim: The reachable sets are monotonic: R(j) ⊆ R(j + 1) for all j
steps.explanation: Given y ∈ R(j) witnessed by a path p, extending p by remaining at y at step j produces a valid temporal walk of length j + 1 reaching y at time j + 1. Case analysis on whether an index i is strictly less than j or equal to j confirms each step is either stationary or a graph edge.
steps.code:
have hmono : ∀ j, R j ⊆ R (j + 1) := by
    intro j y hy
    simp only [R, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hy ⊢
    obtain ⟨p, hp0, hp, hpj⟩ := hy
    refine ⟨fun i => if i ≤ j then p i else y, by simp [hp0], fun i hi => ?_, by simp⟩
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge i j with h | h
    · have := hp i h
      simp only [show i ≤ j from h.le, show i + 1 ≤ j from h, if_true]
      exact this
    · obtain rfl : i = j := by omega
      left; simp [hpj]

steps.claim: The starting vertex v belongs to R(0)
steps.explanation: The constant walk at v has length 0 and vacuously satisfies all step conditions, so v ∈ R(0).
steps.code:
have hv : v ∈ R 0 := by
    simp only [R, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
    exact ⟨fun _ => v, rfl, fun i hi => absurd hi (Nat.not_lt_zero _), rfl⟩

steps.claim: As long as R(j) is not the entire vertex set, its cardinality strictly increases: |R(j)| < |R(j + 1)|
steps.explanation: If R(j) ≠ univ, pick a vertex z ∉ R(j). Since v ∈ R(j) by monotonicity and the snapshot G(t0 + j) is connected, there is a walk from v to z in that snapshot. This walk crosses the boundary of R(j) via some directed edge d from R(j) to its complement. Extending the temporal walk reaching d.fst at time j by following d at step j places d.snd into R(j + 1). Since d.snd ∉ R(j), R(j) is a strict subset of R(j + 1), so its cardinality strictly increases.
steps.code:
have hgrow : ∀ j, R j ≠ Finset.univ → (R j).card < (R (j + 1)).card := by
    intro j hj
    obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ : ∃ z, z ∉ R j := by
      by_contra h; push Not at h; exact hj (Finset.eq_univ_iff_forall.2 h)
    have hvj : v ∈ R j := by
      clear hz hj
      induction j with
      | zero => exact hv
      | succ j ih => exact hmono j ih
    obtain ⟨wk⟩ := (hG (t0 + j)).preconnected v z
    obtain ⟨d, -, hd1, hd2⟩ := wk.exists_boundary_dart (↑(R j) : Set (Fin n)) hvj hz
    refine Finset.card_lt_card ((hmono j).ssubset_of_not_subset fun hsub => hd2 ?_)
    have hy : d.snd ∈ R (j + 1) := by
      have h1 : d.fst ∈ R j := hd1
      simp only [R, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at h1 ⊢
      obtain ⟨p, hp0, hp, hpj⟩ := h1
      refine ⟨fun i => if i ≤ j then p i else d.snd, by simp [hp0], fun i hi => ?_, by simp⟩
      rcases Nat.lt_or_ge i j with h | h
      · simp only [show i ≤ j from h.le, show i + 1 ≤ j from h, if_true]
        exact hp i h
      · obtain rfl : i = j := by omega
        right; simpa [hpj] using d.adj
    exact hsub hy

steps.claim: For every j, |R(j)| ≥ min(j + 1, n)
steps.explanation: We proceed by induction on j. For j = 0, |R(0)| ≥ 1 since v ∈ R(0). In the inductive step, if R(j) is already univ then R(j + 1) = univ with cardinality n; otherwise |R(j + 1)| > |R(j)|, increasing the cardinality by at least 1. Linear arithmetic completes both branches.
steps.code:
have hcard : ∀ j, min (j + 1) n ≤ (R j).card := by
    intro j
    induction j with
    | zero =>
      have := Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨v, hv⟩
      omega
    | succ j ih =>
      by_cases hj : R j = Finset.univ
      · have : R (j + 1) = Finset.univ := Finset.eq_univ_of_forall fun y =>
          hmono j (by rw [hj]; exact Finset.mem_univ y)
        rw [this, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]; omega
      · have := hgrow j hj; omega

steps.claim: R(n − 1) equals the full vertex set, so any target vertex u belongs to R(n − 1)
steps.explanation: Since n ≥ 1 (as Fin n has an element v), the cardinality bound gives |R(n − 1)| ≥ min(n, n) = n. Since any subset of Fin n has cardinality at most n, |R(n − 1)| = n and R(n − 1) = univ. Thus u ∈ R(n − 1).
steps.code:
have hn : 1 ≤ n := Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.2 fun h => by subst h; exact v.elim0
  have hfull : R (n - 1) = Finset.univ := by
    apply Finset.eq_univ_of_card
    have := hcard (n - 1)
    have hle := Finset.card_le_univ (R (n - 1))
    simp only [Fintype.card_fin] at hle ⊢
    omega
  have hu : u ∈ R (n - 1) := by rw [hfull]; exact Finset.mem_univ u

steps.claim: There exists an infinite temporal walk from v reaching u within n − 1 steps
steps.explanation: Extract the path p of length n − 1 reaching u, and extend it infinitely by staying at u at all times i ≥ n − 1. Linear arithmetic and rewriting simplify the conditional cases to verify that this is a valid temporal walk reaching u at step n − 1 ≤ n − 1.
steps.code:
simp only [R, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hu
  obtain ⟨p, hp0, hp, hpj⟩ := hu
  refine ⟨fun i => if i ≤ n - 1 then p i else u, by simp [hp0], fun i => ?_,
    ⟨n - 1, le_rfl, by simp [hpj]⟩⟩
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge i (n - 1) with h | h
  · simp only [show i ≤ n - 1 from h.le, show i + 1 ≤ n - 1 from h, if_true]
    exact hp i h
  · left
    have h1 : ¬ (i + 1 ≤ n - 1) := by omega
    simp only [h1, if_false]
    by_cases h2 : i ≤ n - 1
    · obtain rfl : i = n - 1 := by omega
      simp [hpj]
    · simp [h2]

steps.claim: Base case: the empty list of vertices is visited by the constant walk in 0 steps
steps.explanation: By induction on the list L. For L = [], the constant walk w(i) = v starts at v, stays at v at every time step, and vacuously visits every vertex in the empty list within 0 ≤ 0 * (n − 1) steps.
steps.code:
induction L with
  | nil =>
    intro t0 v
    exact ⟨fun _ => v, rfl, fun _ => Or.inl rfl, fun u hu => absurd hu List.not_mem_nil⟩

steps.claim: Inductive step: concatenate the walk reaching a with the walk visiting L to obtain a temporal walk starting at v
steps.explanation: By temporal_connected_reach_within, some walk q reaches a at time j ≤ n − 1. By the induction hypothesis started at time t0 + j from a, a walk p visits L within |L| * (n − 1) steps. Splicing q before time j and p after time j yields a valid temporal walk starting at v, verified by case analysis on whether the step occurs before, at, or after the splice point j.
steps.code:
| cons a L ih =>
    intro t0 v
    obtain ⟨q, hq0, hq, j, hj, hqj⟩ := temporal_connected_reach_within G hG t0 v a
    obtain ⟨p, hp0, hp, hpL⟩ := ih (t0 + j) a
    refine ⟨fun i => if i ≤ j then q i else p (i - j), by simp [hq0], fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
    · rcases Nat.lt_or_ge i j with h | h
      · simp only [show i ≤ j from h.le, show i + 1 ≤ j from h, if_true]
        exact hq i
      · have h1 : ¬ (i + 1 ≤ j) := by omega
        simp only [h1, if_false]
        have hpi := hp (i - j)
        have e1 : i - j + 1 = i + 1 - j := by omega
        have e2 : t0 + j + (i - j) = t0 + i := by omega
        rw [e1, e2] at hpi
        by_cases h2 : i ≤ j
        · obtain rfl : i = j := by omega
          simp only [le_refl, if_true, hqj]
          simpa [hp0] using hpi
        · simp only [h2, if_false]
          exact hpi

steps.claim: The spliced walk visits every vertex in a :: L within (|L| + 1) * (n − 1) steps
steps.explanation: If u = a, it is reached at step j ≤ n − 1 ≤ (|L| + 1) * (n − 1). If u ∈ L, it is reached by p at step k ≤ |L| * (n − 1), so on the spliced walk it is reached at step j + k ≤ (n − 1) + |L| * (n − 1) = (|L| + 1) * (n − 1).
steps.code:
· intro u hu
      rcases List.mem_cons.1 hu with rfl | hu
      · refine ⟨j, ?_, by simp [hqj]⟩
        rw [List.length_cons]
        exact le_trans hj (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left (n - 1) (Nat.succ_pos _))
      · obtain ⟨k, hk, hpk⟩ := hpL u hu
        refine ⟨j + k, by rw [List.length_cons, add_mul, one_mul]; omega, ?_⟩
        by_cases hk0 : k = 0
        · subst hk0
          simp only [Nat.add_zero, le_refl, if_true]
          rw [hqj, ← hpk, hp0]
        · have : ¬ (j + k ≤ j) := by omega
          simp only [this, if_false, Nat.add_sub_cancel_left, hpk]

steps.claim: Apply temporal_connected_visit_list to the list of all vertices other than s
steps.explanation: We instantiate temporal_connected_visit_list with the list of vertices (Finset.univ.erase s).toList starting from s at time 0, obtaining a temporal walk w starting at s that visits every vertex in that list within length times n − 1 steps.
steps.code:
classical
  intro n G hG s
  obtain ⟨w, hw0, hw, hL⟩ := temporal_connected_visit_list G hG (Finset.univ.erase s).toList 0 s
  refine ⟨w, hw0, fun t => by simpa using hw t, fun u => ?_⟩

steps.claim: The walk w explores all vertices of the graph within (n − 1)² steps
steps.explanation: For any vertex u, if u = s then w visits u at time 0 ≤ (n − 1)². If u ≠ s, u belongs to the erased list, so w visits u at step j bounded by the list length times n − 1. Since the erased finset has cardinality n − 1, the bound is (n − 1) * (n − 1) = (n − 1)².
steps.code:
by_cases hu : u = s
  · exact ⟨0, Nat.zero_le _, hu ▸ hw0⟩
  · obtain ⟨j, hj, hwj⟩ := hL u (by simp [hu])
    refine ⟨j, le_trans hj ?_, hwj⟩
    simp only [Finset.length_toList, Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ s),
      Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
    rw [sq]

glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to the universal finset
glossary.Nat.lt_or_ge: For any natural numbers n and m, either n < m or n ≥ m

glossary.Fintype.card_fin: The cardinality of Fin n is n
glossary.Finset.eq_univ_of_card: A finset whose cardinality equals the cardinality of the type is the universal finset

glossary.Or.inl: Disjunction introduction: p implies p ∨ q
glossary.List.not_mem_nil: No element is a member of the empty list

declarations.name: not_ejr_committee_two_voters_ignored
declarations.informal: If two voters both approve only candidate 0, the committee {1} of size 1 violates EJR.
declarations.statement: theorem not_ejr_committee_two_voters_ignored : ¬ is_ejr_committee (n := 2) (m := 2) ![{0}, {0}] 1 {1}
declarations.source:
theorem not_ejr_committee_two_voters_ignored : ¬ is_ejr_committee (n := 2) (m := 2) ![{0}, {0}] 1 {1} := by
  rintro ⟨-, h⟩
  obtain ⟨i, hi, hl⟩ := h 1 le_rfl {0, 1} (by unfold is_ejr_cohesive_group; decide)
  revert hl; revert hi; revert i; decide

explanation.summary: To show that the committee $\{1\}$ of size 1 violates Extended Justified Representation (EJR) when both voters approve only candidate 0, we argue by contradiction. The set of all voters $G = \{0, 1\}$ forms an EJR cohesive group for $\ell = 1$ because the voters meet the quota requirement and mutually approve candidate 0. Under EJR, at least one voter in $G$ must approve a committee member, but neither voter approves candidate 1, yielding an immediate contradiction.

steps.claim: Assume for contradiction that the committee $\{1\}$ satisfies EJR.
steps.explanation: We assume that $\{1\}$ is an EJR committee. Unfolding this assumption, we discard the committee size condition and retain the representation property $h$: for every quota level $\ell \ge 1$ and every cohesive group $G$, at least one voter in $G$ must approve at least $\ell$ committee members.
steps.code: rintro ⟨-, h⟩

steps.claim: The group of all voters $G = \{0, 1\}$ is cohesive for $\ell = 1$, so EJR implies some voter $i \in G$ approves candidate 1.
steps.explanation: We specialize the EJR hypothesis $h$ to $\ell = 1$ (using reflexivity `le_rfl` for $1 \le 1$) and group $G = \{0, 1\}$. To satisfy cohesiveness, the group must meet the quota threshold $1 \cdot 2 \le |G| \cdot 1$ and have at least 1 candidate approved by all members of $G$; both conditions hold since $|G| = 2$ and both voters approve candidate 0. Unfolding the definition of a cohesive group, Lean verifies this by finite evaluation (`decide`). This yields a voter $i \in \{0, 1\}$ who approves at least 1 candidate in $\{1\}$.
steps.code: obtain ⟨i, hi, hl⟩ := h 1 le_rfl {0, 1} (by unfold is_ejr_cohesive_group; decide)

steps.claim: Contradiction: neither voter approves candidate 1.
steps.explanation: Reverting the voter $i$, the membership $i \in \{0, 1\}$, and the overlap inequality back into the goal transforms it into the statement that no voter $i \in \{0, 1\}$ has $|A_i \cap \{1\}| \ge 1$. Since both voters only approve $\{0\}$, their intersection with $\{1\}$ is empty (cardinality 0), which `decide` verifies by exhaustive evaluation on the two voters, completing the contradiction.
steps.code: revert hl; revert hi; revert i; decide

glossary.le_rfl: Any element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself: $a \le a$.

declarations.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_ne_loss_of_ge
declarations.informal: In Catch-Up on {1, ..., N} with even triangular sum, if Player 2 has a response y ≥ x such that Player 1 does not win from the resulting position with scores (x, y), then Player 2 does not lose after opening move x.
declarations.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_ne_loss_of_ge (N : ℕ) (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2))
    (x y : ℕ) (hx : x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N) (hy : y ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 N).erase x) (hge : x ≤ y)
    (h : catch_up_value_aux (((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase x).erase y) x y false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.win) :
    catch_up_value_aux ((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase x) 0 x false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.loss
declarations.source:
/-- In Catch-Up on {1, ..., N} with even triangular sum, if Player 2 has a response y ≥ x such that Player 1 does not win from the resulting position with scores (x, y), then Player 2 does not lose after opening move x. -/
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_ne_loss_of_ge (N : ℕ) (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2))
    (x y : ℕ) (hx : x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N) (hy : y ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 N).erase x) (hge : x ≤ y)
    (h : catch_up_value_aux (((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase x).erase y) x y false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.win) :
    catch_up_value_aux ((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase x) 0 x false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.loss := by
  rw [catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_ne_loss_iff N h_even x hx]
  refine ⟨y, hy, ?_⟩
  simp [hge, h]
declarations.citation: step towards catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_ne_loss (Catch-Up conjecture (Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates, 2015, Sec. 3.1))

explanation.summary: The proof reduces the goal to an existential statement via `catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_ne_loss_iff`, which characterizes non-losing positions for Player 2 in terms of having at least one valid response. The given move y serves as the witness: since y ≥ x, the condition reduces to Player 1 not winning from scores (x, y), which holds by assumption.

steps.claim: The goal is equivalent to the existence of a valid response y for Player 2 that avoids a loss.
steps.explanation: Rewriting with `catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_ne_loss_iff` transforms the goal into showing that there exists some y ∈ {1, ..., N} \ {x} such that if y ≥ x, Player 1 does not win from scores (x, y), and if y < x, Player 2 does not lose from scores (y, x).
steps.code: rw [catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_ne_loss_iff N h_even x hx]

steps.claim: The given move y satisfies this existential condition.
steps.explanation: We supply y and the hypothesis `hy` (y ∈ {1, ..., N} \ {x}) as the witness for the existential quantifier. Since x ≤ y by hypothesis `hge`, the conditional simplifies to its first branch, which states that Player 1 does not win from scores (x, y). This is precisely hypothesis `h`, closing the goal.

declarations.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_max_ne_loss_iff
declarations.informal: After Player 1 opens with N in Catch-Up on {1, ..., N} with even triangular sum and N > 0, every response y satisfies y < N, so Player 2 does not lose iff there is a response y such that Player 2 does not lose from the resulting position with scores (y, N).
declarations.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_max_ne_loss_iff (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N)
    (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2)) :
    catch_up_value_aux ((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase N) 0 N false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.loss ↔
      ∃ y ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 N).erase N,
        catch_up_value_aux (((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase N).erase y) y N false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.loss
declarations.source:
/-- After Player 1 opens with N in Catch-Up on {1, ..., N} with even triangular sum and N > 0, every response y satisfies y < N, so Player 2 does not lose iff there is a response y such that Player 2 does not lose from the resulting position with scores (y, N). -/
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_max_ne_loss_iff (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N)
    (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2)) :
    catch_up_value_aux ((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase N) 0 N false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.loss ↔
      ∃ y ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 N).erase N,
        catch_up_value_aux (((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase N).erase y) y N false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.loss := by
  have hN_mem : N ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N := Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨hN, le_rfl⟩
  rw [catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_ne_loss_iff N h_even N hN_mem]
  apply exists_congr
  intro y
  apply and_congr_right
  intro hy
  rw [Finset.mem_erase, Finset.mem_Icc] at hy
  have h_not : ¬(y ≥ N) := not_le_of_gt (lt_of_le_of_ne hy.2.2 hy.1)
  rw [if_neg h_not]

explanation.summary: The theorem characterizes when Player 2 avoids losing after Player 1 opens with the maximum tile N. It specializes the general response theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_ne_loss_iff to x = N. Because every remaining response tile y satisfies y ≤ N and y ≠ N, one always has y < N; hence the condition y ≥ N never holds, and the branching outcome simplifies directly to Player 2 not losing from the resulting score position (y, N).

steps.claim: Player 2 avoids a loss after opening move N if and only if there exists a response y ∈ {1, ..., N} \ {N} satisfying the general conditional outcome formula against N.
steps.explanation: Because 0 < N and N ≤ N, N belongs to {1, ..., N} (established as hN_mem). We can therefore rewrite the non-loss condition using the general theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_ne_loss_iff specialized to opening move x = N.
steps.code:
have hN_mem : N ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N := Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨hN, le_rfl⟩
  rw [catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_ne_loss_iff N h_even N hN_mem]

steps.claim: It suffices to show that for any response y ∈ {1, ..., N} \ {N}, the conditional outcome formula against N is equivalent to Player 2 not losing from score position (y, N).
steps.explanation: By exists_congr, equivalence of the two existential statements reduces to equivalence of their predicates for any response y. Then and_congr_right reduces this further: assuming y belongs to {1, ..., N} \ {N}, it suffices to show that the if-then-else condition simplifies to the desired non-loss condition.
steps.code:
apply exists_congr
  intro y
  apply and_congr_right
  intro hy

steps.claim: For any response y ∈ {1, ..., N} \ {N}, the condition y ≥ N is false, simplifying the conditional outcome to the non-loss condition from (y, N).
steps.explanation: Unfolding membership in {1, ..., N} \ {N} shows y ≠ N and y ≤ N, which implies y < N and therefore ¬(y ≥ N). Applying if_neg with this fact selects the else branch of the conditional, which is identically the claim that Player 2 does not lose from scores (y, N).
steps.code:
rw [Finset.mem_erase, Finset.mem_Icc] at hy
  have h_not : ¬(y ≥ N) := not_le_of_gt (lt_of_le_of_ne hy.2.2 hy.1)
  rw [if_neg h_not]

glossary.catch_up_value_aux_icc_erase_ne_loss_iff: In Catch-Up on {1, ..., N} with an even sum, Player 2 does not lose after opening move x iff there is a response y such that: if y ≥ x the continuation from scores (x, y) is not a win, and if y < x the continuation from scores (y, x) is not a loss.
glossary.Finset.mem_Icc.mpr: An element x belongs to the closed discrete interval {a, ..., b} if a ≤ x and x ≤ b.
glossary.le_rfl: Every element is less than or equal to itself (reflexivity of ≤).
glossary.exists_congr: Two existential propositions ∃ a, p a and ∃ a, q a are equivalent if p a ↔ q a for all a.
glossary.and_congr_right: Conjunctions a ∧ b and a ∧ c are equivalent if b ↔ c holds assuming a.
glossary.Finset.mem_erase: An element a belongs to s \ {b} if and only if a ≠ b and a ∈ s.
glossary.Finset.mem_Icc: An element x belongs to {a, ..., b} if and only if a ≤ x and x ≤ b.
glossary.not_le_of_gt: If a < b, then b ≤ a is false.
glossary.lt_of_le_of_ne: If a ≤ b and a ≠ b in a partial order, then a < b.
glossary.if_neg: A conditional expression if c then t else e simplifies to e when c is false.

declarations.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_ne_win_three
declarations.informal: In Catch-Up on {1, 2, 3}, Player 2 does not win after Player 1 opens with 1.
declarations.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_ne_win_three :
    catch_up_value_aux ((Finset.Icc 1 3).erase 1) 0 1 false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.win
declarations.source:
/-- In Catch-Up on {1, 2, 3}, Player 2 does not win after Player 1 opens with 1. -/
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_ne_win_three :
    catch_up_value_aux ((Finset.Icc 1 3).erase 1) 0 1 false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.win := by
  rw [catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_ne_win_iff 3 (by norm_num)]
  intro y hy
  simp only [Finset.mem_erase, Finset.mem_Icc] at hy
  rcases show y = 2 ∨ y = 3 by omega with rfl | rfl
  · have hset : ((Finset.Icc 1 3).erase 1).erase 2 = {3} := by decide
    rw [hset, catch_up_value_aux_singleton]
    decide
  · have hset : ((Finset.Icc 1 3).erase 1).erase 3 = {2} := by decide
    rw [hset, catch_up_value_aux_singleton]
    decide
declarations.citation: step towards catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_ne_win (Catch-Up conjecture (Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates, 2015, Sec. 3.1))

explanation.summary: The proof reduces Player 2's inability to win after Player 1 opens with 1 to checking that neither of Player 2's possible replies, 2 or 3, forces a loss for Player 1. In both cases, exactly one number remains, allowing the game value to be calculated directly: replying with 2 allows Player 1 to take 3 and win (4 > 2), while replying with 3 leaves Player 1 to take 2 and draw (3 = 3).

steps.claim: Player 2 does not win after Player 1 opens with 1 if and only if no subsequent response y ∈ {1, 2, 3} \ {1} by Player 2 forces a loss for Player 1.
steps.explanation: Applying `catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_ne_win_iff` with N = 3 (where 3 ≤ 3 is checked by `norm_num`) rewrites the goal into showing that for every valid response y available to Player 2, the resulting game is not a loss for Player 1.
steps.code: rw [catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_ne_win_iff 3 (by norm_num)]

steps.claim: Player 2's response must be either y = 2 or y = 3.
steps.explanation: Let y be Player 2's move. Unfolding the definition of membership in {1, 2, 3} \ {1} using `Finset.mem_erase` and `Finset.mem_Icc` gives y ≠ 1 and 1 ≤ y ≤ 3. Linear integer arithmetic (`omega`) leaves only two possibilities: y = 2 or y = 3. We split into these two cases.
steps.code:
intro y hy
  simp only [Finset.mem_erase, Finset.mem_Icc] at hy
  rcases show y = 2 ∨ y = 3 by omega with rfl | rfl

steps.claim: If Player 2 plays 2, Player 1 does not lose.
steps.explanation: After removing 2, the remaining set is the singleton {3}, verified by finite evaluation (`decide`). Rewriting with `catch_up_value_aux_singleton`, Player 1 takes 3 and reaches a score of 1 + 3 = 4 against Player 2's 2. Since 4 > 2, Player 1 wins (outcome `win`), which is not a loss; `decide` closes the goal.
steps.code:
· have hset : ((Finset.Icc 1 3).erase 1).erase 2 = {3} := by decide
    rw [hset, catch_up_value_aux_singleton]
    decide

steps.claim: If Player 2 plays 3, Player 1 does not lose.
steps.explanation: After removing 3, the remaining set is the singleton {2}, verified by `decide`. Rewriting with `catch_up_value_aux_singleton`, Player 1 takes 2 and reaches a score of 1 + 2 = 3 against Player 2's 3. Since 3 = 3, the game ends in a draw (outcome `draw`), which is not a loss; `decide` closes the goal.
steps.code:
· have hset : ((Finset.Icc 1 3).erase 1).erase 3 = {2} := by decide
    rw [hset, catch_up_value_aux_singleton]
    decide

glossary.catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_ne_wi: For N ≥ 3, Player 2 does not win after Player 1 opens with 1 if and only if for every subsequent choice y ∈ {1, ..., N} \ {1} by Player 2, the game does not result in a loss for Player 1.
glossary.Finset.mem_Icc: An element x belongs to the closed discrete interval [a, b] if and only if a ≤ x and x ≤ b.
glossary.Finset.mem_erase: An element a belongs to s \ {b} if and only if a ≠ b and a ∈ s.
glossary.catch_up_value_aux_singleton: When a single element x remains, the outcome from the current player's perspective is determined by comparing their final score s_me + x with the opponent's score s_opp: a win if s_me + x > s_opp, a loss if s_me + x < s_opp, and a draw if s_me + x = s_opp.

declarations.name: schwartz_zippel_union_bound_zero_set
declarations.informal: Let F be an integral domain, S a nonempty finite subset of F, n a positive integer, and let k ≥ 0, d ∈ ℕ and p_1, …, p_k be nonzero polynomials in n variables over F whose total degrees are all at most d. Then the number of points x of S^n at which at least one of p_1, …, p_k vanishes is at most k·d·|S|^(n−1). In particular, if k·d < |S| then some point of S^n is nonzero for all of p_1, …, p_k simultaneously.
declarations.statement:
open scoped Finset in
theorem schwartz_zippel_union_bound_zero_set {F : Type*} [CommRing F] [IsDomain F] [DecidableEq F]
    {n k d : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {S : Finset F} (hS : 0 < S.card)
    {p : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) F} (hp : ∀ i, p i ≠ 0)
    (hd : ∀ i, (p i).totalDegree ≤ d) :
    #{x ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S) | ∃ i, MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0}
      ≤ k * (d * S.card ^ (n - 1))
declarations.source:
open scoped Finset in
/-- Schwartz–Zippel with the union bound: at most k·d·|S|^(n−1) points of S^n are zeros of one of k nonzero polynomials of total degree at most d. -/
theorem schwartz_zippel_union_bound_zero_set {F : Type*} [CommRing F] [IsDomain F] [DecidableEq F]
    {n k d : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {S : Finset F} (hS : 0 < S.card)
    {p : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) F} (hp : ∀ i, p i ≠ 0)
    (hd : ∀ i, (p i).totalDegree ≤ d) :
    #{x ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S) | ∃ i, MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0}
      ≤ k * (d * S.card ^ (n - 1)) := by
  let Sn := Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S)
  have h_sub : {x ∈ Sn | ∃ i, MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0} ⊆
      Finset.univ.biUnion (fun i : Fin k => {x ∈ Sn | MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0}) := by
    intro x hx
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_biUnion, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hx ⊢
    rcases hx with ⟨hxs, i, hpi⟩
    exact ⟨i, hxs, hpi⟩
  have h1 : #{x ∈ Sn | ∃ i, MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0} ≤
      #(Finset.univ.biUnion (fun i : Fin k => {x ∈ Sn | MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0})) :=
    Finset.card_le_card h_sub
  have h2 : #(Finset.univ.biUnion (fun i : Fin k => {x ∈ Sn | MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0})) ≤
      k * (d * S.card ^ (n - 1)) := by
    have h_bound : ∀ i ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin k)),
        #{x ∈ Sn | MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0} ≤ d * S.card ^ (n - 1) := by
      intro i _
      have h_sz := schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le hn (hp i) hS
      have h_deg : (p i).totalDegree * S.card ^ (n - 1) ≤ d * S.card ^ (n - 1) :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (hd i)
      exact le_trans h_sz h_deg
    have h_mul := Finset.card_biUnion_le_card_mul (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin k))
      (fun i => {x ∈ Sn | MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0}) (d * S.card ^ (n - 1)) h_bound
    rw [Finset.card_fin] at h_mul
    exact h_mul
  exact le_trans h1 h2
declarations.citation: Schwartz 1980 / Zippel 1979 together with the union bound; the simultaneous form of the identity test as in Motwani & Raghavan, Randomized Algorithms, ch. 7. Concepts anchored by Mathlib `MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_totalDegree` and the knowledge-base node `schwartz_zippel_exists_nonzero_eval`.
declarations.reading:
Let F be a commutative ring that is an integral domain (IsDomain, i.e. no zero divisors and nontrivial) with decidable equality. Let n, k, d : ℕ with n > 0 (hn). Let S be a finite subset of F that is nonempty (hS : 0 < S.card). Let p be a family of k multivariable polynomials over F in n variables, indexed by Fin k, such that (hp) each p i is not the zero polynomial, and (hd) each p i has total degree at most d.

Then: the number of points x in the Cartesian power S^n — i.e. functions x : Fin n → F with x j ∈ S for every j — at which at least one of the polynomials vanishes (∃ i, eval x (p i) = 0), is at most k * (d * |S|^(n-1)).

Equivalently, the size of the union of the zero sets of the p i inside S^n is bounded by k·d·|S|^(n-1), the Schwartz–Zippel union bound.

All binders in order: F (implicit, with [CommRing F] [IsDomain F] [DecidableEq F]), n, k, d (implicit naturals), hn : 0 < n, S : Finset F, hS : 0 < S.card, p : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) F, hp : ∀ i, p i ≠ 0, hd : ∀ i, (p i).totalDegree ≤ d. The hypotheses hn, hS, hp, hd are all genuinely used (hn makes n − 1 well-behaved, hS makes S^n nonempty, hp and hd feed the degree bound).

explanation.summary: The set of points in S^n where at least one of the polynomials p_1, …, p_k vanishes is contained in the union of their individual zero sets. By the single-polynomial Schwartz–Zippel lemma and the degree hypothesis totalDegree(p_i) ≤ d, each individual zero set contains at most d · |S|^(n - 1) points. Applying the union bound across all k polynomials then bounds the total number of vanishing points by k · d · |S|^(n - 1).

steps.claim: The set of points in S^n at which at least one polynomial p_i vanishes is a subset of the union of the individual zero sets ⋃_{i ∈ Fin k} {x ∈ S^n | p_i(x) = 0}.
steps.explanation: Let S^n denote the Cartesian product S^n. Given an element x ∈ S^n where some polynomial p_i vanishes, unfolding the definitions of filtered finsets (Finset.mem_filter), indexed union (Finset.mem_biUnion), and the universal set (Finset.mem_univ, true_and) shows that x belongs to the zero set of that specific polynomial p_i. Thus x belongs to the indexed union of all k zero sets.
steps.code:
let Sn := Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S)
  have h_sub : {x ∈ Sn | ∃ i, MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0} ⊆
      Finset.univ.biUnion (fun i : Fin k => {x ∈ Sn | MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0}) := by
    intro x hx
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_biUnion, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hx ⊢
    rcases hx with ⟨hxs, i, hpi⟩
    exact ⟨i, hxs, hpi⟩

steps.claim: The number of points in S^n where at least one polynomial vanishes is at most the cardinality of the union of the individual zero sets.
steps.explanation: Because a finite set has cardinality at most that of any superset (Finset.card_le_card), the inclusion proved in the previous step immediately yields this cardinality inequality.
steps.code:
have h1 : #{x ∈ Sn | ∃ i, MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0} ≤
      #(Finset.univ.biUnion (fun i : Fin k => {x ∈ Sn | MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0})) :=
    Finset.card_le_card h_sub

steps.claim: The union of the k individual zero sets has cardinality at most k · (d · |S|^(n - 1)).
steps.explanation: For each index i, the Schwartz–Zippel lemma for a single polynomial (schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le) bounds the number of zeros of p_i in S^n by totalDegree(p_i) · |S|^(n - 1). Since totalDegree(p_i) ≤ d, multiplying this degree bound by |S|^(n - 1) on the right (Nat.mul_le_mul_right) and applying transitivity (le_trans) shows that each individual zero set has size at most d · |S|^(n - 1). By the union bound for finite sets (Finset.card_biUnion_le_card_mul), the union of these k sets has cardinality at most the number of polynomials times this uniform bound. Since the index set Fin k has size k (Finset.card_fin), this gives the upper bound k · (d · |S|^(n - 1)).
steps.code:
have h2 : #(Finset.univ.biUnion (fun i : Fin k => {x ∈ Sn | MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0})) ≤
      k * (d * S.card ^ (n - 1)) := by
    have h_bound : ∀ i ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin k)),
        #{x ∈ Sn | MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0} ≤ d * S.card ^ (n - 1) := by
      intro i _
      have h_sz := schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le hn (hp i) hS
      have h_deg : (p i).totalDegree * S.card ^ (n - 1) ≤ d * S.card ^ (n - 1) :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (hd i)
      exact le_trans h_sz h_deg
    have h_mul := Finset.card_biUnion_le_card_mul (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin k))
      (fun i => {x ∈ Sn | MvPolynomial.eval x (p i) = 0}) (d * S.card ^ (n - 1)) h_bound
    rw [Finset.card_fin] at h_mul
    exact h_mul

steps.claim: The number of points in S^n where at least one of p_1, …, p_k vanishes is at most k · d · |S|^(n - 1).
steps.explanation: Combining the inequality bounding the joint zero set by the union's cardinality with the inequality bounding the union's cardinality via transitivity of ≤ (le_trans) yields the theorem.
steps.code: exact le_trans h1 h2

glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to the filtered set {x ∈ s | p(x)} if and only if it belongs to s and satisfies property p.
glossary.Finset.mem_biUnion: An element belongs to the indexed union ⋃_{a ∈ s} t(a) if and only if it belongs to t(a) for some a ∈ s.
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to its universal finset.
glossary.true_and: For any proposition p, True ∧ p is equivalent to p.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card: If a finite set s is a subset of t, then |s| ≤ |t|.
glossary.schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le: For a nonzero multivariate polynomial p in n variables (n > 0) over an integral domain, the number of zeros of p in S^n is at most totalDegree(p) · |S|^(n - 1).
glossary.Nat.mul_le_mul_right: For natural numbers, if n ≤ m, then n · k ≤ m · k.
glossary.le_trans: If a ≤ b and b ≤ c, then a ≤ c (transitivity of inequality).
glossary.Finset.card_biUnion_le_card_mul: If each set f(a) for a ∈ s has cardinality at most c, then the cardinality of the union ⋃_{a ∈ s} f(a) is at most |s| · c.
glossary.Finset.card_fin: The cardinality of the universal finset of Fin n is n.

declarations.name: isotropic_subspace_lower_bound
declarations.informal: If V is an isotropic subspace of (M → ZMod 2) under the standard dot product, the all-ones vector is orthogonal to V, and the all-ones vector is not in V, then 2 * finrank V + 1 ≤ card M.
declarations.statement:
theorem isotropic_subspace_lower_bound {M : Type*} [Fintype M]
    (V : Submodule (ZMod 2) (M → ZMod 2))
    (h_iso : ∀ u ∈ V, ∀ v ∈ V, (∑ m, u m * v m) = 0)
    (h_ones_ortho : ∀ v ∈ V, ∑ m, v m = 0)
    (h_ones_notin : (fun _ : M => (1 : ZMod 2)) ∉ V) :
    2 * Module.finrank (ZMod 2) V + 1 ≤ Fintype.card M
declarations.source:
/-- If V is an isotropic subspace of (M → ZMod 2), the all-ones vector is orthogonal to V, and the all-ones vector is not in V, then 2 * finrank V + 1 ≤ card M. -/
theorem isotropic_subspace_lower_bound {M : Type*} [Fintype M]
    (V : Submodule (ZMod 2) (M → ZMod 2))
    (h_iso : ∀ u ∈ V, ∀ v ∈ V, (∑ m, u m * v m) = 0)
    (h_ones_ortho : ∀ v ∈ V, ∑ m, v m = 0)
    (h_ones_notin : (fun _ : M => (1 : ZMod 2)) ∉ V) :
    2 * Module.finrank (ZMod 2) V + 1 ≤ Fintype.card M := by
  open Matrix LinearMap in
  classical
  let B : LinearMap.BilinForm (ZMod 2) (M → ZMod 2) := toBilin' (1 : Matrix M M (ZMod 2))
  have hB_nondeg : B.Nondegenerate := by
    apply Matrix.Nondegenerate.toBilin'
    rw [nondegenerate_iff_forall_vecMul_and_mulVec_eq_zero]
    simp
  have h_le_ortho : V ≤ B.orthogonal V := by
    intro v hv
    rw [BilinForm.mem_orthogonal_iff]
    intro u hu
    rw [toBilin'_apply']
    simp only [one_mulVec, dotProduct]
    exact h_iso u hu v hv
  have h_rank_ortho : Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (B.orthogonal V) =
      Fintype.card M - Module.finrank (ZMod 2) V := by
    rw [BilinForm.finrank_orthogonal hB_nondeg, Module.finrank_pi]
  have h_le_card : Module.finrank (ZMod 2) V ≤ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (B.orthogonal V) :=
    Submodule.finrank_mono h_le_ortho
  have h_ones_in_ortho : (fun _ : M => (1 : ZMod 2)) ∈ B.orthogonal V := by
    rw [BilinForm.mem_orthogonal_iff]
    intro u hu
    rw [toBilin'_apply']

Dimension counting for nondegenerate forms shows finrank Vᗮ = card M - finrank V, which implies 2 * finrank V ≤ card M. Since the all-ones vector is orthogonal to V but not in V, V cannot equal Vᗮ, ruling out the equality case 2 * finrank V = card M and yielding the strict inequality 2 * finrank V + 1 ≤ card M.

steps.claim: Define B as the bilinear form on M → ZMod 2 corresponding to the identity matrix.
steps.explanation: Working classically within the Matrix and LinearMap namespaces, we define the bilinear form B on M → ZMod 2 to be the one induced by the identity matrix. This bilinear form computes the standard dot product.

steps.claim: The bilinear form B is nondegenerate.
steps.explanation: A matrix bilinear form is nondegenerate whenever the underlying matrix is nondegenerate (`Matrix.Nondegenerate.toBilin'`). In turn, a matrix is nondegenerate if and only if both left and right vector multiplication have trivial kernels (`nondegenerate_iff_forall_vecMul_and_mulVec_eq_zero`). For the identity matrix 1, vector multiplication is the identity map, so both kernels are trivial and simplification completes the step.

have hB_nondeg : B.Nondegenerate := by
    apply Matrix.Nondegenerate.toBilin'
    rw [nondegenerate_iff_forall_vecMul_and_mulVec_eq_zero]
    simp

steps.claim: V is contained in its orthogonal complement Vᗮ with respect to B.
steps.explanation: To show V ≤ B.orthogonal V, take any v ∈ V. By `BilinForm.mem_orthogonal_iff`, v belongs to B.orthogonal V if B(u, v) = 0 for all u ∈ V. Unfolding B via `toBilin'_apply'` and simplifying via `one_mulVec` and `dotProduct`, this condition is ∑ m, u m * v m = 0, which holds because V is isotropic (`h_iso`).

have h_le_ortho : V ≤ B.orthogonal V := by
    intro v hv
    rw [BilinForm.mem_orthogonal_iff]
    intro u hu
    rw [toBilin'_apply']
    simp only [one_mulVec, dotProduct]
    exact h_iso u hu v hv

steps.explanation: Because B is nondegenerate, `BilinForm.finrank_orthogonal` gives finrank Vᗮ = finrank (M → ZMod 2) - finrank V. By `Module.finrank_pi`, the ambient dimension is card M. Furthermore, since V ≤ Vᗮ, monotonicity of dimension (`Submodule.finrank_mono`) ensures finrank V ≤ finrank Vᗮ.

have h_rank_ortho : Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (B.orthogonal V) =
      Fintype.card M - Module.finrank (ZMod 2) V := by
    rw [BilinForm.finrank_orthogonal hB_nondeg, Module.finrank_pi]
  have h_le_card : Module.finrank (ZMod 2) V ≤ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (B.orthogonal V) :=
    Submodule.finrank_mono h_le_ortho

steps.claim: The all-ones vector belongs to Vᗮ.
steps.explanation: By `BilinForm.mem_orthogonal_iff`, the all-ones vector 1 is in Vᗮ if B(u, 1) = 0 for all u ∈ V. Expanding B (`toBilin'_apply'`) and simplifying via `one_mulVec`, `dotProduct`, and `mul_one`, this condition reduces to ∑ m, u m = 0, which is precisely the assumption `h_ones_ortho` that the all-ones vector is orthogonal to V.
steps.code:
have h_ones_in_ortho : (fun _ : M => (1 : ZMod 2)) ∈ B.orthogonal V := by
    rw [BilinForm.mem_orthogonal_iff]
    intro u hu
    rw [toBilin'_apply']
    simp only [one_mulVec, dotProduct, mul_one]
    exact h_ones_ortho u hu

steps.explanation: Combining finrank V ≤ finrank Vᗮ with finrank Vᗮ = card M - finrank V, linear integer arithmetic via `omega` yields 2 * finrank V ≤ card M.
steps.code:
have h_two_rank_le : 2 * Module.finrank (ZMod 2) V ≤ Fintype.card M := by
    omega

steps.claim: 2 * finrank V ≠ card M.
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that 2 * finrank V = card M. Then `omega` gives finrank V = finrank Vᗮ. Because V ≤ Vᗮ and their finite dimensions are equal, `Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq` implies V = Vᗮ. But the all-ones vector belongs to Vᗮ, so it would belong to V, directly contradicting the hypothesis `h_ones_notin`.
steps.code:
have h_ne : 2 * Module.finrank (ZMod 2) V ≠ Fintype.card M := by
    intro h_eq
    have h_ranks_eq : Module.finrank (ZMod 2) V = Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (B.orthogonal V) := by
      omega
    have h_V_eq : V = B.orthogonal V := Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq h_le_ortho h_ranks_eq
    have : (fun _ : M => (1 : ZMod 2)) ∈ V := by
      rw [h_V_eq]
      exact h_ones_in_ortho
    exact h_ones_notin this

steps.claim: 2 * finrank V + 1 ≤ card M.
steps.explanation: From the non-strict inequality 2 * finrank V ≤ card M and the disequality 2 * finrank V ≠ card M, linear integer arithmetic via `omega` concludes 2 * finrank V + 1 ≤ card M.
steps.code: omega

glossary.Matrix.Nondegenerate.toBilin': If a square matrix is nondegenerate, then its associated bilinear form is nondegenerate.
glossary.nondegenerate_iff_forall_vecMul_and_mulV: A matrix is nondegenerate if and only if both left and right multiplication by it have trivial kernels.
glossary.BilinForm.mem_orthogonal_iff: An element m belongs to the orthogonal complement of a submodule N under a bilinear form B if and only if B(n, m) = 0 for all n in N.
glossary.toBilin'_apply': The bilinear form associated with a matrix M evaluates on vectors v and w as the dot product v ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ w).
glossary.one_mulVec: Multiplying a vector by the identity matrix leaves the vector unchanged: 1 *ᵥ v = v.
glossary.dotProduct: The standard dot product of two vectors u and v, defined as ∑ m, u m * v m.
glossary.BilinForm.finrank_orthogonal: For a nondegenerate bilinear form on a finite-dimensional vector space V, the dimension of the orthogonal complement of W is finrank V - finrank W.
glossary.Module.finrank_pi: The dimension of the function space ι → R over R equals the cardinality of ι.
glossary.Submodule.finrank_mono: If a submodule S₁ is contained in a finite-dimensional submodule S₂, then finrank S₁ ≤ finrank S₂.
glossary.mul_one: Multiplying an element by 1 on the right leaves it unchanged: a * 1 = a.
glossary.Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq: If a subspace S₁ is contained in a finite-dimensional subspace S₂ and both have equal dimension, then S₁ = S₂.

caveats: The standard dot product on M → ZMod 2 is represented as the bilinear form associated with the identity matrix, `Matrix.toBilin' 1`.

declarations.name: line_cubic_parity_repr_nonempty
declarations.informal: Every parity representation of the line cubic syndrome for n ≥ 5 is nonempty, because line_syndrome n {0, 1, 2} = 1.
declarations.statement:
theorem line_cubic_parity_repr_nonempty (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n)
    (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n)) :
    S.Nonempty
declarations.source:
/-- Every parity representation of the line cubic syndrome for n ≥ 5 is nonempty. -/
theorem line_cubic_parity_repr_nonempty (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n)
    (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n)) :
    S.Nonempty := by
  let A : Finset (Fin n) := {⟨0, by omega⟩, ⟨1, by omega⟩, ⟨2, by omega⟩}
  have hA_card : A.card = 3 := by
    have h01 : (⟨0, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ≠ ⟨1, by omega⟩ := by
      intro h; injection h with h; omega
    have h02 : (⟨0, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ≠ ⟨2, by omega⟩ := by
      intro h; injection h with h; omega
    have h12 : (⟨1, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ≠ ⟨2, by omega⟩ := by
      intro h; injection h with h; omega
    rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem, Finset.card_insert_of_notMem, Finset.card_singleton]
    · intro h; simp only [Finset.mem_singleton] at h; exact h12 h
    · simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton]; rintro (h | h)
      · exact h01 h
      · exact h02 h
  have h_syn : line_syndrome n A = 1 := by
    unfold line_syndrome
    have h : ∃ i : Fin (n - 2), A = {⟨i.1, by omega⟩, ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩, ⟨i.1 + 2, by omega⟩} := by
      refine ⟨⟨0, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
      rfl
    exact if_pos h
  have h_repr := hS.2 A ⟨by omega, by omega⟩
  rw [h_syn] at h_repr
  by_contra h_empty
  rw [Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty] at h_empty
  have h_sub_empty : {y ∈ S | A ⊆ y} = ∅ := by
    rw [h_empty]
    exact Finset.filter_empty _
  rw [h_sub_empty, Finset.card_empty] at h_repr
  revert h_repr
  decide

explanation.summary: The proof argues by contradiction. Since n ≥ 5, the set A = {0, 1, 2} is a well-defined consecutive triple of size 3, which makes the line syndrome evaluate to 1 on A. By the definition of a parity representation, the number of sets in S containing A must be odd (1 mod 2). If S were empty, this count would be 0, yielding the contradiction 0 = 1 in ℤ/2ℤ.

steps.claim: Define the set A = {0, 1, 2} ⊆ {0, …, n - 1} and establish that |A| = 3.
steps.explanation: Since n ≥ 5, the numbers 0, 1, and 2 are valid indices in Fin n. We establish that 0, 1, and 2 are pairwise distinct in Fin n (via omega on their values), and then compute the cardinality of {0, 1, 2} by repeatedly applying the rule for the cardinality of inserting an element not already present into a set.
steps.code:
let A : Finset (Fin n) := {⟨0, by omega⟩, ⟨1, by omega⟩, ⟨2, by omega⟩}
  have hA_card : A.card = 3 := by
    have h01 : (⟨0, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ≠ ⟨1, by omega⟩ := by
      intro h; injection h with h; omega
    have h02 : (⟨0, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ≠ ⟨2, by omega⟩ := by
      intro h; injection h with h; omega
    have h12 : (⟨1, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ≠ ⟨2, by omega⟩ := by
      intro h; injection h with h; omega
    rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem, Finset.card_insert_of_notMem, Finset.card_singleton]
    · intro h; simp only [Finset.mem_singleton] at h; exact h12 h
    · simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton]; rintro (h | h)
      · exact h01 h
      · exact h02 h

steps.claim: line_syndrome n A = 1.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of line_syndrome, the syndrome is 1 if A is a consecutive triple {i, i + 1, i + 2} for some i < n - 2, and 0 otherwise. Choosing i = 0 (which is valid since n ≥ 5 implies 0 < n - 2) shows that A is of this form, so the conditional evaluates to 1.
steps.code:
have h_syn : line_syndrome n A = 1 := by
    unfold line_syndrome
    have h : ∃ i : Fin (n - 2), A = {⟨i.1, by omega⟩, ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩, ⟨i.1 + 2, by omega⟩} := by
      refine ⟨⟨0, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
      rfl
    exact if_pos h

steps.claim: The number of sets in S that contain A is odd, that is, |{y ∈ S | A ⊆ y}| ≡ 1 (mod 2).
steps.explanation: Since S is a parity representation of line_syndrome n and 1 ≤ |A| = 3 ≤ 3, the representation condition guarantees that |{y ∈ S | A ⊆ y}| mod 2 equals line_syndrome n A. Substituting the value line_syndrome n A = 1 gives the congruence.
steps.code:
have h_repr := hS.2 A ⟨by omega, by omega⟩
  rw [h_syn] at h_repr

steps.claim: S is nonempty.
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that S is empty. Then the subset {y ∈ S | A ⊆ y} is also empty, hence has cardinality 0. But by the parity representation property, its cardinality modulo 2 is 1, giving 0 = 1 in ℤ/2ℤ, which is a contradiction.
steps.code:
by_contra h_empty
  rw [Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty] at h_empty
  have h_sub_empty : {y ∈ S | A ⊆ y} = ∅ := by
    rw [h_empty]
    exact Finset.filter_empty _
  rw [h_sub_empty, Finset.card_empty] at h_repr
  revert h_repr
  decide

glossary.Finset.card_insert_of_notMem: Inserting an element into a finite set that does not already contain it increases its cardinality by 1.
glossary.Finset.mem_singleton: An element belongs to a singleton set {a} if and only if it equals a.
glossary.Finset.mem_insert: An element belongs to insert b s if and only if it equals b or belongs to s.
glossary.if_pos: An if-then-else expression evaluates to its 'then' branch when the condition holds.
glossary.Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty: A finite set is not nonempty if and only if it is the empty set.
glossary.Finset.filter_empty: Filtering the empty set by any predicate yields the empty set.

caveats: On paper, showing that {0, 1, 2} has cardinality 3 is immediate; in Lean, elements of Fin n carry bounds checking (proven via omega), and proving the set has cardinality 3 requires explicitly showing that 0, 1, and 2 are pairwise distinct.
The final contradiction that 0 = 1 in ℤ/2ℤ is dispatched computationally by decide.

declarations.name: line_cubic_parity_repr_ortho
declarations.informal: Every parity representation S of line_syndrome n satisfies ∑_{y ∈ S} (∑_{j ∈ y} c_j)(∑_{k ∈ y} d_k) = 0 and ∑_{y ∈ S} ∑_{j ∈ y} c_j = 0, because singletons and pairs have syndrome 0.
declarations.statement:
theorem line_cubic_parity_repr_ortho (n : ℕ)
    (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n))
    (c d : Fin n → ZMod 2) :
    (∑ y ∈ S, (∑ j ∈ y, c j) * (∑ k ∈ y, d k) = 0) ∧
    (∑ y ∈ S, (∑ j ∈ y, c j) = 0)
declarations.source:
lemma line_cubic_parity_repr_ortho_card_le_two (n : ℕ)
    (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n))
    (A : Finset (Fin n)) (hA1 : 1 ≤ A.card) (hA2 : A.card ≤ 2) :
    ((S.filter (fun y => A ⊆ y)).card : ZMod 2) = 0 := by
  have hA3 : A.card ≤ 3 := by omega
  have hrepr := hS.2 A ⟨hA1, hA3⟩
  rw [hrepr]
  unfold line_syndrome
  split_ifs with h
  · rcases h with ⟨i, hi⟩
    have hc : ({⟨i.val, by omega⟩, ⟨i.val + 1, by omega⟩, ⟨i.val + 2, by omega⟩} : Finset (Fin n)).card = 3 := by
      let a : Fin n := ⟨i.val, by omega⟩
      let b : Fin n := ⟨i.val + 1, by omega⟩
      let c : Fin n := ⟨i.val + 2, by omega⟩
      change ({a, b, c} : Finset (Fin n)).card = 3
      have hab : a ≠ b := by intro h; injection h with h; omega
      have hac : a ≠ c := by intro h; injection h with h; omega
      have hbc : b ≠ c := by intro h; injection h with h; omega
      rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem, Finset.card_insert_of_notMem, Finset.card_singleton]
      · intro h; simp only [Finset.mem_singleton] at h; exact hbc h
      · simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton]; rintro (h | h)
        · exact hab h
        · exact hac h
    have h_card_eq := congr_arg Finset.card hi
    omega
  · rfl

/-- Every parity representation of the line cubic syndrome satisfies bilinear self-orthogonality and linear orthogonality to the all-ones vector. -/
theorem line_cubic_parity_repr_ortho (n : ℕ)
    (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n))
    (c d : Fin n → ZMod 2) :
    (∑ y ∈ S, (∑ j ∈ y, c j) * (∑ k ∈ y, d k) = 0) ∧
    (∑ y ∈ S, (∑ j ∈ y, c j) = 0) := by
  constructor
  · have h1 : (∑ y ∈ S, (∑ j ∈ y, c j) * (∑ k ∈ y, d k)) =
        ∑ y ∈ S, ∑ j : Fin n, ∑ k : Fin n, (if j ∈ y then c j else 0) * (if k ∈ y then d k else 0) := by
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun y _ => ?_)
      rw [← Finset.sum_ite_mem_eq y c, ← Finset.sum_ite_mem_eq y d]
      rw [Finset.sum_mul_sum]
    rw [h1, Finset.sum_comm]
    refine Finset.sum_eq_zero (fun j _ => ?_)
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    refine Finset.sum_eq_zero (fun k _ => ?_)
    have h_split : (∑ y ∈ S, (if j ∈ y then c j else 0) * (if k ∈ y then d k else 0)) =
        (c j * d k) * ∑ y ∈ S, (if j ∈ y ∧ k ∈ y then (1 : ZMod 2) else 0) := by
      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun y _ => ?_)
      by_cases hj : j ∈ y <;> by_cases hk : k ∈ y <;> simp [hj, hk]
    rw [h_split, Finset.sum_boole]
    have h_filt : {x ∈ S | j ∈ x ∧ k ∈ x} = S.filter (fun y => {j, k} ⊆ y) := by
      ext y
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.insert_subset_iff, Finset.singleton_subset_iff]
    rw [h_filt]
    have hne : ({j, k} : Finset (Fin n)).Nonempty := ⟨j, Finset.mem_insert_self j _⟩
    have hcard1 : 1 ≤ ({j, k} : Finset (Fin n)).card := Finset.Nonempty.card_pos hne
    have hcard2 : ({j, k} : Finset (Fin n)).card ≤ 2 := by
      have := Finset.card_insert_le j {k}
      rw [Finset.card_singleton] at this
      omega
    have h_zero := line_cubic_parity_repr_ortho_card_le_two n S hS {j, k} hcard1 hcard2
    rw [h_zero, mul_zero]
  · have h1 : (∑ y ∈ S, ∑ j ∈ y, c j) = ∑ y ∈ S, ∑ j : Fin n, if j ∈ y then c j else 0 := by
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun y _ => ?_)
      exact (Finset.sum_ite_mem_eq y c).symm
    rw [h1, Finset.sum_comm]
    refine Finset.sum_eq_zero (fun j _ => ?_)
    have h_split : (∑ y ∈ S, if j ∈ y then c j else 0) =
        c j * ∑ y ∈ S, (if j ∈ y then (1 : ZMod 2) else 0) := by
      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun y _ => ?_)
      split_ifs <;> ring
    rw [h_split, Finset.sum_boole]
    have h_filt : {x ∈ S | j ∈ x} = S.filter (fun y => {j} ⊆ y) := by
      ext y
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.singleton_subset_iff]
    rw [h_filt]
    have hcard1 : 1 ≤ ({j} : Finset (Fin n)).card := by rw [Finset.card_singleton]
    have hcard2 : ({j} : Finset (Fin n)).card ≤ 2 := by rw [Finset.card_singleton]; omega
    have h_zero := line_cubic_parity_repr_ortho_card_le_two n S hS {j} hcard1 hcard2
    rw [h_zero, mul_zero]

      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun y _ => ?_)
      exact (Finset.sum_ite_mem_eq y c).symm

      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun y _ => ?_)
      split_ifs <;> ring
    rw [h_split, Finset.sum_boole]

      ext y
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.singleton_subset_iff]
    rw [h_filt]
