declarations.name: line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero
declarations.informal: For n ≥ 5, any affine evaluation (∑_{j ∈ y} c_j = b) on all parities y ∈ S of a parity representation S of line_syndrome n forces c = 0.
declarations.statement:
theorem line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n)
    (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n))
    (c : Fin n → ZMod 2) (b : ZMod 2)
    (h : ∀ y ∈ S, (∑ j ∈ y, c j) = b) :
    c = 0
declarations.source:
open Finset

theorem line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_card_le_two (n : ℕ) (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n)))
    (hS : is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n))
    (A : Finset (Fin n)) (hA1 : 1 ≤ A.card) (hA2 : A.card ≤ 2) :
    ((S.filter (fun y => A ⊆ y)).card : ZMod 2) = 0 := by
  have hrepr := hS.2 A ⟨hA1, by omega⟩
  rw [hrepr]
  unfold line_syndrome
  split_ifs with h
  · rcases h with ⟨i, hi⟩
    have hc : ({⟨i.1, by omega⟩, ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩, ⟨i.1 + 2, by omega⟩} : Finset (Fin n)).card = 3 := by
      have h01 : (⟨i.1, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ≠ ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ := by
        intro heq; injection heq with heq; omega
      have h02 : (⟨i.1, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ≠ ⟨i.1 + 2, by omega⟩ := by
        intro heq; injection heq with heq; omega
      have h12 : (⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ≠ ⟨i.1 + 2, by omega⟩ := by
        intro heq; injection heq with heq; omega
      rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem, Finset.card_insert_of_notMem, Finset.card_singleton]
      · intro hm; simp only [Finset.mem_singleton] at hm; exact h12 hm
      · simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton]; rintro (hm | hm)
        · exact h01 hm
        · exact h02 hm
    rw [hi] at hA2
    omega
  · rfl

def line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n - 2)) : Finset (Fin n) :=
  {⟨i.1, by omega⟩, ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩, ⟨i.1 + 2, by omega⟩}

theorem line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n - 2)) (a : Fin n) :
    a ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n i ↔ a.1 = i.1 ∨ a.1 = i.1 + 1 ∨ a.1 = i.1 + 2 := by
  unfold line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple
  simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff]

theorem line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_pair_sum (n : ℕ)
    (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n))
    (c : Fin n → ZMod 2) (b : ZMod 2)
    (h : ∀ y ∈ S, (∑ j ∈ y, c j) = b)
    (p q : Fin n) (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    ∑ j : Fin n, c j * line_syndrome n (insert j {p, q}) = 0 := by
  have h_zero : (∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), (∑ j ∈ y, c j)) = 0 := by
    have h1 : (∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), (∑ j ∈ y, c j)) =
        ∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), b := by
      refine sum_congr rfl (fun y hy => ?_)
      rw [mem_filter] at hy
      exact h y hy.1
    rw [h1, sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
    have hcard1 : 1 ≤ ({p, q} : Finset (Fin n)).card := by
      rw [card_insert_of_notMem (by simpa using hpq), Finset.card_singleton]
      omega
    have hcard2 : ({p, q} : Finset (Fin n)).card ≤ 2 := by
      rw [card_insert_of_notMem (by simpa using hpq), Finset.card_singleton]
    have hz := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_card_le_two n S hS {p, q} hcard1 hcard2
    rw [hz, zero_mul]
  have h_swap : (∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), (∑ j ∈ y, c j)) =
      ∑ j : Fin n, c j * line_syndrome n (insert j {p, q}) := by
    have h1 : (∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), (∑ j ∈ y, c j)) =
        ∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), ∑ j : Fin n, (if j ∈ y then c j else 0) := by
      refine sum_congr rfl (fun y _ => (sum_ite_mem_eq y c).symm)
    rw [h1, sum_comm]
    refine sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => ?_)
    have h2 : (∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), (if j ∈ y then c j else 0)) =
        c j * ∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), (if j ∈ y then (1 : ZMod 2) else 0) := by
      rw [mul_sum]
      refine sum_congr rfl (fun y _ => by split_ifs <;> ring)
    rw [h2, sum_boole]
    have h3 : (S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y)).filter (fun y => j ∈ y) =
        S.filter (fun y => insert j {p, q} ⊆ y) := by
      ext y
      simp only [mem_filter, Finset.insert_subset_iff]
      tauto
    rw [h3]
    have hcard1 : 1 ≤ (insert j ({p, q} : Finset (Fin n))).card := by
      have : (insert j ({p, q} : Finset (Fin n))).Nonempty := ⟨j, mem_insert_self _ _⟩
      exact Nonempty.card_pos this
    have hcard2 : (insert j ({p, q} : Finset (Fin n))).card ≤ 3 := by
      have h_sub := card_insert_le j ({p, q} : Finset (Fin n))
      have h_pq : ({p, q} : Finset (Fin n)).card = 2 := by
        rw [card_insert_of_notMem (by simpa using hpq), Finset.card_singleton]
      omega
    have h_repr := hS.2 (insert j {p, q}) ⟨hcard1, hcard2⟩
    rw [h_repr]
  rw [← h_swap]
  exact h_zero

theorem line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_two_points (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ZMod 2) (a b : Fin n) (hab : a ≠ b) :
    (∑ j : Fin n, c j * (if j = a ∨ j = b then 1 else 0)) = c a + c b := by
  have h : ∀ j : Fin n, c j * (if j = a ∨ j = b then (1 : ZMod 2) else 0) =
      (if j = a then c a else 0) + (if j = b then c b else 0) := by
    intro j
    by_cases hja : j = a
    · rw [if_pos (Or.inl hja), if_pos hja]
      have hjb : j ≠ b := by rw [hja]; exact hab
      rw [if_neg hjb, hja]
      ring
    · by_cases hjb : j = b
      · rw [if_pos (Or.inr hjb), if_neg hja, if_pos hjb, hjb]
        ring
      · have hnab : ¬ (j = a ∨ j = b) := by tauto
        rw [if_neg hnab, if_neg hja, if_neg hjb]
        ring
  simp_rw [h, sum_add_distrib, sum_ite_eq']
  simp

theorem line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mid (n : ℕ)
    (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n))
    (c : Fin n → ZMod 2) (b : ZMod 2)
    (h : ∀ y ∈ S, (∑ j ∈ y, c j) = b)
    (i : Fin (n - 2)) :
    c ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ = 0 := by
  let p : Fin n := ⟨i.1, by omega⟩
  let q : Fin n := ⟨i.1 + 2, by omega⟩
  have hpq : p ≠ q := by
    intro heq
    have : p.1 = q.1 := congrArg Fin.val heq
    change i.1 = i.1 + 2 at this
    omega
  have h_syn : ∀ j : Fin n, line_syndrome n (insert j {p, q}) =
      if j = ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ then 1 else 0 := by
    intro j
    unfold line_syndrome
    by_cases hj : j = ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩
    · rw [if_pos hj]
      have hex : ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
        refine ⟨i, ?_⟩
        ext x
        simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff]
        rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
        dsimp [p, q]
        subst hj
        change x.1 = i.1 + 1 ∨ x.1 = i.1 ∨ x.1 = i.1 + 2 ↔ x.1 = i.1 ∨ x.1 = i.1 + 1 ∨ x.1 = i.1 + 2
        tauto
      exact if_pos hex
    · rw [if_neg hj]
      have h_not : ¬ ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
        rintro ⟨k, hk⟩
        have hp_in : p ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
          rw [← hk]
          simp
        have hq_in : q ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
          rw [← hk]
          simp
        rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple] at hp_in hq_in
        dsimp [p, q] at hp_in hq_in
        have hki : k.1 = i.1 := by omega
        have h_mid : (⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
          dsimp
          omega
        change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
        rw [← hk] at h_mid
        simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff] at h_mid
        dsimp [p, q] at h_mid
        change i.1 + 1 = j.1 ∨ i.1 + 1 = i.1 ∨ i.1 + 1 = i.1 + 2 at h_mid
        have : j = ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ := by
          ext
          change j.1 = i.1 + 1
          omega
        exact hj this
      exact if_neg h_not
  have h_pair := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_pair_sum n S hS c b h p q hpq
  have h_eval : (∑ j : Fin n, c j * line_syndrome n (insert j {p, q})) = c ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ := by
    have h_term : ∀ j : Fin n, c j * line_syndrome n (insert j {p, q}) =
        if j = ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ then c ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ else 0 := by
      intro j
      rw [h_syn]
      split_ifs with hj
      · subst hj; ring
      · ring
    simp_rw [h_term]
    rw [sum_ite_eq']
    simp
  rw [h_eval] at h_pair
  exact h_pair

theorem line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_zero (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n)
    (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n))
    (c : Fin n → ZMod 2) (b : ZMod 2)
    (h : ∀ y ∈ S, (∑ j ∈ y, c j) = b) :
    c ⟨0, by omega⟩ = 0 := by
  let p : Fin n := ⟨1, by omega⟩
  let q : Fin n := ⟨2, by omega⟩
  have hpq : p ≠ q := by
    intro heq
    have : p.1 = q.1 := congrArg Fin.val heq
    change 1 = 2 at this
    omega
  have h_pair := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_pair_sum n S hS c b h p q hpq
  have h_syn : ∀ j : Fin n, line_syndrome n (insert j {p, q}) =
      if j = ⟨0, by omega⟩ ∨ j = ⟨3, by omega⟩ then 1 else 0 := by
    intro j
    unfold line_syndrome
    by_cases hj : j = ⟨0, by omega⟩ ∨ j = ⟨3, by omega⟩
    · rw [if_pos hj]
      rcases hj with hj0 | hj3
      · have hex : ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          refine ⟨⟨0, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
          ext x
          simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff]
          rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
          dsimp [p, q]
          subst hj0
          change x.1 = 0 ∨ x.1 = 1 ∨ x.1 = 2 ↔ x.1 = 0 ∨ x.1 = 0 + 1 ∨ x.1 = 0 + 2
          tauto
        exact if_pos hex
      · have hex : ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          refine ⟨⟨1, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
          ext x
          simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff]
          rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
          dsimp [p, q]
          subst hj3
          change x.1 = 3 ∨ x.1 = 1 ∨ x.1 = 2 ↔ x.1 = 1 ∨ x.1 = 1 + 1 ∨ x.1 = 1 + 2
          tauto
        exact if_pos hex
    · rw [if_neg hj]
      have h_not : ¬ ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
        rintro ⟨k, hk⟩
        have hp_in : p ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
          rw [← hk]
          simp
        have hq_in : q ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
          rw [← hk]
          simp
        rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple] at hp_in hq_in
        dsimp [p, q] at hp_in hq_in
        change 1 = k.1 ∨ 1 = k.1 + 1 ∨ 1 = k.1 + 2 at hp_in
        change 2 = k.1 ∨ 2 = k.1 + 1 ∨ 2 = k.1 + 2 at hq_in
        have hk_cases : k.1 = 0 ∨ k.1 = 1 := by omega
        rcases hk_cases with hk0 | hk1
        · have hj0 : j = ⟨0, by omega⟩ := by
            have h0 : (⟨0, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
              rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
              dsimp
              omega
            change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
            rw [← hk] at h0
            simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff] at h0
            dsimp [p, q] at h0
            ext; change j.1 = 0; omega
          exact hj (Or.inl hj0)
        · have hj3 : j = ⟨3, by omega⟩ := by
            have h3 : (⟨3, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
              rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
              dsimp
              omega
            change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
            rw [← hk] at h3
            simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff] at h3
            dsimp [p, q] at h3
            ext; change j.1 = 3; omega
          exact hj (Or.inr hj3)
      exact if_neg h_not
  simp_rw [h_syn] at h_pair
  have h_eval := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_two_points n c ⟨0, by omega⟩ ⟨3, by omega⟩ (by
    intro heq
    have : (⟨0, by omega⟩ : Fin n).1 = (⟨3, by omega⟩ : Fin n).1 := congrArg Fin.val heq
    change 0 = 3 at this
    omega)
  rw [h_eval] at h_pair
  have h3 : c ⟨3, by omega⟩ = 0 := by
    have := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mid n S hS c b h ⟨2, by omega⟩
    exact this
  rw [h3, add_zero] at h_pair
  exact h_pair

theorem line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_last (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n)
    (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n))
    (c : Fin n → ZMod 2) (b : ZMod 2)
    (h : ∀ y ∈ S, (∑ j ∈ y, c j) = b) :
    c ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ = 0 := by
  let p : Fin n := ⟨n - 3, by omega⟩
  let q : Fin n := ⟨n - 2, by omega⟩
  have hpq : p ≠ q := by
    intro heq
    have : p.1 = q.1 := congrArg Fin.val heq
    change n - 3 = n - 2 at this
    omega
  have h_pair := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_pair_sum n S hS c b h p q hpq
  have h_syn : ∀ j : Fin n, line_syndrome n (insert j {p, q}) =
      if j = ⟨n - 4, by omega⟩ ∨ j = ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ then 1 else 0 := by
    intro j
    unfold line_syndrome
    by_cases hj : j = ⟨n - 4, by omega⟩ ∨ j = ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩
    · rw [if_pos hj]
      rcases hj with hj4 | hj1
      · have hex : ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          refine ⟨⟨n - 4, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
          ext x
          simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff]
          rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
          dsimp [p, q]
          subst hj4
          change x.1 = n - 4 ∨ x.1 = n - 3 ∨ x.1 = n - 2 ↔ x.1 = n - 4 ∨ x.1 = (n - 4) + 1 ∨ x.1 = (n - 4) + 2
          have h1 : (n - 4) + 1 = n - 3 := by omega
          have h2 : (n - 4) + 2 = n - 2 := by omega
          rw [h1, h2]
        exact if_pos hex
      · have hex : ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          refine ⟨⟨n - 3, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
          ext x
          simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff]
          rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
          dsimp [p, q]
          subst hj1
          change x.1 = n - 1 ∨ x.1 = n - 3 ∨ x.1 = n - 2 ↔ x.1 = n - 3 ∨ x.1 = (n - 3) + 1 ∨ x.1 = (n - 3) + 2
          have h1 : (n - 3) + 1 = n - 2 := by omega
          have h2 : (n - 3) + 2 = n - 1 := by omega
          rw [h1, h2]
          tauto
        exact if_pos hex
    · rw [if_neg hj]
      have h_not : ¬ ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
        rintro ⟨k, hk⟩
        have hp_in : p ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
          rw [← hk]
          simp
        have hq_in : q ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
          rw [← hk]
          simp
        rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple] at hp_in hq_in
        dsimp [p, q] at hp_in hq_in
        change n - 3 = k.1 ∨ n - 3 = k.1 + 1 ∨ n - 3 = k.1 + 2 at hp_in
        change n - 2 = k.1 ∨ n - 2 = k.1 + 1 ∨ n - 2 = k.1 + 2 at hq_in
        have hk_cases : k.1 = n - 4 ∨ k.1 = n - 3 := by
          have : k.1 < n - 2 := k.isLt
          omega
        rcases hk_cases with hk4 | hk3
        · have hj4 : j = ⟨n - 4, by omega⟩ := by
            have h0 : (⟨n - 4, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
              rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
              dsimp
              omega
            change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
            rw [← hk] at h0
            simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff] at h0
            dsimp [p, q] at h0
            ext; change j.1 = n - 4; omega
          exact hj (Or.inl hj4)
        · have hj1 : j = ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ := by
            have h0 : (⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
              rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
              dsimp
              omega
            change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
            rw [← hk] at h0
            simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff] at h0
            dsimp [p, q] at h0
            ext; change j.1 = n - 1; omega
          exact hj (Or.inr hj1)
      exact if_neg h_not
  simp_rw [h_syn] at h_pair
  have h_eval := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_two_points n c ⟨n - 4, by omega⟩ ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ (by
    intro heq
    have : (⟨n - 4, by omega⟩ : Fin n).1 = (⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ : Fin n).1 := congrArg Fin.val heq
    change n - 4 = n - 1 at this
    omega)
  rw [h_eval] at h_pair
  have h4 : c ⟨n - 4, by omega⟩ = 0 := by
    have := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mid n S hS c b h ⟨n - 5, by omega⟩
    have heq : (⟨(⟨n - 5, by omega⟩ : Fin (n - 2)).1 + 1, by omega⟩ : Fin n) = ⟨n - 4, by omega⟩ := by
      ext; change (n - 5) + 1 = n - 4; omega
    rw [← heq]
    exact this
  rw [h4, zero_add] at h_pair
  exact h_pair

/-- Any affine evaluation on all parities of a parity representation of the line cubic syndrome forces c = 0. -/
theorem line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n)
    (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n))
    (c : Fin n → ZMod 2) (b : ZMod 2)
    (h : ∀ y ∈ S, (∑ j ∈ y, c j) = b) :
    c = 0 := by
  ext x
  have hx : x.1 = 0 ∨ x.1 = n - 1 ∨ (1 ≤ x.1 ∧ x.1 ≤ n - 2) := by
    have : x.1 < n := x.isLt
    omega
  rcases hx with h0 | hn1 | hmid
  · have heq : x = ⟨0, by omega⟩ := by ext; exact h0
    rw [heq]
    exact line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_zero n hn S hS c b h
  · have heq : x = ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ := by ext; exact hn1
    rw [heq]
    exact line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_last n hn S hS c b h
  · have heq : x = ⟨(⟨x.1 - 1, by omega⟩ : Fin (n - 2)).1 + 1, by omega⟩ := by
      ext; change x.1 = (x.1 - 1) + 1; omega
    rw [heq]
    exact line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mid n S hS c b h ⟨x.1 - 1, by omega⟩

explanation.summary: To prove that any affine evaluation ∑_{j ∈ y} c_j = b on parities y ∈ S of the line cubic syndrome forces c = 0, the argument double counts parities containing a chosen pair {p, q} to establish the orthogonality identity ∑_j c_j • line_syndrome n {j, p, q} = 0 for all p ≠ q. Choosing pairs separated by distance 2 (p = i, q = i + 2) isolates each internal coordinate, showing c_{i+1} = 0 for all 0 ≤ i ≤ n - 3. Finally, choosing the adjacent pairs {1, 2} and {n - 3, n - 2} connects the boundary coordinates c_0 and c_{n-1} to already vanished internal coordinates (c_3 and c_{n-4}), forcing the boundary coordinates to be zero as well.

steps.claim: For any non-empty set of vertices A with |A| ≤ 2, the number of parities in S containing A is 0 modulo 2.
steps.explanation: By definition of a parity representation, the count modulo 2 of parities containing A equals line_syndrome n A. The line syndrome is 1 only for consecutive triples of cardinality 3; since |A| ≤ 2, A cannot be such a triple, so the syndrome evaluates to 0.
steps.code:
have hrepr := hS.2 A ⟨hA1, by omega⟩
  rw [hrepr]
  unfold line_syndrome
  split_ifs with h
  · rcases h with ⟨i, hi⟩
    have hc : ({⟨i.1, by omega⟩, ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩, ⟨i.1 + 2, by omega⟩} : Finset (Fin n)).card = 3 := by
      have h01 : (⟨i.1, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ≠ ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ := by
        intro heq; injection heq with heq; omega
      have h02 : (⟨i.1, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ≠ ⟨i.1 + 2, by omega⟩ := by
        intro heq; injection heq with heq; omega
      have h12 : (⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ≠ ⟨i.1 + 2, by omega⟩ := by
        intro heq; injection heq with heq; omega
      rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem, Finset.card_insert_of_notMem, Finset.card_singleton]
      · intro hm; simp only [Finset.mem_singleton] at hm; exact h12 hm
      · simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton]; rintro (hm | hm)
        · exact h01 hm
        · exact h02 hm
    rw [hi] at hA2
    omega
  · rfl

steps.claim: Membership in the consecutive triple starting at i corresponds to index i, i+1, or i+2.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of the consecutive triple line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple, an index a belongs to the triple if and only if a = i, a = i + 1, or a = i + 2.

steps.claim: For any distinct pair p ≠ q, the sum of affine evaluations over all parities containing {p, q} is 0.
steps.explanation: Since each parity y ∈ S evaluates to the constant b, summing over all parities containing {p, q} yields |{y ∈ S | {p, q} ⊆ y}| • b. Because |{p, q}| = 2, this parity count is 0 modulo 2 by the small-cardinality lemma, so the product is 0.
steps.code:
have h_zero : (∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), (∑ j ∈ y, c j)) = 0 := by
    have h1 : (∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), (∑ j ∈ y, c j)) =
        ∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), b := by
      refine sum_congr rfl (fun y hy => ?_)
      rw [mem_filter] at hy
      exact h y hy.1
    rw [h1, sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
    have hcard1 : 1 ≤ ({p, q} : Finset (Fin n)).card := by
      rw [card_insert_of_notMem (by simpa using hpq), Finset.card_singleton]
      omega
    have hcard2 : ({p, q} : Finset (Fin n)).card ≤ 2 := by
      rw [card_insert_of_notMem (by simpa using hpq), Finset.card_singleton]
    have hz := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_card_le_two n S hS {p, q} hcard1 hcard2
    rw [hz, zero_mul]

steps.claim: For any distinct pair p ≠ q, the pair-sum identity ∑_j c_j • line_syndrome n {j, p, q} = 0 holds.
steps.explanation: Writing the sum over y of ∑_{j ∈ y} c_j and exchanging the order of summation yields ∑_j c_j • |{y ∈ S | {j, p, q} ⊆ y}|. By the parity representation property, this parity count modulo 2 is line_syndrome n {j, p, q}, which equates the sum to the previously established 0.
steps.code:
have h_swap : (∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), (∑ j ∈ y, c j)) =
      ∑ j : Fin n, c j * line_syndrome n (insert j {p, q}) := by
    have h1 : (∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), (∑ j ∈ y, c j)) =
        ∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), ∑ j : Fin n, (if j ∈ y then c j else 0) := by
      refine sum_congr rfl (fun y _ => (sum_ite_mem_eq y c).symm)
    rw [h1, sum_comm]
    refine sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => ?_)
    have h2 : (∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), (if j ∈ y then c j else 0)) =
        c j * ∑ y ∈ S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y), (if j ∈ y then (1 : ZMod 2) else 0) := by
      rw [mul_sum]
      refine sum_congr rfl (fun y _ => by split_ifs <;> ring)
    rw [h2, sum_boole]
    have h3 : (S.filter (fun y => {p, q} ⊆ y)).filter (fun y => j ∈ y) =
        S.filter (fun y => insert j {p, q} ⊆ y) := by
      ext y
      simp only [mem_filter, Finset.insert_subset_iff]
      tauto
    rw [h3]
    have hcard1 : 1 ≤ (insert j ({p, q} : Finset (Fin n))).card := by
      have : (insert j ({p, q} : Finset (Fin n))).Nonempty := ⟨j, mem_insert_self _ _⟩
      exact Nonempty.card_pos this
    have hcard2 : (insert j ({p, q} : Finset (Fin n))).card ≤ 3 := by
      have h_sub := card_insert_le j ({p, q} : Finset (Fin n))
      have h_pq : ({p, q} : Finset (Fin n)).card = 2 := by
        rw [card_insert_of_notMem (by simpa using hpq), Finset.card_singleton]
      omega
    have h_repr := hS.2 (insert j {p, q}) ⟨hcard1, hcard2⟩
    rw [h_repr]
  rw [← h_swap]
  exact h_zero

steps.claim: Evaluating c against the indicator of two distinct points a ≠ b gives c a + c b.
steps.explanation: Decomposing the two-point indicator into a sum of two single-point indicators and distributing the summation over all j isolates c a + c b.
steps.code:
have h : ∀ j : Fin n, c j * (if j = a ∨ j = b then (1 : ZMod 2) else 0) =
      (if j = a then c a else 0) + (if j = b then c b else 0) := by
    intro j
    by_cases hja : j = a
    · rw [if_pos (Or.inl hja), if_pos hja]
      have hjb : j ≠ b := by rw [hja]; exact hab
      rw [if_neg hjb, hja]
      ring
    · by_cases hjb : j = b
      · rw [if_pos (Or.inr hjb), if_neg hja, if_pos hjb, hjb]
        ring
      · have hnab : ¬ (j = a ∨ j = b) := by tauto
        rw [if_neg hnab, if_neg hja, if_neg hjb]
        ring
  simp_rw [h, sum_add_distrib, sum_ite_eq']
  simp

steps.claim: Every internal coordinate c_{i+1} is 0 for 0 ≤ i ≤ n - 3.
steps.explanation: Apply the pair-sum identity to p = i and q = i + 2. The only index j such that {j, i, i + 2} is a consecutive triple is j = i + 1, so the syndrome indicator collapses the sum to c_{i+1} = 0.
steps.code:
c ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ = 0 := by
  let p : Fin n := ⟨i.1, by omega⟩
  let q : Fin n := ⟨i.1 + 2, by omega⟩
  have hpq : p ≠ q := by
    intro heq
    have : p.1 = q.1 := congrArg Fin.val heq
    change i.1 = i.1 + 2 at this
    omega
  have h_syn : ∀ j : Fin n, line_syndrome n (insert j {p, q}) =
      if j = ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ then 1 else 0 := by
    intro j
    unfold line_syndrome
    by_cases hj : j = ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩
    · rw [if_pos hj]
      have hex : ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
        refine ⟨i, ?_⟩
        ext x
        simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff]
        rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
        dsimp [p, q]
        subst hj
        change x.1 = i.1 + 1 ∨ x.1 = i.1 ∨ x.1 = i.1 + 2 ↔ x.1 = i.1 ∨ x.1 = i.1 + 1 ∨ x.1 = i.1 + 2
        tauto
      exact if_pos hex
    · rw [if_neg hj]
      have h_not : ¬ ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
        rintro ⟨k, hk⟩
        have hp_in : p ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
          rw [← hk]
          simp
        have hq_in : q ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
          rw [← hk]
          simp
        rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple] at hp_in hq_in
        dsimp [p, q] at hp_in hq_in
        have hki : k.1 = i.1 := by omega
        have h_mid : (⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
          dsimp
          omega
        change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
        rw [← hk] at h_mid
        simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff] at h_mid
        dsimp [p, q] at h_mid
        change i.1 + 1 = j.1 ∨ i.1 + 1 = i.1 ∨ i.1 + 1 = i.1 + 2 at h_mid
        have : j = ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ := by
          ext
          change j.1 = i.1 + 1
          omega
        exact hj this
      exact if_neg h_not
  have h_pair := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_pair_sum n S hS c b h p q hpq
  have h_eval : (∑ j : Fin n, c j * line_syndrome n (insert j {p, q})) = c ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ := by
    have h_term : ∀ j : Fin n, c j * line_syndrome n (insert j {p, q}) =
        if j = ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ then c ⟨i.1 + 1, by omega⟩ else 0 := by
      intro j
      rw [h_syn]
      split_ifs with hj
      · subst hj; ring
      · ring
    simp_rw [h_term]
    rw [sum_ite_eq']
    simp
  rw [h_eval] at h_pair
  exact h_pair

steps.claim: The first coordinate c 0 is 0.
steps.explanation: Apply the pair-sum identity to the adjacent pair p = 1 and q = 2. The only indices completing {1, 2} to a consecutive triple are j = 0 and j = 3, yielding c 0 + c 3 = 0. Since n ≥ 5, index 3 is an internal coordinate (3 = 2 + 1 ≤ n - 2), so c 3 = 0, which forces c 0 = 0.
steps.code:
c ⟨0, by omega⟩ = 0 := by
  let p : Fin n := ⟨1, by omega⟩
  let q : Fin n := ⟨2, by omega⟩
  have hpq : p ≠ q := by
    intro heq
    have : p.1 = q.1 := congrArg Fin.val heq
    change 1 = 2 at this
    omega
  have h_pair := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_pair_sum n S hS c b h p q hpq
  have h_syn : ∀ j : Fin n, line_syndrome n (insert j {p, q}) =
      if j = ⟨0, by omega⟩ ∨ j = ⟨3, by omega⟩ then 1 else 0 := by
    intro j
    unfold line_syndrome
    by_cases hj : j = ⟨0, by omega⟩ ∨ j = ⟨3, by omega⟩
    · rw [if_pos hj]
      rcases hj with hj0 | hj3
      · have hex : ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          refine ⟨⟨0, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
          ext x
          simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff]
          rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
          dsimp [p, q]
          subst hj0
          change x.1 = 0 ∨ x.1 = 1 ∨ x.1 = 2 ↔ x.1 = 0 ∨ x.1 = 0 + 1 ∨ x.1 = 0 + 2
          tauto
        exact if_pos hex
      · have hex : ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          refine ⟨⟨1, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
          ext x
          simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff]
          rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
          dsimp [p, q]
          subst hj3
          change x.1 = 3 ∨ x.1 = 1 ∨ x.1 = 2 ↔ x.1 = 1 ∨ x.1 = 1 + 1 ∨ x.1 = 1 + 2
          tauto
        exact if_pos hex
    · rw [if_neg hj]
      have h_not : ¬ ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
        rintro ⟨k, hk⟩
        have hp_in : p ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
          rw [← hk]
          simp
        have hq_in : q ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
          rw [← hk]
          simp
        rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple] at hp_in hq_in
        dsimp [p, q] at hp_in hq_in
        change 1 = k.1 ∨ 1 = k.1 + 1 ∨ 1 = k.1 + 2 at hp_in
        change 2 = k.1 ∨ 2 = k.1 + 1 ∨ 2 = k.1 + 2 at hq_in
        have hk_cases : k.1 = 0 ∨ k.1 = 1 := by omega
        rcases hk_cases with hk0 | hk1
        · have hj0 : j = ⟨0, by omega⟩ := by
            have h0 : (⟨0, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
              rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
              dsimp
              omega
            change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
            rw [← hk] at h0
            simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff] at h0
            dsimp [p, q] at h0
            ext; change j.1 = 0; omega
          exact hj (Or.inl hj0)
        · have hj3 : j = ⟨3, by omega⟩ := by
            have h3 : (⟨3, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
              rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
              dsimp
              omega
            change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk
            rw [← hk] at h3
            simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff] at h3
            dsimp [p, q] at h3
            ext; change j.1 = 3; omega
          exact hj (Or.inr hj3)
      exact if_neg h_not
  simp_rw [h_syn] at h_pair
  have h_eval := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_two_points n c ⟨0, by omega⟩ ⟨3, by omega⟩ (by
    intro heq
    have : (⟨0, by omega⟩ : Fin n).1 = (⟨3, by omega⟩ : Fin n).1 := congrArg Fin.val heq
    change 0 = 3 at this
    omega)
  rw [h_eval] at h_pair
  have h3 : c ⟨3, by omega⟩ = 0 := by
    have := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mid n S hS c b h ⟨2, by omega⟩
    exact this
  rw [h3, add_zero] at h_pair
  exact h_pair

steps.claim: The last coordinate c_{n-1} is 0.
steps.explanation: Apply the pair-sum identity to p = n - 3 and q = n - 2. The only indices completing this pair to a consecutive triple are j = n - 4 and j = n - 1, yielding c_{n-4} + c_{n-1} = 0. Since n ≥ 5, n - 4 is an internal coordinate ((n - 5) + 1), so c_{n-4} = 0, forcing c_{n-1} = 0.
steps.code:
c ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ = 0 := by
  let p : Fin n := ⟨n - 3, by omega⟩
  let q : Fin n := ⟨n - 2, by omega⟩
  have hpq : p ≠ q := by
    intro heq
    have : p.1 = q.1 := congrArg Fin.val heq
    change n - 3 = n - 2 at this
    omega
  have h_pair := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_pair_sum n S hS c b h p q hpq
  have h_syn : ∀ j : Fin n, line_syndrome n (insert j {p, q}) =
      if j = ⟨n - 4, by omega⟩ ∨ j = ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ then 1 else 0 := by
    intro j
    unfold line_syndrome
    by_cases hj : j = ⟨n - 4, by omega⟩ ∨ j = ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩
    · rw [if_pos hj]
      rcases hj with hj4 | hj1
      · have hex : ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          refine ⟨⟨n - 4, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
          ext x
          simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff]
          rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
          dsimp [p, q]
          subst hj4
          change x.1 = n - 4 ∨ x.1 = n - 3 ∨ x.1 = n - 2 ↔ x.1 = n - 4 ∨ x.1 = (n - 4) + 1 ∨ x.1 = (n - 4) + 2
          have h1 : (n - 4) + 1 = n - 3 := by omega
          have h2 : (n - 4) + 2 = n - 2 := by omega
          rw [h1, h2]
        exact if_pos hex
      · have hex : ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          refine ⟨⟨n - 3, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
          ext x
          simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, Fin.ext_iff]
          rw [line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_mem_line_triple]
          dsimp [p, q]
          subst hj1
          change x.1 = n - 1 ∨ x.1 = n - 3 ∨ x.1 = n - 2 ↔ x.1 = n - 3 ∨ x.1 = (n - 3) + 1 ∨ x.1 = (n - 3) + 2
          have h1 : (n - 3) + 1 = n - 2 := by omega
          have h2 : (n - 3) + 2 = n - 1 := by omega
          rw [h1, h2]
          tauto
        exact if_pos hex
    · rw [if_neg hj]
      have h_not : ¬ ∃ k : Fin (n - 2), insert j {p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
        rintro ⟨k, hk⟩
        have hp_in : p ∈ line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k := by
          change {j, p, q} = line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero_line_triple n k at hk

declarations.name: line_cubic_t_count_lower_bound
declarations.informal: For any n ≥ 5, every parity representation of the line cubic syndrome has cardinality at least 2n + 1.
declarations.statement: theorem line_cubic_t_count_lower_bound (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n) (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n)) : 2 * n + 1 ≤ S.card
declarations.source:
/-- Proposition 65 floor: every parity representation of the line cubic syndrome has at least 2n + 1 parities for n ≥ 5. -/
theorem line_cubic_t_count_lower_bound (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n) (S : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hS : is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n)) : 2 * n + 1 ≤ S.card := by
  let evalMap : (Fin n → ZMod 2) →ₗ[ZMod 2] (S → ZMod 2) := {
    toFun := fun c y => ∑ j ∈ (y : Finset (Fin n)), c j
    map_add' := by
      intro c d
      ext ⟨y, hy⟩
      dsimp
      rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    map_smul' := by
      intro a c
      ext ⟨y, hy⟩
      dsimp
      exact (Finset.mul_sum _ _ _).symm
  }
  let V : Submodule (ZMod 2) (S → ZMod 2) := LinearMap.range evalMap
  have h_iso : ∀ u ∈ V, ∀ v ∈ V, (∑ m, u m * v m) = 0 := by
    rintro u ⟨c, rfl⟩ v ⟨d, rfl⟩
    have h1 : (∑ m : S, evalMap c m * evalMap d m) =
              ∑ y ∈ S, (∑ j ∈ y, c j) * (∑ k ∈ y, d k) :=
      Finset.sum_coe_sort S (fun y => (∑ j ∈ y, c j) * (∑ k ∈ y, d k))
    rw [h1]
    exact (line_cubic_parity_repr_ortho n S hS c d).1
  have h_ones_ortho : ∀ v ∈ V, ∑ m, v m = 0 := by
    rintro v ⟨c, rfl⟩
    have h1 : (∑ m : S, evalMap c m) = ∑ y ∈ S, ∑ j ∈ y, c j :=
      Finset.sum_coe_sort S (fun y => ∑ j ∈ y, c j)
    rw [h1]
    exact (line_cubic_parity_repr_ortho n S hS c 0).2
  have h_ones_notin : (fun _ : S => (1 : ZMod 2)) ∉ V := by
    intro ⟨c, hc⟩
    have h_eval : ∀ y ∈ S, ∑ j ∈ y, c j = 1 := by
      intro y hy
      exact congr_fun hc ⟨y, hy⟩
    have hc0 : c = 0 := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero n hn S hS c 1 h_eval
    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := line_cubic_parity_repr_nonempty n hn S hS
    have h1 := congr_fun hc ⟨y, hy⟩
    dsimp [evalMap] at h1
    rw [hc0] at h1
    simp only [Pi.zero_apply, Finset.sum_const_zero] at h1
    exact zero_ne_one h1
  have h_inj : Function.Injective evalMap := by
    rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, LinearMap.ker_eq_bot']
    intro c hc
    have h1 : ∀ y ∈ S, ∑ j ∈ y, c j = 0 := by
      intro y hy
      exact congr_fun hc ⟨y, hy⟩
    exact line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero n hn S hS c 0 h1
  have h_rank : Module.finrank (ZMod 2) V = n := by
    rw [LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj h_inj]
    simp
  have h_bound := isotropic_subspace_lower_bound V h_iso h_ones_ortho h_ones_notin
  rw [h_rank] at h_bound
  have h_card : Fintype.card S = S.card := by simp
  rwa [h_card] at h_bound
declarations.reading: For any natural number $n \ge 5$ and any finite set $S$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, if $S$ is a parity representation of the line syndrome of length $n$ (meaning that every set in $S$ is nonempty, and for every subset $A \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ of size between 1 and 3, the number of sets in $S$ containing $A$ is odd if $A$ is a contiguous triple $\{i, i+1, i+2\}$ for some $0 \le i < n-2$, and even otherwise), then $S$ contains at least $2n + 1$ sets.

explanation.summary: The lower bound is established by embedding 𝔽₂ⁿ into 𝔽₂^S via a linear evaluation map sending each vector c to its parity sums over the sets in S. Using the orthogonality relations of parity representations of the line cubic syndrome, the image subspace V is shown to be self-orthogonal and orthogonal to the all-ones vector. Since the evaluation map is injective and non-degenerate, V has dimension n and does not contain the all-ones vector, so an isotropic subspace dimension bound implies |S| ≥ 2n + 1.

steps.claim: The evaluation mapping evalMap : 𝔽₂ⁿ → 𝔽₂^S sending c to (y ↦ ∑_{j ∈ y} c j) is a linear map, and V = range(evalMap) is a linear subspace of 𝔽₂^S.
steps.explanation: Evaluating a vector on a parity set y is linear in c: additivity follows from distributing sums over addition (Finset.sum_add_distrib), and compatibility with scalar multiplication follows from distributing multiplication over sums (Finset.mul_sum). Its image V is then defined as the range subspace in 𝔽₂^S.
steps.code:
let evalMap : (Fin n → ZMod 2) →ₗ[ZMod 2] (S → ZMod 2) := {
    toFun := fun c y => ∑ j ∈ (y : Finset (Fin n)), c j
    map_add' := by
      intro c d
      ext ⟨y, hy⟩
      dsimp
      rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    map_smul' := by
      intro a c
      ext ⟨y, hy⟩
      dsimp
      exact (Finset.mul_sum _ _ _).symm
  }
  let V : Submodule (ZMod 2) (S → ZMod 2) := LinearMap.range evalMap

steps.claim: The subspace V is isotropic (self-orthogonal): for all u, v ∈ V, ∑_{y ∈ S} u(y) v(y) = 0.
steps.explanation: Any u, v ∈ V are the images of vectors c, d ∈ 𝔽₂ⁿ under evalMap. Converting the sum over the subtype S to a sum over the finset S using Finset.sum_coe_sort, the inner product is ∑_{y ∈ S} (∑_{j ∈ y} c j) * (∑_{k ∈ y} d k), which vanishes by the first part of line_cubic_parity_repr_ortho.
steps.code:
have h_iso : ∀ u ∈ V, ∀ v ∈ V, (∑ m, u m * v m) = 0 := by
    rintro u ⟨c, rfl⟩ v ⟨d, rfl⟩
    have h1 : (∑ m : S, evalMap c m * evalMap d m) =
              ∑ y ∈ S, (∑ j ∈ y, c j) * (∑ k ∈ y, d k) :=
      Finset.sum_coe_sort S (fun y => (∑ j ∈ y, c j) * (∑ k ∈ y, d k))
    rw [h1]
    exact (line_cubic_parity_repr_ortho n S hS c d).1

steps.claim: Every vector v ∈ V is orthogonal to the all-ones vector, meaning ∑_{y ∈ S} v(y) = 0.
steps.explanation: Any vector v ∈ V is the evaluation of some c ∈ 𝔽₂ⁿ. Rewriting the sum over the finset S via Finset.sum_coe_sort gives ∑_{y ∈ S} ∑_{j ∈ y} c j, which is zero by the second part of line_cubic_parity_repr_ortho (evaluating at c and the zero vector).
steps.code:
have h_ones_ortho : ∀ v ∈ V, ∑ m, v m = 0 := by
    rintro v ⟨c, rfl⟩
    have h1 : (∑ m : S, evalMap c m) = ∑ y ∈ S, ∑ j ∈ y, c j :=
      Finset.sum_coe_sort S (fun y => ∑ j ∈ y, c j)
    rw [h1]
    exact (line_cubic_parity_repr_ortho n S hS c 0).2

steps.claim: The all-ones vector 1 ∈ 𝔽₂^S is not in V.
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that the all-ones vector is in V, so evalMap(c) = 1 for some c. Then ∑_{j ∈ y} c j = 1 for all y ∈ S by congr_fun. By line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero, this forces c = 0. But S is nonempty by line_cubic_parity_repr_nonempty, so picking any y ∈ S and evaluating evalMap(0) yields 0 = 1 using Pi.zero_apply and Finset.sum_const_zero, contradicting zero_ne_one.
steps.code:
have h_ones_notin : (fun _ : S => (1 : ZMod 2)) ∉ V := by
    intro ⟨c, hc⟩
    have h_eval : ∀ y ∈ S, ∑ j ∈ y, c j = 1 := by
      intro y hy
      exact congr_fun hc ⟨y, hy⟩
    have hc0 : c = 0 := line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero n hn S hS c 1 h_eval
    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := line_cubic_parity_repr_nonempty n hn S hS
    have h1 := congr_fun hc ⟨y, hy⟩
    dsimp [evalMap] at h1
    rw [hc0] at h1
    simp only [Pi.zero_apply, Finset.sum_const_zero] at h1
    exact zero_ne_one h1

steps.claim: The evaluation map evalMap is injective.
steps.explanation: By LinearMap.ker_eq_bot and LinearMap.ker_eq_bot', injectivity is equivalent to having a trivial kernel. If evalMap(c) = 0, then evaluating at each y ∈ S via congr_fun shows that ∑_{j ∈ y} c j = 0 for all y ∈ S. Since n ≥ 5, line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero with constant 0 implies c = 0.
steps.code:
have h_inj : Function.Injective evalMap := by
    rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, LinearMap.ker_eq_bot']
    intro c hc
    have h1 : ∀ y ∈ S, ∑ j ∈ y, c j = 0 := by
      intro y hy
      exact congr_fun hc ⟨y, hy⟩
    exact line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero n hn S hS c 0 h1

steps.claim: The dimension (finite rank) of V over 𝔽₂ is n.
steps.explanation: Because evalMap is injective, LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj shows that the dimension of its image V equals the dimension of its domain 𝔽₂ⁿ, which is n.
steps.code:
have h_rank : Module.finrank (ZMod 2) V = n := by
    rw [LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj h_inj]
    simp

steps.claim: The cardinality of S is at least 2n + 1.
steps.explanation: Applying the general bound isotropic_subspace_lower_bound to the subspace V (which is isotropic, orthogonal to the all-ones vector, and does not contain the all-ones vector) yields 2 * dim(V) + 1 ≤ |S|. Substituting dim(V) = n gives 2n + 1 ≤ |S|.
steps.code:
have h_bound := isotropic_subspace_lower_bound V h_iso h_ones_ortho h_ones_notin
  rw [h_rank] at h_bound
  have h_card : Fintype.card S = S.card := by simp
  rwa [h_card] at h_bound

glossary.Finset.sum_add_distrib: The sum of a sum of functions over a finite set equals the sum of their individual sums.
glossary.Finset.mul_sum: Multiplication distributes over finite sums from the left.
glossary.Finset.sum_coe_sort: A sum over the elements of a subtype coerced from a finite set s equals the sum directly over s.
glossary.line_cubic_parity_repr_ortho: For any parity representation S of the line cubic syndrome and any vectors c and d, the sum over S of the product of evaluations of c and d is 0, and the sum over S of evaluations of c is 0.
glossary.congr_fun: Equal functions take equal values on equal inputs.
glossary.line_cubic_parity_repr_eval_zero: If a vector c has a constant evaluation b across all parity sets y ∈ S for a parity representation of the line cubic syndrome (with n ≥ 5), then c = 0.
glossary.line_cubic_parity_repr_nonempty: A parity representation of the line cubic syndrome is nonempty when n ≥ 5.
glossary.Pi.zero_apply: The zero function evaluated at any input returns zero.
glossary.Finset.sum_const_zero: The sum of zero over any finite set is zero.
glossary.zero_ne_one: Zero is not equal to one.
glossary.LinearMap.ker_eq_bot: A linear map is injective if and only if its kernel is trivial.
glossary.LinearMap.ker_eq_bot': The kernel of a linear map is trivial if and only if every element mapped to zero is zero.
glossary.LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj: An injective linear map preserves the finite rank (dimension) of its domain.
glossary.isotropic_subspace_lower_bound: Any subspace V ⊆ 𝔽₂^M that is self-orthogonal, orthogonal to the all-ones vector, and does not contain the all-ones vector satisfies 2 * dim(V) + 1 ≤ |M|.

declarations.name: bipartite_hall_step_is_vertex_cover
declarations.informal: In a bipartite graph with partition (A, B) and a vertex cover C, for any subset S of A ∩ C, the set (C \ S) ∪ (N(S) ∩ (B \ C)) is also a vertex cover of G.
declarations.statement:
theorem bipartite_hall_step_is_vertex_cover {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (A B C S : Set V)
    (hdisj : Disjoint A B)
    (hadj : ∀ ⦃v w⦄, G.Adj v w → (v ∈ A ∧ w ∈ B) ∨ (v ∈ B ∧ w ∈ A))
    (hC : G.IsVertexCover C) (hS : S ⊆ A ∩ C) :
    G.IsVertexCover ((C \ S) ∪ {b ∈ B \ C | ∃ a ∈ S, G.Adj a b})
declarations.source:
/-- In a bipartite graph, replacing a subset S of a vertex cover C in partition A with its neighbors in partition B outside C preserves the vertex cover property. -/
theorem bipartite_hall_step_is_vertex_cover {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (A B C S : Set V)
    (hdisj : Disjoint A B)
    (hadj : ∀ ⦃v w⦄, G.Adj v w → (v ∈ A ∧ w ∈ B) ∨ (v ∈ B ∧ w ∈ A))
    (hC : G.IsVertexCover C) (hS : S ⊆ A ∩ C) :
    G.IsVertexCover ((C \ S) ∪ {b ∈ B \ C | ∃ a ∈ S, G.Adj a b}) := by
  intro v w hvw
  have h_dir : ∀ {x y : V}, G.Adj x y → x ∈ A → y ∈ B →
      x ∈ (C \ S) ∪ {b ∈ B \ C | ∃ a ∈ S, G.Adj a b} ∨
      y ∈ (C \ S) ∪ {b ∈ B \ C | ∃ a ∈ S, G.Adj a b} := by
    intro x y hxy hxA hyB
    by_cases hyC : y ∈ C
    · right
      left
      exact ⟨hyC, fun hyS => Set.disjoint_iff.mp hdisj ⟨(hS hyS).1, hyB⟩⟩
    · have hxC : x ∈ C := (hC hxy).resolve_right hyC
      by_cases hxS : x ∈ S
      · right
        right
        exact ⟨⟨hyB, hyC⟩, x, hxS, hxy⟩
      · left
        left
        exact ⟨hxC, hxS⟩
  rcases hadj hvw with ⟨hvA, hwB⟩ | ⟨hvB, hwA⟩
  · exact h_dir hvw hvA hwB
  · exact (h_dir (G.adj_symm hvw) hwA hvB).symm

explanation.summary: To show that replacing a subset S ⊆ A ∩ C in a vertex cover C with its neighbors N(S) ∩ (B \ C) yields another vertex cover, we consider an arbitrary edge. By bipartiteness and symmetry, it suffices to show that any edge between x ∈ A and y ∈ B is covered. Since C is a vertex cover, at least one endpoint is in C: if y ∈ C, disjointness of A and B prevents y from belonging to S, so y ∈ C \ S; if y ∉ C, then x ∈ C, and either x ∉ S (so x ∈ C \ S) or x ∈ S (which places y into N(S) ∩ (B \ C)). In all cases, at least one endpoint is in the new set.

steps.claim: To show that the modified set is a vertex cover, it suffices to show that an arbitrary edge has at least one endpoint in it.
steps.explanation: Fix an arbitrary pair of adjacent vertices v and w in G. By definition of a vertex cover, we must show that at least one of v or w belongs to (C \ S) ∪ {b ∈ B \ C | ∃ a ∈ S, G.Adj a b}.
steps.code: intro v w hvw

steps.claim: For any edge between x ∈ A and y ∈ B, if y ∈ C, then y is in the new vertex cover.
steps.explanation: We set up an auxiliary lemma h_dir asserting that any edge directed from A to B is covered by the new set. Given adjacent vertices x ∈ A and y ∈ B, we split into cases on whether y ∈ C. If y ∈ C, we show y ∈ C \ S. If y were in S, then since S ⊆ A, y would belong to A ∩ B, contradicting the assumption that A and B are disjoint (Set.disjoint_iff.mp). Hence y ∉ S, so y ∈ C \ S, placing y in the new vertex cover.
steps.code:
have h_dir : ∀ {x y : V}, G.Adj x y → x ∈ A → y ∈ B →
      x ∈ (C \ S) ∪ {b ∈ B \ C | ∃ a ∈ S, G.Adj a b} ∨
      y ∈ (C \ S) ∪ {b ∈ B \ C | ∃ a ∈ S, G.Adj a b} := by
    intro x y hxy hxA hyB
    by_cases hyC : y ∈ C
    · right
      left
      exact ⟨hyC, fun hyS => Set.disjoint_iff.mp hdisj ⟨(hS hyS).1, hyB⟩⟩

steps.explanation: If y ∉ C, then because C is a vertex cover of G, the edge between x and y must have at least one endpoint in C; since y ∉ C, we have x ∈ C by disjunctive syllogism (resolve_right). We then split on whether x ∈ S: if x ∈ S, then y is a neighbor in B \ C of a vertex in S, so y belongs to {b ∈ B \ C | ∃ a ∈ S, G.Adj a b}; if x ∉ S, then x ∈ C \ S. In either case, one of the endpoints is in the new set, which establishes h_dir.
steps.code:
· have hxC : x ∈ C := (hC hxy).resolve_right hyC
      by_cases hxS : x ∈ S
      · right
        right
        exact ⟨⟨hyB, hyC⟩, x, hxS, hxy⟩
      · left
        left
        exact ⟨hxC, hxS⟩

steps.claim: The edge between v and w is covered by the new set, so the set is a vertex cover.
steps.explanation: By the bipartiteness hypothesis, the edge between v and w has either v ∈ A and w ∈ B, or v ∈ B and w ∈ A. In the first case, h_dir directly shows that v or w is in the new set. In the second case, by symmetry of adjacency (G.adj_symm), w is adjacent to v with w ∈ A and v ∈ B; applying h_dir shows that w or v is in the new set, and swapping the disjunction concludes the proof.
steps.code:
rcases hadj hvw with ⟨hvA, hwB⟩ | ⟨hvB, hwA⟩
  · exact h_dir hvw hvA hwB
  · exact (h_dir (G.adj_symm hvw) hwA hvB).symm

glossary.Set.disjoint_iff.mp: If two sets are disjoint, their intersection is empty (a subset of the empty set).
glossary.resolve_right: Given a disjunction P ∨ Q and the negation ¬Q, the disjunct P holds.
glossary.G.adj_symm: Adjacency in a simple graph is symmetric: if v is adjacent to w, then w is adjacent to v.

declarations.name: isMatching_sup_disjoint_encard
declarations.informal: For two matchings M and M' in G with disjoint vertex sets, their supremum M ⊔ M' is also a matching, and its edge cardinality is the sum of their edge cardinalities.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMatching_sup_disjoint_encard {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} (M M' : SimpleGraph.Subgraph G)
    (hM : M.IsMatching) (hM' : M'.IsMatching) (hd : Disjoint M.verts M'.verts) :
    (M ⊔ M').IsMatching ∧ (M ⊔ M').edgeSet.encard = M.edgeSet.encard + M'.edgeSet.encard
declarations.source:
/-- The supremum of two matchings with disjoint vertex sets is a matching whose edge count is the sum of their edge counts. -/
theorem isMatching_sup_disjoint_encard {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} (M M' : SimpleGraph.Subgraph G)
    (hM : M.IsMatching) (hM' : M'.IsMatching) (hd : Disjoint M.verts M'.verts) :
    (M ⊔ M').IsMatching ∧ (M ⊔ M').edgeSet.encard = M.edgeSet.encard + M'.edgeSet.encard := by
  refine ⟨hM.sup hM' ?_, ?_⟩
  · rwa [hM.support_eq_verts, hM'.support_eq_verts]
  · rw [SimpleGraph.Subgraph.edgeSet_sup, Set.encard_union_eq]
    rw [Set.disjoint_left]
    intro e he he'
    induction e using Sym2.ind with
    | h v w =>
      have hvM : v ∈ M.verts := M.mem_verts_of_mem_edge he (Sym2.mem_mk_left v w)
      have hvM' : v ∈ M'.verts := M'.mem_verts_of_mem_edge he' (Sym2.mem_mk_left v w)
      exact Set.disjoint_left.mp hd hvM hvM'

explanation.summary: The proof splits the theorem into two parts: showing that the supremum M ⊔ M' is a matching, and establishing the edge count equality. First, the supremum of two matchings is a matching whenever their supports are disjoint, which holds because the support of a matching equals its vertex set and the vertex sets are assumed disjoint. Second, the edge set of the supremum is the union of the edge sets, and this union is disjoint because any shared edge would have endpoints belonging to both matchings, contradicting the vertex disjointness assumption.

steps.claim: The supremum M ⊔ M' is a matching.
steps.explanation: We split the conjunction into two goals. For the first conjunct, by general properties of matchings (`hM.sup hM'`), the supremum of two matchings is a matching provided their supports are disjoint. For any matching, the support equals its vertex set (`hM.support_eq_verts`), so the hypothesis `hd` that the vertex sets are disjoint implies their supports are disjoint, closing the first goal.
steps.code:
refine ⟨hM.sup hM' ?_, ?_⟩
  · rwa [hM.support_eq_verts, hM'.support_eq_verts]

steps.claim: To show that the edge count of M ⊔ M' is the sum of their edge counts, it suffices to show that the edge sets of M and M' are disjoint.
steps.explanation: The edge set of M ⊔ M' is the union of their edge sets by `SimpleGraph.Subgraph.edgeSet_sup`. By `Set.encard_union_eq`, the cardinality of the union of two sets is the sum of their cardinalities provided they are disjoint. Rewriting disjointness with `Set.disjoint_left` reduces the goal to showing that no edge belongs to both edge sets.
steps.code:
· rw [SimpleGraph.Subgraph.edgeSet_sup, Set.encard_union_eq]
    rw [Set.disjoint_left]

steps.claim: The edge sets of M and M' are disjoint, completing the proof.
steps.explanation: We assume for contradiction that some edge e belongs to both M.edgeSet and M'.edgeSet. By `Sym2.ind`, the edge e is an unordered pair s(v, w). Since v is an endpoint of e (by `Sym2.mem_mk_left`), v must belong to the vertex set of M, and by the same reasoning v must belong to the vertex set of M'. Applying `Set.disjoint_left.mp` to the disjointness hypothesis `hd` of the vertex sets yields a contradiction.
steps.code:
intro e he he'
    induction e using Sym2.ind with
    | h v w =>
      have hvM : v ∈ M.verts := M.mem_verts_of_mem_edge he (Sym2.mem_mk_left v w)
      have hvM' : v ∈ M'.verts := M'.mem_verts_of_mem_edge he' (Sym2.mem_mk_left v w)
      exact Set.disjoint_left.mp hd hvM hvM'

glossary.SimpleGraph.Subgraph.edgeSet_sup: The edge set of the supremum of two subgraphs is the union of their edge sets.
glossary.Set.encard_union_eq: If two sets are disjoint, the cardinality (encard) of their union is the sum of their cardinalities.
glossary.Set.disjoint_left: Two sets are disjoint if and only if no element in the first set belongs to the second set.
glossary.Sym2.ind: To prove a property for all unordered pairs in a symmetric square, it suffices to prove it for pairs of the form s(x, y).
glossary.Sym2.mem_mk_left: The vertex x is an element of the unordered pair s(x, y).
glossary.Set.disjoint_left.mp: If two sets are disjoint, then an element of the first set cannot be in the second set.

declarations.name: schwartz_zippel_nonzero_count_ge
declarations.informal: Let F be an integral domain, S a nonempty finite subset of F, n a positive integer, and p a nonzero polynomial in n variables over F of total degree d. Then the number of points of S^n at which p does not vanish is at least |S|^n − d·|S|^(n−1); equivalently, at least a fraction 1 − d/|S| of the points of S^n are nonzero for p. This is the guarantee of the random-evaluation identity test: a point where p is nonzero certifies p ≠ 0, so the test has one-sided error and rejects a nonzero p with probability at most d/|S|.
declarations.source:
open scoped Finset in
/-- At least |S|^n − d·|S|^(n−1) points of S^n are nonzero for a nonzero polynomial of total degree d. -/
theorem schwartz_zippel_nonzero_count_ge {F : Type*} [CommRing F] [IsDomain F] [DecidableEq F]
    {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F} (hp : p ≠ 0) {S : Finset F}
    (hS : 0 < S.card) :
    S.card ^ n - p.totalDegree * S.card ^ (n - 1)
      ≤ #{x ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S) | MvPolynomial.eval x p ≠ 0} := by
  have h_le := schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le hn hp hS
  have h_sum := Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not (s := Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S))
    (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x p = 0)
  simp only [Fintype.card_piFinset, Finset.prod_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at h_sum
  simp only [ne_eq]
  omega
declarations.citation: Schwartz 1980; Zippel 1979, in the one-sided-error form used for the randomized identity test (Motwani & Raghavan, Randomized Algorithms, ch. 7); companion of the knowledge-base node `schwartz_zippel_exists_nonzero_eval`.
declarations.reading: The declaration universally quantifies over a type `F` carrying a commutative ring structure, an integral-domain structure, and decidable equality; over a natural number `n` with `0 < n`; over a nonzero multivariate polynomial `p` in `n` variables over `F`; and over a finite subset `S` of `F` with `0 < S.card`. It asserts that the number of `n`-tuples `x : Fin n → F` whose coordinates all lie in `S` and at which `p` evaluates to a nonzero element is at least `S.card ^ n - p.totalDegree * S.card ^ (n - 1)`, where `p.totalDegree` is the total degree of `p` and the subtraction is the truncated subtraction of natural numbers. Equivalently, the count is at least `max(0, |S|^n - deg(p) * |S|^(n-1))`.

explanation.summary: The total number of points in the grid S^n is |S|^n, partitioned into the points where p vanishes and those where p does not vanish. By the Schwartz–Zippel lemma (`schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le`), the zero set contains at most d · |S|^(n−1) points. Subtracting this upper bound from |S|^n yields the required lower bound of |S|^n − d · |S|^(n−1) on the number of nonzeros.

steps.claim: The polynomial p vanishes at at most d · |S|^(n−1) points in S^n, where d is the total degree of p.
steps.explanation: This is the standard Schwartz–Zippel bound (`schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le`), which bounds the number of roots of a nonzero multivariate polynomial over an integral domain in a finite grid S^n.
steps.code: have h_le := schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le hn hp hS

steps.claim: The number of zeros of p in S^n plus the number of nonzeros of p in S^n equals |S|^n.
steps.explanation: Any finite set is partitioned into elements satisfying a predicate and those satisfying its negation (`Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not`). Here the ambient set is the Cartesian product S^n (`Fintype.piFinset`), and simplifying its cardinality via `Fintype.card_piFinset`, `Finset.prod_const`, `Finset.card_univ`, and `Fintype.card_fin` shows that |S^n| = |S|^n.
steps.code:
have h_sum := Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not (s := Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S))
    (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x p = 0)
  simp only [Fintype.card_piFinset, Finset.prod_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at h_sum

steps.claim: The number of points in S^n where p does not vanish is at least |S|^n − d · |S|^(n−1).
steps.explanation: After rewriting p(x) ≠ 0 to ¬(p(x) = 0) via `ne_eq` to match the partition identity, linear integer arithmetic (`omega`) subtracts the upper bound on zeros from the total count |S|^n to obtain the desired lower bound on nonzeros.
steps.code:
simp only [ne_eq]
  omega

glossary.Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not: For any finite set s and predicate p, the number of elements in s satisfying p plus the number of elements satisfying ¬p equals |s|.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal set Finset.univ of a finite type α is the cardinality of α.
glossary.Finset.prod_const: The product of a constant value over a finite set equals the constant raised to the power of the set's size.
glossary.Fintype.card_fin: The finite type Fin n (the integers 0, 1, ..., n − 1) has cardinality n.
glossary.Fintype.card_piFinset: The cardinality of the Cartesian product of a finite family of finite sets is the product of their cardinalities.
glossary.ne_eq: Inequality a ≠ b is equivalent to the negation ¬(a = b).
glossary.schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le: A nonzero polynomial of total degree d in n variables over an integral domain vanishes on at most d · |S|^(n−1) points of S^n.

caveats: Line 12 rewrites `≠` to `¬ ... = ...` using `ne_eq` so that the goal's filtering predicate is syntactically identical to the complement set produced by `Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not`, enabling the linear integer arithmetic tactic `omega` to recognize them as the same quantity.

declarations.name: schwartz_zippel_repeated_trials_zero_count_le
declarations.informal: Let F be an integral domain, S a nonempty finite subset of F, n a positive integer, and p a nonzero polynomial in n variables over F of total degree d. Then for every t the number of t-tuples (x_1, …, x_t) of points of S^n at which p vanishes at every one of the t coordinates is at most (d·|S|^(n−1))^t; equivalently, t independent random trials of the evaluation test all fail with probability at most (d/|S|)^t.
declarations.statement:
open scoped Finset in
theorem schwartz_zippel_repeated_trials_zero_count_le {F : Type*} [CommRing F] [IsDomain F]
    [DecidableEq F] {n t : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F} (hp : p ≠ 0)
    {S : Finset F} (hS : 0 < S.card) :
    #{X ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin t => Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S)) |
        ∀ i, MvPolynomial.eval (X i) p = 0}
      ≤ (p.totalDegree * S.card ^ (n - 1)) ^ t
declarations.source:
open scoped Finset in
/-- Amplification by repetition: the number of t-tuples of points of S^n that are all zeros of a nonzero polynomial of total degree d is at most (d·|S|^(n−1))^t. -/
theorem schwartz_zippel_repeated_trials_zero_count_le {F : Type*} [CommRing F] [IsDomain F]
    [DecidableEq F] {n t : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F} (hp : p ≠ 0)
    {S : Finset F} (hS : 0 < S.card) :
    #{X ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin t => Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S)) |
        ∀ i, MvPolynomial.eval (X i) p = 0}
      ≤ (p.totalDegree * S.card ^ (n - 1)) ^ t := by
  have h_set :
    {X ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin t => Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S)) |
        ∀ i, MvPolynomial.eval (X i) p = 0} =
    Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin t =>
      {x ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S) | MvPolynomial.eval x p = 0}) := by
    ext X
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Fintype.mem_piFinset]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩ i
      exact ⟨h1 i, h2 i⟩
    · intro h
      exact ⟨fun i => (h i).1, fun i => (h i).2⟩
  rw [h_set, Fintype.card_piFinset_const]
  exact Nat.pow_le_pow_left (schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le hn hp hS) t
declarations.citation: Amplification by independent repetition of the random-evaluation identity test of Schwartz 1980 / Zippel 1979 (Motwani & Raghavan, Randomized Algorithms, ch. 7). Concepts anchored by Mathlib `MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_totalDegree`.
declarations.reading:
For every type `F` with a commutative ring structure, an integral domain structure, and decidable equality, for all natural numbers `n` and `t` with `n > 0`, for every nonzero polynomial `p` in `n` variables over `F`, and every finite subset `S` of `F` with positive cardinality, the number of `t`-tuples of points of `S^n` at which `p` vanishes is at most `(p.totalDegree * |S|^(n-1))^t`.

More explicitly, the tuples are functions `X : Fin t → (Fin n → F)` such that every coordinate `X j i` lies in `S`, and the vanishing condition is that for every `j : Fin t`, the evaluation of `p` at the assignment `X j : Fin n → F` is zero. The bound parses as `(p.totalDegree * (S.card ^ (n - 1))) ^ t`, because `^` binds more tightly than `*`; the outer exponent `t` applies to the whole product.

explanation.summary: The argument identifies the set of joint zeros in (S^n)^t with the t-fold Cartesian product of the single-trial zero set Z = {x ∈ S^n | p(x) = 0}, since a polynomial vanishes at every coordinate of a t-tuple if and only if each coordinate independently belongs to Z. The cardinality of this product is therefore |Z|^t. Bounding |Z| by d · |S|^(n - 1) via the single-trial Schwartz-Zippel lemma and raising both sides to the power t establishes the inequality.

steps.claim: The set of t-tuples in (S^n)^t on which p vanishes at every coordinate equals the t-fold Cartesian product of the zero set {x ∈ S^n | p(x) = 0}.
steps.explanation: By set extensionality (`ext`), a t-tuple X belongs to the set on the left if and only if every coordinate X(i) lies in S^n and satisfies p(X(i)) = 0 (using `Finset.mem_filter` and `Fintype.mem_piFinset`). Distributing the universal quantifier over the conjunction shows this is equivalent to requiring X(i) ∈ {x ∈ S^n | p(x) = 0} for every coordinate i, which is the definition of membership in the product set.
steps.code:
have h_set :
    {X ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin t => Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S)) |
        ∀ i, MvPolynomial.eval (X i) p = 0} =
    Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin t =>
      {x ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S) | MvPolynomial.eval x p = 0}) := by
    ext X
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Fintype.mem_piFinset]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩ i
      exact ⟨h1 i, h2 i⟩
    · intro h
      exact ⟨fun i => (h i).1, fun i => (h i).2⟩

steps.claim: The number of such t-tuples is |Z|^t, where Z = {x ∈ S^n | p(x) = 0}.
steps.explanation: Rewriting the set of t-tuples as the Cartesian product Z^t using the set equality `h_set`, its cardinality becomes |Z|^t by `Fintype.card_piFinset_const`.
steps.code: rw [h_set, Fintype.card_piFinset_const]

steps.claim: The t-th power of the number of zeros |Z|^t is bounded by (d · |S|^(n - 1))^t.
steps.explanation: By the Schwartz-Zippel lemma for a single trial (`schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le`), the polynomial p has at most d · |S|^(n - 1) zeros in S^n. Raising both sides of this inequality to the power t via monotonicity of powers (`Nat.pow_le_pow_left`) yields the required bound.
steps.code: exact Nat.pow_le_pow_left (schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le hn hp hS) t

glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element x belongs to the filtered set {y ∈ s | p y} if and only if x ∈ s and p x holds.
glossary.Fintype.mem_piFinset: A function f belongs to the Cartesian product ∏ a, t a if and only if f a ∈ t a for every a.
glossary.Fintype.card_piFinset_const: The cardinality of the Cartesian product of n copies of a finite set s is |s|^n.
glossary.Nat.pow_le_pow_left: If n ≤ m for natural numbers, then n^i ≤ m^i for any exponent i.
glossary.schwartz_zippel_zero_count_le: For a nonzero polynomial p of degree d in n variables over an integral domain and a finite nonempty subset S, the number of zeros of p in S^n is at most d · |S|^(n - 1).

Because all derivatives of the constant zero function vanish, both the second time derivative and the second spatial derivative are identically zero, reducing the equation to $0 = c^2 \cdot 0 = 0$.

declarations.name: quantum_commutator_jacobi_identity
declarations.informal: For any three continuous linear operators A, B, C on a complex inner product space E, their commutators satisfy the Jacobi identity: ⁅A, ⁅B, C⁆⁆ + ⁅B, ⁅C, A⁆⁆ + ⁅C, ⁅A, B⁆⁆ = 0.
declarations.statement:
theorem quantum_commutator_jacobi_identity {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E]
    (A B C : E →L[ℂ] E) :
    ⁅A, ⁅B, C⁆⁆ + ⁅B, ⁅C, A⁆⁆ + ⁅C, ⁅A, B⁆⁆ = 0
declarations.source:
/-- The commutator bracket on continuous linear operators satisfies the Jacobi identity. -/
theorem quantum_commutator_jacobi_identity {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E]
    (A B C : E →L[ℂ] E) :
    ⁅A, ⁅B, C⁆⁆ + ⁅B, ⁅C, A⁆⁆ + ⁅C, ⁅A, B⁆⁆ = 0 := by
  simp only [Ring.lie_def]
  noncomm_ring
declarations.citation: Hall, Quantum Theory for Mathematicians, Chapter 3; Reed & Simon, Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics I, ch. VIII
declarations.reading: For any type $E$ equipped with the structure of a normed additive commutative group and a complex inner product space, and for any three continuous (bounded) $\mathbb{C}$-linear maps $A, B, C : E \toL[ℂ] E$, the Jacobi identity holds for their Lie bracket (commutator): ⁅A, ⁅B, C⁆⁆ + ⁅B, ⁅C, A⁆⁆ + ⁅C, ⁅A, B⁆⁆ = 0, where 0 is the zero continuous linear map on $E$.

explanation.summary: The Jacobi identity for continuous linear operators follows by expanding the Lie bracket into operator multiplication. Rewriting each commutator bracket ⁅X, Y⁆ as X * Y - Y * X yields twelve triple products that cancel in pairs under the axioms of an associative ring.

steps.claim: The Jacobi identity reduces to an algebraic identity in terms of operator multiplication: A * (B * C - C * B) - (B * C - C * B) * A + B * (C * A - A * C) - (C * A - A * C) * B + C * (A * B - B * A) - (A * B - B * A) * C = 0.
steps.explanation: Rewriting with Ring.lie_def replaces each commutator bracket ⁅X, Y⁆ with the difference of products X * Y - Y * X, translating the operator Lie algebra identity into an identity in the underlying associative ring of continuous linear operators.
steps.code: simp only [Ring.lie_def]

steps.claim: The algebraic sum of operator products evaluates to 0.
steps.explanation: The noncomm_ring tactic expands the expressions using the distributive and associative laws of ring multiplication. Each of the six triple products (ABC, ACB, BAC, BCA, CAB, CBA) appears exactly once with a positive sign and once with a negative sign, so all twelve terms cancel in pairs.
steps.code: noncomm_ring

glossary.Ring.lie_def: In any ring, the Lie bracket ⁅x, y⁆ is defined as the commutator x * y - y * x.

declarations.name: regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching
declarations.informal: Every d-regular bipartite simple graph on a finite vertex set, with degree d > 0, has a perfect matching.
declarations.statement:
theorem regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) (hbip : G.IsBipartite) :
    ∃ M : SimpleGraph.Subgraph G, M.IsPerfectMatching
declarations.source:
open scoped Classical
open SimpleGraph Finset Set

lemma regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching_card_le_card_biUnion {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) (S : Finset V) :
    #S ≤ #(S.biUnion (fun x => G.neighborFinset x)) := by
  let T := S.biUnion (fun x => G.neighborFinset x)
  have h_deg (v : V) : #(G.neighborFinset v) = d := by
    rw [card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
    exact hreg v
  have h_above (u : V) (hu : u ∈ S) : #(bipartiteAbove G.Adj T u) = d := by
    have : bipartiteAbove G.Adj T u = G.neighborFinset u := by
      ext v
      simp only [bipartiteAbove, mem_filter, mem_neighborFinset]
      constructor
      · intro ⟨_, hadj⟩
        exact hadj
      · intro hadj
        refine ⟨?_, hadj⟩
        rw [Finset.mem_biUnion]
        exact ⟨u, hu, G.mem_neighborFinset u v |>.mpr hadj⟩
    rw [this, h_deg]
  have h_below (v : V) : #(bipartiteBelow G.Adj S v) ≤ d := by
    have : bipartiteBelow G.Adj S v ⊆ G.neighborFinset v := by
      intro u hu
      simp only [bipartiteBelow, mem_filter] at hu
      simp only [mem_neighborFinset]
      exact hu.2.symm
    exact (Finset.card_le_card this).trans (h_deg v).le
  have h_sum_above : ∑ u ∈ S, #(bipartiteAbove G.Adj T u) = #S * d := by
    rw [sum_congr rfl h_above]
    simp
  have h_sum_below : ∑ v ∈ T, #(bipartiteBelow G.Adj S v) ≤ #T * d := by
    calc ∑ v ∈ T, #(bipartiteBelow G.Adj S v)
      _ ≤ ∑ v ∈ T, d := sum_le_sum fun v _ => h_below v
      _ = #T * d := by simp
  have h_eq := sum_card_bipartiteAbove_eq_sum_card_bipartiteBelow G.Adj (s := S) (t := T)
  have h_mul_le : #S * d ≤ #T * d := by
    rw [← h_sum_above, h_eq]
    exact h_sum_below
  exact Nat.le_of_mul_le_mul_right h_mul_le hd

lemma regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching_ncard_le_ncard_biUnion {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) (s : Set V) :
    s.ncard ≤ (⋃ x ∈ s, G.neighborSet x).ncard := by
  have h_eq : (⋃ x ∈ s, G.neighborSet x).toFinset = s.toFinset.biUnion (fun x => G.neighborFinset x) := by
    ext v
    simp
  rw [Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card' s, Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card' _, h_eq]
  exact regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching_card_le_card_biUnion G hd hreg s.toFinset

/-- Every d-regular bipartite graph with d > 0 has a perfect matching. -/
theorem regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) (hbip : G.IsBipartite) :
    ∃ M : SimpleGraph.Subgraph G, M.IsPerfectMatching := by
  obtain ⟨p₁, p₂, hbipW⟩ := hbip.exists_isBipartiteWith
  exact exists_isPerfectMatching_of_forall_ncard_le hbipW
    (fun s => regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching_ncard_le_ncard_biUnion G hd hreg s)
declarations.reading: For any finite type `V`, any simple graph `G` on `V`, and any natural number `d` such that `0 < d`, if `G` is regular of degree `d` (every vertex in `V` has degree `d`) and `G` is bipartite (2-colorable), then there exists a subgraph `M` of `G` that is a perfect matching of `G` (that is, `M` spans all vertices of `V` and every vertex has degree 1 in `M`).

explanation.summary: To show that every d-regular bipartite graph with d > 0 has a perfect matching, we verify Hall's marriage condition: every vertex subset S satisfies |S| ≤ |N(S)|. Double counting the edges between S and its neighborhood T = N(S) shows that |S| * d = ∑_{u ∈ S} deg_T(u) = ∑_{v ∈ T} deg_S(v) ≤ |T| * d. Since d > 0, dividing by d yields |S| ≤ |T|. Hall's marriage theorem for bipartite graphs then guarantees the existence of a perfect matching.

steps.claim: Define the neighborhood T of S and note that every vertex has degree d.
steps.explanation: Let T = ⋃ u ∈ S, N(u) be the union of the neighborhoods of all vertices in S. By the regularity of G, every vertex v has degree d, so each neighbor finset N(v) has cardinality d.
steps.code:
let T := S.biUnion (fun x => G.neighborFinset x)
  have h_deg (v : V) : #(G.neighborFinset v) = d := by
    rw [card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
    exact hreg v

steps.claim: For every vertex u ∈ S, the number of its neighbors in T is exactly d.
steps.explanation: By definition, `bipartiteAbove G.Adj T u` is the set of neighbors of u that lie in T. Since u ∈ S, every neighbor of u is in T by definition of T as the union of neighborhoods of vertices in S. Hence this set is the entire neighborhood N(u), which has cardinality d.
steps.code:
have h_above (u : V) (hu : u ∈ S) : #(bipartiteAbove G.Adj T u) = d := by
    have : bipartiteAbove G.Adj T u = G.neighborFinset u := by
      ext v
      simp only [bipartiteAbove, mem_filter, mem_neighborFinset]
      constructor
      · intro ⟨_, hadj⟩
        exact hadj
      · intro hadj
        refine ⟨?_, hadj⟩
        rw [Finset.mem_biUnion]
        exact ⟨u, hu, G.mem_neighborFinset u v |>.mpr hadj⟩
    rw [this, h_deg]

steps.claim: For every vertex v ∈ V, the number of its neighbors in S is at most d.
steps.explanation: The set `bipartiteBelow G.Adj S v` consists of the neighbors of v that lie in S. This is a subset of the full neighborhood N(v). Because |N(v)| = d, the cardinality of this subset is at most d.
steps.code:
have h_below (v : V) : #(bipartiteBelow G.Adj S v) ≤ d := by
    have : bipartiteBelow G.Adj S v ⊆ G.neighborFinset v := by
      intro u hu
      simp only [bipartiteBelow, mem_filter] at hu
      simp only [mem_neighborFinset]
      exact hu.2.symm
    exact (Finset.card_le_card this).trans (h_deg v).le

steps.claim: The sum over u ∈ S of the number of its neighbors in T equals |S| * d.
steps.explanation: Since each vertex u ∈ S has exactly d neighbors in T, summing this constant value d over all |S| vertices in S gives |S| * d.
steps.code:
have h_sum_above : ∑ u ∈ S, #(bipartiteAbove G.Adj T u) = #S * d := by
    rw [sum_congr rfl h_above]
    simp

steps.claim: The sum over v ∈ T of the number of its neighbors in S is at most |T| * d.
steps.explanation: Each vertex v ∈ T has at most d neighbors in S. Summing these upper bounds over all vertices in T gives at most ∑ v ∈ T, d = |T| * d.
steps.code:
have h_sum_below : ∑ v ∈ T, #(bipartiteBelow G.Adj S v) ≤ #T * d := by
    calc ∑ v ∈ T, #(bipartiteBelow G.Adj S v)
      _ ≤ ∑ v ∈ T, d := sum_le_sum fun v _ => h_below v
      _ = #T * d := by simp

steps.claim: The cardinality of S is at most the cardinality of its neighborhood T.
steps.explanation: By double counting edges between S and T (`sum_card_bipartiteAbove_eq_sum_card_bipartiteBelow`), the sum of degrees from S into T equals the sum of degrees from T into S. Therefore |S| * d ≤ |T| * d. Because d > 0, dividing by d yields |S| ≤ |T|.
steps.code:
have h_eq := sum_card_bipartiteAbove_eq_sum_card_bipartiteBelow G.Adj (s := S) (t := T)
  have h_mul_le : #S * d ≤ #T * d := by
    rw [← h_sum_above, h_eq]
    exact h_sum_below
  exact Nat.le_of_mul_le_mul_right h_mul_le hd

steps.claim: For any subset s of vertices, |s| ≤ |N(s)|.
steps.explanation: First, the finset corresponding to the set union ⋃ x ∈ s, N(x) is identified with the finset bi-union over the finset coercion of s. Rewriting the set cardinalities (`ncard`) to finset cardinalities via `Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card'`, the inequality follows from the finset version `regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching_card_le_card_biUnion`.
steps.code:
have h_eq : (⋃ x ∈ s, G.neighborSet x).toFinset = s.toFinset.biUnion (fun x => G.neighborFinset x) := by
    ext v
    simp
  rw [Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card' s, Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card' _, h_eq]
  exact regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching_card_le_card_biUnion G hd hreg s.toFinset

steps.claim: The graph G has a perfect matching.
steps.explanation: The assumption that G is bipartite yields a 2-partition of the vertices into independent sets. By Hall's marriage theorem for bipartite graphs (`exists_isPerfectMatching_of_forall_ncard_le`), G has a perfect matching because Hall's condition |s| ≤ |N(s)| holds for every vertex subset s by `regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching_ncard_le_ncard_biUnion`.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨p₁, p₂, hbipW⟩ := hbip.exists_isBipartiteWith
  exact exists_isPerfectMatching_of_forall_ncard_le hbipW
    (fun s => regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching_ncard_le_ncard_biUnion G hd hreg s)

glossary.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree: The cardinality of the neighbor finset of a vertex equals its degree.
glossary.Finset.mem_biUnion: An element belongs to a finset union ⋃ a ∈ s, t a if and only if it belongs to t a for some a ∈ s.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card: If s ⊆ t for finite sets s and t, then |s| ≤ |t|.
glossary.sum_congr: Two sums over finite sets are equal if their index sets are equal and their terms are equal at every element.
glossary.sum_le_sum: A sum of terms is bounded by the sum of term-by-term upper bounds.
glossary.sum_card_bipartiteAbove_eq_sum_card_bipa: For any binary relation between finite sets s and t, the sum over a ∈ s of the number of related elements in t equals the sum over b ∈ t of the number of related elements in s.
glossary.Nat.le_of_mul_le_mul_right: If a * c ≤ b * c and 0 < c, then a ≤ b for natural numbers.
glossary.Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card': The set cardinality (`ncard`) of a finite set equals the cardinality of its coercion to a `Finset`.
glossary.regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching_c: In a d-regular graph on a finite vertex set with d > 0, any finset S satisfies |S| ≤ |N(S)|.
glossary.exists_isPerfectMatching_of_forall_ncard: A locally finite bipartite graph has a perfect matching if Hall's condition |s| ≤ |N(s)| holds for every subset of vertices s.
glossary.regular_bipartite_has_perfect_matching_n: In a d-regular graph on a finite vertex set with d > 0, every subset s of vertices satisfies |s| ≤ |N(s)|.
