declarations.name: list_colorable_two_of_two_involutions
declarations.informal: Let E be a finite set and p, q two involutions; they define two unit-capacity partition matroids on E with classes {e, p e} and {e, q e} of size at most two, whose common independent sets are the matchings of a bipartite multigraph of maximum degree at most two. From any lists of at least two colors per element one can choose colors so that partners under p, and partners under q, always get different colors.
declarations.statement:
theorem list_colorable_two_of_two_involutions {α : Type*} (E : Set α) (hE : E.Finite)
    (p q : α → α) (hp : Function.Involutive p) (hq : Function.Involutive q)
    (L : α → Finset ℕ) (hL : ∀ e ∈ E, 2 ≤ (L e).card) :
    ∃ c : α → ℕ, (∀ e ∈ E, c e ∈ L e) ∧
      ∀ e ∈ E, (p e ∈ E → p e ≠ e → c (p e) ≠ c e) ∧ (q e ∈ E → q e ≠ e → c (q e) ≠ c e)
declarations.source:
/-- Recolouring one vertex `v` of a colouring that is proper on `E \ {v}` for the pairing `r`:
it stays proper on `E` when the new colour differs from that of `v`'s partner. -/
theorem involution_coloring_update {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (E : Finset α) (v : α)
    (c' : α → ℕ) (t : ℕ) (r : α → α) (hr : Function.Involutive r)
    (hc' : ∀ e ∈ E.erase v, r e ∈ E.erase v → r e ≠ e → c' (r e) ≠ c' e)
    (hv : r v ≠ v → r v ∈ E → c' (r v) ≠ t) :
    ∀ e ∈ E, r e ∈ E → r e ≠ e →
      Function.update c' v t (r e) ≠ Function.update c' v t e := by
  intro e he hre hne
  by_cases hev : e = v
  · subst hev
    rw [Function.update_of_ne hne, Function.update_self]
    exact hv hne hre
  · by_cases hrev : r e = v
    · have : e = r v := by rw [← hrev, hr e]
      subst this
      rw [hrev, Function.update_self, Function.update_of_ne hev]
      exact (hv hev he).symm
    · rw [Function.update_of_ne hrev, Function.update_of_ne hev]
      exact hc' e (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hev, he⟩) (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hrev, hre⟩) hne

theorem two_involutions_list_aux {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ (E : Finset α), E.card ≤ n → ∀ (p q : α → α), Function.Involutive p →
    Function.Involutive q → ∀ (L : α → Finset ℕ) (zo : Option α),
      (∀ e ∈ E, zo ≠ some e → 2 ≤ (L e).card) →
      (∀ z, zo = some z → z ∈ E → 1 ≤ (L z).card ∧
          ¬ (p z ∈ E ∧ q z ∈ E ∧ p z ≠ z ∧ q z ≠ z ∧ p z ≠ q z)) →
      ∃ c : α → ℕ, (∀ e ∈ E, c e ∈ L e) ∧
        ∀ e ∈ E, (p e ∈ E → p e ≠ e → c (p e) ≠ c e) ∧
          (q e ∈ E → q e ≠ e → c (q e) ≠ c e) := by
  induction n with
  | zero =>
    intro E hE p q hp hq L zo _ _
    have : E = ∅ := Finset.card_eq_zero.1 (Nat.le_zero.1 hE)
    subst this
    exact ⟨fun _ => 0, by simp, by simp⟩
  | succ n ih =>
    intro E hE p q hp hq L zo hL hz
    by_cases hA : ∃ z, zo = some z ∧ z ∈ E
    · -- a vertex with a short list: it has at most one neighbour, colour it first
      obtain ⟨z, rfl, hzE⟩ := hA
      obtain ⟨h1, hfree⟩ := hz z rfl hzE
      obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := Finset.card_pos.1 h1
      set E' := E.erase z with hE'
      set L' : α → Finset ℕ := fun e =>
        if e ≠ z ∧ (e = p z ∨ e = q z) then (L e).erase t else L e with hL'
      set zo' : Option α :=
        if p z ∈ E' then some (p z) else if q z ∈ E' then some (q z) else none with hzo'
      have hcard : E'.card ≤ n := by rw [hE', Finset.card_erase_of_mem hzE]; omega
      refine (fun H => ?_) (ih E' hcard p q hp hq L' zo' ?_ ?_)
      · obtain ⟨c', hc'L, hc'⟩ := H
        have hpz : p z ≠ z → p z ∈ E → c' (p z) ≠ t := by
          intro h1 h2 h3
          have := hc'L (p z) (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨h1, h2⟩)
          rw [hL'] at this
          simp only [ne_eq, h1, not_false_eq_true, true_or, and_self, if_true] at this
          exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 this).1 h3
        have hqz : q z ≠ z → q z ∈ E → c' (q z) ≠ t := by
          intro h1 h2 h3
          have := hc'L (q z) (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨h1, h2⟩)
          rw [hL'] at this
          simp only [ne_eq, h1, not_false_eq_true, or_true, and_self, if_true] at this
          exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 this).1 h3
        refine ⟨Function.update c' z t, ?_, ?_⟩
        · intro e he
          by_cases hez : e = z
          · subst hez; simpa using ht
          · rw [Function.update_of_ne hez]
            have := hc'L e (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hez, he⟩)
            rw [hL'] at this
            dsimp only at this
            split_ifs at this with h
            all_goals first | exact Finset.mem_of_mem_erase this | exact this
        · intro e he
          exact ⟨involution_coloring_update E z c' t p hp (fun e he => (hc' e he).1) hpz e he,
            involution_coloring_update E z c' t q hq (fun e he => (hc' e he).2) hqz e he⟩
      · intro e he hne
        have hez : e ≠ z := (Finset.mem_erase.1 he).1
        have heE : e ∈ E := (Finset.mem_erase.1 he).2
        by_cases hm : e = p z ∨ e = q z
        · exfalso
          apply hne
          rcases hm with h | h
          · rw [hzo', if_pos (h ▸ he), h]
          · by_cases hp' : p z ∈ E'
            · rw [hzo', if_pos hp']
              have hpz : p z ≠ z := (Finset.mem_erase.1 hp').1
              by_contra hc
              have hpe : p z ≠ e := fun h' => hc (by rw [h'])
              exact hfree ⟨(Finset.mem_erase.1 hp').2, h ▸ heE, hpz, h ▸ hez,
                fun h'' => hpe (h'' ▸ h.symm)⟩
            · rw [hzo', if_neg hp', if_pos (h ▸ he), h]
        · have : L' e = L e := by
            rw [hL']; dsimp only; rw [if_neg (fun h => hm h.2)]
          rw [this]
          exact hL e heE (by simp only [ne_eq, Option.some.injEq]; exact fun h => hez h.symm)
      · intro y hy hyE
        have hyz : y ≠ z := (Finset.mem_erase.1 hyE).1
        have hyE' : y ∈ E := (Finset.mem_erase.1 hyE).2
        have hym : y = p z ∨ y = q z := by
          rw [hzo'] at hy
          split_ifs at hy <;> simp_all
        have hLy : L' y = (L y).erase t := by
          rw [hL']; dsimp only; rw [if_pos ⟨hyz, hym⟩]
        refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
        · rw [hLy]
          have := hL y hyE' (by simp only [ne_eq, Option.some.injEq]; exact fun h => hyz h.symm)
          have := Finset.pred_card_le_card_erase (s := L y) (a := t)
          omega
        · rintro ⟨h1, h2, -, -, -⟩
          rcases hym with h | h
          · have : p y = z := by rw [h, hp z]
            exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 h1).1 this
          · have : q y = z := by rw [h, hq z]
            exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 h2).1 this
    · have hL2 : ∀ e ∈ E, 2 ≤ (L e).card := by
        intro e he
        apply hL e he
        intro h
        exact hA ⟨e, h, he⟩
      by_cases hB1 : ∃ v ∈ E, ¬ (p v ∈ E ∧ q v ∈ E ∧ p v ≠ v ∧ q v ≠ v ∧ p v ≠ q v)
      · -- a vertex with at most one neighbour: colour the rest, then it
        obtain ⟨v, hvE, hfree⟩ := hB1
        have hcard : (E.erase v).card ≤ n := by rw [Finset.card_erase_of_mem hvE]; omega
        obtain ⟨c', hc'L, hc'⟩ := ih (E.erase v) hcard p q hp hq L none
          (fun e he _ => hL2 e (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase he)) (by simp)
        set F : Finset ℕ := (({p v, q v} : Finset α).filter (· ∈ E.erase v)).image c' with hF
        have hFc : F.card ≤ 1 := by
          refine (Finset.card_image_le).trans ?_
          rw [Finset.card_le_one]
          intro a ha b hb
          simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at ha hb
          by_contra hab
          apply hfree
          rcases ha with ⟨rfl | rfl, ha⟩ <;> rcases hb with ⟨rfl | rfl, hb⟩
          · exact absurd rfl hab
          · exact ⟨(Finset.mem_erase.1 ha).2, (Finset.mem_erase.1 hb).2,
              (Finset.mem_erase.1 ha).1, (Finset.mem_erase.1 hb).1, hab⟩
          · exact ⟨(Finset.mem_erase.1 hb).2, (Finset.mem_erase.1 ha).2,
              (Finset.mem_erase.1 hb).1, (Finset.mem_erase.1 ha).1, fun h => hab h.symm⟩
          · exact absurd rfl hab
        obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ : (L v \ F).Nonempty := by
          rw [← Finset.card_pos]
          have := Finset.le_card_sdiff F (L v)
          have := hL2 v hvE
          omega
        have hmem : ∀ y, y = p v ∨ y = q v → y ≠ v → y ∈ E → c' y ≠ t := by
          intro y hy hyv hyE h
          apply (Finset.mem_sdiff.1 ht).2
          rw [hF, Finset.mem_image]
          refine ⟨y, Finset.mem_filter.2 ⟨?_, Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hyv, hyE⟩⟩, h⟩
          rcases hy with rfl | rfl <;> simp
        refine ⟨Function.update c' v t, ?_, ?_⟩
        · intro e he
          by_cases hev : e = v
          · subst hev; simpa using (Finset.mem_sdiff.1 ht).1
          · rw [Function.update_of_ne hev]; exact hc'L e (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hev, he⟩)
        · intro e he
          exact ⟨involution_coloring_update E v c' t p hp (fun e he => (hc' e he).1)
              (fun h1 h2 => hmem _ (Or.inl rfl) h1 h2) e he,
            involution_coloring_update E v c' t q hq (fun e he => (hc' e he).2)
              (fun h1 h2 => hmem _ (Or.inr rfl) h1 h2) e he⟩
      · have hnf : ∀ v ∈ E, p v ∈ E ∧ q v ∈ E ∧ p v ≠ v ∧ q v ≠ v ∧ p v ≠ q v := by
          intro v hv
          by_contra h
          exact hB1 ⟨v, hv, h⟩
        -- an edge whose ends have different lists
        have key : ∀ (r s : α → α), Function.Involutive r → Function.Involutive s →
            (∀ v ∈ E, r v ∈ E ∧ s v ∈ E ∧ r v ≠ v ∧ s v ≠ v ∧ r v ≠ s v) →
            (∃ v ∈ E, ∃ a ∈ L v, a ∉ L (r v)) →
            ∃ c : α → ℕ, (∀ e ∈ E, c e ∈ L e) ∧
              ∀ e ∈ E, (r e ∈ E → r e ≠ e → c (r e) ≠ c e) ∧
                (s e ∈ E → s e ≠ e → c (s e) ≠ c e) := by
          intro r s hr hs hrs ⟨v, hvE, a, haL, har⟩
          obtain ⟨hrv, hsv, hrvv, hsvv, hrsv⟩ := hrs v hvE
          have hcard : (E.erase v).card ≤ n := by rw [Finset.card_erase_of_mem hvE]; omega
          set L' := Function.update L (s v) ((L (s v)).erase a) with hL'
          refine (fun H => ?_) (ih (E.erase v) hcard r s hr hs L' (some (s v)) ?_ ?_)
          · obtain ⟨c', hc'L, hc'⟩ := H
            have hrv' : c' (r v) ∉ ({a} : Finset ℕ) := by
              have := hc'L (r v) (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hrvv, hrv⟩)
              rw [hL', Function.update_of_ne hrsv] at this
              simp only [Finset.mem_singleton]
              exact fun h => har (h ▸ this)
            have hsv' : c' (s v) ≠ a := by
              have := hc'L (s v) (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hsvv, hsv⟩)
              rw [hL', Function.update_self] at this
              exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 this).1
            refine ⟨Function.update c' v a, ?_, ?_⟩
            · intro e he
              by_cases hev : e = v
              · subst hev; simpa using haL
              · rw [Function.update_of_ne hev]
                have := hc'L e (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hev, he⟩)
                by_cases hes : e = s v
                · rw [hes, hL', Function.update_self] at this
                  rw [hes]; exact Finset.mem_of_mem_erase this
                · rwa [hL', Function.update_of_ne hes] at this
            · intro e he
              exact ⟨involution_coloring_update E v c' a r hr (fun e he => (hc' e he).1)
                  (fun _ _ h => hrv' (Finset.mem_singleton.2 h)) e he,
                involution_coloring_update E v c' a s hs (fun e he => (hc' e he).2)
                  (fun _ _ => hsv') e he⟩
          · intro e he hne
            have hes : e ≠ s v := fun h => hne (by rw [h])
            rw [hL', Function.update_of_ne hes]
            exact hL2 e (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase he)
          · intro y hy hyE
            simp only [Option.some.injEq] at hy
            subst hy
            refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
            · rw [hL', Function.update_self]
              have := Finset.pred_card_le_card_erase (s := L (s v)) (a := a)
              have := hL2 (s v) hsv
              omega
            · rintro ⟨-, h2, -⟩
              rw [hs v] at h2
              exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 h2).1 rfl
        by_cases hpa : ∃ v ∈ E, ∃ a ∈ L v, a ∉ L (p v)
        · exact key p q hp hq hnf hpa
        by_cases hqa : ∃ v ∈ E, ∃ a ∈ L v, a ∉ L (q v)
        · obtain ⟨c, hcL, hc⟩ := key q p hq hp (fun v hv => by
            obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4, h5⟩ := hnf v hv
            exact ⟨h2, h1, h4, h3, fun h => h5 h.symm⟩) hqa
          exact ⟨c, hcL, fun e he => ⟨(hc e he).2, (hc e he).1⟩⟩
        -- all lists agree along edges: contract one `p`-pair into a `q`-edge
        have hsub : ∀ v ∈ E, L v ⊆ L (p v) ∧ L v ⊆ L (q v) := by
          intro v hv
          refine ⟨fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
          · by_contra h; exact hpa ⟨v, hv, a, ha, h⟩
          · by_contra h; exact hqa ⟨v, hv, a, ha, h⟩
        rcases E.eq_empty_or_nonempty with hE0 | ⟨v, hvE⟩
        · subst hE0; exact ⟨fun _ => 0, by simp, by simp⟩
        obtain ⟨hwE, huE, hwv, huv, hwu⟩ := hnf v hvE
        set w := p v with hw
        set u := q v with hu
        obtain ⟨-, hxE, -, hxw, -⟩ := hnf w hwE
        set x := q w with hx
        have hxu : x ≠ u := fun h => hwv (hq.injective h)
        have hxv : x ≠ v := fun h => hwu (by rw [← hq w, ← hx, h])
        have hqu : q u = v := hq v
        have hqx : q x = w := hq w
        have hpw : p w = v := hp v
        set q' : α → α := fun y =>
          if y = u then x else if y = x then u else if y = v then v else if y = w then w
          else q y with hq'
        have hq'inv : Function.Involutive q' := by
          intro y
          by_cases h1 : y = u
          · subst h1; simp [hq', hxu]
          by_cases h2 : y = x
          · subst h2; simp [hq', hxu]
          by_cases h3 : y = v
          · subst h3; simp [hq', h1, h2]
          by_cases h4 : y = w
          · subst h4; simp [hq', h1, h2, h3]
          have k1 : q y ≠ u := fun h => h3 (by rw [← hq y, h, hqu])
          have k2 : q y ≠ x := fun h => h4 (by rw [← hq y, h, hqx])
          have k3 : q y ≠ v := fun h => h1 (by rw [← hq y, h])
          have k4 : q y ≠ w := fun h => h2 (by rw [← hq y, h])
          simp [hq', h1, h2, h3, h4, k1, k2, k3, k4, hq y]
        set E'' := (E.erase v).erase w with hE''
        have hcard : E''.card ≤ n := by
          rw [hE'', Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hwv, hwE⟩),
            Finset.card_erase_of_mem hvE]
          omega
        have huE'' : u ∈ E'' := Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨fun h => hwu h.symm,
          Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨huv, huE⟩⟩
        have hxE'' : x ∈ E'' := Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hxw, Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hxv, hxE⟩⟩
        obtain ⟨c', hc'L, hc'⟩ := ih E'' hcard p q' hp hq'inv L none
          (fun e he _ => hL2 e (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase he)))
          (by simp)
        have hux : c' x ≠ c' u := by
          have := (hc' u huE'').2
          simp only [hq', if_true] at this
          exact this hxE'' hxu
        -- `c'` is proper for `q` on `E''`: the edges of `q` inside `E''` are edges of `q'`
        have hc'q : ∀ e ∈ E'', q e ∈ E'' → q e ≠ e → c' (q e) ≠ c' e := by
          intro e he hqe hne
          have hev : e ≠ v := (Finset.mem_erase.1 (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase he)).1
          have hew : e ≠ w := (Finset.mem_erase.1 he).1
          have heu : e ≠ u := fun h => by
            rw [h, hqu] at hqe
            exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hqe)).1 rfl
          have hex : e ≠ x := fun h => by
            rw [h, hqx] at hqe
            exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 hqe).1 rfl
          have : q' e = q e := by simp [hq', heu, hex, hev, hew]
          have := (hc' e he).2
          rw [‹q' e = q e›] at this
          exact this hqe hne
        set c1 := Function.update c' v (c' x) with hc1
        have hE1 : (E.erase w).erase v = E'' := by rw [hE'', Finset.erase_right_comm]
        have hc1p : ∀ e ∈ E.erase w, p e ∈ E.erase w → p e ≠ e → c1 (p e) ≠ c1 e :=
          involution_coloring_update (E.erase w) v c' (c' x) p hp
            (by rw [hE1]; exact fun e he => (hc' e he).1)
            (fun _ h => absurd (Finset.mem_erase.1 h).1 (by simp [hw]))
        have hc1q : ∀ e ∈ E.erase w, q e ∈ E.erase w → q e ≠ e → c1 (q e) ≠ c1 e :=
          involution_coloring_update (E.erase w) v c' (c' x) q hq
            (by rw [hE1]; exact hc'q) (fun _ _ => hux.symm)
        refine ⟨Function.update c1 w (c' u), ?_, ?_⟩
        · intro e he
          by_cases hew : e = w
          · rw [hew, Function.update_self]
            have h1 := hc'L u huE''
            have h2 := (hsub u huE).2 h1
            rw [hqu] at h2
            exact (hsub v hvE).1 h2
          · rw [Function.update_of_ne hew]
            by_cases hev : e = v
            · rw [hev, hc1, Function.update_self]
              have h1 := hc'L x hxE''
              have h2 := (hsub x hxE).2 h1
              rw [hqx] at h2
              have h3 := (hsub w hwE).1 h2
              rwa [hpw] at h3
            · rw [hc1, Function.update_of_ne hev]
              exact hc'L e (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hew, Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hev, he⟩⟩)
        · intro e he
          refine ⟨involution_coloring_update E w c1 (c' u) p hp hc1p ?_ e he,
            involution_coloring_update E w c1 (c' u) q hq hc1q ?_ e he⟩
          · intro _ _
            rw [hpw, hc1, Function.update_self]
            exact hux
          · intro _ _
            rw [hc1, Function.update_of_ne hxv]
            exact hux

theorem list_colorable_two_of_two_involutions {α : Type*} (E : Set α) (hE : E.Finite)
    (p q : α → α) (hp : Function.Involutive p) (hq : Function.Involutive q)
    (L : α → Finset ℕ) (hL : ∀ e ∈ E, 2 ≤ (L e).card) :
    ∃ c : α → ℕ, (∀ e ∈ E, c e ∈ L e) ∧
      ∀ e ∈ E, (p e ∈ E → p e ≠ e → c (p e) ≠ c e) ∧ (q e ∈ E → q e ≠ e → c (q e) ≠ c e) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨c, hcL, hc⟩ := two_involutions_list_aux hE.toFinset.card hE.toFinset le_rfl p q hp hq
    L none (fun e he _ => hL e (hE.mem_toFinset.1 he)) (by simp)
  refine ⟨c, fun e he => hcL e (hE.mem_toFinset.2 he), fun e he => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hc e (hE.mem_toFinset.2 he)
  exact ⟨fun h h' => h1 (hE.mem_toFinset.2 h) h', fun h h' => h2 (hE.mem_toFinset.2 h) h'⟩
declarations.citation: The list edge-coloring theorem for bipartite multigraphs (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 63 (1995)), special case of maximum degree two, in the form used in arXiv:2610.07318 (A note on the list chromatic number of two matroids), proofs of Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 2.3. The proof here differs: a direct induction (a vertex with at most one neighbour is colored last; an edge whose ends have different lists is cut; if all lists agree along edges, a pair is contracted).

explanation.summary: The theorem proves that any sub-2-regular multigraph formed by two involutions is 2-list-colorable. The proof strengthens the claim by allowing one optional vertex of degree at most 1 to have a list of size at least 1, and proceeds by induction on the number of vertices. In the inductive step, vertices of degree at most 1 are removed and colored greedily, and cycles with differing lists across an edge are reduced similarly; on cycles with identical lists, a 2-edge contraction reduces the cycle length by 2 while preserving properness.

steps.claim: Updating a coloring at vertex v with color t preserves properness under an involution r on E, provided it was proper on E \\ {v} and t differs from the color of v's partner.
steps.explanation: To check that the updated coloring assigns different colors to e and r(e) for distinct e, r(e) ∈ E, we consider whether either endpoint is v. If e = v, the updated value at e is t, while at r(e) ≠ v it is c'(r(e)), which differs from t by assumption. Symmetrically, if r(e) = v, then e = r(v) by the involution property, and the two values again differ. If neither endpoint is v, both updated values match c', which was already proper on E \\ {v}.
steps.code:
intro e he hre hne
  by_cases hev : e = v
  · subst hev
    rw [Function.update_of_ne hne, Function.update_self]
    exact hv hne hre
  · by_cases hrev : r e = v
    · have : e = r v := by rw [← hrev, hr e]
      subst this
      rw [hrev, Function.update_self, Function.update_of_ne hev]
      exact (hv hev he).symm
    · rw [Function.update_of_ne hrev, Function.update_of_ne hev]
      exact hc' e (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hev, he⟩) (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hrev, hre⟩) hne

steps.claim: In the base case n = 0, any empty set of vertices has a trivial coloring.
steps.explanation: Since |E| ≤ 0, E is the empty set. Any function, such as the constant zero function, vacuously satisfies the list membership and properness conditions.
steps.code:
induction n with
  | zero =>
    intro E hE p q hp hq L zo _ _
    have : E = ∅ := Finset.card_eq_zero.1 (Nat.le_zero.1 hE)
    subst this
    exact ⟨fun _ => 0, by simp, by simp⟩

steps.claim: In the inductive step, if there is a distinguished vertex z ∈ E with list size at least 1 and degree at most 1, we choose a color for z and set up the induction on E \\ {z}.
steps.explanation: Since |L(z)| ≥ 1, we pick a color t ∈ L(z). We remove z from E to get E', remove t from the lists of z's neighbors p(z) and q(z) to get L', and designate p(z) (or q(z)) as the new distinguished vertex z₀' if it remains in E'. The set E' has size |E| - 1 ≤ n, so the induction hypothesis applies to E'.
steps.code:
| succ n ih =>
    intro E hE p q hp hq L zo hL hz
    by_cases hA : ∃ z, zo = some z ∧ z ∈ E
    · -- a vertex with a short list: it has at most one neighbour, colour it first
      obtain ⟨z, rfl, hzE⟩ := hA
      obtain ⟨h1, hfree⟩ := hz z rfl hzE
      obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := Finset.card_pos.1 h1
      set E' := E.erase z with hE'
      set L' : α → Finset ℕ := fun e =>
        if e ≠ z ∧ (e = p z ∨ e = q z) then (L e).erase t else L e with hL'
      set zo' : Option α :=
        if p z ∈ E' then some (p z) else if q z ∈ E' then some (q z) else none with hzo'
      have hcard : E'.card ≤ n := by rw [hE', Finset.card_erase_of_mem hzE]; omega

steps.claim: The inductive coloring on E' extends to E by coloring z with t.
steps.explanation: By induction, E' has a proper coloring c' drawn from L'. Since t was erased from the lists of p(z) and q(z), neither partner of z receives color t in c'. We set c(z) = t and keep c'(e) for e ≠ z. By involution_coloring_update applied to both p and q, the extended coloring is proper on all of E.
steps.code:
refine (fun H => ?_) (ih E' hcard p q hp hq L' zo' ?_ ?_)
      · obtain ⟨c', hc'L, hc'⟩ := H
        have hpz : p z ≠ z → p z ∈ E → c' (p z) ≠ t := by
          intro h1 h2 h3
          have := hc'L (p z) (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨h1, h2⟩)
          rw [hL'] at this
          simp only [ne_eq, h1, not_false_eq_true, true_or, and_self, if_true] at this
          exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 this).1 h3
        have hqz : q z ≠ z → q z ∈ E → c' (q z) ≠ t := by
          intro h1 h2 h3
          have := hc'L (q z) (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨h1, h2⟩)
          rw [hL'] at this
          simp only [ne_eq, h1, not_false_eq_true, or_true, and_self, if_true] at this
          exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 this).1 h3
        refine ⟨Function.update c' z t, ?_, ?_⟩
        · intro e he
          by_cases hez : e = z
          · subst hez; simpa using ht
          · rw [Function.update_of_ne hez]
            have := hc'L e (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hez, he⟩)
            rw [hL'] at this
            dsimp only at this
            split_ifs at this with h
            all_goals first | exact Finset.mem_of_mem_erase this | exact this
        · intro e he
          exact ⟨involution_coloring_update E z c' t p hp (fun e he => (hc' e he).1) hpz e he,
            involution_coloring_update E z c' t q hq (fun e he => (hc' e he).2) hqz e he⟩

steps.claim: All vertices in E' other than the new distinguished vertex retain list size at least 2.
steps.explanation: For any e ∈ E' with e ≠ z₀', if e is neither p(z) nor q(z), its list is unchanged and has size at least 2. If e were p(z) or q(z), it would have been selected as z₀' unless both p(z) and q(z) were in E' and distinct, which contradicts the hypothesis that z has degree at most 1 in E.
steps.code:
· intro e he hne
        have hez : e ≠ z := (Finset.mem_erase.1 he).1
        have heE : e ∈ E := (Finset.mem_erase.1 he).2
        by_cases hm : e = p z ∨ e = q z
        · exfalso
          apply hne
          rcases hm with h | h
          · rw [hzo', if_pos (h ▸ he), h]
          · by_cases hp' : p z ∈ E'
            · rw [hzo', if_pos hp']
              have hpz : p z ≠ z := (Finset.mem_erase.1 hp').1
              by_contra hc
              have hpe : p z ≠ e := fun h' => hc (by rw [h'])
              exact hfree ⟨(Finset.mem_erase.1 hp').2, h ▸ heE, hpz, h ▸ hez,
                fun h'' => hpe (h'' ▸ h.symm)⟩
            · rw [hzo', if_neg hp', if_pos (h ▸ he), h]
        · have : L' e = L e := by
            rw [hL']; dsimp only; rw [if_neg (fun h => hm h.2)]
          rw [this]

steps.claim: The new distinguished vertex has list size at least 1 and degree at most 1 in E'.
steps.explanation: The new distinguished vertex y ∈ {p(z), q(z)} had at most one color (namely t) removed from its list, so |L'(y)| ≥ |L(y)| - 1 ≥ 1. Moreover, y cannot have degree 2 in E', because one of its neighbors under p or q is z, which has been removed from E'.
steps.code:
exact hL e heE (by simp only [ne_eq, Option.some.injEq]; exact fun h => hez h.symm)
      · intro y hy hyE
        have hyz : y ≠ z := (Finset.mem_erase.1 hyE).1
        have hyE' : y ∈ E := (Finset.mem_erase.1 hyE).2
        have hym : y = p z ∨ y = q z := by
          rw [hzo'] at hy
          split_ifs at hy <;> simp_all
        have hLy : L' y = (L y).erase t := by
          rw [hL']; dsimp only; rw [if_pos ⟨hyz, hym⟩]
        refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
        · rw [hLy]
          have := hL y hyE' (by simp only [ne_eq, Option.some.injEq]; exact fun h => hyz h.symm)
          have := Finset.pred_card_le_card_erase (s := L y) (a := t)
          omega
        · rintro ⟨h1, h2, -, -, -⟩
          rcases hym with h | h
          · have : p y = z := by rw [h, hp z]
            exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 h1).1 this
          · have : q y = z := by rw [h, hq z]
            exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 h2).1 this

steps.claim: When there is no distinguished vertex in E, every element of E has list size at least 2.
steps.explanation: Since no distinguished vertex belongs to E, the hypothesis ensuring size at least 2 applies to all vertices e ∈ E.
steps.code:
· have hL2 : ∀ e ∈ E, 2 ≤ (L e).card := by
        intro e he
        apply hL e he
        intro h
        exact hA ⟨e, h, he⟩

steps.claim: If some vertex v ∈ E has degree at most 1, we can find an available color for v after inductively coloring E \\ {v}.
steps.explanation: We delete v and apply the induction hypothesis to E \\ {v} with no distinguished vertex. The neighbors of v in E \\ {v} span at most one color under c'. Since |L(v)| ≥ 2, the set L(v) \\ F of available colors is nonempty, providing a color t ∈ L(v) distinct from the colors of v's neighbors.
steps.code:
by_cases hB1 : ∃ v ∈ E, ¬ (p v ∈ E ∧ q v ∈ E ∧ p v ≠ v ∧ q v ≠ v ∧ p v ≠ q v)
      · -- a vertex with at most one neighbour: colour the rest, then it
        obtain ⟨v, hvE, hfree⟩ := hB1
        have hcard : (E.erase v).card ≤ n := by rw [Finset.card_erase_of_mem hvE]; omega
        obtain ⟨c', hc'L, hc'⟩ := ih (E.erase v) hcard p q hp hq L none
          (fun e he _ => hL2 e (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase he)) (by simp)
        set F : Finset ℕ := (({p v, q v} : Finset α).filter (· ∈ E.erase v)).image c' with hF
        have hFc : F.card ≤ 1 := by
          refine (Finset.card_image_le).trans ?_
          rw [Finset.card_le_one]
          intro a ha b hb
          simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at ha hb
          by_contra hab
          apply hfree
          rcases ha with ⟨rfl | rfl, ha⟩ <;> rcases hb with ⟨rfl | rfl, hb⟩
          · exact absurd rfl hab
          · exact ⟨(Finset.mem_erase.1 ha).2, (Finset.mem_erase.1 hb).2,
              (Finset.mem_erase.1 ha).1, (Finset.mem_erase.1 hb).1, hab⟩
          · exact ⟨(Finset.mem_erase.1 hb).2, (Finset.mem_erase.1 ha).2,
              (Finset.mem_erase.1 hb).1, (Finset.mem_erase.1 ha).1, fun h => hab h.symm⟩
          · exact absurd rfl hab
        obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ : (L v \ F).Nonempty := by
          rw [← Finset.card_pos]
          have := Finset.le_card_sdiff F (L v)
          have := hL2 v hvE
          omega

steps.claim: Extending the coloring to v with the chosen color t produces a proper coloring on E.
steps.explanation: Setting c(v) = t and c(e) = c'(e) for e ≠ v yields a coloring from L. Since t was chosen outside F, it avoids the colors of both p(v) and q(v). Properness for both p and q then follows by involution_coloring_update.
steps.code:
have hmem : ∀ y, y = p v ∨ y = q v → y ≠ v → y ∈ E → c' y ≠ t := by
          intro y hy hyv hyE h
          apply (Finset.mem_sdiff.1 ht).2
          rw [hF, Finset.mem_image]
          refine ⟨y, Finset.mem_filter.2 ⟨?_, Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hyv, hyE⟩⟩, h⟩
          rcases hy with rfl | rfl <;> simp
        refine ⟨Function.update c' v t, ?_, ?_⟩
        · intro e he
          by_cases hev : e = v
          · subst hev; simpa using (Finset.mem_sdiff.1 ht).1
          · rw [Function.update_of_ne hev]; exact hc'L e (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hev, he⟩)
        · intro e he
          exact ⟨involution_coloring_update E v c' t p hp (fun e he => (hc' e he).1)
              (fun h1 h2 => hmem _ (Or.inl rfl) h1 h2) e he,
            involution_coloring_update E v c' t q hq (fun e he => (hc' e he).2)
              (fun h1 h2 => hmem _ (Or.inr rfl) h1 h2) e he⟩

steps.claim: If no vertex has degree at most 1, every vertex in E has degree exactly 2.
steps.explanation: By the failure of the previous case, every vertex v ∈ E has p(v) ∈ E and q(v) ∈ E, distinct from v and from each other.
steps.code:
· have hnf : ∀ v ∈ E, p v ∈ E ∧ q v ∈ E ∧ p v ≠ v ∧ q v ≠ v ∧ p v ≠ q v := by
          intro v hv
          by_contra h
          exact hB1 ⟨v, hv, h⟩

steps.claim: If an edge has endpoints with different lists, the induction hypothesis can color the graph.
steps.explanation: Suppose some edge has differing lists, say a ∈ L(v) \\ L(r(v)) for an involution r. We remove v, color v with a, and remove a from the list of v's other neighbor s(v). We designate s(v) as the distinguished vertex in E \\ {v}, which now has list size at least 1 and degree at most 1 in E \\ {v}. Inductively coloring E \\ {v} gives c', which extends to v by setting c(v) = a: it avoids r(v) because a ∉ L(r(v)), and avoids s(v) because a was erased from L(s(v)). Properness follows by involution_coloring_update.
steps.code:
-- an edge whose ends have different lists
        have key : ∀ (r s : α → α), Function.Involutive r → Function.Involutive s →
            (∀ v ∈ E, r v ∈ E ∧ s v ∈ E ∧ r v ≠ v ∧ s v ≠ v ∧ r v ≠ s v) →
            (∃ v ∈ E, ∃ a ∈ L v, a ∉ L (r v)) →
            ∃ c : α → ℕ, (∀ e ∈ E, c e ∈ L e) ∧
              ∀ e ∈ E, (r e ∈ E → r e ≠ e → c (r e) ≠ c e) ∧
                (s e ∈ E → s e ≠ e → c (s e) ≠ c e) := by
          intro r s hr hs hrs ⟨v, hvE, a, haL, har⟩
          obtain ⟨hrv, hsv, hrvv, hsvv, hrsv⟩ := hrs v hvE
          have hcard : (E.erase v).card ≤ n := by rw [Finset.card_erase_of_mem hvE]; omega
          set L' := Function.update L (s v) ((L (s v)).erase a) with hL'
          refine (fun H => ?_) (ih (E.erase v) hcard r s hr hs L' (some (s v)) ?_ ?_)
          · obtain ⟨c', hc'L, hc'⟩ := H
            have hrv' : c' (r v) ∉ ({a} : Finset ℕ) := by
              have := hc'L (r v) (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hrvv, hrv⟩)
              rw [hL', Function.update_of_ne hrsv] at this
              simp only [Finset.mem_singleton]
              exact fun h => har (h ▸ this)
            have hsv' : c' (s v) ≠ a := by
              have := hc'L (s v) (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hsvv, hsv⟩)
              rw [hL', Function.update_self] at this
              exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 this).1
            refine ⟨Function.update c' v a, ?_, ?_⟩
            · intro e he
              by_cases hev : e = v
              · subst hev; simpa using haL
              · rw [Function.update_of_ne hev]
                have := hc'L e (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hev, he⟩)
                by_cases hes : e = s v
                · rw [hes, hL', Function.update_self] at this
                  rw [hes]; exact Finset.mem_of_mem_erase this
                · rwa [hL', Function.update_of_ne hes] at this
            · intro e he
              exact ⟨involution_coloring_update E v c' a r hr (fun e he => (hc' e he).1)
                  (fun _ _ h => hrv' (Finset.mem_singleton.2 h)) e he,
                involution_coloring_update E v c' a s hs (fun e he => (hc' e he).2)
                  (fun _ _ => hsv') e he⟩
          · intro e he hne
            have hes : e ≠ s v := fun h => hne (by rw [h])
            rw [hL', Function.update_of_ne hes]
            exact hL2 e (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase he)
          · intro y hy hyE
            simp only [Option.some.injEq] at hy
            subst hy
            refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
            · rw [hL', Function.update_self]
              have := Finset.pred_card_le_card_erase (s := L (s v)) (a := a)
              have := hL2 (s v) hsv
              omega
            · rintro ⟨-, h2, -⟩
              rw [hs v] at h2
              exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 h2).1 rfl

steps.claim: Any difference between lists along a p-edge or a q-edge provides a proper coloring.
steps.explanation: If there is a p-edge with differing lists, we apply the key lemma directly to (p, q). If there is a q-edge with differing lists, we apply the key lemma with the roles of p and q swapped.
steps.code:
by_cases hpa : ∃ v ∈ E, ∃ a ∈ L v, a ∉ L (p v)
        · exact key p q hp hq hnf hpa
        by_cases hqa : ∃ v ∈ E, ∃ a ∈ L v, a ∉ L (q v)
        · obtain ⟨c, hcL, hc⟩ := key q p hq hp (fun v hv => by
            obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4, h5⟩ := hnf v hv
            exact ⟨h2, h1, h4, h3, fun h => h5 h.symm⟩) hqa
          exact ⟨c, hcL, fun e he => ⟨(hc e he).2, (hc e he).1⟩⟩

steps.claim: When no lists differ along edges, lists are identical along all edges, and the empty set is trivially colored.
steps.explanation: Since no color belongs to one endpoint but not the other along any p-edge or q-edge, every vertex shares its list with its neighbors under p and q. If E is empty, the constant coloring works trivially.
steps.code:
-- all lists agree along edges: contract one `p`-pair into a `q`-edge
        have hsub : ∀ v ∈ E, L v ⊆ L (p v) ∧ L v ⊆ L (q v) := by
          intro v hv
          refine ⟨fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
          · by_contra h; exact hpa ⟨v, hv, a, ha, h⟩
          · by_contra h; exact hqa ⟨v, hv, a, ha, h⟩
        rcases E.eq_empty_or_nonempty with hE0 | ⟨v, hvE⟩
        · subst hE0; exact ⟨fun _ => 0, by simp, by simp⟩

steps.claim: For a 2-regular component with identical lists, we contract a p-edge {v, w} into a new q-edge {u, x}.
steps.explanation: Pick v ∈ E, and set w = p(v), u = q(v), x = q(w). We define an involution q' that swaps u and x while fixing v and w, and acts as q elsewhere. This contracts the p-edge {v, w} along the cycle.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨hwE, huE, hwv, huv, hwu⟩ := hnf v hvE
        set w := p v with hw
        set u := q v with hu
        obtain ⟨-, hxE, -, hxw, -⟩ := hnf w hwE
        set x := q w with hx
        have hxu : x ≠ u := fun h => hwv (hq.injective h)
        have hxv : x ≠ v := fun h => hwu (by rw [← hq w, ← hx, h])
        have hqu : q u = v := hq v
        have hqx : q x = w := hq w
        have hpw : p w = v := hp v
        set q' : α → α := fun y =>
          if y = u then x else if y = x then u else if y = v then v else if y = w then w
          else q y with hq'
        have hq'inv : Function.Involutive q' := by
          intro y
          by_cases h1 : y = u
          · subst h1; simp [hq', hxu]
          by_cases h2 : y = x
          · subst h2; simp [hq', hxu]
          by_cases h3 : y = v
          · subst h3; simp [hq', h1, h2]
          by_cases h4 : y = w
          · subst h4; simp [hq', h1, h2, h3]
          have k1 : q y ≠ u := fun h => h3 (by rw [← hq y, h, hqu])
          have k2 : q y ≠ x := fun h => h4 (by rw [← hq y, h, hqx])
          have k3 : q y ≠ v := fun h => h1 (by rw [← hq y, h])
          have k4 : q y ≠ w := fun h => h2 (by rw [← hq y, h])
          simp [hq', h1, h2, h3, h4, k1, k2, k3, k4, hq y]

steps.claim: Inductively color the contracted set E'' = E \\ {v, w} using p and q'.
steps.explanation: Since |E''| = |E| - 2 ≤ n, the induction hypothesis applies to E'' with involutions p and q', yielding a coloring c' satisfying c'(u) ≠ c'(x) because {u, x} is an edge under q'.
steps.code:
set E'' := (E.erase v).erase w with hE''
        have hcard : E''.card ≤ n := by
          rw [hE'', Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hwv, hwE⟩),
            Finset.card_erase_of_mem hvE]
          omega
        have huE'' : u ∈ E'' := Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨fun h => hwu h.symm,
          Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨huv, huE⟩⟩
        have hxE'' : x ∈ E'' := Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hxw, Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hxv, hxE⟩⟩
        obtain ⟨c', hc'L, hc'⟩ := ih E'' hcard p q' hp hq'inv L none
          (fun e he _ => hL2 e (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase he)))
          (by simp)
        have hux : c' x ≠ c' u := by
          have := (hc' u huE'').2
          simp only [hq', if_true] at this
          exact this hxE'' hxu

steps.claim: The coloring c' is proper for the original involution q on E''.
steps.explanation: Any q-edge entirely within E'' cannot have u or x as an endpoint, since q(u) = v and q(x) = w are outside E''. Therefore, q' coincides with q on all edges internal to E'', so c' is proper for q on E''.
steps.code:
-- `c'` is proper for `q` on `E''`: the edges of `q` inside `E''` are edges of `q'`
        have hc'q : ∀ e ∈ E'', q e ∈ E'' → q e ≠ e → c' (q e) ≠ c' e := by
          intro e he hqe hne
          have hev : e ≠ v := (Finset.mem_erase.1 (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase he)).1
          have hew : e ≠ w := (Finset.mem_erase.1 he).1
          have heu : e ≠ u := fun h => by
            rw [h, hqu] at hqe
            exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hqe)).1 rfl
          have hex : e ≠ x := fun h => by
            rw [h, hqx] at hqe
            exact (Finset.mem_erase.1 hqe).1 rfl
          have : q' e = q e := by simp [hq', heu, hex, hev, hew]
          have := (hc' e he).2
          rw [‹q' e = q e›] at this
          exact this hqe hne

steps.claim: Extend c' to v by assigning c₁(v) = c'(x).
steps.explanation: Setting c₁(v) = c'(x) preserves properness on E \\ {w} for both p (since p(v) = w ∉ E \\ {w}) and q (since q(v) = u and c'(x) ≠ c'(u)), using involution_coloring_update.
steps.code:
set c1 := Function.update c' v (c' x) with hc1
        have hE1 : (E.erase w).erase v = E'' := by rw [hE'', Finset.erase_right_comm]
        have hc1p : ∀ e ∈ E.erase w, p e ∈ E.erase w → p e ≠ e → c1 (p e) ≠ c1 e :=
          involution_coloring_update (E.erase w) v c' (c' x) p hp
            (by rw [hE1]; exact fun e he => (hc' e he).1)
            (fun _ h => absurd (Finset.mem_erase.1 h).1 (by simp [hw]))
        have hc1q : ∀ e ∈ E.erase w, q e ∈ E.erase w → q e ≠ e → c1 (q e) ≠ c1 e :=
          involution_coloring_update (E.erase w) v c' (c' x) q hq
            (by rw [hE1]; exact hc'q) (fun _ _ => hux.symm)

steps.claim: Extend c₁ to w by assigning c(w) = c'(u), completing the proof of the auxiliary lemma.
steps.explanation: Setting c(w) = c'(u) preserves properness under p (since p(w) = v and c(w) = c'(u) ≠ c'(x) = c(v)) and under q (since q(w) = x and c(w) = c'(u) ≠ c'(x) = c(x)), by involution_coloring_update. Furthermore, since lists are constant along the cycle, c'(x) ∈ L(x) = L(v) and c'(u) ∈ L(u) = L(w).
steps.code:
refine ⟨Function.update c1 w (c' u), ?_, ?_⟩
        · intro e he
          by_cases hew : e = w
          · rw [hew, Function.update_self]
            have h1 := hc'L u huE''
            have h2 := (hsub u huE).2 h1
            rw [hqu] at h2
            exact (hsub v hvE).1 h2
          · rw [Function.update_of_ne hew]
            by_cases hev : e = v
            · rw [hev, hc1, Function.update_self]
              have h1 := hc'L x hxE''
              have h2 := (hsub x hxE).2 h1
              rw [hqx] at h2
              have h3 := (hsub w hwE).1 h2
              rwa [hpw] at h3
            · rw [hc1, Function.update_of_ne hev]
              exact hc'L e (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hew, Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hev, he⟩⟩)
        · intro e he
          refine ⟨involution_coloring_update E w c1 (c' u) p hp hc1p ?_ e he,
            involution_coloring_update E w c1 (c' u) q hq hc1q ?_ e he⟩
          · intro _ _
            rw [hpw, hc1, Function.update_self]
            exact hux
          · intro _ _
            rw [hc1, Function.update_of_ne hxv]
            exact hux

steps.claim: Every finite set with list sizes at least 2 is list-colorable under two involutions.
steps.explanation: We specialize two_involutions_list_aux to the finite set E with n = |E| and no distinguished vertex (zo = none). Since all lists have size at least 2 on E, the auxiliary lemma yields a valid coloring, which we transfer from Finset to Set.
steps.code:
classical
  obtain ⟨c, hcL, hc⟩ := two_involutions_list_aux hE.toFinset.card hE.toFinset le_rfl p q hp hq
    L none (fun e he _ => hL e (hE.mem_toFinset.1 he)) (by simp)
  refine ⟨c, fun e he => hcL e (hE.mem_toFinset.2 he), fun e he => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hc e (hE.mem_toFinset.2 he)
  exact ⟨fun h h' => h1 (hE.mem_toFinset.2 h) h', fun h h' => h2 (hE.mem_toFinset.2 h) h'⟩

glossary.Function.update_of_ne: If x ≠ a, updating f at a does not change its value at x.
glossary.Function.update_self: Updating f at a with value v yields v when evaluated at a.
glossary.involution_coloring_update: Updating a coloring at vertex v preserves properness under an involution r provided it was proper away from v and the new color avoids v's partner under r.
glossary.Finset.card_erase_of_mem: Erasing an element present in a finite set decreases its cardinality by 1.
glossary.Finset.mem_of_mem_erase: An element of s with an element removed still belongs to s.
glossary.Finset.card_image_le: The image of a finite set under a function has cardinality at most that of the set.
glossary.Finset.card_le_one: A finite set has at most one element if and only if any two elements in it are equal.
glossary.Finset.card_pos: A finite set is nonempty if and only if its cardinality is strictly positive.
glossary.Finset.le_card_sdiff: The cardinality of t \\ s is at least the cardinality of t minus the cardinality of s.
glossary.Finset.mem_image: Membership in the image of a function is defined by existence of a preimage.
glossary.Finset.pred_card_le_card_erase: Erasing an element from a set s decreases its cardinality by at most 1.
glossary.Finset.erase_right_comm: Two erase operations on a finite set commute.
glossary.two_involutions_list_aux: Every finite sub-2-regular graph with list sizes at least 2 (with at most one optional degree-1 vertex with list size at least 1) is list-colorable.
glossary.le_rfl: Every element is less than or equal to itself in a preorder.

declarations.name: matroid_sbo_reduction_pairs_of_two_indep
declarations.informal: Let M be a finite strongly base-orderable matroid whose ground set is the union of two disjoint independent sets I and J. Then M has a reduction to a unit-capacity partition matroid with classes of size at most two: there is an involution p such that every subset T of the ground set containing no two distinct elements e, p e is independent in M.
declarations.statement:
theorem matroid_sbo_reduction_pairs_of_two_indep {α : Type*} (M : Matroid α) [M.Finite]
    (hM : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M) (I J : Set α) (hI : M.Indep I) (hJ : M.Indep J)
    (hIJ : Disjoint I J) (hE : I ∪ J = M.E) :
    ∃ p : α → α, Function.Involutive p ∧
      ∀ T ⊆ M.E, (∀ e ∈ T, p e ∈ T → p e = e) → M.Indep T
declarations.source:
/-- One swap: composing an exchange bijection `φ : B₁ ≃ B₂` with the transposition of
`z = φ⁻¹(k)` and `k` (for `k ∈ B₁ ∩ B₂`) keeps the exchange property. -/
theorem sbo_exchange_swap {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (M : Matroid α) {B₁ B₂ : Set α} (φ : B₁ ≃ B₂)
    (hφ : ∀ X : Set B₁, M.IsBase ((B₁ \ ((↑) '' X)) ∪ ((fun x => (φ x : α)) '' X)))
    (k : B₁) (hk : (k : α) ∈ B₂) (hne : (φ k : α) ≠ k) :
    ∀ X : Set B₁, M.IsBase ((B₁ \ ((↑) '' X)) ∪
      ((fun x => (((Equiv.swap (φ.symm ⟨k, hk⟩) k).trans φ) x : α)) '' X)) := by
  classical
  intro X
  set z := φ.symm ⟨k, hk⟩ with hz
  have hφz : (φ z : α) = k := by simp [hz]
  have hzk : z ≠ k := fun h => hne (by rw [← h, hφz, h])
  have hsz : Equiv.swap z k z = k := Equiv.swap_apply_left z k
  have hsk : Equiv.swap z k k = z := Equiv.swap_apply_right z k
  have hso : ∀ x, x ≠ z → x ≠ k → Equiv.swap z k x = x :=
    fun x h1 h2 => Equiv.swap_apply_of_ne_of_ne h1 h2
  have hkB : (k : α) ∈ B₁ := k.2
  have hcoe : ∀ x : B₁, (x : α) = k → x = k := fun x h => Subtype.ext h
  set Y : Set B₁ := if z ∈ X then insert k X else X \ {k} with hY
  convert hφ Y using 1
  ext a
  simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_sdiff, Set.mem_image, Equiv.trans_apply]
  by_cases hzX : z ∈ X <;> by_cases hkX : k ∈ X
  · have hYX : Y = X := by rw [hY, if_pos hzX, Set.insert_eq_of_mem hkX]
    rw [hYX]
    have hmem : ∀ x ∈ X, Equiv.swap z k x ∈ X := by
      intro x hx
      by_cases h1 : x = z
      · rw [h1, hsz]; exact hkX
      by_cases h2 : x = k
      · rw [h2, hsk]; exact hzX
      rw [hso x h1 h2]; exact hx
    constructor
    · rintro (h | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr ⟨Equiv.swap z k x, hmem x hx, rfl⟩
    · rintro (h | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr ⟨Equiv.swap z k x, hmem x hx, by rw [Equiv.swap_apply_self]⟩
  · have hYX : Y = insert k X := by rw [hY, if_pos hzX]
    rw [hYX]
    constructor
    · rintro (⟨haB, ha⟩ | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · by_cases hak : a = k
        · exact Or.inr ⟨z, Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ hzX, by rw [hφz, hak]⟩
        · refine Or.inl ⟨haB, ?_⟩
          rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
          rcases hx with rfl | hx
          · exact hak rfl
          · exact ha ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
      · refine Or.inr ⟨Equiv.swap z k x, ?_, rfl⟩
        by_cases h1 : x = z
        · rw [h1, hsz]; exact Set.mem_insert _ _
        have h2 : x ≠ k := fun h => hkX (h ▸ hx)
        rw [hso x h1 h2]; exact Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ hx
    · rintro (⟨haB, ha⟩ | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · exact Or.inl ⟨haB, fun ⟨x, hx, hxa⟩ => ha ⟨x, Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ hx, hxa⟩⟩
      · rcases hx with rfl | hx
        · exact Or.inr ⟨z, hzX, by rw [hsz]⟩
        · by_cases h1 : x = z
          · subst h1
            refine Or.inl ⟨by rw [hφz]; exact hkB, ?_⟩
            rintro ⟨y, hy, hya⟩
            rw [hφz] at hya
            exact hkX (hcoe y hya ▸ hy)
          · have h2 : x ≠ k := fun h => hkX (h ▸ hx)
            exact Or.inr ⟨x, hx, by rw [hso x h1 h2]⟩
  · have hYX : Y = X \ {k} := by rw [hY, if_neg hzX]
    rw [hYX]
    constructor
    · rintro (⟨haB, ha⟩ | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · exact Or.inl ⟨haB, fun ⟨x, hx, hxa⟩ => ha ⟨x, hx.1, hxa⟩⟩
      · by_cases h2 : x = k
        · subst h2
          refine Or.inl ⟨by rw [hsk, hφz]; exact hkB, ?_⟩
          rintro ⟨y, hy, hya⟩
          rw [hsk, hφz] at hya
          exact hy.2 (hcoe y hya)
        · have h1 : x ≠ z := fun h => hzX (h ▸ hx)
          exact Or.inr ⟨x, ⟨hx, h2⟩, by rw [hso x h1 h2]⟩
    · rintro (⟨haB, ha⟩ | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · by_cases hak : a = k
        · exact Or.inr ⟨k, hkX, by rw [hsk, hφz, hak]⟩
        · refine Or.inl ⟨haB, ?_⟩
          rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
          exact ha ⟨x, ⟨hx, fun h => hak (by rw [h])⟩, rfl⟩
      · have h1 : x ≠ z := fun h => hzX (h ▸ hx.1)
        exact Or.inr ⟨x, hx.1, by rw [hso x h1 hx.2]⟩
  · have hYX : Y = X := by rw [hY, if_neg hzX, Set.sdiff_singleton_eq_self hkX]
    rw [hYX]
    have hfix : ∀ x ∈ X, Equiv.swap z k x = x := fun x hx =>
      hso x (fun h => hzX (h ▸ hx)) (fun h => hkX (h ▸ hx))
    constructor
    · rintro (h | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr ⟨x, hx, by rw [hfix x hx]⟩
    · rintro (h | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr ⟨x, hx, by rw [hfix x hx]⟩

/-- In a matroid, an exchange bijection between two finite bases can be chosen to fix every
element the two bases share. -/
theorem sbo_exchange_fix_common {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (M : Matroid α) {B₁ B₂ : Set α} (hfin : B₁.Finite)
    (φ : B₁ ≃ B₂)
    (hφ : ∀ X : Set B₁, M.IsBase ((B₁ \ ((↑) '' X)) ∪ ((fun x => (φ x : α)) '' X))) :
    ∃ ψ : B₁ ≃ B₂, (∀ X : Set B₁, M.IsBase ((B₁ \ ((↑) '' X)) ∪ ((fun x => (ψ x : α)) '' X)))
      ∧ ∀ x : B₁, (x : α) ∈ B₂ → (ψ x : α) = x := by
  have : Finite B₁ := hfin.to_subtype
  suffices h : ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ φ : B₁ ≃ B₂,
      (∀ X : Set B₁, M.IsBase ((B₁ \ ((↑) '' X)) ∪ ((fun x => (φ x : α)) '' X))) →
      {x : B₁ | (x : α) ∈ B₂ ∧ (φ x : α) ≠ x}.ncard ≤ n →
      ∃ ψ : B₁ ≃ B₂, (∀ X : Set B₁, M.IsBase ((B₁ \ ((↑) '' X)) ∪ ((fun x => (ψ x : α)) '' X)))
        ∧ ∀ x : B₁, (x : α) ∈ B₂ → (ψ x : α) = x from h _ φ hφ le_rfl
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero =>
    intro φ hφ hn
    refine ⟨φ, hφ, fun x hx => ?_⟩
    by_contra h
    have : {x : B₁ | (x : α) ∈ B₂ ∧ (φ x : α) ≠ x}.Nonempty := ⟨x, hx, h⟩
    rw [← Set.ncard_pos (Set.toFinite _)] at this
    omega
  | succ n ih =>
    intro φ hφ hn
    by_cases hall : ∀ x : B₁, (x : α) ∈ B₂ → (φ x : α) = x
    · exact ⟨φ, hφ, hall⟩
    push Not at hall
    obtain ⟨k, hk, hne⟩ := hall
    set z := φ.symm ⟨k, hk⟩ with hz
    have hφz : (φ z : α) = k := by simp [hz]
    have hzk : z ≠ k := fun h => hne (by rw [← h, hφz, h])
    set φ' := (Equiv.swap z k).trans φ with hφ'
    apply ih φ' (sbo_exchange_swap M φ hφ k hk hne)
    have hsub : {x : B₁ | (x : α) ∈ B₂ ∧ (φ' x : α) ≠ x} ⊆
        {x : B₁ | (x : α) ∈ B₂ ∧ (φ x : α) ≠ x} \ {k} := by
      rintro x ⟨hx2, hxne⟩
      refine ⟨⟨hx2, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
      · by_cases h1 : x = z
        · rw [h1, hφz]; exact fun h => hzk (Subtype.ext h.symm)
        · by_cases h2 : x = k
          · subst h2; exact hne
          · rwa [hφ', Equiv.trans_apply, Equiv.swap_apply_of_ne_of_ne h1 h2] at hxne
      · rintro rfl
        apply hxne
        rw [hφ', Equiv.trans_apply, Equiv.swap_apply_right, hφz]
    have hk' : k ∈ {x : B₁ | (x : α) ∈ B₂ ∧ (φ x : α) ≠ x} := ⟨hk, hne⟩
    have := Set.ncard_le_ncard hsub (Set.toFinite _)
    rw [Set.ncard_sdiff_singleton_of_mem hk'] at this
    omega

theorem matroid_sbo_reduction_pairs_of_two_indep {α : Type*} (M : Matroid α) [M.Finite]
    (hM : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M) (I J : Set α) (hI : M.Indep I) (hJ : M.Indep J)
    (hIJ : Disjoint I J) (hE : I ∪ J = M.E) :
    ∃ p : α → α, Function.Involutive p ∧
      ∀ T ⊆ M.E, (∀ e ∈ T, p e ∈ T → p e = e) → M.Indep T := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨B₁, hB₁, hIB⟩ := hI.exists_isBase_superset
  obtain ⟨B₂, hB₂, hJB⟩ := hJ.exists_isBase_superset
  obtain ⟨φ₀, hφ₀⟩ := hM B₁ B₂ hB₁ hB₂
  obtain ⟨φ, hφ, hfix⟩ := sbo_exchange_fix_common M (M.ground_finite.subset hB₁.subset_ground)
    φ₀ hφ₀
  set p : α → α := fun a =>
    if h : a ∈ B₁ then (φ ⟨a, h⟩ : α) else if h2 : a ∈ B₂ then (φ.symm ⟨a, h2⟩ : α) else a
    with hp
  -- an element of `B₁ \ B₂` is sent outside `B₁`
  have hout : ∀ (a : α) (h : a ∈ B₁), a ∉ B₂ → (φ ⟨a, h⟩ : α) ∉ B₁ := by
    intro a h ha hb
    have h2 : (φ ⟨a, h⟩ : α) ∈ B₂ := (φ ⟨a, h⟩).2
    have := hfix ⟨_, hb⟩ h2
    have hinj : φ ⟨(φ ⟨a, h⟩ : α), hb⟩ = φ ⟨a, h⟩ := Subtype.ext this
    have := φ.injective hinj
    have h3 : (φ ⟨a, h⟩ : α) = a := congrArg Subtype.val this
    exact ha (h3 ▸ h2)
  refine ⟨p, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro a
    by_cases h : a ∈ B₁
    · by_cases h2 : a ∈ B₂
      · have hf := hfix ⟨a, h⟩ h2
        simp only [hp, dif_pos h]
        simp only [hf, dif_pos h]
      · have hb := hout a h h2
        have hb2 : (φ ⟨a, h⟩ : α) ∈ B₂ := (φ ⟨a, h⟩).2
        simp only [hp, dif_pos h, dif_neg hb, dif_pos hb2]
        simp
    · by_cases h2 : a ∈ B₂
      · have hc : (φ.symm ⟨a, h2⟩ : α) ∈ B₁ := (φ.symm ⟨a, h2⟩).2
        simp only [hp, dif_neg h, dif_pos h2, dif_pos hc]
        simp
      · simp only [hp, dif_neg h, dif_neg h2]
  · intro T hT hTp
    set X : Set B₁ := {x | (φ x : α) ∈ T ∧ (x : α) ∉ B₂} with hX
    refine (hφ X).indep.subset ?_
    intro t ht
    by_cases htB : t ∈ B₁
    · refine Or.inl ⟨htB, ?_⟩
      rintro ⟨x, ⟨hxT, hxB⟩, rfl⟩
      have hpx : p x = (φ x : α) := by simp [hp, x.2]
      have := hTp x ht (hpx ▸ hxT)
      rw [hpx] at this
      exact hxB (this ▸ (φ x).2)
    · have htE : t ∈ I ∪ J := hE ▸ hT ht
      have htB2 : t ∈ B₂ := by
        rcases htE with h | h
        · exact absurd (hIB h) htB
        · exact hJB h
      set x := φ.symm ⟨t, htB2⟩ with hx
      have hφx : (φ x : α) = t := by simp [hx]
      have hxB : (x : α) ∉ B₂ := by
        intro h
        have := hfix x h
        rw [hφx] at this
        exact htB (this ▸ x.2)
      exact Or.inr ⟨x, ⟨hφx ▸ ht, hxB⟩, hφx⟩
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.07318 (A note on the list chromatic number of two matroids), Proposition 2.2. The classes are given as the orbits {e, p e} of an involution. The proof differs from the paper's: instead of applying strong base-orderability in the contraction by the common part of the two bases, the exchange bijection is made to fix that common part by successive transpositions, which keep the exchange property; disjointness of I and J is not used.

explanation.summary: The independent sets I and J are extended to bases B₁ and B₂ of the strongly base-orderable matroid M, which guarantees the existence of an exchange bijection between them. By an induction on the number of unfixed shared elements using transpositions, this exchange bijection can be chosen to fix every element in B₁ ∩ B₂. The candidate involution p is defined by swapping each element of B₁ \ B₂ with its image under the bijection, while fixing all other elements. Finally, any subset T containing no non-trivial orbit under p is shown to embed into an exchange base (B₁ \ X) ∪ φ(X), which proves that T is independent in M.

steps.claim: The exchange property for φ composed with the transposition of z = φ⁻¹(k) and k reduces to showing (B₁ \ X) ∪ φ((z k) '' X) = (B₁ \ Y) ∪ φ(Y) for a suitably modified set Y.
steps.explanation: Fix a subset X ⊆ B₁, let k ∈ B₁ ∩ B₂ with φ(k) ≠ k, and let z = φ⁻¹(k) ∈ B₁. Since φ(k) ≠ k, we have z ≠ k. We record the standard action of the swap τ = (z k): it interchanges z and k and fixes every other element. Setting Y = X ∪ {k} if z ∈ X and Y = X \ {k} if z ∉ X, applying the exchange property of φ to Y reduces the exchange property of τ ∘ φ on X to establishing the equality of the two resulting base sets.
steps.code:
classical
  intro X
  set z := φ.symm ⟨k, hk⟩ with hz
  have hφz : (φ z : α) = k := by simp [hz]
  have hzk : z ≠ k := fun h => hne (by rw [← h, hφz, h])
  have hsz : Equiv.swap z k z = k := Equiv.swap_apply_left z k
  have hsk : Equiv.swap z k k = z := Equiv.swap_apply_right z k
  have hso : ∀ x, x ≠ z → x ≠ k → Equiv.swap z k x = x :=
    fun x h1 h2 => Equiv.swap_apply_of_ne_of_ne h1 h2
  have hkB : (k : α) ∈ B₁ := k.2
  have hcoe : ∀ x : B₁, (x : α) = k → x = k := fun x h => Subtype.ext h
  set Y : Set B₁ := if z ∈ X then insert k X else X \ {k} with hY
  convert hφ Y using 1

steps.claim: The set equality (B₁ \ X) ∪ φ((z k) '' X) = (B₁ \ Y) ∪ φ(Y) holds when both z ∈ X and k ∈ X.
steps.explanation: We unfold set membership into logical equivalences and perform a four-way case split on whether z and k belong to X. When both z ∈ X and k ∈ X, the definition of Y simplifies to Y = X. Furthermore, the swap τ = (z k) stabilizes X because it exchanges z and k and fixes the remaining elements. Since τ is an involution preserving X, the image under τ is X itself, and both sides coincide.
steps.code:
ext a
  simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_sdiff, Set.mem_image, Equiv.trans_apply]
  by_cases hzX : z ∈ X <;> by_cases hkX : k ∈ X
  · have hYX : Y = X := by rw [hY, if_pos hzX, Set.insert_eq_of_mem hkX]
    rw [hYX]
    have hmem : ∀ x ∈ X, Equiv.swap z k x ∈ X := by
      intro x hx
      by_cases h1 : x = z
      · rw [h1, hsz]; exact hkX
      by_cases h2 : x = k
      · rw [h2, hsk]; exact hzX
      rw [hso x h1 h2]; exact hx
    constructor
    · rintro (h | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr ⟨Equiv.swap z k x, hmem x hx, rfl⟩
    · rintro (h | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr ⟨Equiv.swap z k x, hmem x hx, by rw [Equiv.swap_apply_self]⟩

steps.claim: The set equality holds when z ∈ X and k ∉ X.
steps.explanation: When z ∈ X and k ∉ X, the definition yields Y = X ∪ {k}. We verify inclusion in both directions: any element a ∈ B₁ \ X is either k (which equals φ(z) ∈ φ(Y)) or differs from k (placing it in B₁ \ Y); conversely, taking k out of B₁ \ X is compensated by φ(z) = k being in the image, while τ maps z ∈ X to k ∈ Y.
steps.code:
· have hYX : Y = insert k X := by rw [hY, if_pos hzX]
    rw [hYX]
    constructor
    · rintro (⟨haB, ha⟩ | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · by_cases hak : a = k
        · exact Or.inr ⟨z, Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ hzX, by rw [hφz, hak]⟩
        · refine Or.inl ⟨haB, ?_⟩
          rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
          rcases hx with rfl | hx
          · exact hak rfl
          · exact ha ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
      · refine Or.inr ⟨Equiv.swap z k x, ?_, rfl⟩
        by_cases h1 : x = z
        · rw [h1, hsz]; exact Set.mem_insert _ _
        have h2 : x ≠ k := fun h => hkX (h ▸ hx)
        rw [hso x h1 h2]; exact Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ hx
    · rintro (⟨haB, ha⟩ | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · exact Or.inl ⟨haB, fun ⟨x, hx, hxa⟩ => ha ⟨x, Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ hx, hxa⟩⟩
      · rcases hx with rfl | hx
        · exact Or.inr ⟨z, hzX, by rw [hsz]⟩
        · by_cases h1 : x = z
          · subst h1
            refine Or.inl ⟨by rw [hφz]; exact hkB, ?_⟩
            rintro ⟨y, hy, hya⟩
            rw [hφz] at hya
            exact hkX (hcoe y hya ▸ hy)
          · have h2 : x ≠ k := fun h => hkX (h ▸ hx)
            exact Or.inr ⟨x, hx, by rw [hso x h1 h2]⟩

steps.claim: The set equality holds when z ∉ X and k ∈ X.
steps.explanation: When z ∉ X and k ∈ X, we have Y = X \ {k}. Symmetrically to the previous case, k ∈ X is mapped by τ to z, and φ(z) = k. Any element in B₁ \ X is already in B₁ \ Y, while in the image, τ(k) = z ensures that φ(τ(k)) = k ∈ B₁ \ Y, matching the two sides.
steps.code:
· have hYX : Y = X \ {k} := by rw [hY, if_neg hzX]
    rw [hYX]
    constructor
    · rintro (⟨haB, ha⟩ | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · exact Or.inl ⟨haB, fun ⟨x, hx, hxa⟩ => ha ⟨x, hx.1, hxa⟩⟩
      · by_cases h2 : x = k
        · subst h2
          refine Or.inl ⟨by rw [hsk, hφz]; exact hkB, ?_⟩
          rintro ⟨y, hy, hya⟩
          rw [hsk, hφz] at hya
          exact hy.2 (hcoe y hya)
        · have h1 : x ≠ z := fun h => hzX (h ▸ hx)
          exact Or.inr ⟨x, ⟨hx, h2⟩, by rw [hso x h1 h2]⟩
    · rintro (⟨haB, ha⟩ | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · by_cases hak : a = k
        · exact Or.inr ⟨k, hkX, by rw [hsk, hφz, hak]⟩
        · refine Or.inl ⟨haB, ?_⟩
          rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
          exact ha ⟨x, ⟨hx, fun h => hak (by rw [h])⟩, rfl⟩
      · have h1 : x ≠ z := fun h => hzX (h ▸ hx.1)
        exact Or.inr ⟨x, hx.1, by rw [hso x h1 hx.2]⟩

steps.claim: The set equality holds when neither z nor k belongs to X.
steps.explanation: When z ∉ X and k ∉ X, we have Y = X. Because neither transposed element lies in X, the swap τ fixes every element of X pointwise. Therefore τ '' X = X, so φ(τ '' X) = φ(X) and both sides are identical.
steps.code:
· have hYX : Y = X := by rw [hY, if_neg hzX, Set.sdiff_singleton_eq_self hkX]
    rw [hYX]
    have hfix : ∀ x ∈ X, Equiv.swap z k x = x := fun x hx =>
      hso x (fun h => hzX (h ▸ hx)) (fun h => hkX (h ▸ hx))
    constructor
    · rintro (h | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr ⟨x, hx, by rw [hfix x hx]⟩
    · rintro (h | ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
      · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr ⟨x, hx, by rw [hfix x hx]⟩

steps.claim: To construct an exchange bijection fixing all common elements, it suffices to show by induction on n that any exchange bijection with at most n unfixed common elements can be modified to fix all of B₁ ∩ B₂.
steps.explanation: Because B₁ is finite, the set of common elements not fixed by φ, {x ∈ B₁ ∩ B₂ | φ(x) ≠ x}, is finite. We formulate an induction principle on the cardinality n of this unfixed set; once proved for all n, the desired result follows by taking n to be the cardinality of the unfixed set for φ.
steps.code:
have : Finite B₁ := hfin.to_subtype
  suffices h : ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ φ : B₁ ≃ B₂,
      (∀ X : Set B₁, M.IsBase ((B₁ \ ((↑) '' X)) ∪ ((fun x => (φ x : α)) '' X))) →
      {x : B₁ | (x : α) ∈ B₂ ∧ (φ x : α) ≠ x}.ncard ≤ n →
      ∃ ψ : B₁ ≃ B₂, (∀ X : Set B₁, M.IsBase ((B₁ \ ((↑) '' X)) ∪ ((fun x => (ψ x : α)) '' X)))
        ∧ ∀ x : B₁, (x : α) ∈ B₂ → (ψ x : α) = x from h _ φ hφ le_rfl
  intro n

steps.claim: In the base case n = 0, any exchange bijection with at most 0 unfixed common elements already fixes every element of B₁ ∩ B₂.
steps.explanation: If the unfixed set has cardinality at most 0, it must be empty. If there were any common element x with φ(x) ≠ x, the set would be nonempty and hence have strictly positive cardinality, contradicting the bound. Thus φ already fixes all common elements, so ψ = φ satisfies the requirements.
steps.code:
induction n with
  | zero =>
    intro φ hφ hn
    refine ⟨φ, hφ, fun x hx => ?_⟩
    by_contra h
    have : {x : B₁ | (x : α) ∈ B₂ ∧ (φ x : α) ≠ x}.Nonempty := ⟨x, hx, h⟩
    rw [← Set.ncard_pos (Set.toFinite _)] at this
    omega

steps.claim: In the inductive step, swapping an unfixed common element with its preimage produces an exchange bijection with strictly fewer unfixed common elements, completing the induction.
steps.explanation: If φ already fixes all common elements, we are done. Otherwise, let k ∈ B₁ ∩ B₂ be an unfixed element, and let z = φ⁻¹(k). By lemma sbo_exchange_swap, the modified bijection φ' = τ ∘ φ (with τ = (z k)) preserves the exchange property. Furthermore, φ'(k) = φ(z) = k, so k is now fixed. Any common element not fixed by φ' was already not fixed by φ and cannot be k, so the unfixed set for φ' is contained in that of φ minus {k}. Its cardinality is at most (n + 1) - 1 = n, so the induction hypothesis applies to φ'.
steps.code:
| succ n ih =>
    intro φ hφ hn
    by_cases hall : ∀ x : B₁, (x : α) ∈ B₂ → (φ x : α) = x
    · exact ⟨φ, hφ, hall⟩
    push Not at hall
    obtain ⟨k, hk, hne⟩ := hall
    set z := φ.symm ⟨k, hk⟩ with hz
    have hφz : (φ z : α) = k := by simp [hz]
    have hzk : z ≠ k := fun h => hne (by rw [← h, hφz, h])
    set φ' := (Equiv.swap z k).trans φ with hφ'
    apply ih φ' (sbo_exchange_swap M φ hφ k hk hne)
    have hsub : {x : B₁ | (x : α) ∈ B₂ ∧ (φ' x : α) ≠ x} ⊆
        {x : B₁ | (x : α) ∈ B₂ ∧ (φ x : α) ≠ x} \ {k} := by
      rintro x ⟨hx2, hxne⟩
      refine ⟨⟨hx2, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
      · by_cases h1 : x = z
        · rw [h1, hφz]; exact fun h => hzk (Subtype.ext h.symm)
        · by_cases h2 : x = k
          · subst h2; exact hne
          · rwa [hφ', Equiv.trans_apply, Equiv.swap_apply_of_ne_of_ne h1 h2] at hxne
      · rintro rfl
        apply hxne
        rw [hφ', Equiv.trans_apply, Equiv.swap_apply_right, hφz]
    have hk' : k ∈ {x : B₁ | (x : α) ∈ B₂ ∧ (φ x : α) ≠ x} := ⟨hk, hne⟩
    have := Set.ncard_le_ncard hsub (Set.toFinite _)
    rw [Set.ncard_sdiff_singleton_of_mem hk'] at this
    omega

steps.claim: Extend I and J to bases B₁ and B₂, obtain an exchange bijection φ fixing B₁ ∩ B₂, and define the candidate involution p.
steps.explanation: We extend the independent sets I and J to bases B₁ and B₂ of M. By strong base orderability, there exists an exchange bijection between them, and by lemma sbo_exchange_fix_common, we may choose an exchange bijection φ : B₁ ≃ B₂ that fixes every element in B₁ ∩ B₂. We then define p : α → α by sending a ∈ B₁ to φ(a), sending a ∈ B₂ \ B₁ to φ⁻¹(a), and fixing all other elements.
steps.code:
classical
  obtain ⟨B₁, hB₁, hIB⟩ := hI.exists_isBase_superset
  obtain ⟨B₂, hB₂, hJB⟩ := hJ.exists_isBase_superset
  obtain ⟨φ₀, hφ₀⟩ := hM B₁ B₂ hB₁ hB₂
  obtain ⟨φ, hφ, hfix⟩ := sbo_exchange_fix_common M (M.ground_finite.subset hB₁.subset_ground)
    φ₀ hφ₀
  set p : α → α := fun a =>
    if h : a ∈ B₁ then (φ ⟨a, h⟩ : α) else if h2 : a ∈ B₂ then (φ.symm ⟨a, h2⟩ : α) else a
    with hp

steps.claim: The bijection φ maps every element of B₁ \ B₂ outside of B₁.
steps.explanation: Let a ∈ B₁ \ B₂. If φ(a) were in B₁, then φ(a) would belong to B₁ ∩ B₂. Since φ fixes every element of B₁ ∩ B₂, we would have φ(φ(a)) = φ(a). By injectivity of φ, this implies φ(a) = a, which would place a in B₂, contradicting a ∉ B₂.
steps.code:
-- an element of `B₁ \ B₂` is sent outside `B₁`
  have hout : ∀ (a : α) (h : a ∈ B₁), a ∉ B₂ → (φ ⟨a, h⟩ : α) ∉ B₁ := by
    intro a h ha hb
    have h2 : (φ ⟨a, h⟩ : α) ∈ B₂ := (φ ⟨a, h⟩).2
    have := hfix ⟨_, hb⟩ h2
    have hinj : φ ⟨(φ ⟨a, h⟩ : α), hb⟩ = φ ⟨a, h⟩ := Subtype.ext this
    have := φ.injective hinj
    have h3 : (φ ⟨a, h⟩ : α) = a := congrArg Subtype.val this
    exact ha (h3 ▸ h2)

steps.claim: The map p is an involution on α.
steps.explanation: We analyze the position of an arbitrary element a with respect to B₁ and B₂. If a ∈ B₁ ∩ B₂, then φ(a) = a, so p(a) = a and p(p(a)) = a. If a ∈ B₁ \ B₂, then p(a) = φ(a) ∈ B₂ \ B₁ by the previous step, so p(p(a)) = φ⁻¹(φ(a)) = a. If a ∈ B₂ \ B₁, then p(a) = φ⁻¹(a) ∈ B₁, so p(p(a)) = φ(φ⁻¹(a)) = a. Finally, if a ∉ B₁ ∪ B₂, p fixes a, so p(p(a)) = a.
steps.code:
refine ⟨p, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro a
    by_cases h : a ∈ B₁
    · by_cases h2 : a ∈ B₂
      · have hf := hfix ⟨a, h⟩ h2
        simp only [hp, dif_pos h]
        simp only [hf, dif_pos h]
      · have hb := hout a h h2
        have hb2 : (φ ⟨a, h⟩ : α) ∈ B₂ := (φ ⟨a, h⟩).2
        simp only [hp, dif_pos h, dif_neg hb, dif_pos hb2]
        simp
    · by_cases h2 : a ∈ B₂
      · have hc : (φ.symm ⟨a, h2⟩ : α) ∈ B₁ := (φ.symm ⟨a, h2⟩).2
        simp only [hp, dif_neg h, dif_pos h2, dif_pos hc]
        simp
      · simp only [hp, dif_neg h, dif_neg h2]

steps.claim: For any T ⊆ M.E containing no distinct pair {e, p(e)}, showing independence of T reduces to showing T ⊆ B' = (B₁ \ X) ∪ φ(X) for X = {x ∈ B₁ | φ(x) ∈ T ∧ x ∉ B₂}, and every t ∈ T ∩ B₁ belongs to B₁ \ X.
steps.explanation: By the exchange property of φ, the set B' = (B₁ \ X) ∪ φ(X) is a base of M, hence independent. Since any subset of an independent set is independent, it suffices to show T ⊆ B'. For t ∈ T ∩ B₁: if t were in X, then φ(t) ∈ T and t ∉ B₂. Since t ∈ B₁ \ B₂, p(t) = φ(t) ∈ T. The condition on T then forces p(t) = t, meaning φ(t) = t ∈ B₂, which contradicts t ∉ B₂. Thus t ∉ X, so t ∈ B₁ \ X ⊆ B'.
steps.code:
· intro T hT hTp
    set X : Set B₁ := {x | (φ x : α) ∈ T ∧ (x : α) ∉ B₂} with hX
    refine (hφ X).indep.subset ?_
    intro t ht
    by_cases htB : t ∈ B₁
    · refine Or.inl ⟨htB, ?_⟩
      rintro ⟨x, ⟨hxT, hxB⟩, rfl⟩
      have hpx : p x = (φ x : α) := by simp [hp, x.2]
      have := hTp x ht (hpx ▸ hxT)
      rw [hpx] at this
      exact hxB (this ▸ (φ x).2)
    · have htE : t ∈ I ∪ J := hE ▸ hT ht

steps.claim: Every element t ∈ T \ B₁ belongs to φ(X) ⊆ B', establishing T ⊆ B' and completing the proof of independence.
steps.explanation: Since t ∈ T ⊆ M.E = I ∪ J and t ∉ B₁ (which contains I), t must belong to J ⊆ B₂. Let x = φ⁻¹(t) ∈ B₁. If x were in B₂, then x ∈ B₁ ∩ B₂, so φ(x) = x, which would imply t = x ∈ B₁, a contradiction. Thus x ∉ B₂, and since φ(x) = t ∈ T, we have x ∈ X. Consequently, t = φ(x) ∈ φ(X) ⊆ B', which shows T ⊆ B' and proves that T is independent.
steps.code:
have htB2 : t ∈ B₂ := by
        rcases htE with h | h
        · exact absurd (hIB h) htB
        · exact hJB h
      set x := φ.symm ⟨t, htB2⟩ with hx
      have hφx : (φ x : α) = t := by simp [hx]
      have hxB : (x : α) ∉ B₂ := by
        intro h
        have := hfix x h
        rw [hφx] at this
        exact htB (this ▸ x.2)
      exact Or.inr ⟨x, ⟨hφx ▸ ht, hxB⟩, hφx⟩

declarations.name: matroid_sbo_list_colorable_two_of_colorable_two
declarations.informal: If M₁ and M₂ are strongly base-orderable matroids on a common finite ground set and each of them is 2-colorable (its ground set is the union of two independent sets), then the pair (M₁, M₂) is 2-list-colorable: from any lists of at least two colors per element one can choose colors so that every color class is independent in both matroids.
declarations.statement:
theorem matroid_sbo_list_colorable_two_of_colorable_two {α : Type*} (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α)
    [M₁.Finite] (hE : M₁.E = M₂.E)
    (h₁ : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₁) (h₂ : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₂)
    (c₁ : matroid_common_colorable M₁ M₁ 2) (c₂ : matroid_common_colorable M₂ M₂ 2) :
    matroid_common_list_colorable M₁ M₂ 2
declarations.source:
theorem matroid_sbo_list_colorable_two_of_colorable_two {α : Type*} (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α)
    [M₁.Finite] (hE : M₁.E = M₂.E)
    (h₁ : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₁) (h₂ : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₂)
    (c₁ : matroid_common_colorable M₁ M₁ 2) (c₂ : matroid_common_colorable M₂ M₂ 2) :
    matroid_common_list_colorable M₁ M₂ 2 := by
  classical
  have : M₂.Finite := ⟨hE ▸ M₁.ground_finite⟩
  -- each matroid reduces to a partition matroid with classes of size at most two
  have red : ∀ (M : Matroid α) [M.Finite], matroid_strongly_base_orderable M →
      matroid_common_colorable M M 2 → ∃ p : α → α, Function.Involutive p ∧
        ∀ T ⊆ M.E, (∀ e ∈ T, p e ∈ T → p e = e) → M.Indep T := by
    intro M _ hM ⟨c, hc, hind⟩
    refine matroid_sbo_reduction_pairs_of_two_indep M hM {e | e ∈ M.E ∧ c e = 0}
      {e | e ∈ M.E ∧ c e = 1} (hind 0).1 (hind 1).1 ?_ ?_
    · rw [Set.disjoint_left]
      rintro e ⟨-, h0⟩ ⟨-, h1⟩
      omega
    · ext e
      simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
      constructor
      · rintro (⟨h, -⟩ | ⟨h, -⟩) <;> exact h
      · intro h
        have := hc e h
        by_cases h0 : c e = 0
        · exact Or.inl ⟨h, h0⟩
        · exact Or.inr ⟨h, by omega⟩
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpT⟩ := red M₁ h₁ c₁
  obtain ⟨q, hq, hqT⟩ := red M₂ h₂ c₂
  intro L hL
  obtain ⟨c, hcL, hc⟩ := list_colorable_two_of_two_involutions M₁.E M₁.ground_finite p q hp hq
    L hL
  refine ⟨c, hcL, fun γ => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · refine hpT _ (fun e he => he.1) ?_
    rintro e ⟨he, hγ⟩ ⟨hpe, hpγ⟩
    by_contra hne
    exact (hc e he).1 hpe hne (hpγ.trans hγ.symm)
  · refine hqT _ (fun e he => hE ▸ he.1) ?_
    rintro e ⟨he, hγ⟩ ⟨hqe, hqγ⟩
    by_contra hne
    exact (hc e he).2 hqe hne (hqγ.trans hγ.symm)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.07318 (A note on the list chromatic number of two matroids), Corollary 2.3 (first statement), proved there via Proposition 2.2 (reduction to a partition matroid with classes of size at most two) and the list edge-coloring theorem for bipartite multigraphs of maximum degree two. Single-matroid 2-colorability is written as a common 2-coloring of the pair (M, M).

explanation.summary: The proof reduces common 2-list-coloring of two strongly base-orderable matroids to 2-list-coloring a graph formed by two involutions. First, an auxiliary reduction lemma (`matroid_sbo_reduction_pairs_of_two_indep`) shows that any finite strongly base-orderable matroid partitioned into two independent sets admits an involution whose transversals are all independent. Applying this to M₁ and M₂ produces two involutions p and q. By `list_colorable_two_of_two_involutions`, any list assignment of size at least two admits a coloring that separates the endpoints of every 2-cycle of p and q, so each color class is a transversal for both involutions and therefore independent in both matroids.

steps.claim: The matroid M₂ is finite.
steps.explanation: We open a classical context. Since M₁ is a finite matroid, its ground set M₁.E is finite. Because M₁.E = M₂.E by hypothesis (hE), the ground set of M₂ is also finite, establishing the finiteness of M₂.
steps.code:
classical
  have : M₂.Finite := ⟨hE ▸ M₁.ground_finite⟩

steps.claim: Any finite, strongly base-orderable, 2-colorable matroid reduces to an involution whose transversals are independent sets.
steps.explanation: We establish an auxiliary lemma `red`. A 2-coloring c of a matroid M partitions the ground set M.E into two independent sets I = {e ∈ M.E | c e = 0} and J = {e ∈ M.E | c e = 1}. These sets are disjoint since an element cannot have color both 0 and 1, and their union is all of M.E because every color in M.E is strictly less than 2 (hence 0 or 1). Applying `matroid_sbo_reduction_pairs_of_two_indep` to I and J yields an involution p on α such that any subset T ⊆ M.E that contains at most one element from each 2-cycle of p (i.e. if e ∈ T and p e ∈ T then p e = e) is independent in M.
steps.code:
-- each matroid reduces to a partition matroid with classes of size at most two
  have red : ∀ (M : Matroid α) [M.Finite], matroid_strongly_base_orderable M →
      matroid_common_colorable M M 2 → ∃ p : α → α, Function.Involutive p ∧
        ∀ T ⊆ M.E, (∀ e ∈ T, p e ∈ T → p e = e) → M.Indep T := by
    intro M _ hM ⟨c, hc, hind⟩
    refine matroid_sbo_reduction_pairs_of_two_indep M hM {e | e ∈ M.E ∧ c e = 0}
      {e | e ∈ M.E ∧ c e = 1} (hind 0).1 (hind 1).1 ?_ ?_
    · rw [Set.disjoint_left]
      rintro e ⟨-, h0⟩ ⟨-, h1⟩
      omega
    · ext e
      simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
      constructor
      · rintro (⟨h, -⟩ | ⟨h, -⟩) <;> exact h
      · intro h
        have := hc e h
        by_cases h0 : c e = 0
        · exact Or.inl ⟨h, h0⟩
        · exact Or.inr ⟨h, by omega⟩

steps.claim: There exist involutions p and q witnessing independence for M₁ and M₂, respectively.
steps.explanation: Applying the reduction lemma `red` to M₁ (using its strong base-orderability h₁ and 2-colorability c₁) yields an involution p on α. Applying `red` to M₂ (using h₂ and c₂) yields an involution q on α. Any subset of the ground set meeting each non-trivial orbit of p (respectively q) in at most one element is independent in M₁ (respectively M₂).
steps.code:
obtain ⟨p, hp, hpT⟩ := red M₁ h₁ c₁
  obtain ⟨q, hq, hqT⟩ := red M₂ h₂ c₂

steps.claim: Given color lists of size at least two, we obtain a coloring c separating non-trivial orbits of p and q, reducing list-colorability to checking each color class.
steps.explanation: Given a list assignment L assigning at least two colors to each element e ∈ M₁.E, we apply `list_colorable_two_of_two_involutions` to obtain a coloring c : α → ℕ choosing c(e) ∈ L(e) that properly colors every non-trivial 2-cycle of both p and q. We propose c as the desired common list-coloring, leaving two subgoals for every color γ: that the color class {e ∈ M₁.E | c e = γ} is independent in M₁, and that it is independent in M₂.
steps.code:
intro L hL
  obtain ⟨c, hcL, hc⟩ := list_colorable_two_of_two_involutions M₁.E M₁.ground_finite p q hp hq
    L hL
  refine ⟨c, hcL, fun γ => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩

steps.claim: For every color γ, the color class {e ∈ M₁.E | c e = γ} is independent in M₁.
steps.explanation: By the property hpT of p, it suffices to check that the color class contains no distinct pair {e, p e}. If e and p e both belonged to the color class with p e ≠ e, they would share the same color γ. But c was chosen so that c(p e) ≠ c e whenever p e ∈ M₁.E and p e ≠ e, reaching a contradiction.
steps.code:
· refine hpT _ (fun e he => he.1) ?_
    rintro e ⟨he, hγ⟩ ⟨hpe, hpγ⟩
    by_contra hne
    exact (hc e he).1 hpe hne (hpγ.trans hγ.symm)

steps.claim: For every color γ, the color class {e ∈ M₁.E | c e = γ} is independent in M₂.
steps.explanation: Similarly, since M₁.E = M₂.E, the color class is a subset of M₂.E. By the property hqT of q, it suffices to check that no distinct pair {e, q e} both lie in the color class. If they did, they would share the color γ, contradicting the property that c(q e) ≠ c e whenever q e ≠ e.
steps.code:
· refine hqT _ (fun e he => hE ▸ he.1) ?_
    rintro e ⟨he, hγ⟩ ⟨hqe, hqγ⟩
    by_contra hne
    exact (hc e he).2 hqe hne (hqγ.trans hγ.symm)

glossary.matroid_sbo_reduction_pairs_of_two_indep: A finite strongly base-orderable matroid whose ground set is the disjoint union of two independent sets admits an involution such that any subset containing at most one element from each 2-cycle is independent.
glossary.Set.disjoint_left: Two sets are disjoint if and only if no element of the first set belongs to the second set.
glossary.Set.mem_union: An element belongs to the union of two sets if and only if it belongs to the first set or to the second set.
glossary.Set.mem_ofPred_eq: An element belongs to a set defined by a predicate if and only if it satisfies the predicate.
glossary.Or.inl: Given a proof of the left disjunct A, infers the disjunction A ∨ B.
glossary.Or.inr: Given a proof of the right disjunct B, infers the disjunction A ∨ B.
glossary.list_colorable_two_of_two_involutions: On a finite set with two involutions, any list assignment with lists of size at least two admits a coloring that assigns different colors to the two elements of every non-trivial 2-cycle of either involution.
