declarations.name: matroid_sbo_common_list_colorable_two_of_common_colorable_two
declarations.informal: If two strongly base-orderable matroids on a common finite ground set have a common coloring with two colors, then they are 2-list-colorable in common. This is the case χ(M₁, M₂) ≤ 2 of the open question whether χ_ℓ = χ for strongly base-orderable pairs.
declarations.statement:
theorem matroid_sbo_common_list_colorable_two_of_common_colorable_two {α : Type*}
    (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α) [M₁.Finite] (hE : M₁.E = M₂.E)
    (h₁ : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₁) (h₂ : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₂)
    (h : matroid_common_colorable M₁ M₂ 2) : matroid_common_list_colorable M₁ M₂ 2
declarations.source:
theorem matroid_sbo_common_list_colorable_two_of_common_colorable_two {α : Type*}
    (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α) [M₁.Finite] (hE : M₁.E = M₂.E)
    (h₁ : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₁) (h₂ : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₂)
    (h : matroid_common_colorable M₁ M₂ 2) : matroid_common_list_colorable M₁ M₂ 2 := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc, hind⟩ := h
  refine matroid_sbo_list_colorable_two_of_colorable_two M₁ M₂ hE h₁ h₂
    ⟨c, hc, fun γ => ⟨(hind γ).1, (hind γ).1⟩⟩ ⟨c, hE ▸ hc, fun γ => ?_⟩
  have hs : {e | e ∈ M₂.E ∧ c e = γ} = {e | e ∈ M₁.E ∧ c e = γ} := by rw [hE]
  rw [hs]
  exact ⟨(hind γ).2, (hind γ).2⟩
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.07318 (A note on the list chromatic number of two matroids), Corollary 2.3 ("in particular" part). The paper derives it through the 1976 theorem on common chromatic numbers of strongly base-orderable matroids; here it follows directly from the first part, since a common 2-coloring 2-colors each matroid.

explanation.summary: To show that two strongly base-orderable matroids M₁ and M₂ on a common finite ground set are commonly 2-list-colorable, the proof extracts the assumed common 2-coloring c of the pair (M₁, M₂). Because every color class of c is independent in both matroids, c serves as an individual 2-coloring for M₁ and, by identifying the ground sets, for M₂. The result then follows by applying matroid_sbo_list_colorable_two_of_colorable_two, which deduces common 2-list-colorability from individual 2-colorability for strongly base-orderable matroids.

steps.claim: There exists a coloring c : α → ℕ assigning each element of M₁.E a color in {0, 1} such that every color class is independent in both M₁ and M₂.
steps.explanation: Unpacking the hypothesis h that M₁ and M₂ are commonly 2-colorable yields the coloring function c, the bound c(e) < 2 for all elements e ∈ M₁.E, and the condition hind asserting that each color class {e ∈ M₁.E | c(e) = γ} is independent in both M₁ and M₂.
steps.code: obtain ⟨c, hc, hind⟩ := h

steps.claim: To show that M₁ and M₂ are commonly 2-list-colorable, it suffices to show that each color class of c restricted to M₂.E is independent in M₂.
steps.explanation: By matroid_sbo_list_colorable_two_of_colorable_two, two strongly base-orderable matroids on the same ground set are commonly 2-list-colorable whenever each is individually 2-colorable. The coloring c is already an individual 2-coloring for M₁ because its color classes are independent in M₁. For M₂, the color bound transfers via the ground-set equality M₁.E = M₂.E (hE), leaving only the obligation to check that the color classes in M₂ are independent in M₂.
steps.code:
refine matroid_sbo_list_colorable_two_of_colorable_two M₁ M₂ hE h₁ h₂
    ⟨c, hc, fun γ => ⟨(hind γ).1, (hind γ).1⟩⟩ ⟨c, hE ▸ hc, fun γ => ?_⟩

steps.claim: Each color class of c restricted to M₂.E is independent in M₂, completing the proof.
steps.explanation: Since M₁.E = M₂.E by hypothesis hE, the color class {e ∈ M₂.E | c(e) = γ} is identical to {e ∈ M₁.E | c(e) = γ}. Rewriting by this set equality, independence in M₂ follows immediately from the second component of hind.
steps.code:
have hs : {e | e ∈ M₂.E ∧ c e = γ} = {e | e ∈ M₁.E ∧ c e = γ} := by rw [hE]
  rw [hs]
  exact ⟨(hind γ).2, (hind γ).2⟩

glossary.matroid_sbo_list_colorable_two_of_colora: If two strongly base-orderable matroids on a common finite ground set are each individually 2-colorable, then they are commonly 2-list-colorable.

caveats: In the formalization, individual 2-colorability of a matroid M is represented as common 2-colorability with itself (matroid_common_colorable M M 2), which explains why the independence condition appears duplicated as ⟨hind₁, hind₁⟩ in the proof.

declarations.name: matroid_common_list_colorable_of_ncard_le
declarations.informal: Two loopless matroids on a common finite ground set E are k-list-colorable whenever k ≥ |E|: from lists of at least |E| colors one can pick pairwise distinct colors, and then every color class has at most one element, which is independent in both matroids because they are loopless. In particular the common list chromatic number of such a pair is well defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem matroid_common_list_colorable_of_ncard_le {α : Type*} (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α)
    [M₁.Finite] (h₁ : M₁.Loopless) (h₂ : M₂.Loopless) (hE : M₁.E = M₂.E) (k : ℕ)
    (hk : M₁.E.ncard ≤ k) : matroid_common_list_colorable M₁ M₂ k
declarations.source:
theorem matroid_common_list_colorable_of_ncard_le {α : Type*} (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α)
    [M₁.Finite] (h₁ : M₁.Loopless) (h₂ : M₂.Loopless) (hE : M₁.E = M₂.E) (k : ℕ)
    (hk : M₁.E.ncard ≤ k) : matroid_common_list_colorable M₁ M₂ k := by
  classical
  intro L hL
  obtain ⟨f, hfinj, hf⟩ := (Finset.all_card_le_biUnion_card_iff_exists_injective
    (fun e : M₁.E => L e)).1 (by
      intro s
      rcases s.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | ⟨e, he⟩
      · simp
      · have : Finite M₁.E := M₁.ground_finite.to_subtype
        have hs : s.card ≤ M₁.E.ncard := by
          rw [← Nat.card_coe_set_eq]
          have := Fintype.ofFinite M₁.E
          rw [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
          exact Finset.card_le_univ s
        calc s.card ≤ k := hs.trans hk
          _ ≤ (L e).card := hL e e.2
          _ ≤ (s.biUnion fun e : M₁.E => L e).card :=
            Finset.card_le_card (Finset.subset_biUnion_of_mem (fun e : M₁.E => L e) he))
  set c : α → ℕ := fun e => if he : e ∈ M₁.E then f ⟨e, he⟩ else 0 with hc
  -- every color class has at most one element, and single elements are independent
  have hsing : ∀ (M : Matroid α), M.Loopless → M.E = M₁.E → ∀ γ : ℕ,
      M.Indep {e | e ∈ M₁.E ∧ c e = γ} := by
    intro M hM hME γ
    have hsub : {e | e ∈ M₁.E ∧ c e = γ}.Subsingleton := by
      rintro a ⟨ha, haγ⟩ b ⟨hb, hbγ⟩
      have : f ⟨a, ha⟩ = f ⟨b, hb⟩ := by
        simp only [hc, dif_pos ha, dif_pos hb] at haγ hbγ
        rw [haγ, hbγ]
      exact congrArg Subtype.val (hfinj this)
    rcases hsub.eq_empty_or_singleton with h | ⟨e, h⟩
    · rw [h]; exact M.empty_indep
    · rw [h, Matroid.indep_singleton]
      have he : e ∈ M.E := by
        have : e ∈ {e | e ∈ M₁.E ∧ c e = γ} := h ▸ rfl
        exact hME ▸ this.1
      exact Matroid.isNonloop_of_loopless he
  refine ⟨c, fun e he => ?_, fun γ => ⟨hsing M₁ h₁ rfl γ, hsing M₂ h₂ hE.symm γ⟩⟩
  simp only [hc, dif_pos he]
  exact hf ⟨e, he⟩
declarations.citation: Helper for the questions of arXiv:2610.07318 (Questions 3.1 and 3.2): it shows the set defining matroid_common_list_chromatic_number is nonempty for finite loopless pairs. Hint: choose distinct representatives with Hall's theorem (Finset.all_card_le_biUnion_card_iff_exists_injective) or greedily.

explanation.summary: To show that two loopless matroids M₁, M₂ on a common finite ground set E are k-list-colorable whenever k ≥ |E|, we apply Hall's Marriage Theorem to select pairwise distinct colors from the lists L(e) for each e ∈ E. Hall's marriage condition holds because any nonempty subset S ⊆ E has |S| ≤ |E| ≤ k ≤ |L(e)| ≤ |⋃_{x ∈ S} L(x)| for each e ∈ S. Extending this injective choice to a coloring c, every color class on E contains at most one element. In a loopless matroid, the empty set and every singleton of the ground set are independent, so every color class is independent in both M₁ and M₂.

steps.claim: Fix a list assignment L assigning at least k colors to each element of the ground set M₁.E.
steps.explanation: We introduce the arbitrary list assignment L and the hypothesis that |L(e)| ≥ k for all e ∈ M₁.E, enabling classical reasoning for noncomputable choices.
steps.code:
classical
  intro L hL

steps.claim: There exists an injective choice function f : M₁.E → ℕ selecting a color f(e) ∈ L(e) for each e ∈ M₁.E.
steps.explanation: By Hall's Marriage Theorem (Finset.all_card_le_biUnion_card_iff_exists_injective), such an injective choice exists if and only if every finite subset s ⊆ M₁.E satisfies |s| ≤ |⋃_{x ∈ s} L(x)|. When s is empty, the inequality holds trivially as 0 ≤ 0. When s is nonempty, pick an element e ∈ s. Since s is a subset of the finite ground set M₁.E, its cardinality satisfies |s| ≤ |M₁.E| ≤ k (using Nat.card_coe_set_eq, Fintype.ofFinite, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, and Finset.card_le_univ). Since |L(e)| ≥ k and L(e) ⊆ ⋃_{x ∈ s} L(x) (via Finset.subset_biUnion_of_mem and Finset.card_le_card), we have |s| ≤ k ≤ |L(e)| ≤ |⋃_{x ∈ s} L(x)|, verifying Hall's condition.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨f, hfinj, hf⟩ := (Finset.all_card_le_biUnion_card_iff_exists_injective
    (fun e : M₁.E => L e)).1 (by
      intro s
      rcases s.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | ⟨e, he⟩
      · simp
      · have : Finite M₁.E := M₁.ground_finite.to_subtype
        have hs : s.card ≤ M₁.E.ncard := by
          rw [← Nat.card_coe_set_eq]
          have := Fintype.ofFinite M₁.E
          rw [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
          exact Finset.card_le_univ s
        calc s.card ≤ k := hs.trans hk
          _ ≤ (L e).card := hL e e.2
          _ ≤ (s.biUnion fun e : M₁.E => L e).card :=
            Finset.card_le_card (Finset.subset_biUnion_of_mem (fun e : M₁.E => L e) he))

steps.claim: Define a coloring c : α → ℕ extending f by setting c(e) = f(e) on M₁.E and c(e) = 0 outside M₁.E.
steps.explanation: We extend the choice function f from the subtype M₁.E to the entire universe α, assigning a default color 0 to elements outside the ground set.
steps.code: set c : α → ℕ := fun e => if he : e ∈ M₁.E then f ⟨e, he⟩ else 0 with hc

steps.claim: In any loopless matroid M with ground set M.E = M₁.E, every color class of c on M₁.E is independent.
steps.explanation: For any color γ, the color class {e ∈ M₁.E | c(e) = γ} contains at most one element: if a, b ∈ M₁.E both have color γ, then f(a) = γ = f(b) by definition of c (via dif_pos), so a = b by injectivity of f (via congrArg and Subtype.val). Being a subsingleton, the color class is either empty, which is independent by matroid axioms, or a singleton {e}. By Matroid.indep_singleton, {e} is independent if and only if e is a nonloop. Since e ∈ M₁.E = M.E and M is loopless, e is a nonloop by Matroid.isNonloop_of_loopless.
steps.code:
have hsing : ∀ (M : Matroid α), M.Loopless → M.E = M₁.E → ∀ γ : ℕ,
      M.Indep {e | e ∈ M₁.E ∧ c e = γ} := by
    intro M hM hME γ
    have hsub : {e | e ∈ M₁.E ∧ c e = γ}.Subsingleton := by
      rintro a ⟨ha, haγ⟩ b ⟨hb, hbγ⟩
      have : f ⟨a, ha⟩ = f ⟨b, hb⟩ := by
        simp only [hc, dif_pos ha, dif_pos hb] at haγ hbγ
        rw [haγ, hbγ]
      exact congrArg Subtype.val (hfinj this)
    rcases hsub.eq_empty_or_singleton with h | ⟨e, h⟩
    · rw [h]; exact M.empty_indep
    · rw [h, Matroid.indep_singleton]
      have he : e ∈ M.E := by
        have : e ∈ {e | e ∈ M₁.E ∧ c e = γ} := h ▸ rfl
        exact hME ▸ this.1
      exact Matroid.isNonloop_of_loopless he

steps.claim: The coloring c is a valid common list coloring for M₁ and M₂ from lists L, completing the proof.
steps.explanation: For every element e ∈ M₁.E, c(e) = f(e) ∈ L(e) by definition of c (evaluating the condition via dif_pos) and the choice of f. For each color γ, the color class is independent in M₁ and M₂ by applying the general independence lemma proved in the previous step to M₁ (with M₁.E = M₁.E) and to M₂ (using the ground set equality M₁.E = M₂.E).
steps.code:
refine ⟨c, fun e he => ?_, fun γ => ⟨hsing M₁ h₁ rfl γ, hsing M₂ h₂ hE.symm γ⟩⟩
  simp only [hc, dif_pos he]
  exact hf ⟨e, he⟩

glossary.Finset.all_card_le_biUnion_card_iff_exis: Hall's marriage condition: an indexed family of finite sets admits an injective system of distinct representatives if and only if every finite subcollection has a union at least as large as the subcollection itself.
glossary.Nat.card_coe_set_eq: The cardinality Nat.card of a set coerced to a subtype equals its set cardinality ncard.
glossary.Fintype.ofFinite: Constructs a Fintype structure from a Finite typeclass instance.
glossary.Nat.card_eq_fintype_card: For a finite type, the Nat.card cardinality equals the Fintype.card cardinality.
glossary.Finset.card_le_univ: The cardinality of any finite subset of a finite type is at most the cardinality of the entire type.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card: If one finite set is a subset of another, its cardinality is less than or equal to the superset's cardinality.
glossary.Finset.subset_biUnion_of_mem: If an index belongs to a set, the corresponding component set is contained in the indexed union.
glossary.dif_pos: In a dependent if-then-else expression, the expression reduces to the then branch when the condition holds.
glossary.congrArg: Functions preserve equality: if a₁ = a₂, then f(a₁) = f(a₂).
glossary.Subtype.val: The canonical projection from a subtype to the underlying carrier type.
glossary.Matroid.indep_singleton: A singleton set {e} is independent in a matroid if and only if e is a nonloop.
glossary.Matroid.isNonloop_of_loopless: In a loopless matroid, every element of the ground set is a nonloop.

caveats: The coloring c is defined on the ambient type α by setting c(e) = 0 for e outside the ground set M₁.E, matching the formalization of matroids on ambient types.
Hall's Marriage Theorem is applied to the subtype of elements in M₁.E, requiring conversions between Set.ncard and Fintype.card.

declarations.name: matroid_common_chromatic_le_list_chromatic
declarations.informal: For two loopless matroids on a common finite ground set, the common chromatic number is at most the common list chromatic number: χ(M₁, M₂) ≤ χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂). Hence the equality χ_ℓ = χ asked for strongly base-orderable pairs is equivalent to χ_ℓ ≤ χ.
declarations.statement:
theorem matroid_common_chromatic_le_list_chromatic {α : Type*} (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α)
    [M₁.Finite] (h₁ : M₁.Loopless) (h₂ : M₂.Loopless) (hE : M₁.E = M₂.E) :
    matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ ≤ matroid_common_list_chromatic_number M₁ M₂
declarations.source:
theorem matroid_common_chromatic_le_list_chromatic {α : Type*} (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α)
    [M₁.Finite] (h₁ : M₁.Loopless) (h₂ : M₂.Loopless) (hE : M₁.E = M₂.E) :
    matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ ≤ matroid_common_list_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ := by
  have hne : {k | matroid_common_list_colorable M₁ M₂ k}.Nonempty :=
    ⟨_, matroid_common_list_colorable_of_ncard_le M₁ M₂ h₁ h₂ hE _ le_rfl⟩
  exact Nat.sInf_le (matroid_common_colorable_of_list_colorable M₁ M₂ _ (Nat.sInf_mem hne))
declarations.citation: Helper for arXiv:2610.07318, Question 3.2 (the inequality χ ≤ χ_ℓ that the paper uses implicitly). Proof: χ_ℓ is attained (the set is nonempty by matroid_common_list_colorable_of_ncard_le, Nat.sInf_mem), list-colorability with constant lists gives a coloring (matroid_common_colorable_of_list_colorable), then Nat.sInf_le.

explanation.summary: The common chromatic and list chromatic numbers are defined as the infima of the natural numbers k for which the matroid pair admits a common k-coloring and a common k-list-coloring, respectively. Since the ground set is finite, a list coloring always exists when k is the ground set size, so the set of list-colorable integers is nonempty and attains its infimum at χ_ℓ. Because every list coloring problem specializes to standard coloring, χ_ℓ is also a valid ordinary color count, and therefore the infimum χ cannot exceed χ_ℓ.

steps.claim: The set of integers k for which (M₁, M₂) is common list colorable is nonempty.
steps.explanation: Because M₁ is finite, loopless, and shares its ground set with the loopless matroid M₂, choosing k = |M₁.E| guarantees common list colorability by `matroid_common_list_colorable_of_ncard_le` with |M₁.E| ≤ |M₁.E| supplied by `le_rfl`. This produces a witness showing that the set of admissible list color counts is nonempty.
steps.code:
have hne : {k | matroid_common_list_colorable M₁ M₂ k}.Nonempty :=
    ⟨_, matroid_common_list_colorable_of_ncard_le M₁ M₂ h₁ h₂ hE _ le_rfl⟩

steps.claim: The common chromatic number of (M₁, M₂) is at most its common list chromatic number: χ(M₁, M₂) ≤ χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂).
steps.explanation: The common list chromatic number χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) is defined as the infimum of the nonempty set of list-colorable numbers, so `Nat.sInf_mem` shows that (M₁, M₂) is indeed common list colorable with k = χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) colors. By `matroid_common_colorable_of_list_colorable`, any common list coloring specializes to an ordinary common coloring, meaning χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) also belongs to the set of valid ordinary color counts. Finally, since the common chromatic number χ(M₁, M₂) is the infimum of ordinary color counts, `Nat.sInf_le` concludes that χ(M₁, M₂) ≤ χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂).
steps.code: exact Nat.sInf_le (matroid_common_colorable_of_list_colorable M₁ M₂ _ (Nat.sInf_mem hne))

glossary.le_rfl: Every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself: a ≤ a.
glossary.matroid_common_list_colorable_of_ncard_l: For two loopless matroids on the same finite ground set, they are common list colorable using k colors whenever k is at least the cardinality of the ground set.
glossary.matroid_common_colorable_of_list_colorab: If a pair of matroids is common list colorable with k colors, it is also common colorable with k colors (by choosing identical lists of size k for each element).
glossary.Nat.sInf_mem: A nonempty set of natural numbers contains its infimum (minimum).
glossary.Nat.sInf_le: If m is an element of a set of natural numbers s, then the infimum of s is at most m.

declarations.name: matroid_sbo_common_list_chromatic_eq_of_le_two
declarations.informal: For two loopless strongly base-orderable matroids on a common finite ground set whose common chromatic number is at most 2, the common list chromatic number equals the common chromatic number: χ(M₁, M₂) ≤ 2 implies χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) = χ(M₁, M₂). This settles the open question χ_ℓ = χ for strongly base-orderable pairs in all cases with χ ≤ 2.
declarations.statement:
theorem matroid_sbo_common_list_chromatic_eq_of_le_two {α : Type*} (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α)
    [M₁.Finite] (h₁ : M₁.Loopless) (h₂ : M₂.Loopless) (hE : M₁.E = M₂.E)
    (hs₁ : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₁) (hs₂ : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₂)
    (h : matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ ≤ 2) :
    matroid_common_list_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ = matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂
declarations.source:
theorem matroid_sbo_common_list_chromatic_eq_of_le_two {α : Type*} (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α)
    [M₁.Finite] (h₁ : M₁.Loopless) (h₂ : M₂.Loopless) (hE : M₁.E = M₂.E)
    (hs₁ : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₁) (hs₂ : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₂)
    (h : matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ ≤ 2) :
    matroid_common_list_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ = matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ (matroid_common_chromatic_le_list_chromatic M₁ M₂ h₁ h₂ hE)
  have hne : {k | matroid_common_colorable M₁ M₂ k}.Nonempty :=
    ⟨_, matroid_common_colorable_of_list_colorable M₁ M₂ _
      (matroid_common_list_colorable_of_ncard_le M₁ M₂ h₁ h₂ hE _ le_rfl)⟩
  have hmem : matroid_common_colorable M₁ M₂ (matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂) :=
    Nat.sInf_mem hne
  have key : matroid_common_list_colorable M₁ M₂ (matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂) := by
    generalize matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ = χ at h hmem ⊢
    interval_cases χ
    · obtain ⟨c, hc, hind⟩ := hmem
      exact fun L _ => ⟨c, fun e he => absurd (hc e he) (Nat.not_lt_zero _), hind⟩
    · exact matroid_common_list_colorable_one_of_colorable_one M₁ M₂ hmem
    · exact matroid_sbo_common_list_colorable_two_of_common_colorable_two M₁ M₂ hE hs₁ hs₂ hmem
  exact Nat.sInf_le key
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.07318 (A note on the list chromatic number of two matroids), Corollary 2.3 ("in particular": χ = 2 implies χ_ℓ = 2), stated here with the chromatic numbers and including the cases χ = 0 and χ = 1; the paper's step through the 1976 common-chromatic-number theorem is not needed, since a common 2-coloring 2-colors each matroid.

explanation.summary: The inequality χ(M₁, M₂) ≤ χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) holds in general, so it suffices to show χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) ≤ χ(M₁, M₂). Because χ(M₁, M₂) ≤ 2, the common chromatic number χ must be 0, 1, or 2. Since the pair is common χ-colorable, a case split on χ shows that common χ-colorability implies common list χ-colorability in all three cases, using the strong base-orderability hypothesis when χ = 2. It follows that χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) ≤ χ(M₁, M₂), yielding equality.

steps.claim: It suffices to show that χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) ≤ χ(M₁, M₂).
steps.explanation: By antisymmetry of ≤ (`le_antisymm`), establishing equality reduces to two inequalities. The opposite inequality χ(M₁, M₂) ≤ χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) is known unconditionally for loopless finite matroids on a common ground set (`matroid_common_chromatic_le_list_chromatic`).
steps.code: refine le_antisymm ?_ (matroid_common_chromatic_le_list_chromatic M₁ M₂ h₁ h₂ hE)

steps.claim: The set of integers k for which M₁ and M₂ are common k-colorable is nonempty.
steps.explanation: Setting k = |M₁.E|, the pair is common list k-colorable by `matroid_common_list_colorable_of_ncard_le` using |M₁.E| ≤ |M₁.E| (`le_rfl`). Because any list-colorable pair is also colorable (`matroid_common_colorable_of_list_colorable`), |M₁.E| provides a witness that the set is nonempty.
steps.code:
have hne : {k | matroid_common_colorable M₁ M₂ k}.Nonempty :=
    ⟨_, matroid_common_colorable_of_list_colorable M₁ M₂ _
      (matroid_common_list_colorable_of_ncard_le M₁ M₂ h₁ h₂ hE _ le_rfl)⟩

steps.claim: The pair (M₁, M₂) is common χ(M₁, M₂)-colorable.
steps.explanation: By definition, the common chromatic number χ(M₁, M₂) is the infimum of the set of integers for which a common coloring exists. Because this set of natural numbers is nonempty, its infimum belongs to the set (`Nat.sInf_mem`).
steps.code:
have hmem : matroid_common_colorable M₁ M₂ (matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂) :=
    Nat.sInf_mem hne

steps.claim: The pair (M₁, M₂) is common list χ(M₁, M₂)-colorable.
steps.explanation:
Letting χ = χ(M₁, M₂), the hypothesis gives χ ≤ 2, so we analyze the three possible values χ ∈ {0, 1, 2}:
- If χ = 0, the coloring hypothesis asserts that every element e ∈ M₁.E has color c(e) < 0, which is impossible in ℕ (`Nat.not_lt_zero`), so the list-coloring condition holds vacuously.
- If χ = 1, common 1-colorability implies common list 1-colorability by `matroid_common_list_colorable_one_of_colorable_one`.
- If χ = 2, common 2-colorability implies common list 2-colorability for strongly base-orderable matroids by `matroid_sbo_common_list_colorable_two_of_common_colorable_two`.
steps.code:
have key : matroid_common_list_colorable M₁ M₂ (matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂) := by
    generalize matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ = χ at h hmem ⊢
    interval_cases χ
    · obtain ⟨c, hc, hind⟩ := hmem
      exact fun L _ => ⟨c, fun e he => absurd (hc e he) (Nat.not_lt_zero _), hind⟩
    · exact matroid_common_list_colorable_one_of_colorable_one M₁ M₂ hmem
    · exact matroid_sbo_common_list_colorable_two_of_common_colorable_two M₁ M₂ hE hs₁ hs₂ hmem

steps.claim: χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) ≤ χ(M₁, M₂), completing the proof.
steps.explanation: The common list chromatic number χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) is defined as the infimum of the set of integers k for which the pair is common list k-colorable. Since χ(M₁, M₂) belongs to this set, the infimum is at most χ(M₁, M₂) by `Nat.sInf_le`.
steps.code: exact Nat.sInf_le key

glossary.le_antisymm: if a ≤ b and b ≤ a in a partial order, then a = b
glossary.matroid_common_chromatic_le_list_chromat: for any loopless finite matroids M₁ and M₂ on a common ground set, χ(M₁, M₂) ≤ χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂)
glossary.matroid_common_colorable_of_list_colorab: if a pair of matroids is common list k-colorable, then it is common k-colorable
glossary.matroid_common_list_colorable_of_ncard_l: for loopless finite matroids M₁ and M₂ on a common ground set, if |M₁.E| ≤ k, then the pair is common list k-colorable
glossary.le_rfl: the inequality relation ≤ is reflexive: a ≤ a
glossary.Nat.sInf_mem: every nonempty set of natural numbers contains its infimum (minimum)
glossary.Nat.not_lt_zero: no natural number is strictly less than 0
glossary.matroid_common_list_colorable_one_of_col: if a pair of matroids is common 1-colorable, then it is common list 1-colorable
glossary.matroid_sbo_common_list_colorable_two_of: for two finite strongly base-orderable matroids on a common ground set, common 2-colorability implies common list 2-colorability
glossary.Nat.sInf_le: if a natural number m belongs to a set s ⊆ ℕ, then sInf s ≤ m

declarations.name: matrix_det_eq_permanent_of_char_two
declarations.informal: For every commutative ring R of characteristic 2 and any square matrix M over R indexed by a finite type n with decidable equality, the determinant of M equals the permanent of M.
declarations.statement: theorem matrix_det_eq_permanent_of_char_two {n R : Type*} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] [CommRing R] [CharP R 2] (M : Matrix n n R) : M.det = M.permanent
declarations.source:
/-- Over any commutative ring of characteristic 2, the determinant of any square matrix equals its permanent. -/
theorem matrix_det_eq_permanent_of_char_two {n R : Type*} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] [CommRing R] [CharP R 2] (M : Matrix n n R) : M.det = M.permanent := by
  rw [Matrix.det_apply', Matrix.permanent]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun σ _ => ?_)
  have hsign : (↑↑(Equiv.Perm.sign σ) : R) = 1 := by
    rcases Int.units_eq_one_or (Equiv.Perm.sign σ) with h | h <;> rw [h]
    · simp
    · simp [CharTwo.neg_eq]
  rw [hsign, one_mul]
declarations.citation: Valiant 1979, 'Completeness classes in algebra', STOC 1979, Sec. 3
declarations.reading: For any finite type $n$ with decidable equality, any commutative ring $R$ of characteristic 2, and any $n \times n$ matrix $M$ with entries in $R$, the determinant of $M$ is equal to the permanent of $M$.

explanation.summary: The determinant and the permanent of a square matrix are both defined as sums over all permutations of the product of the entries chosen by the permutation, differing only by the sign factor sgn(σ) in the determinant. In any commutative ring of characteristic 2, -1 = 1, so the sign of every permutation evaluates to 1. Consequently, the summands of the determinant and the permanent coincide term by term, and the two values are equal.

steps.claim: The identity det M = permanent M reduces to showing that the determinant term equals the permanent term for each permutation σ.
steps.explanation: By Matrix.det_apply' and the definition Matrix.permanent, both the determinant and the permanent are sums indexed by the permutations σ of n. Applying Finset.sum_congr, the two sums are equal if their terms agree for every permutation σ, that is, if sgn(σ) ∏ᵢ M_{σ(i), i} = ∏ᵢ M_{σ(i), i}.
steps.code:
rw [Matrix.det_apply', Matrix.permanent]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun σ _ => ?_)

steps.claim: In a ring of characteristic 2, the sign of any permutation σ evaluates to 1.
steps.explanation: The sign of a permutation σ belongs to ℤˣ, so it is either 1 or -1 by Int.units_eq_one_or. If sgn(σ) = 1, its canonical image in R is 1. If sgn(σ) = -1, its image in R is -1, which equals 1 by CharTwo.neg_eq because R has characteristic 2.
steps.code:
have hsign : (↑↑(Equiv.Perm.sign σ) : R) = 1 := by
    rcases Int.units_eq_one_or (Equiv.Perm.sign σ) with h | h <;> rw [h]
    · simp
    · simp [CharTwo.neg_eq]

steps.claim: The summands of the determinant and permanent agree for every permutation σ, concluding the proof.
steps.explanation: Substituting the fact that the sign factor is 1 (hsign), the summand simplifies via 1 * a = a (one_mul) to the permanent summand ∏ᵢ M_{σ(i), i}.
steps.code: rw [hsign, one_mul]

glossary.Matrix.det_apply': The determinant of a square matrix M equals the Leibniz sum over all permutations σ of sgn(σ) multiplied by the product of the diagonal entries M_{σ(i), i}.
glossary.Matrix.permanent: The permanent of a square matrix M is defined as the sum over all permutations σ of the product of the diagonal entries M_{σ(i), i}.
glossary.Finset.sum_congr: Two sums over the same finite set are equal if their corresponding terms are equal for all elements of the set.
glossary.Int.units_eq_one_or: The only invertible elements (units) in the integers ℤ are 1 and -1.
glossary.CharTwo.neg_eq: In any ring of characteristic 2, the additive inverse of any element equals the element itself (-x = x).
glossary.one_mul: Multiplying any element on the left by 1 leaves it unchanged (1 * a = a).

declarations.name: mv_polynomial_eq_zero_of_eval_eq_zero_on_finset
declarations.informal: Let R be an integral domain and p be a multivariate polynomial in n variables over R. If S is a finite subset of R with cardinality strictly greater than the total degree of p, and p evaluates to zero at every point of the product S^n, then p is the zero polynomial.
declarations.statement: theorem mv_polynomial_eq_zero_of_eval_eq_zero_on_finset {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] (p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (S : Finset R) (hcard : p.totalDegree < S.card) (h_eval : ∀ f : Fin n → R, (∀ i, f i ∈ S) → MvPolynomial.eval f p = 0) : p = 0
declarations.source:
/-- A multivariate polynomial over an integral domain vanishing on a grid S^n with |S| > deg(p) is zero. -/
theorem mv_polynomial_eq_zero_of_eval_eq_zero_on_finset {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] (p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (S : Finset R) (hcard : p.totalDegree < S.card) (h_eval : ∀ f : Fin n → R, (∀ i, f i ∈ S) → MvPolynomial.eval f p = 0) : p = 0 := by
  classical
  by_contra hp
  have h_sz := MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_totalDegree hp S
  have h_eq : {f ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun (_ : Fin n) ↦ S) | MvPolynomial.eval f p = 0} = Fintype.piFinset (fun (_ : Fin n) ↦ S) := by
    apply Finset.filter_true_of_mem
    intro f hf
    apply h_eval
    intro i
    rw [Fintype.mem_piFinset] at hf
    exact hf i
  rw [h_eq] at h_sz
  rw [Fintype.card_piFinset] at h_sz
  simp only [Finset.prod_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at h_sz
  push_cast at h_sz
  have hScard_pos : 0 < S.card := by omega
  have hpow_pos : (0 : ℚ≥0) < (S.card : ℚ≥0) ^ n := by positivity
  rw [div_self (ne_of_gt hpow_pos)] at h_sz
  have hS_pos : (0 : ℚ≥0) < (S.card : ℚ≥0) := by positivity
  have h_lt : (p.totalDegree : ℚ≥0) / (S.card : ℚ≥0) < 1 := by
    rw [div_lt_one hS_pos]
    exact Nat.cast_lt.mpr hcard
  exact not_le_of_gt h_lt h_sz
declarations.reading: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $R$ be a commutative ring that is an integral domain. Let $p$ be a multivariate polynomial with variables indexed by `Fin n` and coefficients in $R$ (`MvPolynomial (Fin n) R`), and let $S$ be a finite subset of $R$ (`Finset R`). If the total degree of $p$ is strictly less than the cardinality of $S$ (`p.totalDegree < S.card`), and if for every function $f : \text{Fin } n \to R$ such that $f(i) \in S$ for all $i : \text{Fin } n$, the evaluation of $p$ at $f$ is zero (`MvPolynomial.eval f p = 0`), then $p = 0$.

explanation.summary: The proof proceeds by contradiction: assume p ≠ 0. The Schwartz-Zippel lemma states that the fraction of points in the grid S^n on which p vanishes is at most deg(p) / |S|. Since p evaluates to zero on all of S^n by assumption, this fraction is |S|^n / |S|^n = 1. However, the hypothesis deg(p) < |S| implies deg(p) / |S| < 1, yielding the contradiction 1 ≤ deg(p) / |S| < 1.

steps.claim: Assume for contradiction that p ≠ 0.
steps.explanation: We enable classical logic (allowing decidability of propositions) and begin an indirect proof by assuming p ≠ 0.
steps.code:
classical
  by_contra hp

steps.claim: The proportion of zeros of p in the grid S^n is bounded above by deg(p) / |S|.
steps.explanation: Applying the Schwartz-Zippel lemma (MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_totalDegree) to the nonzero polynomial p and finite set S bounds the fraction of roots in S^n by deg(p) / |S| in ℚ≥0.
steps.code: have h_sz := MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_totalDegree hp S

steps.claim: The zero set of p on S^n is the entire grid S^n.
steps.explanation: By assumption h_eval, p evaluates to 0 on every point f whose coordinates all belong to S. Applying Finset.filter_true_of_mem shows that filtering the Cartesian product S^n by the vanishing condition p(f) = 0 leaves the entire set S^n.
steps.code:
have h_eq : {f ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun (_ : Fin n) ↦ S) | MvPolynomial.eval f p = 0} = Fintype.piFinset (fun (_ : Fin n) ↦ S) := by
    apply Finset.filter_true_of_mem
    intro f hf
    apply h_eval
    intro i
    rw [Fintype.mem_piFinset] at hf
    exact hf i

steps.claim: The Schwartz-Zippel inequality reduces to |S|^n / |S|^n ≤ deg(p) / |S|.
steps.explanation: Substituting the identity of the root set into the Schwartz-Zippel inequality gives |S^n| / |S|^n ≤ deg(p) / |S|. The cardinality of the product is |S|^n by Fintype.card_piFinset and Finset.prod_const. Pushing the natural-number casts into ℚ≥0 yields |S|^n / |S|^n ≤ deg(p) / |S|.
steps.code:
rw [h_eq] at h_sz
  rw [Fintype.card_piFinset] at h_sz
  simp only [Finset.prod_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at h_sz
  push_cast at h_sz

steps.claim: The left-hand side of the Schwartz-Zippel inequality equals 1, yielding 1 ≤ deg(p) / |S|.
steps.explanation: Since |S| > deg(p) ≥ 0, S is non-empty, so |S|^n is strictly positive. Dividing |S|^n by itself gives 1 via div_self, simplifying the bound to 1 ≤ deg(p) / |S|.
steps.code:
have hScard_pos : 0 < S.card := by omega
  have hpow_pos : (0 : ℚ≥0) < (S.card : ℚ≥0) ^ n := by positivity
  rw [div_self (ne_of_gt hpow_pos)] at h_sz

steps.claim: The ratio deg(p) / |S| is strictly less than 1.
steps.explanation: Because |S| > 0, the quotient deg(p) / |S| is strictly less than 1 if and only if deg(p) < |S| (by div_lt_one). This holds by casting the hypothesis hcard from ℕ to ℚ≥0.
steps.code:
have hS_pos : (0 : ℚ≥0) < (S.card : ℚ≥0) := by positivity
  have h_lt : (p.totalDegree : ℚ≥0) / (S.card : ℚ≥0) < 1 := by
    rw [div_lt_one hS_pos]
    exact Nat.cast_lt.mpr hcard

steps.claim: Contradiction, concluding p = 0.
steps.explanation: The strict inequality deg(p) / |S| < 1 contradicts 1 ≤ deg(p) / |S| via not_le_of_gt, concluding the proof by contradiction.
steps.code: exact not_le_of_gt h_lt h_sz

glossary.MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_totalDegree: For a nonzero multivariate polynomial p over an integral domain and a finite set S, the fraction of points in S^n where p evaluates to 0 is at most deg(p) / |S| (in ℚ≥0).
glossary.Finset.filter_true_of_mem: Filtering a finite set by a predicate that holds for all of its elements returns the entire set.
glossary.Fintype.mem_piFinset: A function belongs to the Cartesian product ∏_i S_i if and only if each coordinate value f(i) belongs to S_i.
glossary.Fintype.card_piFinset: The cardinality of a Cartesian product of finite sets is the product of the cardinalities of the factors.
glossary.Finset.prod_const: The product of a constant element over a finite set equals that element raised to the cardinality of the set.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal finset of a finite type equals the cardinality of the type.
glossary.Fintype.card_fin: The cardinality of Fin n is n.
glossary.div_self: Any nonzero element divided by itself equals 1.
glossary.ne_of_gt: If b < a in a preorder, then a ≠ b.
glossary.div_lt_one: For a strictly positive denominator b, a / b < 1 if and only if a < b.
glossary.Nat.cast_lt.mpr: If a < b for natural numbers, then their casts into a linearly ordered semiring satisfy ↑a < ↑b.
glossary.not_le_of_gt: If a < b in a preorder, then b ≤ a does not hold.

caveats: The Schwartz-Zippel inequality and subsequent comparisons are formally carried out in the non-negative rationals ℚ≥0. This necessitates non-trivial type casts (push_cast) and non-zeroness proofs (via positivity and omega) that are standard or implicit in a pen-and-paper presentation.

declarations.name: condorcet_paradox
declarations.informal: The Condorcet paradox: there exists a preference profile of 3 voters over 3 alternatives, where each voter has a strict linear order of preferences, such that no alternative is a Condorcet winner.
declarations.statement:
theorem condorcet_paradox :
    ∃ (P : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → Fin 3 → Prop) (_ : ∀ v, DecidableRel (P v)),
      (∀ v, IsStrictTotalOrder (Fin 3) (P v)) ∧ ∀ x : Fin 3, ¬ condorcet_winner P x
declarations.source:
def condorcet_paradox_score : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℕ
  | 0, 0 => 2
  | 0, 1 => 1
  | 0, 2 => 0
  | 1, 1 => 2
  | 1, 2 => 1
  | 1, 0 => 0
  | 2, 2 => 2
  | 2, 0 => 1
  | 2, 1 => 0

def condorcet_paradox_pref (v : Fin 3) (x y : Fin 3) : Prop :=
  condorcet_paradox_score v x > condorcet_paradox_score v y

instance condorcet_paradox_decidable_rel (v : Fin 3) :
    DecidableRel (condorcet_paradox_pref v) := by
  intro x y
  unfold condorcet_paradox_pref
  infer_instance

theorem condorcet_paradox_strict_order (v : Fin 3) :
    IsStrictTotalOrder (Fin 3) (condorcet_paradox_pref v) where
  trichotomous := by
    revert v
    decide
  irrefl := by
    revert v
    decide
  trans := by
    revert v
    decide

theorem condorcet_paradox_no_winner (x : Fin 3) :
    ¬ condorcet_winner condorcet_paradox_pref x := by
  intro h
  unfold condorcet_winner at h
  revert x h
  decide

/-- The Condorcet paradox: there exists an election with 3 voters and 3 candidates with strict linear preferences admitting no Condorcet winner. -/
theorem condorcet_paradox :
    ∃ (P : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → Fin 3 → Prop) (_ : ∀ v, DecidableRel (P v)),
      (∀ v, IsStrictTotalOrder (Fin 3) (P v)) ∧ ∀ x : Fin 3, ¬ condorcet_winner P x := by
  refine ⟨condorcet_paradox_pref, condorcet_paradox_decidable_rel,
          condorcet_paradox_strict_order, condorcet_paradox_no_winner⟩
declarations.citation: Condorcet 1785, Essai sur l'application de l'analyse à la probabilité des décisions rendues à la pluralité des voix
declarations.reading:
There exists a preference profile $P : \text{Fin } 3 \to \text{Fin } 3 \to \text{Fin } 3 \to \text{Prop}$ (representing binary preferences of 3 voters over 3 alternatives) with decidable relations for each voter, such that:
1. For every voter $v \in \text{Fin } 3$, $P(v)$ is a strict total order on $\text{Fin } 3$.
2. For every alternative $x \in \text{Fin } 3$, $x$ is not a Condorcet winner under $P$.

explanation.summary: The Condorcet paradox is demonstrated by constructing an explicit cyclic preference profile for 3 voters and 3 alternatives, where voter 0 prefers 0 > 1 > 2, voter 1 prefers 1 > 2 > 0, and voter 2 prefers 2 > 0 > 1. Each voter's preference is a strict total order induced by scoring, verified by exhaustive computation on the finite domain Fin 3. Pairwise majority votes form a cycle (0 beats 1, 1 beats 2, 2 beats 0), so no alternative defeats all others, meaning there is no Condorcet winner.

steps.claim: For each voter v, the preference relation between any two alternatives is decidable.
steps.explanation: By unfolding the definition of the preference relation, deciding whether voter v prefers x to y reduces to checking whether the score of x is strictly greater than the score of y. Since the scores are natural numbers, this comparison is decidable by typeclass resolution.
steps.code:
intro x y
  unfold condorcet_paradox_pref
  infer_instance

steps.claim: Each voter's preference relation is trichotomous.
steps.explanation: Reverting voter v yields a universally quantified statement over the finite domain Fin 3: for any voter and any two alternatives a and b, if a is not preferred to b and b is not preferred to a, then a = b. Since the domain is finite and the relation is decidable, Lean's decision procedure checks all cases by computation.
steps.code:
revert v
    decide

steps.claim: Each voter's preference relation is irreflexive.
steps.explanation: Reverting voter v leaves the claim that no voter prefers an alternative to itself. Since there are only 3 voters and 3 alternatives, the decision procedure verifies this by checking all 9 cases.
steps.code:
revert v
    decide

steps.claim: Each voter's preference relation is transitive.
steps.explanation: Reverting voter v yields the transitivity claim for all triples of alternatives. The decision procedure verifies all 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81 combinations by exhaustive computation.
steps.code:
revert v
    decide

steps.claim: No alternative is a Condorcet winner under this preference profile.
steps.explanation: Assume for contradiction that some alternative x is a Condorcet winner. Unfolding the definition, this means x wins the majority vote against every other alternative y. Reverting x and this hypothesis, the decision procedure exhaustively checks each candidate and determines that each candidate loses pairwise to another candidate (0 loses to 2, 1 loses to 0, and 2 loses to 1), deriving a contradiction.
steps.code:
intro h
  unfold condorcet_winner at h
  revert x h
  decide

steps.claim: There exists a preference profile of 3 voters over 3 alternatives with strict total orders having no Condorcet winner.
steps.explanation: The existential claim is witnessed by the cyclic preference relation condorcet_paradox_pref, together with its decidability instance condorcet_paradox_decidable_rel, the strict total order proof condorcet_paradox_strict_order, and the theorem condorcet_paradox_no_winner showing that no candidate wins.
steps.code:
refine ⟨condorcet_paradox_pref, condorcet_paradox_decidable_rel,
          condorcet_paradox_strict_order, condorcet_paradox_no_winner⟩

glossary.condorcet_paradox_pref: The preference relation for voter v, where v prefers x to y iff v assigns a higher score to x than to y.
glossary.condorcet_paradox_decidable_rel: Proof that condorcet_paradox_pref v is decidable for all alternatives x and y.
glossary.condorcet_paradox_strict_order: Proof that condorcet_paradox_pref v is a strict total order for every voter v.
glossary.condorcet_paradox_no_winner: Proof that no alternative x is a Condorcet winner under condorcet_paradox_pref.

declarations.name: droop_monroe_satisfies_droop_jr
declarations.informal: Every committee W of size k selected by the Droop Monroe rule satisfies Droop-JR: every voter group S of size strictly greater than n/(k+1) that jointly approves some candidate contains a voter who approves at least one candidate in W.
declarations.statement:
theorem droop_monroe_satisfies_droop_jr (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Finset (Fin m)) (k : ℕ)
    (W : Finset (Fin m)) (hW : is_droop_monroe_committee A k W) :
    is_droop_jr A k W
declarations.source:
/-- Every winning committee under the Droop Monroe rule satisfies Droop-JR for all n and k. -/
theorem droop_monroe_satisfies_droop_jr (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Finset (Fin m)) (k : ℕ)
    (W : Finset (Fin m)) (hW : is_droop_monroe_committee A k W) :
    is_droop_jr A k W := by
  intro S hS ⟨c, hc⟩
  by_contra hno
  push Not at hno
  obtain ⟨π, hv, hopt⟩ := hW
  have hSne : S.Nonempty := by
    rw [← Finset.card_pos]
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos S.card with h | h
    · rw [h] at hS; simp at hS
    · exact h
  have hcW : c ∉ W := by
    intro hcW
    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hSne
    exact hno i hi c hcW (hc i hi)
  have hun : ∀ i ∈ S, ¬ ∃ d, π i = some d ∧ d ∈ A i := by
    intro i hi ⟨d, hd, hdA⟩
    have hdW : d ∈ W := hv.2.1 i d hd
    exact hno i hi d hdW hdA
  have hS_not_all_none : ∃ i ∈ S, π i ≠ none := by
    by_contra hall
    push Not at hall
    have hsub : S ⊆ Finset.univ.filter fun i => π i = none := by
      intro i hi
      simp [hall i hi]
    have hle := Finset.card_le_card hsub
    rw [hv.2.2.2] at hle
    have : (k + 1) * S.card ≤ (k + 1) * (n / (k + 1)) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left (k + 1) hle
    have : (k + 1) * (n / (k + 1)) ≤ n := Nat.mul_div_le n (k + 1)
    omega
  obtain ⟨i₀, hi₀, hni₀⟩ := hS_not_all_none
  obtain ⟨c₀, hc₀⟩ := Option.ne_none_iff_exists'.1 hni₀
  have hc₀W : c₀ ∈ W := hv.2.1 i₀ c₀ hc₀
  obtain ⟨π', hv', hsc⟩ := droop_monroe_exchange A k W π hv c₀ c hc₀W hcW S hc hun
  have hopt_le := hopt _ π' hv'
  set R := Finset.univ.filter fun i => π i = some c₀ with hR
  have hR_le_ceil : R.card ≤ (n + k) / (k + 1) := (hv.2.2.1 c₀ hc₀W).2
  have hfloor_lt : n / (k + 1) < S.card := by
    rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul (Nat.succ_pos k), mul_comm]
    exact hS
  have hceil_le_S : (n + k) / (k + 1) ≤ S.card := by
    have h1 : n + k ≤ n + (k + 1) := by omega
    have h2 : (n + k) / (k + 1) ≤ (n + (k + 1)) / (k + 1) := Nat.div_le_div_right h1
    have h3 : (n + (k + 1)) / (k + 1) = n / (k + 1) + 1 := Nat.add_div_right n (Nat.succ_pos k)
    rw [h3] at h2
    omega
  have hR_le_S : R.card ≤ S.card := hR_le_ceil.trans hceil_le_S
  have hmin : min R.card S.card = R.card := min_eq_left hR_le_S
  rw [hmin] at hsc
  have hsplit : R.card = (R.filter fun i => i ∉ S).card + (R.filter fun i => i ∈ S).card := by
    have := (Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not (s := R) (p := fun i => i ∈ S)).symm
    rw [add_comm] at this
    exact this
  have hin : i₀ ∈ R.filter fun i => i ∈ S := by
    simp [hR, hc₀, hi₀]
  have hpos : 0 < (R.filter fun i => i ∈ S).card := Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨i₀, hin⟩
  omega
declarations.reading: For any number of voters n and candidates m, any approval voting profile A (assigning to each voter i : Fin n a finite set of approved candidates A(i) ⊆ Fin m), any committee size k, and any candidate subset W ⊆ Fin m: if W is a Droop-Monroe committee of size k for profile A, then W satisfies Droop Justified Representation (Droop JR) for A and k.

explanation.summary: The proof proceeds by contradiction: suppose a voter group S of size strictly greater than the Droop quota n/(k+1) jointly approves a candidate c, yet no voter in S approves any candidate in the optimal Droop-Monroe committee W. Since the number of unassigned voters under any valid Droop-Monroe assignment π is at most ⌊n/(k+1)⌋ < |S|, some voter i₀ ∈ S must be assigned to a committee member c₀ ∈ W. Exchanging c₀ for c yields a new valid assignment π' whose score improvement is bounded below by the exchange lemma, and because the cluster size of c₀ is at most the quota upper bound ⌊(n+k)/(k+1)⌋ ≤ |S|, this exchange strictly increases the Monroe score, contradicting the optimality of W.

steps.claim: Assume for contradiction that Droop-JR is violated for a Droop-Monroe committee W.
steps.explanation: We introduce a voter group S with (k + 1) * |S| > n jointly approving a candidate c, and suppose for contradiction that no voter in S approves any candidate in W. We unpack the hypothesis that W is a Droop-Monroe committee to obtain a valid assignment π whose Monroe score is maximal among all valid committees and assignments.
steps.code:
intro S hS ⟨c, hc⟩
  by_contra hno
  push Not at hno
  obtain ⟨π, hv, hopt⟩ := hW

steps.claim: The group S is nonempty.
steps.explanation: Since (k + 1) * |S| > n ≥ 0, |S| cannot be zero. A finite set with positive cardinality is nonempty.
steps.code:
have hSne : S.Nonempty := by
    rw [← Finset.card_pos]
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos S.card with h | h
    · rw [h] at hS; simp at hS
    · exact h

steps.claim: The jointly approved candidate c is not in W.
steps.explanation: If c were in W, then every voter in S (and S is nonempty) would approve a candidate in W, contradicting the assumption that Droop-JR is violated.
steps.code:
have hcW : c ∉ W := by
    intro hcW
    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hSne
    exact hno i hi c hcW (hc i hi)

steps.claim: No voter in S is assigned to an approved candidate under π.
steps.explanation: Every candidate assigned under a valid assignment belongs to W. Since voters in S approve no candidate in W, they cannot approve their assigned candidates.
steps.code:
have hun : ∀ i ∈ S, ¬ ∃ d, π i = some d ∧ d ∈ A i := by
    intro i hi ⟨d, hd, hdA⟩
    have hdW : d ∈ W := hv.2.1 i d hd
    exact hno i hi d hdW hdA

steps.claim: At least one voter in S is assigned to a candidate under π.
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that all voters in S were unassigned (π(i) = none). Then S would be a subset of the unassigned voters. By definition of a valid Droop-Monroe assignment, the number of unassigned voters is exactly ⌊n / (k + 1)⌋, which implies (k + 1) * |S| ≤ (k + 1) * ⌊n / (k + 1)⌋ ≤ n, contradicting the hypothesis that (k + 1) * |S| > n.
steps.code:
have hS_not_all_none : ∃ i ∈ S, π i ≠ none := by
    by_contra hall
    push Not at hall
    have hsub : S ⊆ Finset.univ.filter fun i => π i = none := by
      intro i hi
      simp [hall i hi]
    have hle := Finset.card_le_card hsub
    rw [hv.2.2.2] at hle
    have : (k + 1) * S.card ≤ (k + 1) * (n / (k + 1)) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left (k + 1) hle
    have : (k + 1) * (n / (k + 1)) ≤ n := Nat.mul_div_le n (k + 1)
    omega

steps.claim: There exist a voter i₀ ∈ S and a committee candidate c₀ ∈ W such that π(i₀) = c₀.
steps.explanation: Since not all voters in S are unassigned, some i₀ ∈ S has π(i₀) ≠ none, so π(i₀) = some c₀. By the validity of assignment π, any assigned candidate c₀ must be in W.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨i₀, hi₀, hni₀⟩ := hS_not_all_none
  obtain ⟨c₀, hc₀⟩ := Option.ne_none_iff_exists'.1 hni₀
  have hc₀W : c₀ ∈ W := hv.2.1 i₀ c₀ hc₀

steps.claim: Exchanging c₀ for c produces a valid assignment π' on (W \ {c₀}) ∪ {c} satisfying the exchange score inequality.
steps.explanation: Applying droop_monroe_exchange with c₀ ∈ W, c ∉ W, and voter set S yields a valid assignment π' for the updated committee, satisfying score(π) + min(|R|, |S|) ≤ score(π') + |R \ S|, where R is the set of voters assigned to c₀ under π.
steps.code: obtain ⟨π', hv', hsc⟩ := droop_monroe_exchange A k W π hv c₀ c hc₀W hcW S hc hun

steps.claim: The score of the new assignment cannot exceed that of π.
steps.explanation: By the optimality of W and π under the Droop-Monroe rule, any valid assignment π' has score(π') ≤ score(π).
steps.code: have hopt_le := hopt _ π' hv'

steps.claim: Let R = {i | π(i) = c₀}; then |R| ≤ ⌊(n + k) / (k + 1)⌋ and ⌊n / (k + 1)⌋ < |S|.
steps.explanation: Validity of π imposes the upper quota constraint |R| ≤ ⌊(n + k) / (k + 1)⌋ on candidate c₀ ∈ W. Furthermore, the condition n < (k + 1) * |S| is equivalent to ⌊n / (k + 1)⌋ < |S| by integer division properties.
steps.code:
set R := Finset.univ.filter fun i => π i = some c₀ with hR
  have hR_le_ceil : R.card ≤ (n + k) / (k + 1) := (hv.2.2.1 c₀ hc₀W).2
  have hfloor_lt : n / (k + 1) < S.card := by
    rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul (Nat.succ_pos k), mul_comm]
    exact hS

steps.claim: The upper quota bound satisfies ⌊(n + k) / (k + 1)⌋ ≤ |S|.
steps.explanation: Since n + k ≤ n + k + 1, we have ⌊(n + k) / (k + 1)⌋ ≤ ⌊(n + k + 1) / (k + 1)⌋ = ⌊n / (k + 1)⌋ + 1. Because ⌊n / (k + 1)⌋ < |S|, the strict inequality implies ⌊n / (k + 1)⌋ + 1 ≤ |S|.
steps.code:
have hceil_le_S : (n + k) / (k + 1) ≤ S.card := by
    have h1 : n + k ≤ n + (k + 1) := by omega
    have h2 : (n + k) / (k + 1) ≤ (n + (k + 1)) / (k + 1) := Nat.div_le_div_right h1
    have h3 : (n + (k + 1)) / (k + 1) = n / (k + 1) + 1 := Nat.add_div_right n (Nat.succ_pos k)
    rw [h3] at h2
    omega

steps.claim: |R| ≤ |S|, so min(|R|, |S|) = |R| in the exchange inequality.
steps.explanation: Chaining |R| ≤ ⌊(n + k) / (k + 1)⌋ and ⌊(n + k) / (k + 1)⌋ ≤ |S| gives |R| ≤ |S|, which simplifies min(|R|, |S|) to |R| in the exchange score inequality.
steps.code:
have hR_le_S : R.card ≤ S.card := hR_le_ceil.trans hceil_le_S
  have hmin : min R.card S.card = R.card := min_eq_left hR_le_S
  rw [hmin] at hsc

steps.claim: The size of R partitions as |R| = |R \ S| + |R ∩ S|.
steps.explanation: Splitting R into the voters outside S and those inside S, the size of R is the sum of the cardinalities of these disjoint subsets.
steps.code:
have hsplit : R.card = (R.filter fun i => i ∉ S).card + (R.filter fun i => i ∈ S).card := by
    have := (Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not (s := R) (p := fun i => i ∈ S)).symm
    rw [add_comm] at this
    exact this

steps.claim: The intersection R ∩ S contains i₀, so |R ∩ S| > 0.
steps.explanation: Because i₀ ∈ S and π(i₀) = c₀ (so i₀ ∈ R), voter i₀ belongs to R ∩ S, making the set nonempty and its cardinality strictly positive.
steps.code:
have hin : i₀ ∈ R.filter fun i => i ∈ S := by
    simp [hR, hc₀, hi₀]
  have hpos : 0 < (R.filter fun i => i ∈ S).card := Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨i₀, hin⟩

steps.claim: The score bounds yield a contradiction, completing the proof.
steps.explanation: Combining score(π') ≤ score(π) with score(π) + |R \ S| + |R ∩ S| ≤ score(π') + |R \ S| implies |R ∩ S| ≤ 0, contradicting |R ∩ S| > 0.
steps.code: omega

glossary.Finset.card_pos: A finite set has strictly positive cardinality if and only if it is nonempty.
glossary.Nat.eq_zero_or_pos: Every natural number is either equal to zero or strictly positive.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card: A subset of a finite set has cardinality at most that of the superset.
glossary.Nat.mul_le_mul_left: Multiplying both sides of an inequality by a natural number preserves the inequality.
glossary.Nat.mul_div_le: For natural numbers m and n, the product n * ⌊m / n⌋ is at most m.
glossary.Option.ne_none_iff_exists': An optional value is not none if and only if it is some x for some element x.
glossary.droop_monroe_exchange: Given an optimal Droop-Monroe committee and assignment, swapping a member c₀ with an external candidate c approved by S yields a valid assignment π' whose score satisfies score(π) + min(|R|, |S|) ≤ score(π') + |R \ S|, where R is the set of voters assigned to c₀.
glossary.Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul: For positive k, ⌊x / k⌋ < y is equivalent to x < y * k.
glossary.Nat.succ_pos: The successor of any natural number is strictly positive (0 < n + 1).
glossary.mul_comm: Multiplication of natural numbers is commutative.
glossary.Nat.div_le_div_right: Dividing both sides of an inequality by a common divisor preserves the inequality in integer division.
glossary.Nat.add_div_right: For positive z, integer division satisfies (x + z) / z = x / z + 1.
glossary.min_eq_left: If a ≤ b, then min a b = a.
glossary.Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not: The cardinality of a finite set equals the sum of the cardinalities of the elements satisfying a predicate and those satisfying its negation.
glossary.add_comm: Addition of natural numbers is commutative.

caveats: The upper quota constraint on each candidate's assigned voters is written as $(n + k) / (k + 1)$ in Lean natural number division, representing the ceiling $\lceil n / (k + 1) \rceil$.

declarations.name: matrix_permanent_from_blocks_zero_one_two
declarations.informal: For any commutative semiring R and any square matrices A over m and D over n, the permanent of the block matrix with A in the top-left, 0 in the top-right, C in the bottom-left, and D in the bottom-right equals the permanent of A times the permanent of D.
declarations.statement: theorem matrix_permanent_from_blocks_zero_one_two {m n R : Type*} [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [CommSemiring R] (A : Matrix m m R) (C : Matrix n m R) (D : Matrix n n R) : (Matrix.fromBlocks A 0 C D).permanent = A.permanent * D.permanent
declarations.source:
theorem matrix_permanent_from_blocks_zero_one_two_zero_two_one
    {m n R : Type*} [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype m]
    [Fintype n] [CommSemiring R] (A : Matrix m m R) (B : Matrix m n R) (D : Matrix n n R) :
    (Matrix.fromBlocks A B 0 D).permanent = A.permanent * D.permanent := by
  classical
  simp_rw [Matrix.permanent]
  convert!
    Eq.symm <|
      Finset.sum_subset (M := R) (Finset.subset_univ ((Equiv.Perm.sumCongrHom m n).range : Set (Equiv.Perm (m ⊕ n))).toFinset) ?_
  · simp_rw [Finset.sum_mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_product', Finset.univ_product_univ]
    refine Finset.sum_nbij (fun σ ↦ σ.fst.sumCongr σ.snd) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · intro σ₁₂ _
      rw [Set.mem_toFinset]
      exact ⟨σ₁₂, rfl⟩
    · intro σ₁ _ σ₂ _
      dsimp only
      intro h
      have h2 : ∀ x, Equiv.Perm.sumCongr σ₁.fst σ₁.snd x = Equiv.Perm.sumCongr σ₂.fst σ₂.snd x :=
        DFunLike.congr_fun h
      simp only [Sum.map_inr, Sum.map_inl, Equiv.Perm.sumCongr_apply, Sum.forall, Sum.inl.injEq,
        Sum.inr.injEq] at h2
      ext x
      · exact h2.left x
      · exact h2.right x
    · intro σ hσ
      rw [Finset.mem_coe, Set.mem_toFinset] at hσ
      obtain ⟨σ₁₂, hσ₁₂⟩ := hσ
      use σ₁₂
      rw [← hσ₁₂]
      simp
    · simp only [forall_prop_of_true, Prod.forall, Finset.mem_univ]
      intro σ₁ σ₂
      rw [Fintype.prod_sum_type]
      simp_rw [Equiv.sumCongr_apply, Sum.map_inr, Sum.map_inl, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₁,
        Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₂]
  · rintro σ - hσn
    have h1 : ¬∀ x, ∃ y, Sum.inl y = σ (Sum.inl x) := by
      rw [Set.mem_toFinset] at hσn
      simpa only [Set.MapsTo, Set.mem_range, forall_exists_index, forall_apply_eq_imp_iff] using
        mt Equiv.Perm.mem_sumCongrHom_range_of_perm_mapsTo_inl hσn
    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := not_forall.mp h1
    rcases hx : σ (Sum.inl a) with a2 | b
    · have hn := (not_exists.mp ha) a2
      exact absurd hx.symm hn
    · rw [Finset.prod_eq_zero (Finset.mem_univ (Sum.inl a))]
      rw [hx, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₁, Matrix.zero_apply]

/-- The permanent of a block lower-triangular matrix is the product of the permanents of the diagonal blocks. -/
theorem matrix_permanent_from_blocks_zero_one_two {m n R : Type*} [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [CommSemiring R] (A : Matrix m m R) (C : Matrix n m R) (D : Matrix n n R) : (Matrix.fromBlocks A 0 C D).permanent = A.permanent * D.permanent := by
  rw [← Matrix.permanent_transpose, Matrix.fromBlocks_transpose, Matrix.transpose_zero,
    matrix_permanent_from_blocks_zero_one_two_zero_two_one, Matrix.permanent_transpose,
    Matrix.permanent_transpose]
declarations.reading: For all types $m$, $n$, and $R$ such that $m$ and $n$ have decidable equality and are finite types, and $R$ is a commutative semiring, and for any matrices $A : \mathrm{Matrix}\ m\ m\ R$, $C : \mathrm{Matrix}\ n\ m\ R$, and $D : \mathrm{Matrix}\ n\ n\ R$, the permanent of the lower block-triangular matrix $\begin{pmatrix} A & 0 \\ C & D \end{pmatrix}$ (formed by `Matrix.fromBlocks A 0 C D` with row and column index type $m \oplus n$) is equal to the product of the permanent of $A$ and the permanent of $D$.

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by first establishing that the permanent of a block upper-triangular matrix with zero in the bottom-left position equals the product of the permanents of its diagonal blocks, and then deducing the lower-triangular case by transposition. For the upper-triangular case, the sum over all permutations of m ⊕ n reduces to the subgroup of block-preserving permutations, because any permutation mapping an element of the first block into the second block encounters a zero entry in the bottom-left block. Evaluating the product on these block-preserving permutations splits each term into independent products over the two diagonal blocks.

steps.claim: The permanent of the block upper-triangular matrix equals the sum of entry products over the subgroup of permutations preserving the block structure.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of the permanent (`Matrix.permanent`), the permanent of the block matrix is the sum over all permutations of m ⊕ n. By `Finset.sum_subset`, since the subgroup of block-preserving permutations (the image of `Equiv.Perm.sumCongrHom`) is contained in all permutations, it suffices to prove two subgoals: first, that the sum over this subgroup equals the product of permanents, and second, that all permutations outside the subgroup have product zero.
steps.code:
classical
  simp_rw [Matrix.permanent]
  convert!
    Eq.symm <|
      Finset.sum_subset (M := R) (Finset.subset_univ ((Equiv.Perm.sumCongrHom m n).range : Set (Equiv.Perm (m ⊕ n))).toFinset) ?_

steps.claim: The product of the permanents of A and D is rewritten as a sum over pairs of permutations, mapped into the block-preserving permutations.
steps.explanation: We expand the product of sums `perm(A) * perm(D)` into a single sum over pairs (σ₁, σ₂) ∈ Sₘ × Sₙ via `Finset.sum_mul_sum`, `Finset.sum_product'`, and `Finset.univ_product_univ`. We then apply `Finset.sum_nbij` with the direct sum map (σ₁, σ₂) ↦ σ₁ ⊕ σ₂, showing first that this map lands in the range of `sumCongrHom`.
steps.code:
· simp_rw [Finset.sum_mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_product', Finset.univ_product_univ]
    refine Finset.sum_nbij (fun σ ↦ σ.fst.sumCongr σ.snd) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · intro σ₁₂ _
      rw [Set.mem_toFinset]
      exact ⟨σ₁₂, rfl⟩

steps.claim: The direct sum map from pairs of permutations into permutations of m ⊕ n is injective.
steps.explanation: If σ₁ ⊕ σ₂ = τ₁ ⊕ τ₂, then evaluating both sides on left injections `Sum.inl` implies σ₁ = τ₁, and evaluating on right injections `Sum.inr` implies σ₂ = τ₂. Equality of the pairs follows by extensionality.
steps.code:
· intro σ₁ _ σ₂ _
      dsimp only
      intro h
      have h2 : ∀ x, Equiv.Perm.sumCongr σ₁.fst σ₁.snd x = Equiv.Perm.sumCongr σ₂.fst σ₂.snd x :=
        DFunLike.congr_fun h
      simp only [Sum.map_inr, Sum.map_inl, Equiv.Perm.sumCongr_apply, Sum.forall, Sum.inl.injEq,
        Sum.inr.injEq] at h2
      ext x
      · exact h2.left x
      · exact h2.right x

steps.claim: The direct sum map is surjective onto the range of `sumCongrHom`.
steps.explanation: By definition of the range of the homomorphism `Equiv.Perm.sumCongrHom`, any permutation in the range is of the form σ₁ ⊕ σ₂ for some pair of permutations.
steps.code:
· intro σ hσ
      rw [Finset.mem_coe, Set.mem_toFinset] at hσ
      obtain ⟨σ₁₂, hσ₁₂⟩ := hσ
      use σ₁₂
      rw [← hσ₁₂]
      simp

steps.claim: For any pair of permutations (σ₁, σ₂), the product of entries of the block matrix under σ₁ ⊕ σ₂ equals the product of entries of A under σ₁ times the product of entries of D under σ₂.
steps.explanation: The product over m ⊕ n factors into a product over m and a product over n by `Fintype.prod_sum_type`. Under the direct sum permutation, elements in m map to m with entries from the top-left block A (`Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₁`), and elements in n map to n with entries from the bottom-right block D (`Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₂`).
steps.code:
· simp only [forall_prop_of_true, Prod.forall, Finset.mem_univ]
      intro σ₁ σ₂
      rw [Fintype.prod_sum_type]
      simp_rw [Equiv.sumCongr_apply, Sum.map_inr, Sum.map_inl, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₁,
        Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₂]

steps.claim: Any permutation outside the image of `sumCongrHom` must map some element of m to an element of n.
steps.explanation: By `Equiv.Perm.mem_sumCongrHom_range_of_perm_mapsTo_inl`, any permutation of m ⊕ n on finite types that maps the range of `Sum.inl` into itself must belong to the image of `sumCongrHom`. Taking the contrapositive via modus tollens (`mt`), a permutation outside this subgroup cannot preserve the range of `Sum.inl`.
steps.code:
· rintro σ - hσn
    have h1 : ¬∀ x, ∃ y, Sum.inl y = σ (Sum.inl x) := by
      rw [Set.mem_toFinset] at hσn
      simpa only [Set.MapsTo, Set.mem_range, forall_exists_index, forall_apply_eq_imp_iff] using
        mt Equiv.Perm.mem_sumCongrHom_range_of_perm_mapsTo_inl hσn

steps.claim: Any permutation outside the image of `sumCongrHom` yields a product of zero.
steps.explanation: Since σ does not preserve m, there exists an element a ∈ m whose image under σ is not in the range of `Sum.inl`, meaning σ(Sum.inl a) = Sum.inr b for some b ∈ n. At this position, the matrix entry comes from the bottom-left block, which is zero (`Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₁` and `Matrix.zero_apply`). Since one factor is zero, the entire product is zero by `Finset.prod_eq_zero`.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := not_forall.mp h1
    rcases hx : σ (Sum.inl a) with a2 | b
    · have hn := (not_exists.mp ha) a2
      exact absurd hx.symm hn
    · rw [Finset.prod_eq_zero (Finset.mem_univ (Sum.inl a))]
      rw [hx, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₁, Matrix.zero_apply]

steps.claim: The permanent of a block lower-triangular matrix equals the product of the permanents of its diagonal blocks.
steps.explanation: Transposing the block lower-triangular matrix yields a block upper-triangular matrix whose bottom-left block is zero (`Matrix.fromBlocks_transpose` and `Matrix.transpose_zero`). Since matrix transposition preserves the permanent (`Matrix.permanent_transpose`), applying `matrix_permanent_from_blocks_zero_one_two_zero_two_one` to the transposed matrix gives perm(Aᵀ) * perm(Dᵀ) = perm(A) * perm(D).
steps.code:
rw [← Matrix.permanent_transpose, Matrix.fromBlocks_transpose, Matrix.transpose_zero,
    matrix_permanent_from_blocks_zero_one_two_zero_two_one, Matrix.permanent_transpose,
    Matrix.permanent_transpose]

glossary.absurd: From a contradiction (both a proposition and its negation), any proposition follows.
glossary.DFunLike.congr_fun: If two functions or permutations are equal, their values agree on every argument: f = g → ∀ x, f x = g x.
glossary.Eq.symm: Symmetry of equality: if a = b, then b = a.
glossary.Equiv.Perm.sumCongr_apply: The direct sum permutation σ₁ ⊕ σ₂ acts by applying σ₁ on left injections and σ₂ on right injections.
glossary.Equiv.Perm.sumCongrHom: The group homomorphism embedding Perm(α) × Perm(β) into Perm(α ⊕ β) by componentwise action.
glossary.Equiv.Perm.mem_sumCongrHom_range_of_perm: On finite types, any permutation of α ⊕ β that maps the range of Sum.inl into itself lies in the image of sumCongrHom.
glossary.Equiv.sumCongr_apply: The direct sum of equivalences on a sum type acts componentwise via Sum.map.
glossary.Finset.mem_coe: An element belongs to the coercion of a finset to a set if and only if it belongs to the finset.
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to the universal finset Finset.univ.
glossary.Finset.prod_eq_zero: A finite product is zero if one of its factors is zero.
glossary.Finset.subset_univ: Every finset on a finite type is a subset of the universal finset Finset.univ.
glossary.Finset.sum_mul_sum: The product of two finite sums equals the double sum of pairwise products: (∑ i, f i) * (∑ j, g j) = ∑ i, ∑ j, f i * g j.
glossary.Finset.sum_nbij: Two sums over finite sets are equal if their index sets are in bijection and the bijection preserves the values of the summands.
glossary.Finset.sum_product': A sum over a Cartesian product of finsets equals the iterated sum over each component finset.
glossary.Finset.sum_subset: A sum over a finset equals the sum over a subset if all terms outside the subset vanish.
glossary.Finset.univ_product_univ: The Cartesian product of two universal finsets is the universal finset of the product type.
glossary.Fintype.prod_sum_type: A product over a sum type α₁ ⊕ α₂ factors into the product over α₁ times the product over α₂.
glossary.Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₁: The (inl i, inl j) entry of a 2 × 2 block matrix is the (i, j) entry of the top-left block A.
glossary.Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₁: The (inr i, inl j) entry of a 2 × 2 block matrix is the (i, j) entry of the bottom-left block C.
glossary.Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₂: The (inr i, inr j) entry of a 2 × 2 block matrix is the (i, j) entry of the bottom-right block D.
glossary.Matrix.fromBlocks_transpose: The transpose of a 2 × 2 block matrix transposes each block and swaps the off-diagonal blocks.
glossary.Matrix.permanent: The permanent of a square matrix M, defined as the sum over all permutations σ of the product of entries ∏ i, M (σ i) i.
glossary.Matrix.permanent_transpose: Transposing a matrix preserves its permanent: perm(Mᵀ) = perm(M).
glossary.Matrix.transpose_zero: The transpose of the zero matrix is the zero matrix.
glossary.Matrix.zero_apply: Every entry of the zero matrix is zero: 0 i j = 0.
glossary.matrix_permanent_from_blocks_zero_one_tw: The permanent of a block upper-triangular matrix with zero in the bottom-left position equals the product of the permanents of the diagonal blocks.
glossary.mt: Modus tollens: from a → b and ¬b, infer ¬a.
glossary.not_exists.mp: If a property does not have a witness, it is false for all elements: (¬∃ x, p x) → ∀ x, ¬p x.
glossary.not_forall.mp: If a property does not hold for all elements, there exists a counterexample: (¬∀ x, p x) → ∃ x, ¬p x.
glossary.forall_prop_of_true: Universal quantification over a true proposition is equivalent to evaluating the proposition at that truth.
glossary.forall_apply_eq_imp_iff: Quantifying over values equal to an application reduces to evaluating the property at the application: (∀ b a, f a = b → p b) ↔ ∀ a, p (f a).
glossary.forall_exists_index: Quantifying over an existential hypothesis is equivalent to quantifying over the witness and the property.
glossary.Set.MapsTo: A function maps a set into a set: MapsTo f s t means ∀ x ∈ s, f x ∈ t.
glossary.Set.mem_range: An element belongs to the range of a function f if and only if it is the image of some argument.
glossary.Set.mem_toFinset: An element belongs to the finset of a set with finite type if and only if it belongs to the set.
glossary.Sum.forall: Universal quantification over a sum type α ⊕ β is equivalent to universal quantification over α and over β.
glossary.Sum.inl.injEq: The left inclusion Sum.inl is injective: Sum.inl x = Sum.inl y ↔ x = y.
glossary.Sum.inr.injEq: The right inclusion Sum.inr is injective: Sum.inr x = Sum.inr y ↔ x = y.
glossary.Sum.map_inl: Sum.map f g applied to a left injection Sum.inl x yields Sum.inl (f x).
glossary.Sum.map_inr: Sum.map f g applied to a right injection Sum.inr x yields Sum.inr (g x).
glossary.Prod.forall: Universal quantification over a product type α × β is equivalent to universal quantification over both components.

caveats: The helper theorem `matrix_permanent_from_blocks_zero_one_two_zero_two_one` establishes the identity for block upper-triangular matrices with the zero block in the bottom-left position. The main theorem `matrix_permanent_from_blocks_zero_one_two` for block lower-triangular matrices is then proved directly in three lines using matrix transposition.

declarations.name: matrix_permanent_mul_of_char_two
declarations.informal: For every commutative ring R of characteristic 2 and any square matrices A and B over R indexed by a finite type n with decidable equality, the permanent of the matrix product A * B equals the product of the permanent of A and the permanent of B.
declarations.statement: theorem matrix_permanent_mul_of_char_two {n R : Type*} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] [CommRing R] [CharP R 2] (A B : Matrix n n R) : (A * B).permanent = A.permanent * B.permanent
declarations.source:
/-- Over any commutative ring of characteristic 2, the permanent of a product of square matrices equals the product of their permanents. -/
theorem matrix_permanent_mul_of_char_two {n R : Type*} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] [CommRing R] [CharP R 2] (A B : Matrix n n R) : (A * B).permanent = A.permanent * B.permanent := by
  rw [← matrix_det_eq_permanent_of_char_two, ← matrix_det_eq_permanent_of_char_two A, ← matrix_det_eq_permanent_of_char_two B]
  exact Matrix.det_mul A B
declarations.reading: For any finite type $n$ with decidable equality and any commutative ring $R$ of characteristic 2, and for any two $n \times n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ with entries in $R$, the permanent of their matrix product $A * B$ equals the product of their permanents, $\operatorname{perm}(A) \cdot \operatorname{perm}(B)$.

explanation.summary: The proof reduces the multiplicativity of the permanent to that of the determinant. Over a commutative ring of characteristic 2, signs of permutations are trivial, so the permanent and the determinant of a square matrix are identical. Rewriting each permanent as a determinant allows the claim to follow directly from the standard multiplicativity of the determinant.

steps.claim: The statement reduces to the multiplicativity of the determinant: det(A * B) = det(A) * det(B).
steps.explanation: In characteristic 2, 1 = -1, so the sign of any permutation is 1 and the determinant coincides with the permanent (matrix_det_eq_permanent_of_char_two). Replacing each permanent in the goal—(A * B).permanent, A.permanent, and B.permanent—with the corresponding determinant converts the equation into one about determinants.
steps.code: rw [← matrix_det_eq_permanent_of_char_two, ← matrix_det_eq_permanent_of_char_two A, ← matrix_det_eq_permanent_of_char_two B]

steps.claim: det(A * B) = det(A) * det(B), closing the goal.
steps.explanation: The determinant is multiplicative over any commutative ring, as established by Matrix.det_mul.
steps.code: exact Matrix.det_mul A B

glossary.matrix_det_eq_permanent_of_char_two: Over a commutative ring of characteristic 2, the determinant of any square matrix equals its permanent.
glossary.Matrix.det_mul: The determinant of the product of two square matrices over a commutative ring equals the product of their determinants.

declarations.name: matrix_permanent_succ_row_zero
declarations.informal: For any commutative semiring R, any natural number n, and any square matrix A of size (n+1) x (n+1) over R, the permanent of A equals the sum over all columns j : Fin (n+1) of A 0 j times the permanent of the submatrix obtained by deleting row 0 and column j: permanent A = ∑ j : Fin (n+1), A 0 j * permanent (A.submatrix Fin.succ j.succAbove).
declarations.statement:
theorem matrix_permanent_succ_row_zero {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    (A : Matrix (Fin n.succ) (Fin n.succ) R) :
    A.permanent = ∑ j : Fin n.succ, A 0 j * (A.submatrix Fin.succ j.succAbove).permanent
declarations.source:
theorem matrix_permanent_succ_row_zero_column_zero {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    (A : Matrix (Fin n.succ) (Fin n.succ) R) :
    A.permanent = ∑ i : Fin n.succ, A i 0 * (A.submatrix i.succAbove Fin.succ).permanent := by
  rw [Matrix.permanent, Finset.univ_perm_fin_succ, ← Finset.univ_product_univ]
  simp only [Finset.sum_map, Equiv.toEmbedding_apply, Finset.sum_product, Matrix.submatrix]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => Fin.cases ?_ (fun i => ?_) i
  · simp only [Fin.prod_univ_succ, Matrix.permanent, Finset.mul_sum,
      Equiv.Perm.decomposeFin_symm_apply_zero,
      Equiv.swap_self, id,
      Equiv.Perm.decomposeFin_symm_apply_succ, Fin.succAbove_zero, Equiv.coe_refl,
      Matrix.of_apply]
  · rw [← Matrix.permanent_permute_cols (Fin.cycleRange i), Matrix.permanent, Finset.mul_sum]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun σ _ => ?_
    simp only [Fin.prod_univ_succ, Fin.succAbove_cycleRange,
      Equiv.Perm.decomposeFin_symm_apply_zero, Equiv.Perm.decomposeFin_symm_apply_succ,
      Matrix.submatrix_apply, Matrix.of_apply, id]

/-- Laplacian expansion of the permanent of an (n+1) x (n+1) matrix along row 0. -/
theorem matrix_permanent_succ_row_zero {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    (A : Matrix (Fin n.succ) (Fin n.succ) R) :
    A.permanent = ∑ j : Fin n.succ, A 0 j * (A.submatrix Fin.succ j.succAbove).permanent := by
  rw [← Matrix.permanent_transpose A, matrix_permanent_succ_row_zero_column_zero]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
  rw [← Matrix.permanent_transpose]
  simp only [Matrix.transpose_apply, Matrix.transpose_submatrix, Matrix.transpose_transpose]
declarations.reading: For every natural number $n$, commutative semiring $R$, and $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix $A$ with entries in $R$, the permanent of $A$ equals the sum over all column indices $j \in \mathrm{Fin}(n+1)$ of $A_{0, j}$ multiplied by the permanent of the $n \times n$ submatrix obtained by removing row $0$ (indexed via `Fin.succ`) and column $j$ (indexed via `Fin.succAbove j`).
