declarations.name: matrix_permanent_succ_row
declarations.informal: For any commutative semiring R, any natural number n, any square matrix A of size (n+1) x (n+1) over R, and any row index i : Fin (n+1), the permanent of A equals the sum over all columns j : Fin (n+1) of A i j times the permanent of the submatrix obtained by deleting row i and column j: permanent A = ∑ j : Fin (n+1), A i j * permanent (A.submatrix i.succAbove j.succAbove).
declarations.statement:
theorem matrix_permanent_succ_row {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    (A : Matrix (Fin n.succ) (Fin n.succ) R) (i : Fin n.succ) :
    A.permanent = ∑ j : Fin n.succ, A i j * (A.submatrix i.succAbove j.succAbove).permanent
declarations.source:
/-- Laplacian expansion of the permanent of an (n+1) x (n+1) matrix along row i. -/
theorem matrix_permanent_succ_row {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    (A : Matrix (Fin n.succ) (Fin n.succ) R) (i : Fin n.succ) :
    A.permanent = ∑ j : Fin n.succ, A i j * (A.submatrix i.succAbove j.succAbove).permanent := by
  rw [← Matrix.permanent_permute_cols i.cycleRange⁻¹, matrix_permanent_succ_row_zero]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
  simp only [Matrix.submatrix_apply, Matrix.submatrix_submatrix, Equiv.Perm.inv_def]
  have h1 : i.cycleRange.symm 0 = i := Fin.cycleRange_symm_zero i
  have h2 : (⇑i.cycleRange.symm ∘ Fin.succ) = i.succAbove := funext (Fin.cycleRange_symm_succ i)
  have h3 : (id ∘ j.succAbove) = j.succAbove := rfl
  rw [h1, h2, h3]
  rfl
declarations.reading: For any natural number $n$, any commutative semiring $R$, any $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix $A$ with entries in $R$, and any row index $i \in \mathrm{Fin}(n+1)$: the permanent of $A$ equals the sum over all column indices $j \in \mathrm{Fin}(n+1)$ of $A_{i, j}$ multiplied by the permanent of the $n \times n$ submatrix of $A$ obtained by deleting row $i$ and column $j$ (via `i.succAbove` and `j.succAbove`).

explanation.summary: The Laplace expansion along an arbitrary row i is proved by reducing it to the expansion along row 0 via a row permutation. Applying the inverse cyclic permutation `i.cycleRange⁻¹` moves row i to row 0 while preserving the permanent. Expanding along row 0 and comparing the terms shows that the (0, j) entry is A i j and the submatrix omitting row 0 corresponds precisely to deleting row i from A.

steps.claim: The permanent of A equals the row-0 Laplace expansion of the row-permuted matrix obtained by applying `i.cycleRange⁻¹` to the rows of A.
steps.explanation: By `Matrix.permanent_permute_cols`, permuting the rows of A by the permutation `i.cycleRange⁻¹` leaves the permanent unchanged. Applying the known base case `matrix_permanent_succ_row_zero` to this permuted matrix then expresses the permanent as the sum over columns j of the product of its (0, j) entry and the permanent of the submatrix omitting row 0 and column j.
steps.code: rw [← Matrix.permanent_permute_cols i.cycleRange⁻¹, matrix_permanent_succ_row_zero]

steps.claim: It suffices to show that for every column j, the j-th summand of the permuted expansion simplifies to `A ((Equiv.symm i.cycleRange) 0) j * (A.submatrix (⇑(Equiv.symm i.cycleRange) ∘ Fin.succ) (id ∘ j.succAbove)).permanent`, and equals `A i j * (A.submatrix i.succAbove j.succAbove).permanent`.
steps.explanation: Using `Finset.sum_congr`, equality of the two sums reduces to equality of each column's summand. Simplifying the submatrix operations on the left-hand side evaluates the (0, j) entry using `Matrix.submatrix_apply`, merges the nested submatrix extractions into composed row and column maps using `Matrix.submatrix_submatrix`, and rewrites the permutation inverse using `Equiv.Perm.inv_def`.
steps.code:
refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
  simp only [Matrix.submatrix_apply, Matrix.submatrix_submatrix, Equiv.Perm.inv_def]

steps.claim: For each column j, the j-th summand in the row-0 expansion matches the j-th summand in the expansion along row i, completing the proof.
steps.explanation: The inverse cycle permutation maps 0 to i by `Fin.cycleRange_symm_zero`, so the entry at row 0 is A i j. Furthermore, precomposing the inverse permutation with `Fin.succ` yields `i.succAbove` by `Fin.cycleRange_symm_succ`, showing that omitting row 0 of the permuted matrix corresponds to omitting row i of A. Along with `id ∘ j.succAbove = j.succAbove`, substituting these three identities makes both sides definitionally equal.
steps.code:
have h1 : i.cycleRange.symm 0 = i := Fin.cycleRange_symm_zero i
  have h2 : (⇑i.cycleRange.symm ∘ Fin.succ) = i.succAbove := funext (Fin.cycleRange_symm_succ i)
  have h3 : (id ∘ j.succAbove) = j.succAbove := rfl
  rw [h1, h2, h3]
  rfl

glossary.Matrix.permanent_permute_cols: Permuting the rows of a square matrix by an equivalence permutation does not change its permanent: `(M.submatrix (⇑σ) id).permanent = M.permanent`.
glossary.matrix_permanent_succ_row_zero: Laplace expansion of the permanent of an (n+1) × (n+1) matrix along row 0: the permanent equals the sum over all columns j of `A 0 j` times the permanent of the submatrix deleting row 0 and column j.
glossary.Finset.sum_congr: Two finite sums are equal if their index sets are equal and their summands agree on every element in the index set.
glossary.Matrix.submatrix_apply: The (i, j)-th entry of a submatrix is obtained by evaluating the original matrix at the reindexed row and column: `(A.submatrix r c) i j = A (r i) (c j)`.
glossary.Matrix.submatrix_submatrix: Taking successive submatrices corresponds to composing the respective row and column indexing functions: `(A.submatrix r₁ c₁).submatrix r₂ c₂ = A.submatrix (r₁ ∘ r₂) (c₁ ∘ c₂)`.
glossary.Equiv.Perm.inv_def: The group inverse `f⁻¹` of a permutation equals its inverse equivalence `Equiv.symm f`.
glossary.Fin.cycleRange_symm_zero: The inverse of the cyclic permutation `i.cycleRange` maps 0 to i.
glossary.Fin.cycleRange_symm_succ: For any index j, the inverse of `i.cycleRange` maps `j.succ` to `i.succAbove j` (omitting index i).

caveats: Despite its name mentioning columns, the lemma `Matrix.permanent_permute_cols` actually permutes the rows of the matrix, as shown by its type `(M.submatrix (⇑σ) id).permanent = M.permanent`.

declarations.name: matrix_permanent_succ_column
declarations.informal: For any commutative semiring R, any natural number n, any square matrix A of size (n+1) x (n+1) over R, and any column index j : Fin (n+1), the permanent of A equals the sum over all row indices i : Fin (n+1) of A i j times the permanent of the submatrix obtained by deleting row i and column j: A.permanent = ∑ i : Fin n.succ, A i j * (A.submatrix i.succAbove j.succAbove).permanent.
declarations.statement:
theorem matrix_permanent_succ_column {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    (A : Matrix (Fin n.succ) (Fin n.succ) R) (j : Fin n.succ) :
    A.permanent = ∑ i : Fin n.succ, A i j * (A.submatrix i.succAbove j.succAbove).permanent
declarations.source:
/-- Laplace column expansion for the permanent over a commutative semiring. -/
theorem matrix_permanent_succ_column {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    (A : Matrix (Fin n.succ) (Fin n.succ) R) (j : Fin n.succ) :
    A.permanent = ∑ i : Fin n.succ, A i j * (A.submatrix i.succAbove j.succAbove).permanent := by
  rw [← Matrix.permanent_transpose A]
  rw [matrix_permanent_succ_row A.transpose j]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
  simp only [Matrix.transpose_apply]
  congr 1
  rw [← Matrix.permanent_transpose (A.submatrix i.succAbove j.succAbove)]
  rw [Matrix.transpose_submatrix]
declarations.citation: Minc, Permanents, Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications, Addison-Wesley, 1978, Section 1.2
declarations.reading: For any natural number $n$, any commutative semiring $R$, any $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix $A$ with entries in $R$, and any column index $j \in \mathrm{Fin}(n+1)$, the permanent of $A$ equals the sum over all row indices $i \in \mathrm{Fin}(n+1)$ of $A_{i, j}$ multiplied by the permanent of the $n \times n$ submatrix obtained by deleting row $i$ and column $j$ (via `i.succAbove` and `j.succAbove`).

explanation.summary: The column expansion formula for the permanent is derived from the row expansion formula by transposition. Because transposition preserves the permanent, expanding the permanent of A along column j is equivalent to expanding the permanent of Aᵀ along row j. Comparing the two expansions term by term, each scalar entry (Aᵀ) j i matches A i j, and the resulting minor of Aᵀ is the transpose of the corresponding minor of A, which therefore has the same permanent.

steps.claim: The permanent of A equals the row expansion of Aᵀ along row j.
steps.explanation: Because transposition preserves the permanent (Matrix.permanent_transpose), we rewrite the permanent of A as the permanent of Aᵀ. Applying row expansion along row j to Aᵀ (matrix_permanent_succ_row) expresses this permanent as the sum over i of (Aᵀ) j i times the permanent of the minor of Aᵀ deleting row j and column i.
steps.code:
rw [← Matrix.permanent_transpose A]
  rw [matrix_permanent_succ_row A.transpose j]

steps.claim: It suffices to show that the minor of Aᵀ deleting row j and column i has the same permanent as the minor of A deleting row i and column j.
steps.explanation: By Finset.sum_congr, the two sums are equal if their corresponding terms agree for each row index i. Transposition swaps indices, so (Aᵀ) j i = A i j by Matrix.transpose_apply. Removing this matching scalar factor (congr 1) reduces the goal to showing that the permanents of the respective submatrices are equal.
steps.code:
refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
  simp only [Matrix.transpose_apply]
  congr 1

steps.claim: The permanent of the submatrix of Aᵀ deleting row j and column i equals the permanent of the submatrix of A deleting row i and column j.
steps.explanation: Using Matrix.permanent_transpose, the permanent of the submatrix of A deleting row i and column j is equal to the permanent of its transpose. By Matrix.transpose_submatrix, transposing this submatrix yields precisely the submatrix of Aᵀ deleting row j and column i, which closes the goal.
steps.code:
rw [← Matrix.permanent_transpose (A.submatrix i.succAbove j.succAbove)]
  rw [Matrix.transpose_submatrix]

glossary.Matrix.permanent_transpose: The permanent of the transpose of a square matrix equals the permanent of the original matrix.
glossary.matrix_permanent_succ_row: Laplace row expansion for the permanent: the permanent of an (n+1) × (n+1) matrix equals the sum along any row of each entry times the permanent of the corresponding minor.
glossary.Finset.sum_congr: Two finite sums are equal if their index sets are identical and their terms are equal at every element.
glossary.Matrix.transpose_apply: The entry at (i, j) of the transpose of a matrix is the entry at (j, i) of the original matrix.
glossary.Matrix.transpose_submatrix: The transpose of a submatrix formed by row map r and column map c equals the submatrix of the transpose formed by swapping r and c.

declarations.name: matrix_permanent_from_blocks_anti_diagonal
declarations.informal: For any commutative semiring R, any finite type n with decidable equality, and any square matrices B and C of size n x n over R, the permanent of the block matrix with 0 in the top-left block, B in the top-right block, C in the bottom-left block, and 0 in the bottom-right block equals the product of the permanent of B and the permanent of C: (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix n n R) B C 0).permanent = B.permanent * C.permanent.
declarations.statement:
theorem matrix_permanent_from_blocks_anti_diagonal {n : Type*} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n]
    {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (B C : Matrix n n R) :
    (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix n n R) B C 0).permanent = B.permanent * C.permanent
declarations.source:
/-- The permanent of a block anti-diagonal matrix with square blocks equals the product of the permanents of the off-diagonal blocks. -/
theorem matrix_permanent_from_blocks_anti_diagonal {n : Type*} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n]
    {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (B C : Matrix n n R) :
    (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix n n R) B C 0).permanent = B.permanent * C.permanent := by
  have h1 : (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix n n R) B C 0).permanent =
      ((Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix n n R) B C 0).submatrix (Equiv.sumComm n n) id).permanent := by
    rw [Matrix.permanent_permute_cols (Equiv.sumComm n n)]
  have h2 : (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix n n R) B C 0).submatrix (Equiv.sumComm n n) id =
      Matrix.fromBlocks C 0 0 B := by
    ext (i | i) (j | j) <;> simp [Matrix.fromBlocks]
  rw [h1, h2, matrix_permanent_from_blocks_zero_one_two, mul_comm]
declarations.citation: Minc, Permanents (1978), Chapter 2; Valiant, Completeness classes in algebra (1979)
declarations.reading: For every finite type $n$ with decidable equality, every commutative semiring $R$, and any two $n \times n$ matrices $B$ and $C$ over $R$, the permanent of the block matrix $\begin{pmatrix} 0 & B \\ C & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ (constructed via `Matrix.fromBlocks 0 B C 0`) is equal to the product of the permanent of $B$ and the permanent of $C$ (`B.permanent * C.permanent`).

explanation.summary: The proof evaluates the permanent of an anti-diagonal block matrix by swapping its two row blocks to convert it into a block diagonal matrix. Since permuting rows preserves the permanent, the permanent of the original matrix equals that of the resulting block matrix with diagonal blocks C and B. The claim then follows from the formula for the permanent of a block matrix with a zero upper-right block and the commutativity of multiplication.

steps.claim: Permuting the row blocks of the block anti-diagonal matrix does not change its permanent.
steps.explanation: Applying Matrix.permanent_permute_cols with the equivalence Equiv.sumComm n n (which interchanges the two copies of n) shows that the permanent of the block matrix with blocks 0, B, C, 0 equals the permanent of the submatrix obtained by swapping the row blocks.
steps.code:
have h1 : (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix n n R) B C 0).permanent =
      ((Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix n n R) B C 0).submatrix (Equiv.sumComm n n) id).permanent := by
    rw [Matrix.permanent_permute_cols (Equiv.sumComm n n)]

steps.claim: Swapping the row blocks of the anti-diagonal matrix yields the block diagonal matrix with diagonal blocks C and B.
steps.explanation: By matrix extensionality, we compare entries across the four combinations of row and column blocks (Sum.inl and Sum.inr). In each of the four cases, unfolding the definition of Matrix.fromBlocks verifies that swapping the row blocks via Equiv.sumComm moves block C to the top-left and block B to the bottom-right, while the off-diagonal blocks become 0.
steps.code:
have h2 : (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix n n R) B C 0).submatrix (Equiv.sumComm n n) id =
      Matrix.fromBlocks C 0 0 B := by
    ext (i | i) (j | j) <;> simp [Matrix.fromBlocks]

steps.claim: The permanent of the anti-diagonal block matrix equals the product of the permanents of B and C.
steps.explanation: Rewriting by the two previous equalities replaces the permanent of the anti-diagonal matrix with the permanent of the block matrix with diagonal blocks C and B (and upper-right block 0). By matrix_permanent_from_blocks_zero_one_two, this permanent equals perm(C) * perm(B), which equals perm(B) * perm(C) by commutativity of multiplication (mul_comm).
steps.code: rw [h1, h2, matrix_permanent_from_blocks_zero_one_two, mul_comm]

glossary.Matrix.permanent_permute_cols: Permuting the rows of a square matrix by an equivalence σ via submatrix σ id preserves its permanent.
glossary.Matrix.fromBlocks: Forms a block matrix from four submatrices indexed by sum types of rows and columns.
glossary.matrix_permanent_from_blocks_zero_one_tw: The permanent of a block matrix with a zero upper-right block equals the product of the permanents of its diagonal blocks: perm (fromBlocks A 0 C D) = perm(A) * perm(D).
glossary.mul_comm: Multiplication is commutative: a * b = b * a.

caveats: Despite its name, the lemma Matrix.permanent_permute_cols asserts that M.submatrix σ id has the same permanent as M; because the first index of submatrix acts on rows, this actually permutes row blocks rather than column blocks.

declarations.name: matrix_permanent_from_blocks_anti_diagonal_of_ne_card
declarations.informal: For any commutative semiring R, any finite types m and n with decidable equality such that the cardinality of m does not equal the cardinality of n, and any matrices B : Matrix m n R and C : Matrix n m R, the permanent of the block matrix Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix m m R) B C 0 equals 0.
declarations.statement:
theorem matrix_permanent_from_blocks_anti_diagonal_of_ne_card {m n R : Type*}
    [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [CommSemiring R]
    (hm : Fintype.card m ≠ Fintype.card n) (B : Matrix m n R) (C : Matrix n m R) :
    (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix m m R) B C 0).permanent = 0
declarations.source:
/-- The permanent of a block anti-diagonal matrix with zero diagonal blocks of unequal dimensions vanishes. -/
theorem matrix_permanent_from_blocks_anti_diagonal_of_ne_card {m n R : Type*}
    [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [CommSemiring R]
    (hm : Fintype.card m ≠ Fintype.card n) (B : Matrix m n R) (C : Matrix n m R) :
    (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix m m R) B C 0).permanent = 0 := by
  have h_prod (σ : Equiv.Perm (m ⊕ n)) :
      ∏ i : m ⊕ n, (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix m m R) B C 0) (σ i) i = 0 := by
    by_contra h_ne
    have h_none : ∀ x, (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix m m R) B C 0) (σ x) x ≠ 0 := by
      intro x hx
      apply h_ne
      exact Finset.prod_eq_zero (Finset.mem_univ x) hx
    have h1 : ∀ i : m, ∃ b : n, σ (Sum.inl i) = Sum.inr b := by
      intro i
      cases h_case : σ (Sum.inl i) with
      | inl a =>
        exfalso
        have h_zero : (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix m m R) B C 0) (σ (Sum.inl i)) (Sum.inl i) = 0 := by
          rw [h_case, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₁]
          rfl
        exact h_none (Sum.inl i) h_zero
      | inr b =>
        exact ⟨b, rfl⟩
    have h2 : ∀ j : n, ∃ a : m, σ (Sum.inr j) = Sum.inl a := by
      intro j
      cases h_case : σ (Sum.inr j) with
      | inl a =>
        exact ⟨a, rfl⟩
      | inr b =>
        exfalso
        have h_zero : (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix m m R) B C 0) (σ (Sum.inr j)) (Sum.inr j) = 0 := by
          rw [h_case, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₂]
          rfl
        exact h_none (Sum.inr j) h_zero
    let f : m → n := fun i => (h1 i).choose
    have hf : ∀ i, σ (Sum.inl i) = Sum.inr (f i) := fun i => (h1 i).choose_spec
    have h_inj_f : Function.Injective f := by
      intro i₁ i₂ h_eq
      have : σ (Sum.inl i₁) = σ (Sum.inl i₂) := by rw [hf, hf, h_eq]
      exact Sum.inl_injective (σ.injective this)
    have h_le1 : Fintype.card m ≤ Fintype.card n := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f h_inj_f
    let g : n → m := fun j => (h2 j).choose
    have hg : ∀ j, σ (Sum.inr j) = Sum.inl (g j) := fun j => (h2 j).choose_spec
    have h_inj_g : Function.Injective g := by
      intro j₁ j₂ h_eq
      have : σ (Sum.inr j₁) = σ (Sum.inr j₂) := by rw [hg, hg, h_eq]
      exact Sum.inr_injective (σ.injective this)
    have h_le2 : Fintype.card n ≤ Fintype.card m := Fintype.card_le_of_injective g h_inj_g
    exact hm (le_antisymm h_le1 h_le2)
  simp [Matrix.permanent, h_prod]

declarations.reading: For all types `m`, `n`, and `R` such that `m` and `n` have decidable equality and are finite, and `R` is a commutative semiring: if the cardinalities of `m` and `n` are unequal (`Fintype.card m ≠ Fintype.card n`), then for any `m × n` matrix `B` over `R` and any `n × m` matrix `C` over `R`, the permanent of the block matrix $\begin{pmatrix} 0 & B \\ C & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ (indexed by `m ⊕ n`) is equal to 0.

explanation.summary: The proof proceeds by showing that every term in the sum defining the permanent of the block matrix is zero. For any permutation σ of the disjoint union m ⊕ n, if the product of matrix entries along σ were non-zero, no entry could lie in the zero diagonal blocks. This forces σ to map all indices of m into n and all indices of n into m, yielding injections between m and n in both directions and implying |m| = |n|. Since the cardinalities of m and n are assumed unequal, every permutation yields a zero product, and thus the permanent vanishes.

steps.explanation: To establish that ∏ i, M (σ i) i = 0 for every permutation σ, we assume for contradiction that the product is non-zero. If any single factor in the product over m ⊕ n were zero, the entire product would vanish by Finset.prod_eq_zero. Thus, every factor M (σ x) x must be non-zero.

    by_contra h_ne
    have h_none : ∀ x, (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix m m R) B C 0) (σ x) x ≠ 0 := by
      intro x hx
      apply h_ne
      exact Finset.prod_eq_zero (Finset.mem_univ x) hx

steps.claim: The permutation σ maps every index in m to an index in n.
steps.explanation: For any index i ∈ m, we check whether σ(i) falls in m or n. If σ(i) were in m, the entry M (σ(i)) i would lie in the top-left block of the block matrix, which is the zero matrix 0_{m × m} by Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₁. This would make the entry zero, contradicting the fact that no factor along σ can be zero. Hence σ(i) must fall in n.

have h1 : ∀ i : m, ∃ b : n, σ (Sum.inl i) = Sum.inr b := by
      intro i
      cases h_case : σ (Sum.inl i) with
      | inl a =>
        exfalso
        have h_zero : (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix m m R) B C 0) (σ (Sum.inl i)) (Sum.inl i) = 0 := by
          rw [h_case, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₁]
          rfl
        exact h_none (Sum.inl i) h_zero
      | inr b =>
        exact ⟨b, rfl⟩

steps.claim: The permutation σ maps every index in n to an index in m.
steps.explanation: Similarly, for any index j ∈ n, we check whether σ(j) falls in m or n. If σ(j) were in n, the entry M (σ(j)) j would lie in the bottom-right block, which is 0_{n × n} by Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₂. That would again produce a zero entry, contradicting the non-vanishing assumption. Therefore, σ(j) must fall in m.
steps.code:
have h2 : ∀ j : n, ∃ a : m, σ (Sum.inr j) = Sum.inl a := by
      intro j
      cases h_case : σ (Sum.inr j) with
      | inl a =>
        exact ⟨a, rfl⟩
      | inr b =>
        exfalso
        have h_zero : (Matrix.fromBlocks (0 : Matrix m m R) B C 0) (σ (Sum.inr j)) (Sum.inr j) = 0 := by
          rw [h_case, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₂]
          rfl
        exact h_none (Sum.inr j) h_zero

steps.explanation: Define a function f : m → n sending each i ∈ m to the component in n given by σ(i). Because σ is a permutation (hence injective) and the inclusion of m into m ⊕ n is injective by Sum.inl_injective, f is an injective function. By Fintype.card_le_of_injective, this implies |m| ≤ |n|.

    have hf : ∀ i, σ (Sum.inl i) = Sum.inr (f i) := fun i => (h1 i).choose_spec

      have : σ (Sum.inl i₁) = σ (Sum.inl i₂) := by rw [hf, hf, h_eq]
      exact Sum.inl_injective (σ.injective this)

steps.explanation: Symmetrically, define g : n → m sending each j ∈ n to the component in m given by σ(j). Because σ and the inclusion of n into m ⊕ n are injective (the latter by Sum.inr_injective), g is injective. By Fintype.card_le_of_injective, this implies |n| ≤ |m|.

    have hg : ∀ j, σ (Sum.inr j) = Sum.inl (g j) := fun j => (h2 j).choose_spec
    have h_inj_g : Function.Injective g := by
      intro j₁ j₂ h_eq
      have : σ (Sum.inr j₁) = σ (Sum.inr j₂) := by rw [hg, hg, h_eq]
      exact Sum.inr_injective (σ.injective this)

steps.explanation: The two inequalities |m| ≤ |n| and |n| ≤ |m| imply |m| = |n| by antisymmetry (le_antisymm). This contradicts the theorem's hypothesis that |m| ≠ |n|. steps.claim: The permanent of the block matrix is 0.
steps.explanation: The permanent of a matrix is defined by Matrix.permanent as the sum over all permutations σ of the product of the entries chosen by σ. Since every term in this sum is zero by the previous step, the entire sum evaluates to 0.

declarations.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_not_le_iff_ge_succ
declarations.informal: For any commutative semiring R and any natural number r, the tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over R is not at most r if and only if every valid triad decomposition of 3x3 matrix multiplication over R has length at least r + 1.
declarations.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_not_le_iff_ge_succ (R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] (r : ℕ) : (¬ matrix3_tensor_rank_le R r) ↔ matrix3_tensor_rank_ge R (r + 1)
declarations.source:
/-- For any commutative semiring R and bound r, 3x3 matrix multiplication does not have rank at most r iff its rank is at least r + 1. -/
theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_not_le_iff_ge_succ (R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] (r : ℕ) : (¬ matrix3_tensor_rank_le R r) ↔ matrix3_tensor_rank_ge R (r + 1) := by
  dsimp [matrix3_tensor_rank_le, matrix3_tensor_rank_ge]
  constructor
  · intro h L hL
    by_contra! hlt
    exact h ⟨L, by omega, hL⟩
  · intro h ⟨L, hlen, hL⟩
    have := h L hL
    omega
declarations.reading: For any commutative semiring $R$ and any natural number $r$, it is not the case that `matrix3_tensor_rank_le R r` holds (i.e., there is no list of triads of length at most $r$ that forms a valid matrix multiplication decomposition) if and only if `matrix3_tensor_rank_ge R (r + 1)` holds (i.e., every list of triads that forms a valid matrix multiplication decomposition has length at least $r + 1$).

explanation.summary: The equivalence is established by expanding the definitions of upper and lower bounds on tensor rank into conditions on triad decomposition lengths, then proving both implications by contradiction. If no valid decomposition has length at most r, any valid decomposition must have length at least r + 1 because a length strictly smaller than r + 1 would be at most r. Conversely, if every valid decomposition has length at least r + 1, no decomposition can have length at most r, as the two length bounds are contradictory.

steps.claim: The equivalence reduces to proving two implications: that the non-existence of a valid decomposition of length at most r implies every valid decomposition has length at least r + 1, and conversely.
steps.explanation: Expanding the definitions of `matrix3_tensor_rank_le` (existence of a valid decomposition of length at most r) and `matrix3_tensor_rank_ge` (every valid decomposition has length at least r + 1) expresses the equivalence in terms of decomposition lengths. Splitting the equivalence with `constructor` yields the forward and backward directions as separate subgoals.
steps.code:
dsimp [matrix3_tensor_rank_le, matrix3_tensor_rank_ge]
  constructor

steps.claim: If no valid decomposition has length at most r, then every valid decomposition has length at least r + 1.
steps.explanation: Assume no valid decomposition of length at most r exists, and let L be an arbitrary valid decomposition. Arguing by contradiction, suppose the length of L is strictly less than r + 1. Since L.length is a natural number, L.length < r + 1 implies L.length ≤ r (justified by linear arithmetic via `omega`). Thus L is a valid decomposition of length at most r, which contradicts the initial assumption.
steps.code:
· intro h L hL
    by_contra! hlt
    exact h ⟨L, by omega, hL⟩

steps.claim: If every valid decomposition has length at least r + 1, then no valid decomposition has length at most r.
steps.explanation: Assume every valid decomposition has length at least r + 1. To prove that no decomposition has length at most r, suppose for contradiction that there exists a valid decomposition L with L.length ≤ r. Specializing the universal assumption to L yields r + 1 ≤ L.length. The simultaneous inequalities r + 1 ≤ L.length and L.length ≤ r contradict each other in the natural numbers, and `omega` closes the goal.
steps.code:
· intro h ⟨L, hlen, hL⟩
    have := h L hL
    omega

declarations.name: is_condorcet_winning_set_mono
declarations.informal: Condorcet winning sets are upward closed: if S is a Condorcet winning set and S is a subset of T, then T is also a Condorcet winning set.
declarations.statement:
theorem is_condorcet_winning_set_mono {n m : ℕ} (P : Fin n → Equiv.Perm (Fin m))
    {S T : Finset (Fin m)} (hS : is_condorcet_winning_set P S) (hST : S ⊆ T) :
    is_condorcet_winning_set P T
declarations.source:
/-- Monotonicity of Condorcet winning sets: any superset of a Condorcet winning set is also a Condorcet winning set. -/
theorem is_condorcet_winning_set_mono {n m : ℕ} (P : Fin n → Equiv.Perm (Fin m))
    {S T : Finset (Fin m)} (hS : is_condorcet_winning_set P S) (hST : S ⊆ T) :
    is_condorcet_winning_set P T := by
  intro a ha
  have haS : a ∉ S := fun h => ha (hST h)
  have hScard := hS a haS
  have hsub : (Finset.univ.filter fun v => ∀ b ∈ T, P v a < P v b) ⊆
              (Finset.univ.filter fun v => ∀ b ∈ S, P v a < P v b) := by
    intro v hv
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hv ⊢
    intro b hb
    exact hv b (hST hb)
  have hcard_le := Finset.card_le_card hsub
  linarith
declarations.reading: For any natural numbers $n$ and $m$, any profile of voter preferences $P : \text{Fin } n \to \text{Equiv.Perm}(\text{Fin } m)$, and any subsets of alternatives $S, T \subseteq \text{Fin } m$, if $S$ is a Condorcet winning set with respect to $P$ and $S \subseteq T$, then $T$ is also a Condorcet winning set with respect to $P$.

explanation.summary: To prove that any superset T of a Condorcet winning set S is also a Condorcet winning set, consider any candidate a ∉ T. Since S ⊆ T, candidate a is also not in S, so by the Condorcet winning property for S fewer than n / 2 voters prefer a to all of S. Because any voter who prefers a to all candidates in T must also prefer a to all candidates in S, the voters favoring a over T form a subset of those favoring a over S; their count is thus at most that for S, and hence strictly less than n / 2.

steps.claim: For any candidate a ∉ T, candidate a is also not in S, and fewer than n / 2 voters prefer a to every candidate in S.
steps.explanation: To show that T is a Condorcet winning set, fix any candidate a ∉ T. Because S ⊆ T, candidate a cannot belong to S either. Applying the definition of a Condorcet winning set for S to a ∉ S yields the inequality 2 * |{v | ∀ b ∈ S, P v a < P v b}| < n.
steps.code:
intro a ha
  have haS : a ∉ S := fun h => ha (hST h)
  have hScard := hS a haS

steps.claim: The set of voters who prefer a to every candidate in T is a subset of the set of voters who prefer a to every candidate in S.
steps.explanation: Take an arbitrary voter v who prefers candidate a to every candidate in T. Simplifying the membership condition in the filtered universal set using `Finset.mem_filter`, `Finset.mem_univ`, and `true_and`, this means that v prefers a to b for all b ∈ T. Since S ⊆ T, any b ∈ S is also in T, so v in particular prefers a to every b ∈ S. Therefore, v belongs to the corresponding set of voters for S.
steps.code:
have hsub : (Finset.univ.filter fun v => ∀ b ∈ T, P v a < P v b) ⊆
              (Finset.univ.filter fun v => ∀ b ∈ S, P v a < P v b) := by
    intro v hv
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hv ⊢
    intro b hb
    exact hv b (hST hb)

steps.claim: The number of voters preferring a to all of T is at most the number of voters preferring a to all of S.
steps.explanation: Applying `Finset.card_le_card` to the subset inclusion established in the previous step gives |{v | ∀ b ∈ T, P v a < P v b}| ≤ |{v | ∀ b ∈ S, P v a < P v b}|.
steps.code: have hcard_le := Finset.card_le_card hsub

steps.claim: Twice the number of voters preferring a to all of T is strictly less than n, concluding that T is a Condorcet winning set.
steps.explanation: Combining the cardinality bound |V_T| ≤ |V_S| with the strict inequality 2 * |V_S| < n, linear integer arithmetic (`linarith`) immediately yields 2 * |V_T| < n.
steps.code: linarith

declarations.name: condorcet_dimension_le_two_of_le_three
declarations.informal: Every election with at most three candidates and at least one voter has a Condorcet winning set of at most two candidates.
declarations.statement:
theorem condorcet_dimension_le_two_of_le_three (n m : ℕ) (P : Fin n → Equiv.Perm (Fin m))
    (hn : 0 < n) (hm : m ≤ 3) :
    ∃ S : Finset (Fin m), S.card ≤ 2 ∧ is_condorcet_winning_set P S
declarations.source:
/-- Every election with at most three candidates and at least one voter has a Condorcet winning set of at most two candidates. -/
theorem condorcet_dimension_le_two_of_le_three (n m : ℕ) (P : Fin n → Equiv.Perm (Fin m))
    (hn : 0 < n) (hm : m ≤ 3) :
    ∃ S : Finset (Fin m), S.card ≤ 2 ∧ is_condorcet_winning_set P S := by
  classical
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge m 3 with hm2 | hm3
  · exact ⟨Finset.univ, by simp; omega, condorcet_winning_set_univ P⟩
  obtain rfl : m = 3 := by omega
  let top : Fin 3 → Finset (Fin n) := fun a =>
    Finset.univ.filter fun v => ∀ b ∈ Finset.univ.erase a, P v a < P v b
  have hdisj : (↑(Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 3)) : Set (Fin 3)).PairwiseDisjoint top := by
    intro a _ b _ hab
    rw [Function.onFun, Finset.disjoint_left]
    intro v hva hvb
    simp only [top, Finset.mem_filter] at hva hvb
    have h1 := hva.2 b (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨Ne.symm hab, Finset.mem_univ _⟩)
    have h2 := hvb.2 a (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hab, Finset.mem_univ _⟩)
    exact absurd (h1.trans h2) (lt_irrefl _)
  have hsum : ∑ a, (top a).card ≤ n := by
    rw [← Finset.card_biUnion hdisj]
    exact (Finset.card_le_univ _).trans (by simp)
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ : ∃ a, 2 * (top a).card < n := by
    by_contra h
    push Not at h
    have h3 : ∑ _a : Fin 3, n ≤ ∑ a, 2 * (top a).card := Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => h a
    rw [← Finset.mul_sum] at h3
    simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul] at h3
    omega
  refine ⟨Finset.univ.erase a, by simp, fun x hx => ?_⟩
  have : x = a := by simpa using hx
  subst this
  exact ha
declarations.reading: For any natural numbers $n$ and $m$, and any profile $P : \mathrm{Fin}\ n \to \mathrm{Equiv.Perm}(\mathrm{Fin}\ m)$ assigning each voter $v \in \mathrm{Fin}\ n$ a permutation of alternatives $\mathrm{Fin}\ m$, if $n > 0$ and $m \le 3$, then there exists a subset $S \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\ m$ of size at most 2 such that $S$ is a Condorcet winning set under $P$ (i.e., `is_condorcet_winning_set P S`).

explanation.summary: The proof splits on whether the candidate count m is strictly less than 3 or equal to 3. If m < 3, the universal set of all candidates already has size at most 2 and vacuously forms a Condorcet winning set. If m = 3, we define the sets of voters who rank each candidate first; since voter preferences are strict, these three sets are pairwise disjoint and their sizes sum to at most n. Because n > 0, an averaging argument shows that at least one candidate a is ranked first by strictly fewer than n/2 voters. Removing candidate a leaves a two-candidate set S = univ \ {a}, which is a Condorcet winning set because a is the sole candidate outside S and cannot beat all of S with a majority.

steps.claim: If m < 3, the entire set of candidates is a Condorcet winning set of size at most 2.
steps.explanation: Under classical logic, we split on whether m < 3 or m ≥ 3 (`Nat.lt_or_ge`). If m < 3, the universal set of candidates has size at most 2 (`Finset.univ`), and the full candidate set is always a Condorcet winning set (`condorcet_winning_set_univ`).
steps.code:
classical
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge m 3 with hm2 | hm3
  · exact ⟨Finset.univ, by simp; omega, condorcet_winning_set_univ P⟩

steps.claim: In the remaining case, m = 3.
steps.explanation: From the branch hypothesis m ≥ 3 and the global assumption m ≤ 3, linear integer arithmetic (`omega`) establishes that m = 3, which is substituted into the goal.
steps.code: obtain rfl : m = 3 := by omega

steps.claim: The sets of voters who rank each candidate first are pairwise disjoint.
steps.explanation: For each candidate a ∈ Fin 3, define `top a` to be the set of voters who rank a strictly ahead of every other candidate b ≠ a. To prove these sets are pairwise disjoint (`Function.onFun`, `Finset.disjoint_left`), suppose some voter v belongs to both `top a` and `top b` for a ≠ b. Then v ∈ `top a` implies P(v)(a) < P(v)(b) (`Finset.mem_filter`, `Finset.mem_erase.2`, `Ne.symm`, `Finset.mem_univ`), while v ∈ `top b` implies P(v)(b) < P(v)(a). By transitivity of <, this implies P(v)(a) < P(v)(a), contradicting the irreflexivity of strict order (`lt_irrefl`).
steps.code:
let top : Fin 3 → Finset (Fin n) := fun a =>
    Finset.univ.filter fun v => ∀ b ∈ Finset.univ.erase a, P v a < P v b
  have hdisj : (↑(Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 3)) : Set (Fin 3)).PairwiseDisjoint top := by
    intro a _ b _ hab
    rw [Function.onFun, Finset.disjoint_left]
    intro v hva hvb
    simp only [top, Finset.mem_filter] at hva hvb
    have h1 := hva.2 b (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨Ne.symm hab, Finset.mem_univ _⟩)
    have h2 := hvb.2 a (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hab, Finset.mem_univ _⟩)
    exact absurd (h1.trans h2) (lt_irrefl _)

steps.claim: The sum of the numbers of voters ranking each candidate first is at most n.
steps.explanation: Because the sets `top a` are pairwise disjoint, the sum of their cardinalities equals the cardinality of their disjoint union (`Finset.card_biUnion`). Since the union is a subset of the n voters, its cardinality is bounded by |Fin n| = n (`Finset.card_le_univ`).
steps.code:
have hsum : ∑ a, (top a).card ≤ n := by
    rw [← Finset.card_biUnion hdisj]
    exact (Finset.card_le_univ _).trans (by simp)

steps.claim: There exists a candidate who is ranked first by strictly fewer than n/2 voters.
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that every candidate a satisfies 2 * |top a| ≥ n. Summing this inequality over all three candidates (`Finset.sum_le_sum`) and factoring out the constant 2 (`Finset.mul_sum`) yields 3n ≤ 2 * ∑ a, |top a| (`Finset.sum_const`, `Finset.card_univ`, `Fintype.card_fin`, `smul_eq_mul`). Combined with ∑ a, |top a| ≤ n, this forces 3n ≤ 2n, which contradicts n > 0 by linear arithmetic (`omega`).
steps.code:
obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ : ∃ a, 2 * (top a).card < n := by
    by_contra h
    push Not at h
    have h3 : ∑ _a : Fin 3, n ≤ ∑ a, 2 * (top a).card := Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => h a
    rw [← Finset.mul_sum] at h3
    simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul] at h3
    omega

steps.claim: Removing this candidate leaves a Condorcet winning set of at most two candidates.
steps.explanation: Let a be the candidate with 2 * |top a| < n. We choose S to be all candidates except a (`Finset.univ.erase a`). Since there are 3 candidates in total, |S| = 2 ≤ 2. Any challenger x ∉ S must be a itself. The voters preferring x = a to all members of S are precisely those who rank a first among all candidates, which is the set `top a`. Since 2 * |top a| < n by the choice of a, no majority can defeat S, proving that S is a Condorcet winning set.
steps.code:
refine ⟨Finset.univ.erase a, by simp, fun x hx => ?_⟩
  have : x = a := by simpa using hx
  subst this
  exact ha

glossary.Nat.lt_or_ge: For any natural numbers n and m, either n < m or n ≥ m.
glossary.condorcet_winning_set_univ: The set of all candidates is always a Condorcet winning set, as there are no candidates outside it.
glossary.Function.onFun: The composition of a binary relation with a function on each argument: `Function.onFun f g x y = f (g x) (g y)`.
glossary.Finset.disjoint_left: Two finite sets are disjoint if and only if no element of the first set belongs to the second set.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to `Finset.filter p s` if and only if it belongs to s and satisfies the predicate p.
glossary.Finset.mem_erase.2: If a ≠ b and a ∈ s, then a belongs to s with b removed (`s.erase b`).
glossary.Ne.symm: Inequality is symmetric: if a ≠ b, then b ≠ a.
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to the universal finite set of that type.
glossary.lt_irrefl: Strict inequality is irreflexive: no element is strictly less than itself.
glossary.Finset.card_biUnion: The cardinality of a pairwise disjoint union of finite sets equals the sum of their individual cardinalities.
glossary.Finset.card_le_univ: The cardinality of any finite subset is at most the total cardinality of the ambient finite type.
glossary.Finset.sum_le_sum: If f(i) ≤ g(i) for all elements i in a finite set, then the sum of f(i) is at most the sum of g(i).
glossary.Finset.mul_sum: A constant factor distributes over a finite sum: `c * ∑ i, f i = ∑ i, c * f i`.
glossary.Finset.sum_const: The sum of a constant value over a finite set equals the cardinality of the set scalar-multiplied by the constant.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal set of a finite type equals the cardinality of the type.
glossary.Fintype.card_fin: The finite type `Fin n` has cardinality n.
glossary.smul_eq_mul: Scalar multiplication on a semiring coincides with multiplication: `a • b = a * b`.

caveats: In the definition of `is_condorcet_winning_set`, voter preferences are represented as permutations where a smaller value indicates a higher preference: `P v a < P v b` means voter `v` prefers candidate `a` over `b`.

A set of candidates S is a Condorcet winning set if no outside candidate a ∉ S is strictly preferred to every member of S by at least half the voters (encoded by the inequality `2 * |{v | ∀ b ∈ S, P v a < P v b}| < n`).

declarations.name: card_piFinset_filter_apply_mem
declarations.informal: For any type α with decidable equality, any positive integer n, any finite subset S of α, any subset T of α with T ⊆ S, and any coordinate index i₀ : Fin n, the cardinality of the set of points in the product S^n whose i₀-th coordinate belongs to T equals T.card * S.card ^ (n - 1).
declarations.statement:
theorem card_piFinset_filter_apply_mem {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (S : Finset α) (T : Finset α) (hT : T ⊆ S) (i₀ : Fin n) :
    Finset.card (Finset.filter (fun x => x i₀ ∈ T) (Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S))) =
      T.card * S.card ^ (n - 1)
declarations.source:
/-- The number of points in S^n whose i₀-th coordinate belongs to a subset T ⊆ S equals |T| * |S|^(n-1). -/
theorem card_piFinset_filter_apply_mem {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (S : Finset α) (T : Finset α) (hT : T ⊆ S) (i₀ : Fin n) :
    Finset.card (Finset.filter (fun x => x i₀ ∈ T) (Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S))) =
      T.card * S.card ^ (n - 1) := by
  have _ := hn
  have h_set : Finset.filter (fun x => x i₀ ∈ T) (Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S)) =
      Fintype.piFinset (Function.update (fun _ : Fin n => S) i₀ T) := by
    ext x
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Fintype.mem_piFinset, Function.update_apply]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩ i
      split_ifs with h
      · subst h; exact h2
      · exact h1 i
    · intro h
      refine ⟨fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
      · specialize h i
        split_ifs at h with hi
        · subst hi; exact hT h
        · exact h
      · specialize h i₀
        simpa using h
  rw [h_set, Fintype.card_piFinset]
  have h1 : (fun i : Fin n => (Function.update (fun _ : Fin n => S) i₀ T i).card) =
      Function.update (fun _ : Fin n => S.card) i₀ T.card := by
    ext i
    by_cases h : i = i₀
    · subst h; simp
    · simp [h]
  rw [h1]
  have hmem : i₀ ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)) := Finset.mem_univ i₀
  rw [Finset.prod_update_of_mem hmem]
  have h_sdiff : ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)) \ {i₀}) = Finset.univ.erase i₀ :=
    Finset.sdiff_singleton_eq_erase i₀ Finset.univ
  rw [h_sdiff, Finset.prod_const, Finset.card_erase_of_mem hmem, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
declarations.reading: Let `α` be a type with decidable equality, and let `n` be a natural number such that `0 < n`. Let `S` and `T` be finite sets of elements of `α` such that `T ⊆ S`, and let `i₀ : Fin n` be an index. Then the cardinality of the set of functions `x : Fin n → α` (taking values in `S` at every coordinate) such that `x i₀ ∈ T` is equal to `T.card * S.card ^ (n - 1)`.

explanation.summary: The proof recognizes the filtered subset of points in S^n whose i₀-th coordinate belongs to T as a generalized Cartesian product where the i₀-th factor is replaced by T and all other n - 1 factors remain S. By the product rule for finite sets, its cardinality is the product of the cardinalities of the individual factors. Factoring out |T| at index i₀ leaves a constant product of |S| over the remaining n - 1 indices, yielding |T| * |S|^(n - 1).

steps.claim: The filtered set `{x ∈ S^n | x i₀ ∈ T}` is identical to the Cartesian product `∏ (i : Fin n) Sᵢ`, where `Sᵢ = T` when `i = i₀` and `Sᵢ = S` otherwise.
steps.explanation: We first bring `hn` into scope, then prove by set extensionality that the filtered set equals `Fintype.piFinset (Function.update (fun _ => S) i₀ T)`. A point `x` belongs to the filtered set if and only if `x i ∈ S` for all `i` and `x i₀ ∈ T`. In the forward direction, setting `i = i₀` yields `x i₀ ∈ T`, while for `i ≠ i₀` we have `x i ∈ S`. In the reverse direction, specializing at `i₀` gives `x i₀ ∈ T`, and for any index `i`, either `i = i₀` (so `x i ∈ T ⊆ S` using the hypothesis `hT : T ⊆ S`) or `i ≠ i₀` (so `x i ∈ S`), confirming that `x ∈ S^n`.
steps.code:
have _ := hn
  have h_set : Finset.filter (fun x => x i₀ ∈ T) (Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S)) =
      Fintype.piFinset (Function.update (fun _ : Fin n => S) i₀ T) := by
    ext x
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Fintype.mem_piFinset, Function.update_apply]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩ i
      split_ifs with h
      · subst h; exact h2
      · exact h1 i
    · intro h
      refine ⟨fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
      · specialize h i
        split_ifs at h with hi
        · subst hi; exact hT h
        · exact h
      · specialize h i₀
        simpa using h

steps.claim: The cardinality of the filtered set equals the product `∏ (i : Fin n) |Sᵢ|` of the cardinalities of its factor sets.
steps.explanation: Rewriting the filtered set with the Cartesian product equality `h_set`, we apply `Fintype.card_piFinset` to express the size of the product as the product of the sizes of the coordinate sets.
steps.code: rw [h_set, Fintype.card_piFinset]

steps.claim: The factor-cardinality function `i ↦ |Sᵢ|` equals the constant function `|S|` updated to `|T|` at `i₀`.
steps.explanation: By function extensionality and case distinction on whether `i = i₀` or `i ≠ i₀`, we show that `(i ↦ |Sᵢ|) = Function.update (fun _ => |S|) i₀ |T|`. Rewriting with this identity expresses the goal as the product of this updated function over `Finset.univ`.
steps.code:
have h1 : (fun i : Fin n => (Function.update (fun _ : Fin n => S) i₀ T i).card) =
      Function.update (fun _ : Fin n => S.card) i₀ T.card := by
    ext i
    by_cases h : i = i₀
    · subst h; simp
    · simp [h]
  rw [h1]

steps.claim: The product factors into `|T|` times the product of `|S|` over all other coordinates `Finset.univ \ {i₀}`.
steps.explanation: Since `i₀` is in the universe of coordinates (`Finset.mem_univ`), `Finset.prod_update_of_mem` pulls out the factor `|T|` at `i₀`, leaving the product of the constant `|S|` over the punctured universe `Finset.univ \ {i₀}`.
steps.code:
have hmem : i₀ ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)) := Finset.mem_univ i₀
  rw [Finset.prod_update_of_mem hmem]

steps.claim: The product of `|S|` over the remaining `n - 1` coordinates equals `|S| ^ (n - 1)`, completing the proof.
steps.explanation: The complement `Finset.univ \ {i₀}` is rewritten as `Finset.univ.erase i₀` via `Finset.sdiff_singleton_eq_erase`. By `Finset.prod_const`, the constant product over this set equals `|S|` raised to the cardinality of the erased set. Finally, erasing `i₀` from the universe leaves `|Finset.univ| - 1` elements (`Finset.card_erase_of_mem`), and `Finset.univ` has size `n` (`Finset.card_univ`, `Fintype.card_fin`), leaving exponent `n - 1`.
steps.code:
have h_sdiff : ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)) \ {i₀}) = Finset.univ.erase i₀ :=
    Finset.sdiff_singleton_eq_erase i₀ Finset.univ
  rw [h_sdiff, Finset.prod_const, Finset.card_erase_of_mem hmem, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]

glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to a filtered set `{x ∈ s | p x}` if and only if it belongs to `s` and satisfies `p`.
glossary.Fintype.mem_piFinset: A dependent function `f` belongs to a product of finite sets `Fintype.piFinset t` if and only if `f a ∈ t a` for every coordinate `a`.
glossary.Function.update_apply: Evaluating a function updated at `a'` at an input `a` yields the new value if `a = a'` and the original function value otherwise.
glossary.Fintype.card_piFinset: The cardinality of a Cartesian product of finite sets equals the product of the cardinalities of the individual factor sets.
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to its universal set `Finset.univ`.
glossary.Finset.prod_update_of_mem: The product of a function updated at an element `i ∈ s` equals the updated value at `i` times the product of the original function over `s \ {i}`.
glossary.Finset.sdiff_singleton_eq_erase: Removing a singleton `{a}` from a finite set `s` by set difference is equal to erasing `a` from `s`.
glossary.Finset.prod_const: The product of a constant value `b` over a finite set `s` equals `b ^ |s|`.
glossary.Finset.card_erase_of_mem: Removing an element `a ∈ s` from a finite set `s` decreases its cardinality by 1.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of `Finset.univ` for a finite type equals the cardinality of the type.
glossary.Fintype.card_fin: The cardinality of the standard finite type `Fin n` is `n`.

caveats: The hypothesis `hn : 0 < n` is formally redundant: the existence of the coordinate `i₀ : Fin n` already implies that `n > 0` (since `Fin 0` is empty), and natural number subtraction saturates at zero. Line 6 (`have _ := hn`) serves only to prevent an unused variable warning.

declarations.name: schwartz_zippel_zero_count_tight
declarations.informal: For any integral domain F with decidable equality, any positive integer n, any finite subset S of F, and any natural number d with d ≤ S.card, there exists a nonzero multivariate polynomial p in n variables over F with total degree at most d such that the number of points in S^n at which p evaluates to zero equals d * S.card ^ (n - 1).
declarations.statement:
theorem schwartz_zippel_zero_count_tight {F : Type*} [CommRing F] [IsDomain F] [DecidableEq F]
    {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {S : Finset F} {d : ℕ} (hd : d ≤ S.card) :
    ∃ p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F, p ≠ 0 ∧ p.totalDegree ≤ d ∧
      Finset.card (Finset.filter (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x p = 0)
        (Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S))) = d * S.card ^ (n - 1)
declarations.source:
lemma schwartz_zippel_zero_count_tight_x_sub_c_ne_zero {F : Type*} [CommRing F] [IsDomain F]
    {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n) (s : F) : (MvPolynomial.X i - MvPolynomial.C s : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F) ≠ 0 := by
  intro h
  have h2 := congr_arg (MvPolynomial.coeff (Finsupp.single i 1)) h
  rw [MvPolynomial.coeff_sub, MvPolynomial.coeff_zero, MvPolynomial.coeff_X, if_pos rfl, MvPolynomial.coeff_C] at h2
  have hne : (0 : Fin n →₀ ℕ) ≠ Finsupp.single i 1 := by
    intro h3
    have h4 := Finsupp.ext_iff.mp h3 i
    simp at h4
  rw [if_neg hne, sub_zero] at h2
  exact one_ne_zero h2

/-- Tightness of the Schwartz-Zippel zero count upper bound via a product of univariate linear factors. -/
theorem schwartz_zippel_zero_count_tight {F : Type*} [CommRing F] [IsDomain F] [DecidableEq F]
    {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {S : Finset F} {d : ℕ} (hd : d ≤ S.card) :
    ∃ p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F, p ≠ 0 ∧ p.totalDegree ≤ d ∧
      Finset.card (Finset.filter (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x p = 0)
        (Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S))) = d * S.card ^ (n - 1) := by
  obtain ⟨T, hT, hTcard⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq hd
  let i₀ : Fin n := ⟨0, hn⟩
  let p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F := ∏ s ∈ T, (MvPolynomial.X i₀ - MvPolynomial.C s)
  use p
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff]
    intro s hs
    exact schwartz_zippel_zero_count_tight_x_sub_c_ne_zero i₀ s
  · refine (MvPolynomial.totalDegree_finsetProd T _).trans ?_
    have h1 (s : F) (hs : s ∈ T) :
        (MvPolynomial.X i₀ - MvPolynomial.C s : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F).totalDegree ≤ 1 :=
      (MvPolynomial.totalDegree_sub_C_le (MvPolynomial.X i₀) s).trans (MvPolynomial.totalDegree_X i₀).le
    have h2 : ∑ s ∈ T, (MvPolynomial.X i₀ - MvPolynomial.C s : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F).totalDegree ≤ ∑ s ∈ T, 1 :=
      Finset.sum_le_sum h1
    simp only [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one] at h2
    rw [hTcard] at h2
    exact h2
  · have h_filter :
        Finset.filter (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x p = 0) (Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S)) =
        Finset.filter (fun x => x i₀ ∈ T) (Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : Fin n => S)) := by
      apply Finset.filter_congr
      intro x hx
      dsimp [p]
      rw [map_prod]
      have : (∏ s ∈ T, MvPolynomial.eval x (MvPolynomial.X i₀ - MvPolynomial.C s)) = ∏ s ∈ T, (x i₀ - s) := by
        apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
        intro s hs
        simp
      rw [this, Finset.prod_eq_zero_iff]
      simp [sub_eq_zero]
    rw [h_filter]
    rw [card_piFinset_filter_apply_mem hn S T hT i₀]
    rw [hTcard]
declarations.citation: Burgisser, Clausen & Shokrollahi, Algebraic Complexity Theory
declarations.reading:
Given a commutative domain $F$ with decidable equality, a positive natural number $n > 0$, a finite subset $S \subseteq F$, and a natural number $d \le |S|$, there exists a non-zero multivariate polynomial $p \in F[X_0, \ldots, X_{n-1}]$ (indexed by `Fin n`) such that:
1. The total degree of $p$ is at most $d$, and
2. The number of tuples $x \in S^n$ (viewed as functions `Fin n → F` with all values in $S$, formed by `Fintype.piFinset`) at which $p$ evaluates to $0$ is exactly $d \cdot |S|^{n - 1}$.

explanation.summary: To prove tightness of the Schwartz-Zippel upper bound, we construct an explicit polynomial p that depends on only one variable X₀. Choosing a subset T ⊆ S of size d, we set p = ∏_{s ∈ T} (X₀ - s). In an integral domain, p is nonzero with total degree at most d, and p(x) = 0 if and only if x₀ ∈ T, so the number of zeros in S^n is precisely |T| · |S|^(n - 1) = d · |S|^(n - 1).

steps.claim: The linear polynomial X_i - C(s) is nonzero for any variable index i and scalar s.
steps.explanation: Assume for contradiction that X_i - C(s) = 0. Comparing the coefficient of the monomial X_i on both sides via congr_arg and MvPolynomial.coeff_sub, the coefficient of X_i in X_i - C(s) is 0. Since the coefficient of X_i in X_i is 1 (MvPolynomial.coeff_X, if_pos) and its coefficient in the constant polynomial C(s) is 0 (MvPolynomial.coeff_C, if_neg) because the monomial exponent for X_i is nonzero (Finsupp.ext_iff.mp), we simplify with sub_zero to obtain 1 = 0, which contradicts one_ne_zero.
steps.code:
intro h
  have h2 := congr_arg (MvPolynomial.coeff (Finsupp.single i 1)) h
  rw [MvPolynomial.coeff_sub, MvPolynomial.coeff_zero, MvPolynomial.coeff_X, if_pos rfl, MvPolynomial.coeff_C] at h2
  have hne : (0 : Fin n →₀ ℕ) ≠ Finsupp.single i 1 := by
    intro h3
    have h4 := Finsupp.ext_iff.mp h3 i
    simp at h4
  rw [if_neg hne, sub_zero] at h2
  exact one_ne_zero h2

steps.claim: Choose a subset T ⊆ S of cardinality d and define the polynomial p = ∏_{s ∈ T} (X_{i₀} - s).
steps.explanation: Using Finset.exists_subset_card_eq on the hypothesis d ≤ |S|, we obtain a subset T ⊆ S of cardinality d. Since n > 0, we select the coordinate index i₀ = 0 ∈ Fin n. We define p as the product of the linear factors X_{i₀} - C(s) over all s ∈ T, and supply p as the existential witness, splitting the remaining goal into three parts: nonzeroness, total degree at most d, and the zero count.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨T, hT, hTcard⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq hd
  let i₀ : Fin n := ⟨0, hn⟩
  let p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F := ∏ s ∈ T, (MvPolynomial.X i₀ - MvPolynomial.C s)
  use p
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩

steps.claim: The polynomial p is nonzero.
steps.explanation: In an integral domain, a finite product is nonzero if and only if every factor is nonzero (Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff). Each factor X_{i₀} - C(s) is nonzero by schwartz_zippel_zero_count_tight_x_sub_c_ne_zero.
steps.code:
· rw [Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff]
    intro s hs
    exact schwartz_zippel_zero_count_tight_x_sub_c_ne_zero i₀ s

steps.claim: The total degree of p is at most d.
steps.explanation: The total degree of a product is bounded by the sum of total degrees (MvPolynomial.totalDegree_finsetProd). Subtracting a constant does not increase total degree (MvPolynomial.totalDegree_sub_C_le), and the single variable X_{i₀} has total degree 1 (MvPolynomial.totalDegree_X), so each factor has total degree at most 1. Summing these bounds over T (Finset.sum_le_sum) yields |T| · 1 = d (Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one), matching the cardinality |T| = d.
steps.code:
· refine (MvPolynomial.totalDegree_finsetProd T _).trans ?_
    have h1 (s : F) (hs : s ∈ T) :
        (MvPolynomial.X i₀ - MvPolynomial.C s : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F).totalDegree ≤ 1 :=
      (MvPolynomial.totalDegree_sub_C_le (MvPolynomial.X i₀) s).trans (MvPolynomial.totalDegree_X i₀).le
    have h2 : ∑ s ∈ T, (MvPolynomial.X i₀ - MvPolynomial.C s : MvPolynomial (Fin n) F).totalDegree ≤ ∑ s ∈ T, 1 :=
      Finset.sum_le_sum h1
    simp only [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one] at h2
    rw [hTcard] at h2
    exact h2

steps.claim: A point x ∈ S^n is a zero of p if and only if its i₀-th coordinate lies in T.
steps.explanation: Evaluating p at x distributes over the product (map_prod) to yield ∏_{s ∈ T} (x(i₀) - s) via Finset.prod_congr. Because F is an integral domain with no zero divisors (Finset.prod_eq_zero_iff), this product vanishes if and only if x(i₀) - s = 0 for some s ∈ T, which means x(i₀) = s (sub_eq_zero). Hence, the set of zeros of p in S^n equals the set of points whose i₀-th coordinate lies in T (Finset.filter_congr).
steps.code:
· have h_filter :

declarations.name: is_single_peaked
declarations.informal: A strict preference relation P over a linearly ordered set of alternatives A is single-peaked with peak p if moving toward p strictly increases preference: for x < y ≤ p or p ≤ y < x, y is strictly preferred to x.
declarations.statement: def is_single_peaked {A : Type*} [LinearOrder A] (P : A → A → Prop) (p : A) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Single-peakedness of a pairwise strict preference relation along a linear order of alternatives. -/
def is_single_peaked {A : Type*} [LinearOrder A] (P : A → A → Prop) (p : A) : Prop := ∀ x y : A, ((x < y ∧ y ≤ p) ∨ (p ≤ y ∧ y < x)) → P y x
declarations.citation: Black (1948), The Decisions of a Committee Using a Special Majority; Arrow (1951)
declarations.reading:
For a linearly ordered type $A$, a binary relation $P$ on $A$, and an element $p \in A$, `is_single_peaked P p` is defined to hold if and only if:
1. For all $x, y \in A$, if $x < y$ and $y \le p$, then $P(y, x)$; and
2. For all $x, y \in A$, if $p \le y$ and $y < x$, then $P(y, x)$.

declarations.name: single_peaked_median_defeats_greater
declarations.informal: Under single-peaked preferences with asymmetric preferences, if strictly more than half of the voters have peak at most m, then for any alternative y > m, the number of voters preferring y to m is strictly less than the number preferring m to y.
declarations.statement:
theorem single_peaked_median_defeats_greater {V A : Type*} [Fintype V] [LinearOrder A]
    (P : V → A → A → Prop) [∀ v, DecidableRel (P v)]
    (hasymm : ∀ v x y, P v x y → ¬ P v y x)
    (peak : V → A) (hsp : ∀ v, is_single_peaked (P v) (peak v))
    (m : A) (hm : Fintype.card V < 2 * (Finset.filter (fun v => peak v ≤ m) Finset.univ).card)
    (y : A) (hym : m < y) :
    (Finset.filter (fun v => P v y m) Finset.univ).card < (Finset.filter (fun v => P v m y) Finset.univ).card
declarations.source:
/-- Under single-peaked preferences, if strictly more than half of voters have peak at most m, then for any y > m strictly fewer voters prefer y to m than prefer m to y. -/
theorem single_peaked_median_defeats_greater {V A : Type*} [Fintype V] [LinearOrder A]
    (P : V → A → A → Prop) [∀ v, DecidableRel (P v)]
    (hasymm : ∀ v x y, P v x y → ¬ P v y x)
    (peak : V → A) (hsp : ∀ v, is_single_peaked (P v) (peak v))
    (m : A) (hm : Fintype.card V < 2 * (Finset.filter (fun v => peak v ≤ m) Finset.univ).card)
    (y : A) (hym : m < y) :
    (Finset.filter (fun v => P v y m) Finset.univ).card < (Finset.filter (fun v => P v m y) Finset.univ).card := by
  classical
  set S := Finset.filter (fun v => peak v ≤ m) Finset.univ
  set M := Finset.filter (fun v => P v m y) Finset.univ
  set Y := Finset.filter (fun v => P v y m) Finset.univ
  have hSM : S ⊆ M := by
    intro v hv
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hv ⊢
    refine ⟨hv.1, ?_⟩
    apply hsp v y m
    right
    exact ⟨hv.2, hym⟩
  have hS_card : S.card ≤ M.card := Finset.card_le_card hSM
  have hdisj : Disjoint Y S := by
    rw [Finset.disjoint_left]
    intro v hvY hvS
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hvY hvS
    have hPmy : P v m y := by
      apply hsp v y m
      right
      exact ⟨hvS.2, hym⟩
    exact hasymm v m y hPmy hvY.2
  have hle : Y.card + S.card ≤ Fintype.card V := by
    have hsub : Y ∪ S ⊆ Finset.univ := Finset.subset_univ (Y ∪ S)
    have hunion := Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisj
    have hcard := Finset.card_le_card hsub
    rw [hunion] at hcard
    rw [Finset.card_univ] at hcard
    exact hcard
  change Y.card < M.card
  have hm' : Fintype.card V < 2 * S.card := hm
  omega
declarations.citation: Duncan Black, 'On the Rationale of Group Decision-making', Journal of Political Economy 56(1):23-34 (1948)
declarations.reading:
Let `V` be a finite type (representing voters) and `A` a linearly ordered type (representing alternatives).

Let `P : V → A → A → Prop` be a binary relation on `A` for each `v : V`, with `P v` decidable for all `v`. Assume that for all `v : V` and all `x, y : A`, `P v x y` implies `¬ P v y x` (asymmetry).

Let `peak : V → A` be a function such that for every voter `v : V`, `P v` is single-peaked at `peak v` (in the sense of `is_single_peaked`).

Let `m : A` be an alternative such that strictly more than half of all voters have their peak less than or equal to `m` (specifically, `Fintype.card V < 2 * |{v : V | peak v ≤ m}|`).

Let `y : A` be an alternative strictly greater than `m` (`m < y`).

Then the number of voters `v : V` for whom `P v y m` holds is strictly less than the number of voters `v : V` for whom `P v m y` holds.

explanation.summary: The proof compares the number of voters who prefer y to m with those who prefer m to y by focusing on the majority S of voters whose peak is at most m. By single-peakedness, every voter in S prefers m to y, meaning S is a subset of the voters preferring m to y and is disjoint from the voters preferring y to m. Since these two groups are disjoint subsets of all voters, their combined cardinality cannot exceed the total population; combined with the fact that S contains strictly more than half of all voters, this forces strictly fewer voters to prefer y over m than prefer m over y.

steps.claim: Define the three relevant subsets of voters: S (peaks at most m), M (preferring m to y), and Y (preferring y to m).
steps.explanation: Assuming classical logic, we introduce names for three subsets of the finite voter set V: S = {v ∈ V | peak(v) ≤ m}, M = {v ∈ V | P v m y}, and Y = {v ∈ V | P v y m}.
steps.code:
classical
  set S := Finset.filter (fun v => peak v ≤ m) Finset.univ
  set M := Finset.filter (fun v => P v m y) Finset.univ
  set Y := Finset.filter (fun v => P v y m) Finset.univ

steps.claim: S ⊆ M, and consequently |S| ≤ |M|.
steps.explanation: Take any voter v ∈ S, so peak(v) ≤ m. Since m < y, the peak lies to the left of both m and y (peak(v) ≤ m < y). By the single-peakedness hypothesis (hsp), voter v prefers m to y, so v ∈ M. Thus S ⊆ M, which implies |S| ≤ |M| by monotonicity of cardinality (Finset.card_le_card).
steps.code:
have hSM : S ⊆ M := by
    intro v hv
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hv ⊢
    refine ⟨hv.1, ?_⟩
    apply hsp v y m
    right
    exact ⟨hv.2, hym⟩
  have hS_card : S.card ≤ M.card := Finset.card_le_card hSM

steps.claim: The subsets Y and S are disjoint.
steps.explanation: By Finset.disjoint_left, it suffices to show that no voter belongs to both Y and S. If v ∈ S, single-peakedness implies that v prefers m to y (P v m y). If v ∈ Y, then v prefers y to m (P v y m). But preferences are asymmetric (hasymm), so both cannot hold simultaneously.
steps.code:
have hdisj : Disjoint Y S := by
    rw [Finset.disjoint_left]
    intro v hvY hvS
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hvY hvS
    have hPmy : P v m y := by
      apply hsp v y m
      right
      exact ⟨hvS.2, hym⟩
    exact hasymm v m y hPmy hvY.2

steps.explanation: Because Y and S are disjoint, the cardinality of their union is |Y| + |S| by Finset.card_union_of_disjoint. Since Y ∪ S is a subset of all voters V (Finset.subset_univ), its cardinality is at most |V| by Finset.card_le_card and Finset.card_univ.
steps.code:
have hle : Y.card + S.card ≤ Fintype.card V := by
    have hsub : Y ∪ S ⊆ Finset.univ := Finset.subset_univ (Y ∪ S)
    have hunion := Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisj
    have hcard := Finset.card_le_card hsub
    rw [hunion] at hcard
    rw [Finset.card_univ] at hcard
    exact hcard

steps.explanation: The goal is to show |Y| < |M|. We know that |Y| + |S| ≤ |V|, that |V| < 2 * |S| by the majority hypothesis (hm), and that |S| ≤ |M|. Together, these inequalities force |Y| < |S| ≤ |M|, which the omega tactic establishes via Presburger arithmetic.
steps.code:
change Y.card < M.card
  have hm' : Fintype.card V < 2 * S.card := hm
  omega

glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to a filtered finite set if and only if it belongs to the original set and satisfies the predicate.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card: If one finite set is a subset of another, its cardinality is at most that of the superset.
glossary.Finset.disjoint_left: Two finite sets are disjoint if and only if no element of the first belongs to the second.
glossary.Finset.subset_univ: Every finite set of elements of a finite type is a subset of the universal set.
glossary.Finset.card_union_of_disjoint: The cardinality of the union of two disjoint finite sets is the sum of their cardinalities.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal set of a finite type equals the cardinality of that type.

declarations.name: single_peaked_median_defeats_less
declarations.informal: Under single-peaked preferences with asymmetric preferences, if strictly more than half of the voters have peak at least m, then for any alternative y < m, the number of voters preferring y to m is strictly less than the number preferring m to y.
declarations.statement:
theorem single_peaked_median_defeats_less {V A : Type*} [Fintype V] [LinearOrder A]
    (P : V → A → A → Prop) [∀ v, DecidableRel (P v)]
    (hasymm : ∀ v x y, P v x y → ¬ P v y x)
    (peak : V → A) (hsp : ∀ v, is_single_peaked (P v) (peak v))
    (m : A) (hm : Fintype.card V < 2 * (Finset.filter (fun v => m ≤ peak v) Finset.univ).card)
    (y : A) (hym : y < m) :
    (Finset.filter (fun v => P v y m) Finset.univ).card < (Finset.filter (fun v => P v m y) Finset.univ).card
declarations.source:
/-- Under single-peaked preferences, an alternative strictly to the left of a right-majority median is majority defeated. -/
theorem single_peaked_median_defeats_less {V A : Type*} [Fintype V] [LinearOrder A]
    (P : V → A → A → Prop) [∀ v, DecidableRel (P v)]
    (hasymm : ∀ v x y, P v x y → ¬ P v y x)
    (peak : V → A) (hsp : ∀ v, is_single_peaked (P v) (peak v))
    (m : A) (hm : Fintype.card V < 2 * (Finset.filter (fun v => m ≤ peak v) Finset.univ).card)
    (y : A) (hym : y < m) :
    (Finset.filter (fun v => P v y m) Finset.univ).card < (Finset.filter (fun v => P v m y) Finset.univ).card := by
  classical
  set Sy := Finset.filter (fun v => P v y m) Finset.univ
  set Sm := Finset.filter (fun v => P v m y) Finset.univ
  set Speak := Finset.filter (fun v => m ≤ peak v) Finset.univ
  have hsub : Speak ⊆ Sm := by
    intro v hv
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hv ⊢
    refine ⟨hv.1, ?_⟩
    apply hsp v y m
    left
    exact ⟨hym, hv.2⟩
  have hcard_sub : Speak.card ≤ Sm.card := Finset.card_le_card hsub
  have hdisj : Disjoint Sy Sm := by
    rw [Finset.disjoint_filter]
    intro v _ hp
    exact hasymm v y m hp
  have hsum : Sy.card + Sm.card ≤ Fintype.card V := by
    have := Finset.card_le_univ (Sy ∪ Sm)
    rw [Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisj] at this
    exact this
  omega
declarations.citation: Black (1948), The Decisions of a Committee Using a Special Majority
declarations.reading:
Given a finite type $V$ of voters and a linearly ordered type $A$ of alternatives:
Let $P : V \to A \to A \to \mathrm{Prop}$ be a relation such that each $P(v)$ is decidable.
Assume that for all $v \in V$ and all $x, y \in A$, $P\ v\ x\ y \implies \neg P\ v\ y\ x$ (asymmetry).
Let $\mathrm{peak} : V \to A$ be a function such that for all $v \in V$, $P(v)$ is single-peaked with respect to $\mathrm{peak}(v)$ (in the sense of `is_single_peaked`).
Let $m \in A$ be an alternative such that strictly more than half of all voters have their peak greater than or equal to $m$, i.e., $|V| < 2 \cdot |\{v \in V \mid m \le \mathrm{peak}(v)\}|$.
Let $y \in A$ be an alternative such that $y < m$.
Then the number of voters $v \in V$ for whom $P\ v\ y\ m$ holds is strictly less than the number of voters $v \in V$ for whom $P\ v\ m\ y$ holds.

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by a counting argument using single-peakedness and preference asymmetry. First, single-peakedness implies that every voter with peak at least $m$ strictly prefers $m$ to any alternative $y < m$, so this group of voters forms a subset of those preferring $m$ to $y$. Second, preference asymmetry ensures that the voters preferring $y$ to $m$ and those preferring $m$ to $y$ are disjoint, bounding their combined size by the total electorate. Since the voters with peak at least $m$ constitute a strict majority, those preferring $m$ to $y$ must strictly outnumber those preferring $y$ to $m$.

steps.claim: Define the sets of voters $S_y$ (preferring $y$ to $m$), $S_m$ (preferring $m$ to $y$), and $S_{\\text{peak}}$ (having peak at least $m$).
steps.explanation: We enable classical reasoning and introduce abbreviations for the three relevant finite sets of voters: $S_y = \\{v \\in V \\mid P(v, y, m)\\}$, $S_m = \\{v \\in V \\mid P(v, m, y)\\}$, and $S_{\\text{peak}} = \\{v \\in V \\mid m \\le \\text{peak}(v)\\}$.
steps.code:
classical
  set Sy := Finset.filter (fun v => P v y m) Finset.univ
  set Sm := Finset.filter (fun v => P v m y) Finset.univ
  set Speak := Finset.filter (fun v => m ≤ peak v) Finset.univ

steps.claim: Every voter whose peak is at least $m$ prefers $m$ to $y$, so $S_{\\text{peak}} \\subseteq S_m$ and $|S_{\\text{peak}}| \\le |S_m|$.
steps.explanation: Let $v \\in S_{\\text{peak}}$, so $m \\le \\text{peak}(v)$. Given $y < m$, we have $y < m \\le \\text{peak}(v)$. By definition of single-peaked preferences (hypothesis `hsp`), whenever an alternative $m$ lies between $y$ and the voter's peak, the voter prefers $m$ to $y$. Hence $P(v, m, y)$ holds, placing $v$ in $S_m$. Since $S_{\\text{peak}} \\subseteq S_m$, monotonicity of cardinality (`Finset.card_le_card`) yields $|S_{\\text{peak}}| \\le |S_m|$.
steps.code:
have hsub : Speak ⊆ Sm := by
    intro v hv
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hv ⊢
    refine ⟨hv.1, ?_⟩
    apply hsp v y m
    left
    exact ⟨hym, hv.2⟩
  have hcard_sub : Speak.card ≤ Sm.card := Finset.card_le_card hsub

steps.claim: The sets $S_y$ and $S_m$ are disjoint.
steps.explanation: By `Finset.disjoint_filter`, the two filtered sets are disjoint if no voter satisfies both conditions. If a voter $v$ prefers $y$ to $m$, the asymmetry assumption on preferences (`hasymm`) guarantees that $v$ does not prefer $m$ to $y$, so $v \\notin S_m$.
steps.code:
have hdisj : Disjoint Sy Sm := by
    rw [Finset.disjoint_filter]
    intro v _ hp
    exact hasymm v y m hp

steps.explanation: The union $S_y \\cup S_m$ is a subset of all voters $V$, so its size is at most $|V|$ by `Finset.card_le_univ`. Because $S_y$ and $S_m$ are disjoint, the size of their union equals the sum of their individual sizes (`Finset.card_union_of_disjoint`), giving $|S_y| + |S_m| \\le |V|$.
steps.code:
have hsum : Sy.card + Sm.card ≤ Fintype.card V := by
    have := Finset.card_le_univ (Sy ∪ Sm)
    rw [Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisj] at this
    exact this

steps.explanation: By hypothesis `hm`, strictly more than half of the voters have their peak at least $m$, so $|V| < 2 \\cdot |S_{\\text{peak}}|$. Combining this with $|S_{\\text{peak}}| \\le |S_m|$ gives $|V| < 2 \\cdot |S_m|$. Together with $|S_y| + |S_m| \\le |V|$, we obtain $|S_y| + |S_m| < 2 \\cdot |S_m|$, which simplifies to $|S_y| < |S_m|$. The `omega` tactic verifies this linear arithmetic over the natural numbers.
steps.code: omega

glossary.Finset.card_le_card: If one finite set is a subset of another, its cardinality is less than or equal to the cardinality of the other.
glossary.Finset.disjoint_filter: Two subsets obtained by filtering the same set with two predicates are disjoint if and only if no element satisfies both predicates simultaneously.
glossary.Finset.card_le_univ: The cardinality of any finite subset of a finite type is at most the total cardinality of the type.
glossary.Finset.card_union_of_disjoint: The cardinality of the union of two disjoint finite sets is the sum of their individual cardinalities.
