declarations.name: finset_has_no_unique_sums_sumset_of_balanced
declarations.informal: If B is a nonempty balanced finite subset of an abelian group, then its sumset B + B has no unique sums.
declarations.statement:
theorem finset_has_no_unique_sums_sumset_of_balanced {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G]
    [DecidableEq G] (B : Finset G) (hB : finset_is_midpoint_balanced B) :
    finset_has_no_unique_sums ((B ×ˢ B).image (fun x => x.1 + x.2))
declarations.source:
theorem finset_has_no_unique_sums_sumset_of_balanced {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G]
    [DecidableEq G] (B : Finset G) (hB : finset_is_midpoint_balanced B) :
    finset_has_no_unique_sums ((B ×ˢ B).image (fun x => x.1 + x.2)) := by
  classical
  set A := (B ×ˢ B).image (fun x : G × G => x.1 + x.2) with hA
  have memA : ∀ a ∈ B, ∀ b ∈ B, a + b ∈ A := fun a ha b hb =>
    Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨(a, b), Finset.mem_product.2 ⟨ha, hb⟩, rfl⟩
  -- two different unordered pairs with the same total give two representations
  have two : ∀ p q r t : G, p ∈ A → q ∈ A → r ∈ A → t ∈ A → p + q = r + t →
      r ≠ p → r ≠ q → 2 ≤ finset_unordered_sum_rep_count A (p + q) := by
    intro p q r t hp hq hr ht hsum hrp hrq
    unfold finset_unordered_sum_rep_count
    rw [Nat.succ_le_iff, Finset.one_lt_card]
    refine ⟨s(p, q), ?_, s(r, t), ?_, ?_⟩
    · simp [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff, hp, hq]
    · simp [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff, hr, ht, hsum]
    · intro h
      have : r ∈ s(p, q) := h ▸ Sym2.mem_mk_left r t
      rcases Sym2.mem_iff.1 this with h' | h'
      · exact hrp h'
      · exact hrq h'
  -- the repair of a pair `{x + x, x + y}`, from the balance of `x`
  have key : ∀ x ∈ B, ∀ y ∈ B, ∃ r ∈ A, ∃ t ∈ A, r + t = (x + x) + (x + y) ∧
      r ≠ x + x ∧ r ≠ x + y := by
    intro x hx y hy
    obtain ⟨u, hu, v, hv, hux, hvx, huv, hxuv⟩ := hB.2 x hx
    by_cases hu' : u + y = x + x
    · refine ⟨v + y, memA v hv y hy, u + x, memA u hu x hx, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [hxuv]; abel
      · intro h; exact huv (add_right_cancel (hu'.trans h.symm))
      · intro h; exact hvx (add_right_cancel h)
    · refine ⟨u + y, memA u hu y hy, v + x, memA v hv x hx, ?_, hu', ?_⟩
      · rw [hxuv]; abel
      · intro h; exact hux (add_right_cancel h)
  have fin : ∀ x ∈ B, ∀ y ∈ B, ∀ p q : G, p ∈ A → q ∈ A →
      ((p = x + x ∧ q = x + y) ∨ (p = x + y ∧ q = x + x)) →
      2 ≤ finset_unordered_sum_rep_count A (p + q) := by
    intro x hx y hy p q hp hq hpq
    obtain ⟨r, hr, t, ht, hs, hr1, hr2⟩ := key x hx y hy
    rcases hpq with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    · exact two _ _ r t hp hq hr ht hs.symm hr1 hr2
    · exact two _ _ r t hp hq hr ht (by rw [hs]; abel) hr2 hr1
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hB.1
    obtain ⟨u, hu, v, hv, -, -, huv, -⟩ := hB.2 b hb
    rw [Nat.succ_le_iff, Finset.one_lt_card]
    exact ⟨b + u, memA b hb u hu, b + v, memA b hb v hv, fun h => huv (add_left_cancel h)⟩
  · intro p hp q hq
    obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, hab, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hp
    obtain ⟨⟨c, d⟩, hcd, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hq
    obtain ⟨ha, hb⟩ := Finset.mem_product.1 hab
    obtain ⟨hc, hd⟩ := Finset.mem_product.1 hcd
    dsimp only at hp hq ⊢
    by_cases h1 : a + c ≠ a + b ∧ a + c ≠ c + d
    · exact two _ _ (a + c) (b + d) hp hq (memA a ha c hc) (memA b hb d hd) (by abel) h1.1 h1.2
    by_cases h2 : a + d ≠ a + b ∧ a + d ≠ c + d
    · exact two _ _ (a + d) (b + c) hp hq (memA a ha d hd) (memA b hb c hc) (by abel) h2.1 h2.2
    have hcb : c = b ∨ a = d := by
      by_contra hne
      push_neg at hne
      exact h1 ⟨fun h => hne.1 (add_left_cancel h),
        fun h => hne.2 (add_right_cancel (h.trans (add_comm c d)))⟩
    have hdb : d = b ∨ a = c := by
      by_contra hne
      push_neg at hne
      exact h2 ⟨fun h => hne.1 (add_left_cancel h), fun h => hne.2 (add_right_cancel h)⟩
    rcases hcb with hcb | had <;> rcases hdb with hdb | hac
    · exact fin b hb a ha _ _ hp hq (Or.inr ⟨add_comm a b, by rw [hcb, hdb]⟩)
    · have hab' : a = b := hac.trans hcb
      exact fin b hb d hd _ _ hp hq (Or.inl ⟨by rw [hab'], by rw [hcb]⟩)
    · have hab' : a = b := had.trans hdb
      exact fin b hb c hc _ _ hp hq (Or.inl ⟨by rw [hab'], by rw [hdb, add_comm]⟩)
    · exact fin a ha b hb _ _ hp hq (Or.inr ⟨rfl, by rw [← hac, ← had]⟩)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.09349 (A near-quadratic lower bound for sets with no unique sums), Lemma A.2. Stated in any abelian group (the paper: F_p); B + B is written as the image of B × B under addition.

explanation.summary: To show that the sumset $A = B + B$ of a midpoint-balanced finite set $B$ has no unique sums, we verify that $|A| \ge 2$ and that every sum of elements of $A$ has at least two unordered sum representations. The size condition $|A| \ge 2$ follows because any element $b \in B$ has distinct balance witnesses $u, v \in B$, yielding distinct sums $b + u, b + v \in A$. For any $p = a + b$ and $q = c + d$ in $A$, regrouping $(a + b) + (c + d)$ as $(a + c) + (b + d)$ or $(a + d) + (b + c)$ provides a second representation whenever these pairs are distinct from $\{p, q\}$. When both regroupings collapse, cancellation forces $\{p, q\}$ to be of the degenerate form $\{2x, x + y\}$ for some $x, y \in B$. In this degenerate case, the midpoint balance condition $2x = u + v$ supplies an alternative representation by splitting the total as $(u + y) + (v + x)$ or $(v + y) + (u + x)$.

steps.claim: The sumset $A = B + B$ is defined, and any sum $a + b$ with $a, b \in B$ belongs to $A$.
steps.explanation: We define $A$ as the image of the Cartesian product $B \times B$ under addition and establish the helper lemma `memA`: for all $a, b \in B$, the sum $a + b$ lies in $A$.
steps.code:
classical
  set A := (B ×ˢ B).image (fun x : G × G => x.1 + x.2) with hA
  have memA : ∀ a ∈ B, ∀ b ∈ B, a + b ∈ A := fun a ha b hb =>
    Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨(a, b), Finset.mem_product.2 ⟨ha, hb⟩, rfl⟩

steps.claim: If $p, q, r, t \in A$ satisfy $p + q = r + t$ with $r \ne p$ and $r \ne q$, then $p + q$ has at least two unordered sum representations in $A$.
steps.explanation: By definition, the representation count of $p + q$ is the cardinality of the fiber of addition on the symmetric square $A.sym2$. By `Nat.succ_le_iff` and `Finset.one_lt_card`, it suffices to exhibit two distinct elements in this fiber. We show $s(p, q)$ and $s(r, t)$ both belong to the fiber, and they are distinct because $r \ne p$ and $r \ne q$ prevent $r$ from belonging to $\{p, q\}$.
steps.code:
-- two different unordered pairs with the same total give two representations
  have two : ∀ p q r t : G, p ∈ A → q ∈ A → r ∈ A → t ∈ A → p + q = r + t →
      r ≠ p → r ≠ q → 2 ≤ finset_unordered_sum_rep_count A (p + q) := by
    intro p q r t hp hq hr ht hsum hrp hrq
    unfold finset_unordered_sum_rep_count
    rw [Nat.succ_le_iff, Finset.one_lt_card]
    refine ⟨s(p, q), ?_, s(r, t), ?_, ?_⟩
    · simp [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff, hp, hq]
    · simp [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff, hr, ht, hsum]
    · intro h
      have : r ∈ s(p, q) := h ▸ Sym2.mem_mk_left r t
      rcases Sym2.mem_iff.1 this with h' | h'
      · exact hrp h'
      · exact hrq h'

steps.claim: For any $x, y \in B$, there exist $r, t \in A$ with $r + t = 2x + (x + y)$ such that $r \ne 2x$ and $r \ne x + y$.
steps.explanation:
Because $B$ is midpoint-balanced, $x$ has distinct balance witnesses $u, v \in B \setminus \{x\}$ with $2x = u + v$. The candidates $u + y$ and $v + x$ in $A$ sum to $(u + v) + (x + y) = 2x + (x + y)$. If $u + y 
e 2x$, this pair works, since $u + y = x + y$ would imply $u = x$ by cancellation, a contradiction. If instead $u + y = 2x$, we take $v + y$ and $u + x$; then $v + y 
e 2x$ (which would force $v = u$) and $v + y 
e x + y$ (which would force $v = x$).
steps.code:
-- the repair of a pair `{x + x, x + y}`, from the balance of `x`
  have key : ∀ x ∈ B, ∀ y ∈ B, ∃ r ∈ A, ∃ t ∈ A, r + t = (x + x) + (x + y) ∧
      r ≠ x + x ∧ r ≠ x + y := by
    intro x hx y hy
    obtain ⟨u, hu, v, hv, hux, hvx, huv, hxuv⟩ := hB.2 x hx
    by_cases hu' : u + y = x + x
    · refine ⟨v + y, memA v hv y hy, u + x, memA u hu x hx, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [hxuv]; abel
      · intro h; exact huv (add_right_cancel (hu'.trans h.symm))
      · intro h; exact hvx (add_right_cancel h)
    · refine ⟨u + y, memA u hu y hy, v + x, memA v hv x hx, ?_, hu', ?_⟩
      · rw [hxuv]; abel
      · intro h; exact hux (add_right_cancel h)

steps.claim: Any sum of elements in $A$ forming an unordered pair $\{2x, x + y\}$ for $x, y \in B$ has representation count at least 2 in $A$.
steps.explanation: Applying the repair lemma `key` provides an alternative pair of summands $r, t \in A$ that total $2x + (x + y)$ and differ from $\{2x, x + y\}$. The criterion `two` then immediately guarantees at least two unordered representations.
steps.code:
have fin : ∀ x ∈ B, ∀ y ∈ B, ∀ p q : G, p ∈ A → q ∈ A →
      ((p = x + x ∧ q = x + y) ∨ (p = x + y ∧ q = x + x)) →
      2 ≤ finset_unordered_sum_rep_count A (p + q) := by
    intro x hx y hy p q hp hq hpq
    obtain ⟨r, hr, t, ht, hs, hr1, hr2⟩ := key x hx y hy
    rcases hpq with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    · exact two _ _ r t hp hq hr ht hs.symm hr1 hr2
    · exact two _ _ r t hp hq hr ht (by rw [hs]; abel) hr2 hr1

steps.claim: The sumset $A$ contains at least two distinct elements, so $|A| \ge 2$.
steps.explanation: To verify the first clause of `finset_has_no_unique_sums`, we choose an element $b \in B$ (nonempty by balance) and distinct balance witnesses $u, v \in B$. The sums $b + u$ and $b + v$ belong to $A$ and are distinct by additive cancellation of $b$, so $A$ has cardinality at least 2 by `Finset.one_lt_card`.
steps.code:
refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hB.1
    obtain ⟨u, hu, v, hv, -, -, huv, -⟩ := hB.2 b hb
    rw [Nat.succ_le_iff, Finset.one_lt_card]
    exact ⟨b + u, memA b hb u hu, b + v, memA b hb v hv, fun h => huv (add_left_cancel h)⟩

steps.claim: For $p = a + b$ and $q = c + d$ in $A$, if either generic regrouping $(a + c) + (b + d)$ or $(a + d) + (b + c)$ avoids $\{p, q\}$, then $p + q$ has representation count at least 2.
steps.explanation: Any elements $p, q \in A$ can be written as $a + b$ and $c + d$ with $a, b, c, d \in B$. Their sum can be rearranged as $(a + c) + (b + d)$ or $(a + d) + (b + c)$, each a sum of two elements of $A$. If $a + c$ differs from both $a + b$ and $c + d$, the first regrouping yields a second representation by lemma `two`. Otherwise, if $a + d$ differs from both, the second regrouping yields a second representation by lemma `two`.
steps.code:
· intro p hp q hq
    obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, hab, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hp
    obtain ⟨⟨c, d⟩, hcd, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hq
    obtain ⟨ha, hb⟩ := Finset.mem_product.1 hab
    obtain ⟨hc, hd⟩ := Finset.mem_product.1 hcd
    dsimp only at hp hq ⊢
    by_cases h1 : a + c ≠ a + b ∧ a + c ≠ c + d
    · exact two _ _ (a + c) (b + d) hp hq (memA a ha c hc) (memA b hb d hd) (by abel) h1.1 h1.2
    by_cases h2 : a + d ≠ a + b ∧ a + d ≠ c + d
    · exact two _ _ (a + d) (b + c) hp hq (memA a ha d hd) (memA b hb c hc) (by abel) h2.1 h2.2

steps.claim: If both generic regroupings collide with $\{p, q\}$, then $(c = b \lor a = d)$ and $(d = b \lor a = c)$.
steps.explanation: Failure of the first regrouping means $a + c = a + b$ or $a + c = c + d$, which cancels to $c = b$ or $a = d$. Similarly, failure of the second regrouping means $a + d = a + b$ or $a + d = c + d$, which cancels to $d = b$ or $a = c$.
steps.code:
have hcb : c = b ∨ a = d := by
      by_contra hne
      push_neg at hne
      exact h1 ⟨fun h => hne.1 (add_left_cancel h),
        fun h => hne.2 (add_right_cancel (h.trans (add_comm c d)))⟩
    have hdb : d = b ∨ a = c := by
      by_contra hne
      push_neg at hne
      exact h2 ⟨fun h => hne.1 (add_left_cancel h), fun h => hne.2 (add_right_cancel h)⟩

steps.claim: In all cases where both regroupings collide, the representation count of $p + q$ is at least 2.
steps.explanation: We analyze the four combinations of $c = b \lor a = d$ and $d = b \lor a = c$: if $c = b$ and $d = b$, then $\{p, q\} = \{b + a, 2b\}$; if $c = b$ and $a = c$, then $a = b$ and $\{p, q\} = \{2b, b + d\}$; if $a = d$ and $d = b$, then $a = b$ and $\{p, q\} = \{2b, b + c\}$; if $a = d$ and $a = c$, then $c = d$ and $\{p, q\} = \{a + b, 2a\}$. In every subcase, $\{p, q\}$ matches the form $\{2x, x + y\}$, so lemma `fin` applies and completes the proof.
steps.code:
rcases hcb with hcb | had <;> rcases hdb with hdb | hac
    · exact fin b hb a ha _ _ hp hq (Or.inr ⟨add_comm a b, by rw [hcb, hdb]⟩)
    · have hab' : a = b := hac.trans hcb
      exact fin b hb d hd _ _ hp hq (Or.inl ⟨by rw [hab'], by rw [hcb]⟩)
    · have hab' : a = b := had.trans hdb
      exact fin b hb c hc _ _ hp hq (Or.inl ⟨by rw [hab'], by rw [hdb, add_comm]⟩)
    · exact fin a ha b hb _ _ hp hq (Or.inr ⟨rfl, by rw [← hac, ← had]⟩)

glossary.add_comm: In an abelian group, addition is commutative: $a + b = b + a$.
glossary.add_left_cancel: In an additive group, left cancellation holds: $c + a = c + b$ implies $a = b$.
glossary.add_right_cancel: In an additive group, right cancellation holds: $a + c = b + c$ implies $a = b$.
glossary.Finset.mem_image.1: An element $y$ belongs to the image $f(s)$ if and only if there is some $x \in s$ with $f(x) = y$; here used in the forward direction.
glossary.Finset.mem_image.2: An element $y$ belongs to the image $f(s)$ if there is some $x \in s$ with $f(x) = y$; here used in the reverse direction to construct membership.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to the filtered finset $\{x \in s \mid P(x)\}$ if and only if it belongs to $s$ and satisfies $P$.
glossary.Finset.mem_product.1: A pair $(x, y)$ belongs to the Cartesian product $s \times t$ implies $x \in s$ and $y \in t$.
glossary.Finset.mem_product.2: If $x \in s$ and $y \in t$, then $(x, y) \in s \times t$.
glossary.Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff: An unordered pair $s(a, b)$ belongs to the symmetric square $s.sym2$ if and only if both $a \in s$ and $b \in s$.
glossary.Finset.one_lt_card: A finite set has cardinality strictly greater than 1 if and only if it contains at least two distinct elements.
glossary.Nat.succ_le_iff: For natural numbers, $m + 1 \le n$ if and only if $m < n$.
glossary.Or.inl: If $A$ holds, then the disjunction $A \lor B$ holds.
glossary.Or.inr: If $B$ holds, then the disjunction $A \lor B$ holds.
glossary.Sym2.mem_iff.1: If an element belongs to an unordered pair $s(x, y)$, it equals either $x$ or $y$.
glossary.Sym2.mem_mk_left: The element $x$ is always a member of the unordered pair $s(x, y)$.

caveats: Lean formalizes unordered pairs of elements using the symmetric square type `Sym2 G`, with notation `s(x, y)`, and evaluates the number of unordered representations by filtering the symmetric square `A.sym2`.

declarations.name: cycle_labeling_complete
declarations.informal: Placing the labels L (a permutation of 1, …, n) in order around an n-cycle gives a complete cycle: every k ∈ {1, …, n(n+1)/2} is the sum of the labels on some arc (l ∈ {1, …, n} consecutive positions starting at some position i < n).
declarations.statement: def cycle_labeling_complete (n : ℕ) (L : List ℕ) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- The labels `L` (a list of length `n`), placed in order around an `n`-cycle, form a complete cycle: `L` is a permutation of `1, …, n`, and every `k ∈ {1, …, n(n+1)/2}` is the sum of the labels on some arc, i.e. on `l ∈ {1, …, n}` consecutive positions of the cycle starting at a position `i < n`. -/
def cycle_labeling_complete (n : ℕ) (L : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  L.Perm (List.range' 1 n) ∧ ∀ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n * (n + 1) / 2),
    ∃ i < n, ∃ l ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, (((L ++ L).drop i).take l).sum = k
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.08889 (Consecutive Cycle Sums), Sec. 1–2 (complete n-cycle; arcs and arc sums), for an arbitrary placement of 1, …, n around the cycle as in list entry OP-121 (the paper places them in increasing order). Arcs are all windows of length 1..n of the doubled list.

declarations.name: simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing
declarations.informal: D_v(G): the dominating sets of G that contain v, where S dominates G when every vertex is in S or adjacent to a vertex of S.
declarations.statement:
def simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) : Finset (Finset V)
declarations.source:
/-- `𝒟_v(G)`: the dominating sets of `G` that contain the vertex `v` (a set `S` dominates `G` when every vertex is in `S` or adjacent to a vertex of `S`). -/
def simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) : Finset (Finset V) :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun S => v ∈ S ∧ ∀ w, w ∈ S ∨ ∃ u ∈ S, G.Adj u w)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.11446 (On the local average order of dominating sets), Sec. 1 (dominating sets; D_v(G)).

declarations.name: simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order
declarations.informal: avd_v(G): the local average order of dominating sets containing v, i.e. the average size of the dominating sets of G that contain v.
declarations.statement:
def simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) : ℚ
declarations.source:
/-- `avd_v(G)`: the local average order of dominating sets containing `v`, the average size of the dominating sets of `G` that contain `v`. -/
def simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) : ℚ :=
  (∑ S ∈ simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing G v, (S.card : ℚ)) /
    (simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing G v).card
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.11446 (On the local average order of dominating sets), Sec. 1 (avd_v(G) = Σ_{S ∈ D_v(G)} |S| / |D_v(G)|).

declarations.name: simple_graph_leaf_neighbor_count
declarations.informal: The number of leaf neighbours (neighbours of degree one) of a vertex v; v is an l-stem when this number is l ≥ 1.
declarations.statement:
def simple_graph_leaf_neighbor_count {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) : ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- The number of leaf neighbours of `v` (neighbours of degree one): `v` is an `l`-stem when this is `l ≥ 1`. -/
def simple_graph_leaf_neighbor_count {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) : ℕ :=
  ((G.neighborFinset v).filter (fun u => G.degree u = 1)).card
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.11446 (On the local average order of dominating sets), Sec. 1 (leaf, stem, l-stem: a stem with l leaf neighbours).

declarations.name: simple_graph_is_star_like
declarations.informal: G is star-like: every vertex is either a leaf (degree one) or an l-stem with 1 ≤ l ≤ 2.
declarations.statement:
def simple_graph_is_star_like {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- `G` is star-like: every vertex is a leaf (degree one) or an `l`-stem with `1 ≤ l ≤ 2`. -/
def simple_graph_is_star_like {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Prop :=
  ∀ w, G.degree w = 1 ∨ (1 ≤ simple_graph_leaf_neighbor_count G w ∧
    simple_graph_leaf_neighbor_count G w ≤ 2)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.11446 (On the local average order of dominating sets), Lemma 5.1 (star-like graphs: every vertex is a leaf or an l-stem with l ≤ 2).

declarations.name: simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_complete_four
declarations.informal: In K₄, the dominating sets containing a fixed vertex have average size 5/2 = (4+1)/2.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_complete_four :
    simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)) 0 = 5 / 2
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_complete_four :
    simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)) 0 = 5 / 2 := by
  have h1 : (simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)) 0).card = 8 := by
    unfold simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing; decide
  have h2 : ∑ S ∈ simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)) 0,
      S.card = 20 := by
    unfold simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing; decide
  unfold simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order
  rw [← Nat.cast_sum, h1, h2]; norm_num
declarations.citation: Sanity check of the definitions of arXiv:2610.11446 (On the local average order of dominating sets). Sec. 1 gives avd_v(K_n) = (n+1)/2.

explanation.summary: The average size of a dominating set containing vertex 0 in the complete graph K₄ is computed directly from its definition as the total size of all such dominating sets divided by their count. In K₄, any set containing 0 is automatically dominating, yielding 2³ = 8 such sets whose sizes sum to 20. The proof determines both the count (8) and the sum of sizes (20) by exhaustive computational evaluation, and then simplifies the quotient 20 / 8 to 5 / 2.

steps.claim: There are 8 dominating sets in K₄ that contain vertex 0.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of dominating sets containing a given vertex leaves a decidable predicate over the power set of Fin 4. The `decide` tactic checks every subset of the 4-element vertex set exhaustively to determine that exactly 8 subsets contain 0 and dominate the complete graph.

declarations.name: finset_down_closed_family_avg_card_le
declarations.informal: A nonempty downward-closed family I of subsets of a finite set X has average set size at most |X|/2, with equality exactly when I is the whole power set of X.
declarations.statement:
theorem finset_down_closed_family_avg_card_le {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (X : Finset α)
    (I : Finset (Finset α)) (hI : I.Nonempty) (hsub : ∀ S ∈ I, S ⊆ X)
    (hdown : ∀ S ∈ I, ∀ T ⊆ S, T ∈ I) :
    (∑ S ∈ I, (S.card : ℚ)) / I.card ≤ (X.card : ℚ) / 2 ∧
      ((∑ S ∈ I, (S.card : ℚ)) / I.card = (X.card : ℚ) / 2 ↔ I = X.powerset)
declarations.source:
theorem finset_down_closed_family_avg_card_le {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (X : Finset α)
    (I : Finset (Finset α)) (hI : I.Nonempty) (hsub : ∀ S ∈ I, S ⊆ X)
    (hdown : ∀ S ∈ I, ∀ T ⊆ S, T ∈ I) :
    (∑ S ∈ I, (S.card : ℚ)) / I.card ≤ (X.card : ℚ) / 2 ∧
      ((∑ S ∈ I, (S.card : ℚ)) / I.card = (X.card : ℚ) / 2 ↔ I = X.powerset) := by
  classical
  -- `a x` members containing `x`, `b x` members avoiding `x`
  set a : α → ℕ := fun x => (I.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)).card with ha
  set b : α → ℕ := fun x => (I.filter (fun S => x ∉ S)).card with hb
  have hab : ∀ x, a x + b x = I.card := fun x =>
    Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not _
  have hsum : ∑ S ∈ I, S.card = ∑ x ∈ X, a x := by
    have h : ∀ S ∈ I, S.card = ∑ x ∈ X, if x ∈ S then 1 else 0 := by
      intro S hS
      rw [← Finset.card_filter, Finset.filter_mem_eq_inter,
        Finset.inter_eq_right.2 (hsub S hS)]
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl h, Finset.sum_comm]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => ?_
    simp only [ha]; rw [Finset.card_filter]
  -- deleting `x` is injective on the members containing `x`
  have erase_inj : ∀ x, Set.InjOn (fun S : Finset α => S.erase x)
      ↑(I.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)) := by
    intro x S hS T hT h
    simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at hS hT
    rw [← Finset.insert_erase hS.2, ← Finset.insert_erase hT.2]
    exact congrArg (insert x) h
  have erase_maps : ∀ x, ∀ S ∈ I.filter (fun S => x ∈ S), S.erase x ∈ I.filter (fun S => x ∉ S) := by
    intro x S hS
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hS ⊢
    exact ⟨hdown S hS.1 _ (Finset.erase_subset x S), by simp⟩
  have hle : ∀ x, a x ≤ b x := by
    intro x
    simp only [ha, hb]; rw [← Finset.card_image_of_injOn (erase_inj x)]
    apply Finset.card_le_card
    intro T hT
    obtain ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hT
    exact erase_maps x S hS
  -- with insertion also closed, the two counts agree
  have hge : (∀ S ∈ I, ∀ x ∈ X, x ∉ S → insert x S ∈ I) → ∀ x ∈ X, b x ≤ a x := by
    intro hup x hx
    have inj : Set.InjOn (fun S : Finset α => insert x S) ↑(I.filter (fun S => x ∉ S)) := by
      intro S hS T hT h
      simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at hS hT
      rw [← Finset.erase_insert hS.2, ← Finset.erase_insert hT.2]
      exact congrArg (fun U => Finset.erase U x) h
    simp only [ha, hb]; rw [← Finset.card_image_of_injOn inj]
    apply Finset.card_le_card
    intro T hT
    obtain ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hT
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hS ⊢
    exact ⟨hup S hS.1 x hx hS.2, Finset.mem_insert_self x S⟩
  have htot : ∑ x ∈ X, (a x + b x) = X.card * I.card := by
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => hab x, Finset.sum_const, smul_eq_mul]
  have hIpos : (0 : ℚ) < I.card := by exact_mod_cast hI.card_pos
  have havg : (∑ S ∈ I, (S.card : ℚ)) / I.card = ((∑ x ∈ X, a x : ℕ) : ℚ) / I.card := by
    rw [← hsum, Nat.cast_sum]
  have hnat : 2 * ∑ x ∈ X, a x ≤ X.card * I.card := by
    rw [← htot, Finset.sum_add_distrib, two_mul]
    exact Nat.add_le_add_left (Finset.sum_le_sum fun x _ => hle x) _
  refine ⟨?_, ⟨fun heq => ?_, fun hI' => ?_⟩⟩
  · rw [havg, div_le_iff₀ hIpos]
    have : (2 : ℚ) * ((∑ x ∈ X, a x : ℕ) : ℚ) ≤ (X.card : ℚ) * I.card := by exact_mod_cast hnat
    linarith
  · -- equality: every count agrees, so the family is closed under insertion
    rw [havg, div_eq_iff hIpos.ne'] at heq
    have h2 : 2 * ∑ x ∈ X, a x = X.card * I.card := by
      have : (2 : ℚ) * ((∑ x ∈ X, a x : ℕ) : ℚ) = (X.card : ℚ) * I.card := by linarith
      exact_mod_cast this
    have hsab : ∑ x ∈ X, a x = ∑ x ∈ X, b x := by
      rw [← htot, Finset.sum_add_distrib] at h2
      omega
    have hpt := (Finset.sum_eq_sum_iff_of_le fun x _ => hle x).1 hsab
    have hup : ∀ S ∈ I, ∀ x ∈ X, x ∉ S → insert x S ∈ I := by
      intro S hS x hx hxS
      have himg : (I.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)).image (fun S => S.erase x) =
          I.filter (fun S => x ∉ S) := by
        apply Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le
        · intro T hT
          obtain ⟨U, hU, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hT
          exact erase_maps x U hU
        · rw [Finset.card_image_of_injOn (erase_inj x)]
          exact (hpt x hx).ge
      have hmem : S ∈ (I.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)).image (fun S => S.erase x) := by
        rw [himg, Finset.mem_filter]; exact ⟨hS, hxS⟩
      obtain ⟨T, hT, hTS⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hmem
      rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hT
      rw [← hTS, Finset.insert_erase hT.2]
      exact hT.1
    have hempty : ∅ ∈ I := by
      obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := hI
      exact hdown S hS ∅ (Finset.empty_subset S)
    ext T
    rw [Finset.mem_powerset]
    refine ⟨hsub T, fun hT => ?_⟩
    induction T using Finset.induction_on with
    | empty => exact hempty
    | insert x T hxT ih =>
      have hTX : T ⊆ X := (Finset.subset_insert x T).trans hT
      exact hup T (ih hTX) x (hT (Finset.mem_insert_self x T)) hxT
  · -- the whole power set: the two counts agree
    have hup : ∀ S ∈ I, ∀ x ∈ X, x ∉ S → insert x S ∈ I := by
      intro S hS x hx _
      rw [hI', Finset.mem_powerset] at hS ⊢
      exact Finset.insert_subset hx hS
    have hpt : ∀ x ∈ X, a x = b x := fun x hx => le_antisymm (hle x) (hge hup x hx)
    have h2 : 2 * ∑ x ∈ X, a x = X.card * I.card := by
      rw [← htot, Finset.sum_add_distrib, two_mul, Finset.sum_congr rfl hpt]
    rw [havg, div_eq_iff hIpos.ne']
    have : (2 : ℚ) * ((∑ x ∈ X, a x : ℕ) : ℚ) = (X.card : ℚ) * I.card := by exact_mod_cast h2
    linarith
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.11446 (On the local average order of dominating sets), Lemma 2.1 (quoted there from earlier work on the average order of dominating sets, Proposition 2.3), serving Theorem 2.2.

explanation.summary: By double counting element-set incidences, the total sum of set sizes in I equals the sum over x ∈ X of the number a(x) of members containing x. Because I is downward-closed, deleting x injectively maps members containing x to members avoiding x, which gives a(x) ≤ b(x) and thus 2 a(x) ≤ a(x) + b(x) = |I| for each x. Summing this over X proves that the average cardinality is at most |X|/2. Equality holds precisely when a(x) = b(x) for all x ∈ X, making deletion a bijection; this forces I to be closed under element insertion, which inductively implies that I is the full power set of X.

steps.claim: For every element x, the number a(x) of sets in I containing x plus the number b(x) avoiding x equals |I|.
steps.explanation: We define a(x) as the cardinality of {S ∈ I | x ∈ S} and b(x) as the cardinality of {S ∈ I | x ∉ S}. Partitioning I into members containing x and members avoiding x gives a(x) + b(x) = |I| for all x.

  set b : α → ℕ := fun x => (I.filter (fun S => x ∉ S)).card with hb
  have hab : ∀ x, a x + b x = I.card := fun x =>
    Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not _

steps.claim: The sum of the sizes of all sets in I equals the sum of a(x) over all x ∈ X.
steps.explanation: Because every set S in I is a subset of X, its cardinality |S| is the sum of the indicator function [x ∈ S] over x ∈ X. Exchanging the order of summation gives ∑_{S ∈ I} |S| = ∑_{x ∈ X} a(x).

        Finset.inter_eq_right.2 (hsub S hS)]
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl h, Finset.sum_comm]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => ?_
    simp only [ha]; rw [Finset.card_filter]

steps.explanation: The operation S ↦ S \ {x} is injective on {S ∈ I | x ∈ S} because reinserting x recovers S. Since I is downward-closed, S \ {x} belongs to I, and by construction it avoids x. Hence deletion injectively maps the sets containing x into the sets avoiding x, which implies a(x) ≤ b(x).

      ↑(I.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)) := by

    rw [← Finset.insert_erase hS.2, ← Finset.insert_erase hT.2]
    exact congrArg (insert x) h

    intro x S hS
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hS ⊢
    exact ⟨hdown S hS.1 _ (Finset.erase_subset x S), by simp⟩
  have hle : ∀ x, a x ≤ b x := by
    intro x
    simp only [ha, hb]; rw [← Finset.card_image_of_injOn (erase_inj x)]
    apply Finset.card_le_card
    intro T hT
    obtain ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hT
    exact erase_maps x S hS

steps.explanation: Under this hypothesis, the map S ↦ S ∪ {x} injectively sends {S ∈ I | x ∉ S} into {S ∈ I | x ∈ S}, since erasing x recovers S. Therefore, the size b(x) of the domain is at most the size a(x) of the codomain.

have hge : (∀ S ∈ I, ∀ x ∈ X, x ∉ S → insert x S ∈ I) → ∀ x ∈ X, b x ≤ a x := by
    intro hup x hx

      intro S hS T hT h
      simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at hS hT
      rw [← Finset.erase_insert hS.2, ← Finset.erase_insert hT.2]
      exact congrArg (fun U => Finset.erase U x) h
    simp only [ha, hb]; rw [← Finset.card_image_of_injOn inj]
    apply Finset.card_le_card
    intro T hT
    obtain ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hT

    rw [← htot, Finset.sum_add_distrib, two_mul]
    exact Nat.add_le_add_left (Finset.sum_le_sum fun x _ => hle x) _

steps.claim: The average set size in I is at most |X| / 2.
steps.explanation: We split the goal into the average inequality and the equivalence for equality. Using the relation ∑_{S ∈ I} |S| = ∑_{x ∈ X} a(x) and the fact that |I| > 0, dividing the integer inequality 2 ∑_{x ∈ X} a(x) ≤ |X| · |I| by 2 |I| gives (∑_{S ∈ I} |S|) / |I| ≤ |X| / 2.
steps.code:
refine ⟨?_, ⟨fun heq => ?_, fun hI' => ?_⟩⟩
  · rw [havg, div_le_iff₀ hIpos]
    have : (2 : ℚ) * ((∑ x ∈ X, a x : ℕ) : ℚ) ≤ (X.card : ℚ) * I.card := by exact_mod_cast hnat
    linarith

steps.claim: If the average set size in I equals |X| / 2, then I is the power set of X.
steps.explanation: Equality implies 2 ∑_{x ∈ X} a(x) = |X| · |I| = ∑_{x ∈ X} (a(x) + b(x)), so ∑_{x ∈ X} a(x) = ∑_{x ∈ X} b(x). Since a(x) ≤ b(x) pointwise, we must have a(x) = b(x) for all x ∈ X. The injection S ↦ S \ {x} between equinumerous finite sets is therefore surjective, meaning every set in I avoiding x comes from deleting x from a member of I; thus I is closed under inserting x. Since I is nonempty and downward-closed, ∅ ∈ I. By finite set induction, starting from ∅ and inserting elements of X shows every subset of X belongs to I, so I = powerset(X).
steps.code:
rw [havg, div_eq_iff hIpos.ne'] at heq
    have h2 : 2 * ∑ x ∈ X, a x = X.card * I.card := by
      have : (2 : ℚ) * ((∑ x ∈ X, a x : ℕ) : ℚ) = (X.card : ℚ) * I.card := by linarith
      exact_mod_cast this
    have hsab : ∑ x ∈ X, a x = ∑ x ∈ X, b x := by
      rw [← htot, Finset.sum_add_distrib] at h2
      omega
    have hpt := (Finset.sum_eq_sum_iff_of_le fun x _ => hle x).1 hsab
    have hup : ∀ S ∈ I, ∀ x ∈ X, x ∉ S → insert x S ∈ I := by
      intro S hS x hx hxS
      have himg : (I.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)).image (fun S => S.erase x) =
          I.filter (fun S => x ∉ S) := by
        apply Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le
        · intro T hT
          obtain ⟨U, hU, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hT
          exact erase_maps x U hU
        · rw [Finset.card_image_of_injOn (erase_inj x)]
          exact (hpt x hx).ge
      have hmem : S ∈ (I.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)).image (fun S => S.erase x) := by
        rw [himg, Finset.mem_filter]; exact ⟨hS, hxS⟩
      obtain ⟨T, hT, hTS⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hmem
      rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hT
      rw [← hTS, Finset.insert_erase hT.2]
      exact hT.1
    have hempty : ∅ ∈ I := by
      obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := hI
      exact hdown S hS ∅ (Finset.empty_subset S)
    ext T
    rw [Finset.mem_powerset]
    refine ⟨hsub T, fun hT => ?_⟩
    induction T using Finset.induction_on with
    | empty => exact hempty
    | insert x T hxT ih =>
      have hTX : T ⊆ X := (Finset.subset_insert x T).trans hT
      exact hup T (ih hTX) x (hT (Finset.mem_insert_self x T)) hxT

steps.claim: If I is the power set of X, then the average set size in I equals |X| / 2.
steps.explanation: When I is the full power set of X, it is closed under inserting elements of X, so b(x) ≤ a(x) for all x ∈ X. Combined with a(x) ≤ b(x), this gives a(x) = b(x) everywhere on X. Then 2 ∑_{x ∈ X} a(x) = ∑_{x ∈ X} (a(x) + b(x)) = |X| · |I|, which implies that the average set size is exactly |X| / 2.
steps.code:
have hup : ∀ S ∈ I, ∀ x ∈ X, x ∉ S → insert x S ∈ I := by
      intro S hS x hx _
      rw [hI', Finset.mem_powerset] at hS ⊢
      exact Finset.insert_subset hx hS
    have hpt : ∀ x ∈ X, a x = b x := fun x hx => le_antisymm (hle x) (hge hup x hx)
    have h2 : 2 * ∑ x ∈ X, a x = X.card * I.card := by
      rw [← htot, Finset.sum_add_distrib, two_mul, Finset.sum_congr rfl hpt]
    rw [havg, div_eq_iff hIpos.ne']
    have : (2 : ℚ) * ((∑ x ∈ X, a x : ℕ) : ℚ) = (X.card : ℚ) * I.card := by exact_mod_cast h2
    linarith

glossary.Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not: For any finite set and predicate, the number of elements satisfying the predicate plus the number not satisfying it equals the cardinality of the set.
glossary.Finset.card_filter: The number of elements in a finite set satisfying a predicate equals the sum over the set of the indicator function of the predicate.
glossary.Finset.filter_mem_eq_inter: Filtering a finite set by membership in another set equals the intersection of the two sets.
glossary.Finset.sum_congr: Two sums over finite sets are equal if the index sets are equal and the summands agree on every element.
glossary.Finset.sum_comm: Swapping the order of summation in a double sum over two finite sets preserves the sum.
glossary.Finset.coe_filter: The coercion to a set of a filtered finite set equals the set comprehension of elements satisfying the predicate.
glossary.Set.mem_ofPred_eq: Membership of an element in a set comprehension {y | p y} is equivalent to the predicate p holding for that element.
glossary.Finset.insert_erase: Inserting an element into a finite set from which it was erased recovers the original set, provided the element belonged to the set.
glossary.congrArg: Applying a function to equal inputs yields equal results.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to a filtered finite set if and only if it belongs to the set and satisfies the predicate.
glossary.Finset.erase_subset: Erasing an element from a finite set produces a subset of the original set.
glossary.Finset.card_image_of_injOn: If a map is injective on a finite set, the cardinality of its image equals the cardinality of the original set.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card: If one finite set is a subset of another, its cardinality is less than or equal to that of the superset.
glossary.Finset.erase_insert: Erasing an element from a set after inserting it recovers the original set, provided the element was not originally in the set.
glossary.Finset.mem_insert_self: An element always belongs to the set formed by inserting it into any finite set.
glossary.Finset.sum_const: Summing a constant value over a finite set equals the cardinality of the set scalar-multiplied by the constant.
glossary.smul_eq_mul: Scalar multiplication by a natural number in a semiring agrees with ordinary multiplication.
glossary.Nat.cast_sum: The coercion of a sum of natural numbers to another semiring equals the sum of the coerced terms.
glossary.Finset.sum_add_distrib: The sum of a pointwise sum of two functions over a finite set equals the sum of the first function plus the sum of the second.
glossary.two_mul: Multiplying an element by 2 is equal to adding the element to itself.
glossary.Nat.add_le_add_left: Adding a natural number to both sides of an inequality preserves the inequality.
glossary.Finset.sum_le_sum: If a function is pointwise at most another on a finite set, the sum of the first is at most the sum of the second.
glossary.div_le_iff₀: For a positive divisor, a quotient is at most a value if and only if the numerator is at most the product of the value and the divisor.
glossary.div_eq_iff: For a nonzero denominator, a quotient equals a value if and only if the numerator equals the product of the value and the denominator.
glossary.Finset.sum_eq_sum_iff_of_le: When one function is pointwise bounded by another on a finite set, their sums are equal if and only if the functions agree pointwise everywhere on the set.
glossary.Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le: If a finite set is a subset of another and has cardinality at least that of the other, the two sets are equal.
glossary.Finset.empty_subset: The empty set is a subset of every finite set.
glossary.Finset.mem_powerset: A finite set belongs to the powerset of another if and only if it is a subset of that set.
glossary.Finset.induction_on: To prove a property for all finite sets, it suffices to prove it for the empty set and show it is preserved under inserting an element.
glossary.Finset.subset_insert: A finite set is a subset of the set obtained by inserting an element into it.
glossary.Finset.insert_subset: Inserting an element belonging to a superset into a subset yields another subset of the superset.
glossary.le_antisymm: In a partial order, if two elements are less than or equal to each other, they are equal.

caveats: The double counting of incidences is formalized by writing the size of each subset as a sum of indicator variables over X and exchanging the order of summation.

To prove that the deletion map is surjective when a(x) = b(x), the proof uses Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le, which deduces equality of two finite sets from inclusion and equal cardinality, avoiding the need to construct an explicit inverse.

declarations.name: simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_ge
declarations.informal: For every finite graph G of order n and every vertex v, the dominating sets containing v have average size at least (n+1)/2, with equality if and only if v is adjacent to all other vertices (deg v = n − 1).
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_ge {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) :
    ((Fintype.card V : ℚ) + 1) / 2 ≤ simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v ∧
      (simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v = ((Fintype.card V : ℚ) + 1) / 2 ↔
        G.degree v = Fintype.card V - 1)
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_ge {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) :
    ((Fintype.card V : ℚ) + 1) / 2 ≤ simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v ∧
      (simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v = ((Fintype.card V : ℚ) + 1) / 2 ↔
        G.degree v = Fintype.card V - 1) := by
  classical
  set D := simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing G v with hD
  set n := Fintype.card V with hn
  set X : Finset V := Finset.univ.erase v with hX
  set I := D.image (fun S => Sᶜ) with hI
  have memD : ∀ S, S ∈ D ↔ v ∈ S ∧ ∀ w, w ∈ S ∨ ∃ u ∈ S, G.Adj u w := by
    intro S; rw [hD]; unfold simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing; simp
  have hcompl_inj : Set.InjOn (fun S : Finset V => Sᶜ) ↑D := fun S _ T _ h => compl_injective h
  have hDne : D.Nonempty := ⟨Finset.univ, (memD _).2 ⟨Finset.mem_univ v, fun w => Or.inl (Finset.mem_univ w)⟩⟩
  have hIne : I.Nonempty := hDne.image _
  have hIsub : ∀ T ∈ I, T ⊆ X := by
    intro T hT
    obtain ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hT
    intro w hw
    rw [hX, Finset.mem_erase]
    refine ⟨?_, Finset.mem_univ w⟩
    rintro rfl
    exact (Finset.mem_compl.1 hw) ((memD S).1 hS).1
  have hIdown : ∀ T ∈ I, ∀ U ⊆ T, U ∈ I := by
    intro T hT U hU
    obtain ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hT
    have hSU : S ⊆ Uᶜ := by
      intro w hw
      rw [Finset.mem_compl]
      intro hwU
      exact (Finset.mem_compl.1 (hU hwU)) hw
    refine Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨Uᶜ, (memD _).2 ⟨hSU ((memD S).1 hS).1, fun w => ?_⟩, compl_compl U⟩
    rcases ((memD S).1 hS).2 w with h | ⟨u, hu, hadj⟩
    · exact Or.inl (hSU h)
    · exact Or.inr ⟨u, hSU hu, hadj⟩
  have hcardI : I.card = D.card := Finset.card_image_of_injOn hcompl_inj
  have hsumI : ∑ T ∈ I, (T.card : ℚ) = ∑ S ∈ D, ((n : ℚ) - S.card) := by
    rw [hI, Finset.sum_image hcompl_inj]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun S _ => ?_
    rw [Finset.card_compl, Nat.cast_sub (Finset.card_le_univ S)]
  have hXcard : X.card = n - 1 := by rw [hX, Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ v)]; rfl
  have hn1 : 1 ≤ n := Fintype.card_pos_iff.2 ⟨v⟩
  have hDpos : (0 : ℚ) < D.card := by exact_mod_cast hDne.card_pos
  have key := finset_down_closed_family_avg_card_le X I hIne hIsub hIdown
  rw [hsumI, hcardI, hXcard, Nat.cast_sub hn1, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_const,
    nsmul_eq_mul] at key
  have havd : simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v = (∑ S ∈ D, (S.card : ℚ)) / D.card := rfl
  have hsplit : ((D.card : ℚ) * n - ∑ S ∈ D, (S.card : ℚ)) / D.card =
      n - (∑ S ∈ D, (S.card : ℚ)) / D.card := by
    field_simp
  rw [hsplit, Nat.cast_one] at key
  obtain ⟨k1, k2⟩ := key
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [havd]; push_cast at k1 ⊢; linarith
  · rw [havd]
    have e1 : (∑ S ∈ D, (S.card : ℚ)) / D.card = ((n : ℚ) + 1) / 2 ↔
        (n : ℚ) - (∑ S ∈ D, (S.card : ℚ)) / D.card = ((n : ℚ) - 1) / 2 := by
      constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith
    rw [e1, k2]
    -- the complements fill the power set iff `v` is adjacent to every other vertex
    have hdeg : G.degree v = n - 1 ↔ ∀ w, w ≠ v → G.Adj v w := by
      rw [← G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
      have hsubN : G.neighborFinset v ⊆ X := by
        intro w hw
        rw [hX, Finset.mem_erase]
        exact ⟨(G.ne_of_adj ((G.mem_neighborFinset v w).1 hw)).symm, Finset.mem_univ w⟩
      constructor
      · intro h w hw
        have heq : G.neighborFinset v = X :=
          Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le hsubN (by rw [hXcard, h])
        have : w ∈ X := by rw [hX, Finset.mem_erase]; exact ⟨hw, Finset.mem_univ w⟩
        rw [← heq, G.mem_neighborFinset] at this
        exact this
      · intro h
        have heq : G.neighborFinset v = X := by
          refine Finset.Subset.antisymm hsubN fun w hw => ?_
          rw [hX, Finset.mem_erase] at hw
          rw [G.mem_neighborFinset]; exact h w hw.1
        rw [heq, hXcard]
    rw [hdeg]
    constructor
    · intro hIX w hw
      have hXI : X ∈ I := by rw [hIX]; exact Finset.mem_powerset_self X
      obtain ⟨S, hS, hSX⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hXI
      have hSv : S = {v} := by
        rw [← compl_compl S, hSX, hX]
        ext u; simp
      rcases ((memD S).1 hS).2 w with h | ⟨u, hu, hadj⟩
      · rw [hSv, Finset.mem_singleton] at h; exact absurd h hw
      · rw [hSv, Finset.mem_singleton] at hu; rw [← hu]; exact hadj
    · intro hall
      refine Finset.Subset.antisymm (fun T hT => Finset.mem_powerset.2 (hIsub T hT)) fun T hT => ?_
      rw [Finset.mem_powerset] at hT
      have hvT : v ∈ Tᶜ := by
        rw [Finset.mem_compl]; intro h
        have := hT h
        rw [hX, Finset.mem_erase] at this
        exact this.1 rfl
      refine Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨Tᶜ, (memD _).2 ⟨hvT, fun w => ?_⟩, compl_compl T⟩
      by_cases hw : w = v
      · exact Or.inl (hw ▸ hvT)
      · exact Or.inr ⟨v, hvT, hall w hw⟩
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.11446 (On the local average order of dominating sets), Theorem 2.2.

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by rephrasing dominating sets containing v in terms of their complements in X = V \ {v}. The family of complements I = {Sᶜ | S ∈ D} forms a nonempty down-closed family of subsets of X, so a general bound on down-closed families (finset_down_closed_family_avg_card_le) implies its average size is at most |X| / 2 = (n - 1) / 2, with equality if and only if I = 𝒫(X). Converting back from complements expresses the average size of D as n - avg(I), immediately yielding avg(D) ≥ (n + 1) / 2, with equality precisely when {v} is a dominating set, which occurs if and only if deg(v) = n - 1.

steps.claim: Define the family D of dominating sets containing v, the order n = |V|, the universe X = V \ {v}, and the family of complements I = {Sᶜ | S ∈ D}, and unfold the membership condition for D.
steps.explanation: We work in classical logic. We name the family of dominating sets containing v as D, the total number of vertices as n, the set of all other vertices as X = V \ {v}, and the family of complements of sets in D as I. We then unfold the definition of dominating sets containing v to characterize membership in D: a set S ⊆ V belongs to D if and only if v ∈ S and every vertex w ∈ V is either in S or adjacent to some vertex in S.
steps.code:
classical
  set D := simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing G v with hD
  set n := Fintype.card V with hn
  set X : Finset V := Finset.univ.erase v with hX
  set I := D.image (fun S => Sᶜ) with hI
  have memD : ∀ S, S ∈ D ↔ v ∈ S ∧ ∀ w, w ∈ S ∨ ∃ u ∈ S, G.Adj u w := by
    intro S; rw [hD]; unfold simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing; simp

steps.claim: Complementation is injective on D, and both D and I are nonempty.
steps.explanation: Complementation is globally injective by compl_injective, hence injective on D. The full vertex set V is a dominating set containing v by Finset.mem_univ, so D is nonempty. Since I is the image of D under complementation, I is also nonempty.
steps.code:
have hcompl_inj : Set.InjOn (fun S : Finset V => Sᶜ) ↑D := fun S _ T _ h => compl_injective h
  have hDne : D.Nonempty := ⟨Finset.univ, (memD _).2 ⟨Finset.mem_univ v, fun w => Or.inl (Finset.mem_univ w)⟩⟩
  have hIne : I.Nonempty := hDne.image _

steps.claim: Every set in I is a subset of X.
steps.explanation: Let T ∈ I, so T = Sᶜ for some S ∈ D. By definition of D, v ∈ S. Therefore, v ∉ Sᶜ = T. Since X = V \ {v}, any element w ∈ T satisfies w ≠ v and w ∈ V, which by Finset.mem_erase means w ∈ X, showing T ⊆ X.
steps.code:
have hIsub : ∀ T ∈ I, T ⊆ X := by
    intro T hT
    obtain ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hT
    intro w hw
    rw [hX, Finset.mem_erase]
    refine ⟨?_, Finset.mem_univ w⟩
    rintro rfl
    exact (Finset.mem_compl.1 hw) ((memD S).1 hS).1

steps.claim: The family I is down-closed (an ideal): any subset of a set in I also belongs to I.
steps.explanation: Let T ∈ I and U ⊆ T. Write T = Sᶜ with S ∈ D. Since U ⊆ Sᶜ, contraposition yields S ⊆ Uᶜ via Finset.mem_compl. Because S contains v, its superset Uᶜ also contains v. Furthermore, since S is a dominating set, any vertex w ∈ V is dominated by some vertex in S, which also lies in Uᶜ. Hence Uᶜ ∈ D, and by compl_compl, U = (Uᶜ)ᶜ ∈ I.
steps.code:
have hIdown : ∀ T ∈ I, ∀ U ⊆ T, U ∈ I := by
    intro T hT U hU
    obtain ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hT
    have hSU : S ⊆ Uᶜ := by
      intro w hw
      rw [Finset.mem_compl]
      intro hwU
      exact (Finset.mem_compl.1 (hU hwU)) hw
    refine Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨Uᶜ, (memD _).2 ⟨hSU ((memD S).1 hS).1, fun w => ?_⟩, compl_compl U⟩
    rcases ((memD S).1 hS).2 w with h | ⟨u, hu, hadj⟩
    · exact Or.inl (hSU h)
    · exact Or.inr ⟨u, hSU hu, hadj⟩

steps.claim: Compute |I| = |D|, ∑_{T ∈ I} |T| = ∑_{S ∈ D} (n - |S|), and |X| = n - 1 with n ≥ 1 and |D| > 0.
steps.explanation: Because complementation is injective on D, Finset.card_image_of_injOn gives |I| = |D|, and Finset.sum_image with Finset.sum_congr rewrites the sum of cardinalities over I as the sum of |Sᶜ| over S ∈ D. By Finset.card_compl, Nat.cast_sub, and Finset.card_le_univ, |Sᶜ| = n - |S|. Since X is obtained by erasing v from V, Finset.card_erase_of_mem gives |X| = n - 1. The vertex v witnesses n ≥ 1, and nonemptiness of D gives |D| > 0.
steps.code:
have hcardI : I.card = D.card := Finset.card_image_of_injOn hcompl_inj
  have hsumI : ∑ T ∈ I, (T.card : ℚ) = ∑ S ∈ D, ((n : ℚ) - S.card) := by
    rw [hI, Finset.sum_image hcompl_inj]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun S _ => ?_
    rw [Finset.card_compl, Nat.cast_sub (Finset.card_le_univ S)]
  have hXcard : X.card = n - 1 := by rw [hX, Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ v)]; rfl
  have hn1 : 1 ≤ n := Fintype.card_pos_iff.2 ⟨v⟩
  have hDpos : (0 : ℚ) < D.card := by exact_mod_cast hDne.card_pos

steps.claim: Apply the down-closed family inequality to I ⊆ 𝒫(X), expressing it as an upper bound on n - avg(D).
steps.explanation: Since I is a nonempty down-closed family of subsets of X, finset_down_closed_family_avg_card_le gives that the average size of sets in I is at most |X| / 2, with equality if and only if I = 𝒫(X). Substituting |I| = |D|, |X| = n - 1, and ∑_{T ∈ I} |T| = |D| * n - ∑_{S ∈ D} |S| using Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_const, and nsmul_eq_mul, the average size of sets in I simplifies via field arithmetic to n - avg(D). Thus, n - avg(D) ≤ (n - 1) / 2, with equality if and only if I = 𝒫(X), using Nat.cast_one.
steps.code:
have key := finset_down_closed_family_avg_card_le X I hIne hIsub hIdown
  rw [hsumI, hcardI, hXcard, Nat.cast_sub hn1, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_const,
    nsmul_eq_mul] at key
  have havd : simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v = (∑ S ∈ D, (S.card : ℚ)) / D.card := rfl
  have hsplit : ((D.card : ℚ) * n - ∑ S ∈ D, (S.card : ℚ)) / D.card =
      n - (∑ S ∈ D, (S.card : ℚ)) / D.card := by
    field_simp
  rw [hsplit, Nat.cast_one] at key
  obtain ⟨k1, k2⟩ := key

steps.claim: The average dominating order satisfies avg(D) ≥ (n + 1) / 2.
steps.explanation: We split the conjunction into the inequality and the equivalence. From the bound n - avg(D) ≤ (n - 1) / 2, linear arithmetic over ℚ deduces avg(D) ≥ n - (n - 1) / 2 = (n + 1) / 2.
steps.code:
refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [havd]; push_cast at k1 ⊢; linarith

steps.claim: Equality avg(D) = (n + 1) / 2 holds if and only if I = 𝒫(X).
steps.explanation: Linear arithmetic shows that avg(D) = (n + 1) / 2 is equivalent to n - avg(D) = (n - 1) / 2. By the equality condition from the down-closed family bound, this occurs if and only if I = 𝒫(X).
steps.code:
· rw [havd]
    have e1 : (∑ S ∈ D, (S.card : ℚ)) / D.card = ((n : ℚ) + 1) / 2 ↔
        (n : ℚ) - (∑ S ∈ D, (S.card : ℚ)) / D.card = ((n : ℚ) - 1) / 2 := by
      constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith
    rw [e1, k2]

steps.claim: The degree of v is n - 1 if and only if v is adjacent to every vertex w ≠ v.
steps.explanation: The degree of v equals the cardinality of its neighbor finset N(v). Since G has no self-loops, N(v) ⊆ X = V \ {v}. If deg(v) = n - 1 = |X|, then by Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le, N(v) = X, so every w ≠ v is adjacent to v. Conversely, if v is adjacent to every w ≠ v, then X ⊆ N(v), so by Finset.Subset.antisymm, N(v) = X, which has size n - 1.
steps.code:
-- the complements fill the power set iff `v` is adjacent to every other vertex
    have hdeg : G.degree v = n - 1 ↔ ∀ w, w ≠ v → G.Adj v w := by
      rw [← G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
      have hsubN : G.neighborFinset v ⊆ X := by
        intro w hw
        rw [hX, Finset.mem_erase]
        exact ⟨(G.ne_of_adj ((G.mem_neighborFinset v w).1 hw)).symm, Finset.mem_univ w⟩
      constructor
      · intro h w hw
        have heq : G.neighborFinset v = X :=
          Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le hsubN (by rw [hXcard, h])
        have : w ∈ X := by rw [hX, Finset.mem_erase]; exact ⟨hw, Finset.mem_univ w⟩
        rw [← heq, G.mem_neighborFinset] at this
        exact this
      · intro h
        have heq : G.neighborFinset v = X := by
          refine Finset.Subset.antisymm hsubN fun w hw => ?_
          rw [hX, Finset.mem_erase] at hw
          rw [G.mem_neighborFinset]; exact h w hw.1
        rw [heq, hXcard]
    rw [hdeg]

steps.claim: The complement family I equals 𝒫(X) if and only if v is adjacent to every vertex w ≠ v.
steps.explanation: We prove both directions of I = 𝒫(X) ↔ ∀ w ≠ v, G.Adj v w. First, if I = 𝒫(X), then X ∈ I by Finset.mem_powerset_self. Hence X = Sᶜ for some dominating set S ∈ D, which by compl_compl means S = Xᶜ = {v}. Since {v} dominates every vertex w, if w ≠ v it cannot be in {v}, so by Finset.mem_singleton it must be adjacent to the unique vertex in {v}, namely v. Conversely, suppose v is adjacent to all w ≠ v. Since I ⊆ 𝒫(X) is known, it suffices to show 𝒫(X) ⊆ I. Given T ∈ 𝒫(X), T ⊆ X by Finset.mem_powerset. Since v ∉ X, v ∉ T, so v ∈ Tᶜ by Finset.mem_compl. Any vertex w is either v ∈ Tᶜ, or w ≠ v, in which case w is adjacent to v ∈ Tᶜ. Thus Tᶜ ∈ D, and by compl_compl, T = (Tᶜ)ᶜ ∈ I. By Finset.Subset.antisymm, I = 𝒫(X).
steps.code:
constructor
    · intro hIX w hw
      have hXI : X ∈ I := by rw [hIX]; exact Finset.mem_powerset_self X
      obtain ⟨S, hS, hSX⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hXI
      have hSv : S = {v} := by
        rw [← compl_compl S, hSX, hX]
        ext u; simp
      rcases ((memD S).1 hS).2 w with h | ⟨u, hu, hadj⟩
      · rw [hSv, Finset.mem_singleton] at h; exact absurd h hw
      · rw [hSv, Finset.mem_singleton] at hu; rw [← hu]; exact hadj
    · intro hall
      refine Finset.Subset.antisymm (fun T hT => Finset.mem_powerset.2 (hIsub T hT)) fun T hT => ?_
      rw [Finset.mem_powerset] at hT
      have hvT : v ∈ Tᶜ := by
        rw [Finset.mem_compl]; intro h
        have := hT h
        rw [hX, Finset.mem_erase] at this
        exact this.1 rfl
      refine Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨Tᶜ, (memD _).2 ⟨hvT, fun w => ?_⟩, compl_compl T⟩
      by_cases hw : w = v
      · exact Or.inl (hw ▸ hvT)
      · exact Or.inr ⟨v, hvT, hall w hw⟩

glossary.Finset.card_image_of_injOn: The image of a finite set under a map injective on that set has the same cardinality as the original set.
glossary.Finset.sum_image: Summing a function over the image of a finite set under an injective map equals summing the composite function over the original set.
glossary.Finset.sum_congr: Two sums over finite sets are equal if their index sets are equal and their summands agree on every element.
glossary.Finset.card_compl: The cardinality of the complement of a subset s is the total number of elements minus the cardinality of s (|sᶜ| = |V| - |s|).
glossary.Nat.cast_sub: The coercion of a difference of natural numbers n - m to an additive group with one equals the difference of coercions ↑n - ↑m, provided m ≤ n.
glossary.Finset.card_le_univ: The cardinality of any subset of a finite type is at most the total number of elements in the type.
glossary.Finset.card_erase_of_mem: Removing an element from a finite set decreases its cardinality by 1, provided the element belongs to the set.
glossary.finset_down_closed_family_avg_card_le: For any nonempty down-closed family I of subsets of a finite set X, the average cardinality of sets in I is at most |X| / 2, with equality if and only if I is the full power set of X.
glossary.Finset.sum_sub_distrib: A finite sum of differences equals the difference of the finite sums (∑ (f - g) = ∑ f - ∑ g).
glossary.Finset.sum_const: Summing a constant value over a finite set equals the cardinality of the set scalar-multiplied by the constant.
glossary.nsmul_eq_mul: Scalar multiplication of an element by a natural number n equals multiplication by the coercion of n (n • a = ↑n * a).
glossary.Nat.cast_one: The coercion of the natural number 1 into an additive monoid with one equals 1.
glossary.Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le: If s ⊆ t and |t| ≤ |s| for finite sets, then s = t.
glossary.Finset.Subset.antisymm: Two finite sets are equal if each is a subset of the other.
glossary.Finset.mem_powerset_self: Every finite set belongs to its own power set (s ∈ 𝒫(s)).
glossary.Finset.mem_singleton: An element belongs to the singleton {a} if and only if it equals a.
glossary.compl_compl: The double complement of a set is the set itself ((xᶜ)ᶜ = x).
glossary.Finset.mem_compl: An element belongs to the complement sᶜ of a finite set if and only if it does not belong to s.
glossary.Finset.mem_erase: An element belongs to s.erase b if and only if it is not equal to b and belongs to s.

declarations.name: finset_is_midpoint_balanced_of_has_no_unique_sums
declarations.informal: For an odd prime p, every subset of Z/pZ with no unique sums is balanced.
declarations.statement:
theorem finset_is_midpoint_balanced_of_has_no_unique_sums {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2)
    (A : Finset (ZMod p)) (hA : finset_has_no_unique_sums A) : finset_is_midpoint_balanced A
declarations.source:
theorem finset_is_midpoint_balanced_of_has_no_unique_sums {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2)
    (A : Finset (ZMod p)) (hA : finset_has_no_unique_sums A) : finset_is_midpoint_balanced A := by
  classical
  have hcard := hA.1
  refine ⟨Finset.card_pos.1 (by omega), fun b hb => ?_⟩
  have h2 := hA.2 b hb b hb
  unfold finset_unordered_sum_rep_count at h2
  obtain ⟨z, hz, hzb⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_ne (lt_of_lt_of_le one_lt_two h2) s(b, b)
  rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hz
  induction z using Sym2.ind with
  | h u v =>
    rw [Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff, Sym2.lift_mk] at hz
    obtain ⟨⟨hu, hv⟩, huv⟩ := hz
    have two_ne : (2 : ZMod p) ≠ 0 := by
      intro h
      have h' : ((2 : ℕ) : ZMod p) = 0 := by exact_mod_cast h
      rw [ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff] at h'
      exact hp ((Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq Fact.out Nat.prime_two).1 h')
    refine ⟨u, hu, v, hv, ?_, ?_, ?_, huv.symm⟩
    · intro h
      rw [h] at huv
      have hvb := add_left_cancel huv
      exact hzb (by rw [h, hvb])
    · intro h
      rw [h] at huv
      have hub := add_right_cancel huv
      exact hzb (by rw [h, hub])
    · intro h
      rw [h] at huv
      have hvb : v = b := mul_left_cancel₀ two_ne (by rw [two_mul, two_mul]; exact huv)
      exact hzb (by rw [h, hvb])
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.09349 (A near-quadratic lower bound for sets with no unique sums), Lemma B.1 (first statement: every NUS set in odd characteristic is balanced).

explanation.summary: To show that a subset A ⊆ Z/pZ with no unique sums is midpoint-balanced, we show that A is non-empty and that every b ∈ A is the midpoint of two distinct elements u, v ∈ A ∖ {b}. Non-emptiness is immediate since |A| ≥ 2. For any b ∈ A, the sum b + b has at least two unordered sum representations from A, so there exists a non-trivial representation {u, v} ≠ {b, b} with u + v = b + b. Setting u = b or v = b immediately forces the other element to equal b by additive cancellation, while setting u = v gives 2u = 2b, which forces u = v = b because p ≠ 2 implies 2 is non-zero (and hence invertible) in Z/pZ.

steps.claim: The set A is non-empty, and it suffices to find distinct witnesses u, v ∈ A ∖ {b} with b + b = u + v for each b ∈ A.
steps.explanation: By assumption, 2 ≤ |A|, so |A| > 0, which implies A is non-empty via Finset.card_pos.1. By definition of midpoint-balanced, it then suffices to fix an arbitrary b ∈ A and show the existence of u, v ∈ A distinct from each other and from b such that b + b = u + v.
steps.code:
classical
  have hcard := hA.1
  refine ⟨Finset.card_pos.1 (by omega), fun b hb => ?_⟩

steps.claim: There exists an unordered pair z in A.sym2 distinct from s(b, b) whose sum is b + b.
steps.explanation: Because A has no unique sums, the sum b + b has at least two unordered sum representations from A. Since 1 < 2 ≤ |{z ∈ A.sym2 | sum(z) = b + b}|, Finset.exists_mem_ne provides an unordered pair z in this filtered set that is not equal to the trivial pair s(b, b).
steps.code:
have h2 := hA.2 b hb b hb
  unfold finset_unordered_sum_rep_count at h2
  obtain ⟨z, hz, hzb⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_ne (lt_of_lt_of_le one_lt_two h2) s(b, b)
  rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hz

steps.claim: The pair z has the form s(u, v) with u, v ∈ A, u + v = b + b, and s(u, v) ≠ s(b, b).
steps.explanation: By Sym2.ind, every element of the symmetric square can be written as s(u, v). Unfolding membership in A.sym2 gives u, v ∈ A, and evaluating the lifted sum yields u + v = b + b.
steps.code:
induction z using Sym2.ind with
  | h u v =>
    rw [Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff, Sym2.lift_mk] at hz
    obtain ⟨⟨hu, hv⟩, huv⟩ := hz

steps.claim: 2 ≠ 0 in ZMod p.
steps.explanation: If 2 = 0 in ZMod p, then p divides 2 by ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff. Since both p and 2 are prime, this would force p = 2 by Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq, which contradicts the hypothesis p ≠ 2.
steps.code:
have two_ne : (2 : ZMod p) ≠ 0 := by
      intro h
      have h' : ((2 : ℕ) : ZMod p) = 0 := by exact_mod_cast h
      rw [ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff] at h'
      exact hp ((Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq Fact.out Nat.prime_two).1 h')

steps.claim: Choosing u and v as the candidates, it remains to verify u ≠ b, v ≠ b, and u ≠ v.
steps.explanation: Since u, v ∈ A and u + v = b + b (hence b + b = u + v), the elements u and v satisfy the midpoint condition once they are shown to be distinct from b and each other.
steps.code: refine ⟨u, hu, v, hv, ?_, ?_, ?_, huv.symm⟩

steps.claim: u ≠ b.
steps.explanation: Assuming u = b, substituting into u + v = b + b gives b + v = b + b. Left additive cancellation forces v = b, which implies s(u, v) = s(b, b), contradicting s(u, v) ≠ s(b, b).
steps.code:
· intro h
      rw [h] at huv
      have hvb := add_left_cancel huv
      exact hzb (by rw [h, hvb])

steps.claim: v ≠ b.
steps.explanation: Assuming v = b, substituting into u + v = b + b gives u + b = b + b. Right additive cancellation forces u = b, which implies s(u, v) = s(b, b), again contradicting s(u, v) ≠ s(b, b).
steps.code:
· intro h
      rw [h] at huv
      have hub := add_right_cancel huv
      exact hzb (by rw [h, hub])

steps.claim: u ≠ v.
steps.explanation: Assuming u = v, we have v + v = b + b, which rewrites as 2 * v = 2 * b via two_mul. Since 2 ≠ 0 in ZMod p, we can cancel 2 using mul_left_cancel₀ to conclude v = b, and hence u = b, which once more contradicts s(u, v) ≠ s(b, b).
steps.code:
· intro h
      rw [h] at huv
      have hvb : v = b := mul_left_cancel₀ two_ne (by rw [two_mul, two_mul]; exact huv)
      exact hzb (by rw [h, hvb])

glossary.Finset.card_pos.1: A finite set is non-empty if and only if its cardinality is strictly positive.
glossary.Finset.exists_mem_ne: In any finite set with cardinality greater than 1, there exists an element distinct from any specified element.
glossary.lt_of_lt_of_le: Strict inequality combined with non-strict inequality is strictly transitive: if a < b and b ≤ c, then a < c.
glossary.one_lt_two: The number 1 is strictly less than 2.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to a filtered finset if and only if it belongs to the finset and satisfies the filter predicate.
glossary.Sym2.ind: Induction principle for the symmetric square: any property of unordered pairs holds if it holds for all pairs s(x, y).
glossary.Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff: An unordered pair s(a, b) belongs to the symmetric square of s if and only if both a and b belong to s.
glossary.Sym2.lift_mk: Lifting a symmetric binary function to the symmetric square evaluates on s(a, b) as the function applied to a and b.
glossary.ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff: The canonical image of a natural number a in ZMod b is zero if and only if b divides a.
glossary.Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq: For prime numbers p and q, p divides q if and only if p = q.
glossary.Fact.out: Extracts the underlying fact from a Fact typeclass instance.
glossary.add_left_cancel: Left cancellation in an additive structure: if a + b = a + c, then b = c.
glossary.add_right_cancel: Right cancellation in an additive structure: if a + b = c + b, then a = c.
glossary.mul_left_cancel₀: Left cancellation of multiplication by a non-zero element in a domain: if a ≠ 0 and a * b = a * c, then b = c.
glossary.two_mul: Multiplication by 2 in a semiring satisfies 2 * n = n + n.

declarations.name: redistribution_fill_in
declarations.informal: The fill-in operation on the reports θ_1..θ_n: (A f)(t) = (1/n) Σ_j f(t + θ_j).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def redistribution_fill_in {n : ℕ} (θ : Fin n → ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ → ℝ
declarations.source:
/-- The fill-in operation on reports `θ`: `(A f)(t) = (1/n) ∑_j f(t + θ_j)`. -/
noncomputable def redistribution_fill_in {n : ℕ} (θ : Fin n → ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun t => (1 / (n : ℝ)) * ∑ j, f (t + θ j)

declarations.source:
/-- The fill-in operation on the reports other than `i`:
`(A_{-i} f)(t) = (1/(n-1)) ∑_{j ≠ i} f(t + θ_j)`. -/
noncomputable def redistribution_fill_in_without {n : ℕ} (θ : Fin n → ℝ) (i : Fin n)
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun t => (1 / ((n : ℝ) - 1)) * ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, f (t + θ j)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.10995 (Asymptotically optimal public project redistribution without bounded precision), Sec. 4.3, (25).

declarations.name: redistribution_trade
declarations.informal: The trade operation on the reports: (T f)(t) = (1/n²) Σ_{j,k} f(t − θ_j + θ_k).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def redistribution_trade {n : ℕ} (θ : Fin n → ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ → ℝ
declarations.source:
/-- The trade operation on reports `θ`: `(T f)(t) = (1/n²) ∑_{j,k} f(t - θ_j + θ_k)`. -/
noncomputable def redistribution_trade {n : ℕ} (θ : Fin n → ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun t => (1 / (n : ℝ) ^ 2) * ∑ j, ∑ k, f (t - θ j + θ k)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.10995 (Asymptotically optimal public project redistribution without bounded precision), Sec. 4 (trade operation T).

declarations.name: redistribution_trade_without
declarations.informal: The trade operation on the reports other than agent i: (T_{-i} f)(t) = (1/(n−1)²) Σ_{j≠i} Σ_{k≠i} f(t − θ_j + θ_k).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def redistribution_trade_without {n : ℕ} (θ : Fin n → ℝ) (i : Fin n)
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ → ℝ
declarations.source:
/-- The trade operation on the reports other than `i`:
`(T_{-i} f)(t) = (1/(n-1)²) ∑_{j ≠ i} ∑_{k ≠ i} f(t - θ_j + θ_k)`. -/
noncomputable def redistribution_trade_without {n : ℕ} (θ : Fin n → ℝ) (i : Fin n)
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun t => (1 / ((n : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2) *
    ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, ∑ k ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, f (t - θ j + θ k)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.10995 (Asymptotically optimal public project redistribution without bounded precision), Sec. 4.3, (25).

declarations.name: redistribution_one_draw_gap
declarations.informal: The one-draw gap of agent i: d_i = (1/n)(θ_i + s_{−i}/(n−1)), where s_{−i} is the sum of the other reports.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def redistribution_one_draw_gap {n : ℕ} (θ : Fin n → ℝ) (i : Fin n) : ℝ
declarations.source:
/-- The one-draw gap of agent `i`: `d_i = (1/n)(θ_i + s_{-i}/(n-1))`, `s_{-i} = ∑_{j ≠ i} θ_j`. -/
noncomputable def redistribution_one_draw_gap {n : ℕ} (θ : Fin n → ℝ) (i : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  (1 / (n : ℝ)) * (θ i + (∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, θ j) / ((n : ℝ) - 1))
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.10995 (Asymptotically optimal public project redistribution without bounded precision), Sec. 4.3 (one-draw gap d_i).

declarations.name: redistribution_fill_in_const

declarations.statement:
theorem redistribution_fill_in_const {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (θ : Fin n → ℝ) (c t : ℝ) :
    redistribution_fill_in θ (fun _ => c) t = c
declarations.source:
theorem redistribution_fill_in_const {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (θ : Fin n → ℝ) (c t : ℝ) :
    redistribution_fill_in θ (fun _ => c) t = c := by
  unfold redistribution_fill_in
  simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]
  have : (n : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hn.ne'
  field_simp

explanation.summary: The fill-in operation computes the average over the $n$-element index set $\\mathrm{Fin}(n)$. For a constant function $c$, each term in the sum is $c$, so the sum evaluates to $n \\cdot c$. Since $n > 0$, $n$ is non-zero in $\\mathbb{R}$ and cancels with $1/n$, yielding $c$.

steps.claim: The fill-in operation on a constant function reduces to $\\frac{1}{n} \\cdot (n \\cdot c) = c$.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of `redistribution_fill_in`, the operation is the average $\\frac{1}{n} \\sum_{j \\in \\mathrm{Fin}(n)} c$. The sum has $n$ constant terms equal to $c$, so it simplifies to $n \\cdot c$.
steps.code:
unfold redistribution_fill_in
  simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]

steps.claim: $n \\neq 0$ as a real number.
steps.explanation: Since $n > 0$ as a natural number, $n \\neq 0$, which casts to $n \\neq 0$ in the real numbers.
steps.code: have : (n : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hn.ne'

steps.claim: $\\frac{1}{n} \\cdot (n \\cdot c) = c$.
steps.explanation: Clearing denominators and cancelling the non-zero factor $n$ completes the proof.
steps.code: field_simp

glossary.Finset.sum_const: Summing a constant value $b$ over a finite set $s$ equals $|s| \\cdot b$ (represented as scalar multiplication by the natural number $|s|$).
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal finset of a finite type is the cardinality of the type.
glossary.Fintype.card_fin: The type $\\mathrm{Fin}(n)$ of natural numbers strictly less than $n$ has cardinality $n$.

declarations.name: finset_has_no_unique_sums_univ_zmod
declarations.informal: For an odd prime p, the whole of Z/pZ has no unique sums.
declarations.statement:
theorem finset_has_no_unique_sums_univ_zmod {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2) :
    finset_has_no_unique_sums (Finset.univ : Finset (ZMod p))
declarations.source:
theorem finset_has_no_unique_sums_univ_zmod {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2) :
    finset_has_no_unique_sums (Finset.univ : Finset (ZMod p)) := by
  constructor
  · rw [Finset.card_univ, ZMod.card p]
    have : 2 < p := Nat.lt_of_le_of_ne (Fact.out : p.Prime).two_le (Ne.symm hp)
    exact le_of_lt this
  · intros a _ b _
    unfold finset_unordered_sum_rep_count
    set s : ZMod p := a + b
    by_cases hs : s = 1
    · rw [Nat.add_one_le_iff]
      apply Finset.one_lt_card.2
      refine ⟨s(0, 1), ?_, s(2, -1), ?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [Finset.mem_filter]
        refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
        show (0 : ZMod p) + 1 = s
        rw [hs, zero_add]
      · rw [Finset.mem_filter]
        refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
        show (2 : ZMod p) + (-1) = s
        rw [hs]
        ring
      · intro h
        rw [Sym2.eq_iff] at h
        rcases h with ⟨h02, -⟩ | ⟨h0neg, -⟩
        · have hp2 : p ∣ 2 := (CharP.cast_eq_zero_iff (ZMod p) p 2).mp h02.symm
          have hle := Nat.le_of_dvd (by decide) hp2
          have hge : 2 ≤ p := (Fact.out : p.Prime).two_le
          exact hp (Nat.le_antisymm hle hge)
        · have : (1 : ZMod p) = 0 := by
            calc (1 : ZMod p) = - (-1) := by ring
            _ = - 0 := by rw [← h0neg]
            _ = 0 := by ring
          exact one_ne_zero this
    · rw [Nat.add_one_le_iff]
      apply Finset.one_lt_card.2
      refine ⟨s(0, s), ?_, s(1, s - 1), ?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [Finset.mem_filter]
        refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
        show (0 : ZMod p) + s = s
        exact zero_add s
      · rw [Finset.mem_filter]
        refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
        show (1 : ZMod p) + (s - 1) = s
        ring
      · intro h
        rw [Sym2.eq_iff] at h
        rcases h with ⟨h01, -⟩ | ⟨-, hs1⟩
        · exact one_ne_zero h01.symm
        · exact hs hs1
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.09349 (A near-quadratic lower bound for sets with no unique sums), Sec. 1 (F_p itself is NUS: each s has (p+1)/2 ≥ 2 unordered representations).

explanation.summary: For an odd prime p, the entire group ℤ/pℤ has no unique sums, meaning that |ℤ/pℤ| ≥ 2 and every sum s = a + b has at least two representations as an unordered pair sum. Since p is an odd prime, the cardinality |ℤ/pℤ| = p is at least 3, which is ≥ 2. To find two distinct representations for any sum s, the proof branches on whether s = 1: if s = 1, the pairs {0, 1} and {2, -1} both sum to 1 and are distinct because p ≠ 2 and 1 ≠ 0; if s ≠ 1, the pairs {0, s} and {1, s - 1} both sum to s and are distinct because s ≠ 1 and 1 ≠ 0.

steps.claim: The universe ℤ/pℤ has cardinality at least 2.
steps.explanation: By definition, a finset has no unique sums if its cardinality is at least 2 and every pair sum has at least two representations. Splitting the goal with `constructor`, the first requirement asks that |univ| ≥ 2. Rewriting using `Finset.card_univ` and `ZMod.card` transforms this into 2 ≤ p. Since p is prime, 2 ≤ p, and since p ≠ 2, we have 2 < p via `Nat.lt_of_le_of_ne`, which implies 2 ≤ p by `le_of_lt`.
steps.code:
constructor
  · rw [Finset.card_univ, ZMod.card p]
    have : 2 < p := Nat.lt_of_le_of_ne (Fact.out : p.Prime).two_le (Ne.symm hp)
    exact le_of_lt this

steps.claim: To show every sum s = a + b in ℤ/pℤ has at least two representations, it suffices to consider separately the cases s = 1 and s ≠ 1.
steps.explanation: Fixing arbitrary elements a, b ∈ ℤ/pℤ, we unfold `finset_unordered_sum_rep_count` to reveal that we must show the set of unordered pairs in (ℤ/pℤ)⁽²⁾ summing to s = a + b has cardinality at least 2. We then split into two cases: s = 1 and s ≠ 1.
steps.code:
· intros a _ b _
    unfold finset_unordered_sum_rep_count
    set s : ZMod p := a + b
    by_cases hs : s = 1

steps.claim: When s = 1, it suffices to show that the unordered pairs {0, 1} and {2, -1} both sum to 1 and are distinct.
steps.explanation: To show the fiber has cardinality at least 2, we rewrite 2 ≤ |S| as 1 < |S| using `Nat.add_one_le_iff`. By `Finset.one_lt_card.2`, it suffices to exhibit two distinct elements in the fiber. We candidate the unordered pairs s(0, 1) and s(2, -1).
steps.code:
· rw [Nat.add_one_le_iff]
      apply Finset.one_lt_card.2
      refine ⟨s(0, 1), ?_, s(2, -1), ?_, ?_⟩

steps.claim: Both {0, 1} and {2, -1} belong to the fiber of sums equal to s = 1.
steps.explanation: Unfolding membership in the filtered finset via `Finset.mem_filter`, membership in the universe holds trivially. We then check the sum conditions: 0 + 1 = 1 = s holds by `zero_add` and the hypothesis s = 1, while 2 + (-1) = 1 = s holds by ring arithmetic and s = 1.
steps.code:
· rw [Finset.mem_filter]
        refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
        show (0 : ZMod p) + 1 = s
        rw [hs, zero_add]
      · rw [Finset.mem_filter]
        refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
        show (2 : ZMod p) + (-1) = s
        rw [hs]
        ring

steps.claim: Assuming {0, 1} = {2, -1}, the equality branch 0 = 2 is impossible because p ≠ 2.
steps.explanation: By `Sym2.eq_iff`, equality of the unordered pairs {0, 1} = {2, -1} implies either (0 = 2 ∧ 1 = -1) or (0 = -1 ∧ 1 = 2). In the first branch, 0 = 2 in ℤ/pℤ implies p ∣ 2 by `CharP.cast_eq_zero_iff`. Since 2 > 0, this yields p ≤ 2 by `Nat.le_of_dvd`. Combined with 2 ≤ p for primes, antisymmetry gives p = 2, which contradicts the hypothesis p ≠ 2.
steps.code:
· intro h
        rw [Sym2.eq_iff] at h
        rcases h with ⟨h02, -⟩ | ⟨h0neg, -⟩
        · have hp2 : p ∣ 2 := (CharP.cast_eq_zero_iff (ZMod p) p 2).mp h02.symm
          have hle := Nat.le_of_dvd (by decide) hp2
          have hge : 2 ≤ p := (Fact.out : p.Prime).two_le
          exact hp (Nat.le_antisymm hle hge)

steps.claim: Assuming {0, 1} = {2, -1}, the equality branch 0 = -1 is impossible because 1 ≠ 0.
steps.explanation: In the second branch where 0 = -1 in ℤ/pℤ, negating both sides gives 1 = -(-1) = -0 = 0. But 1 ≠ 0 by `one_ne_zero`, yielding a contradiction.
steps.code:
· have : (1 : ZMod p) = 0 := by
            calc (1 : ZMod p) = - (-1) := by ring
            _ = - 0 := by rw [← h0neg]
            _ = 0 := by ring
          exact one_ne_zero this

steps.claim: When s ≠ 1, it suffices to show that {0, s} and {1, s - 1} both sum to s and are distinct.
steps.explanation: Rewriting 2 ≤ |S| as 1 < |S| via `Nat.add_one_le_iff` and applying `Finset.one_lt_card.2`, it suffices to exhibit two distinct elements in the fiber. We candidate the unordered pairs s(0, s) and s(1, s - 1).
steps.code:
· rw [Nat.add_one_le_iff]
      apply Finset.one_lt_card.2
      refine ⟨s(0, s), ?_, s(1, s - 1), ?_, ?_⟩

steps.claim: Both {0, s} and {1, s - 1} belong to the fiber of sums equal to s.
steps.explanation: Using `Finset.mem_filter`, membership in the universe is trivial. The sum condition 0 + s = s holds by `zero_add`, and 1 + (s - 1) = s holds by ring arithmetic.
steps.code:
· rw [Finset.mem_filter]
        refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
        show (0 : ZMod p) + s = s
        exact zero_add s
      · rw [Finset.mem_filter]
        refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
        show (1 : ZMod p) + (s - 1) = s
        ring

steps.claim: The unordered pairs {0, s} and {1, s - 1} are distinct when s ≠ 1.
steps.explanation: Assuming equality of the unordered pairs, `Sym2.eq_iff` implies either (0 = 1 ∧ s = s - 1) or (0 = s - 1 ∧ s = 1). The first case is refuted by 1 ≠ 0 via `one_ne_zero`. The second case gives s = 1, directly contradicting the assumption s ≠ 1.
steps.code:
· intro h
        rw [Sym2.eq_iff] at h
        rcases h with ⟨h01, -⟩ | ⟨-, hs1⟩
        · exact one_ne_zero h01.symm
        · exact hs hs1

glossary.CharP.cast_eq_zero_iff: In a ring of characteristic p, the cast of a natural number x is zero if and only if p divides x.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal finset `Finset.univ` on a finite type equals the cardinality of the type.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to a filtered finset if and only if it belongs to the base finset and satisfies the predicate.
glossary.Finset.one_lt_card.2: If a finite set contains at least two distinct elements, its cardinality is strictly greater than 1.
glossary.Fact.out: Extracts the underlying proposition asserted by a `Fact` typeclass instance.
glossary.Nat.add_one_le_iff: For natural numbers, n + 1 ≤ m if and only if n < m.
glossary.Nat.le_antisymm: If n ≤ m and m ≤ n for natural numbers, then n = m.
glossary.Nat.le_of_dvd: If a natural number divides a strictly positive natural number, it is less than or equal to it.
glossary.Nat.lt_of_le_of_ne: A natural number less than or equal to another and not equal to it is strictly less than it.
glossary.Ne.symm: Disequality is symmetric: if a ≠ b, then b ≠ a.
glossary.Sym2.eq_iff: Two unordered pairs {x, y} and {z, w} are equal if and only if (x = z ∧ y = w) or (x = w ∧ y = z).
glossary.ZMod.card: The cardinality of the ring ℤ/nℤ is n.
glossary.le_of_lt: A strict inequality implies the corresponding non-strict inequality.
glossary.one_ne_zero: In a nontrivial ring, 1 is not equal to 0.
glossary.zero_add: Zero is an additive identity on the left: 0 + a = a.

caveats: `Sym2` denotes the symmetric square of a type, representing unordered pairs, with notation `s(x, y)`.
`Finset.one_lt_card.2` uses projection notation for the right-to-left direction (`mpr`) of `Finset.one_lt_card`.
