declarations.name: simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_le_of_no_isolated
declarations.informal: If the finite graph G of order n has no isolated vertices, then for every vertex v the dominating sets containing v have average size at most (5n − 2 deg(v) + 1)/6 (hence at most (5n − 1)/6).
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_le_of_no_isolated {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hiso : ∀ w, 0 < G.degree w)
    (v : V) :
    simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v ≤
      (5 * (Fintype.card V : ℚ) - 2 * G.degree v + 1) / 6
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_le_of_no_isolated {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hiso : ∀ w, 0 < G.degree w)
    (v : V) :
    simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v ≤
      (5 * (Fintype.card V : ℚ) - 2 * G.degree v + 1) / 6 := by
  classical
  set D := simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing G v with hD
  set n := Fintype.card V with hn
  have memD : ∀ S, S ∈ D ↔ v ∈ S ∧ ∀ w, w ∈ S ∨ ∃ u ∈ S, G.Adj u w := by
    intro S; rw [hD]; unfold simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing; simp
  -- `D` is closed under supersets
  have hup : ∀ S ∈ D, ∀ T, S ⊆ T → T ∈ D := by
    intro S hS T hST
    rw [memD] at hS ⊢
    refine ⟨hST hS.1, fun w => ?_⟩
    rcases hS.2 w with h | ⟨u, hu, h⟩
    · exact Or.inl (hST h)
    · exact Or.inr ⟨u, hST hu, h⟩
  have hDne : D.Nonempty :=
    ⟨Finset.univ, (memD _).2 ⟨Finset.mem_univ v, fun w => Or.inl (Finset.mem_univ w)⟩⟩
  -- closed neighbourhoods and the vertices outside `N[v]`
  set N : V → Finset V := fun w => insert w (G.neighborFinset w) with hN
  set U : Finset V := (Finset.univ.erase v) \ G.neighborFinset v with hU
  have hUcard : U.card = n - 1 - G.degree v := by
    rw [hU, Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset, Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ v),
      G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
    · rfl
    · intro w hw
      rw [Finset.mem_erase]
      exact ⟨(G.ne_of_adj ((G.mem_neighborFinset v w).1 hw)).symm, Finset.mem_univ w⟩
  have hdegle : G.degree v ≤ n - 1 := by
    rw [← G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
    have : G.neighborFinset v ⊆ Finset.univ.erase v := by
      intro w hw
      rw [Finset.mem_erase]
      exact ⟨(G.ne_of_adj ((G.mem_neighborFinset v w).1 hw)).symm, Finset.mem_univ w⟩
    calc (G.neighborFinset v).card ≤ (Finset.univ.erase v).card := Finset.card_le_card this
      _ = n - 1 := by rw [Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ v)]; rfl
  have hn1 : 1 ≤ n := Fintype.card_pos_iff.2 ⟨v⟩
  -- counts: `a x` sets containing `x`, `b x` avoiding `x`, `c x` sets in which `x` is critical
  set a : V → ℕ := fun x => (D.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)).card with ha
  set b : V → ℕ := fun x => (D.filter (fun S => x ∉ S)).card with hb
  set c : V → ℕ := fun x => (D.filter (fun S => x ∈ S ∧ S.erase x ∉ D)).card with hc
  have hab : ∀ x, a x + b x = D.card := fun x => Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not _
  have habc : ∀ x, a x = b x + c x := by
    intro x
    simp only [ha, hb, hc]
    have hsplit : (D.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)).card =
        ((D.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)).filter (fun S => S.erase x ∈ D)).card +
        ((D.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)).filter (fun S => ¬ S.erase x ∈ D)).card :=
      (Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not _).symm
    rw [Finset.filter_filter, Finset.filter_filter] at hsplit
    rw [hsplit]
    congr 1
    -- erasing `x` matches the sets with `x` removable with the sets avoiding `x`
    apply le_antisymm
    · have inj : Set.InjOn (fun S : Finset V => S.erase x)
          ↑(D.filter (fun S => x ∈ S ∧ S.erase x ∈ D)) := by
        intro S hS T hT h
        simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_filter] at hS hT
        rw [← Finset.insert_erase hS.2.1, ← Finset.insert_erase hT.2.1]
        exact congrArg (insert x) h
      rw [← Finset.card_image_of_injOn inj]
      apply Finset.card_le_card
      intro T hT
      obtain ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hT
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter] at hS ⊢
      exact ⟨hS.2.2, by simp⟩
    · have inj : Set.InjOn (fun S : Finset V => insert x S) ↑(D.filter (fun S => x ∉ S)) := by
        intro S hS T hT h
        simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_filter] at hS hT
        rw [← Finset.erase_insert hS.2, ← Finset.erase_insert hT.2]
        exact congrArg (fun W => Finset.erase W x) h
      rw [← Finset.card_image_of_injOn inj]
      apply Finset.card_le_card
      intro T hT
      obtain ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hT
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter] at hS ⊢
      refine ⟨hup S hS.1 _ (Finset.subset_insert x S), Finset.mem_insert_self x S, ?_⟩
      rw [Finset.erase_insert hS.2]; exact hS.1
  have hsum : ∑ S ∈ D, S.card = ∑ x, a x := by
    have h : ∀ S ∈ D, S.card = ∑ x, if x ∈ S then 1 else 0 := by
      intro S _
      rw [← Finset.card_filter, Finset.filter_mem_eq_inter, Finset.univ_inter]
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl h, Finset.sum_comm]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => ?_
    simp only [ha]; rw [Finset.card_filter]
  -- `x ≠ v` critical in `S`: `S` meets some `N[w]`, `w ∉ N[v]`, exactly in `x`
  set E : V → V → Finset (Finset V) := fun w x => D.filter (fun S => S ∩ N w = {x}) with hE
  have hcrit : ∀ x, x ≠ v → c x ≤ ∑ w ∈ U, (E w x).card := by
    intro x hxv
    simp only [hc]
    refine le_trans (Finset.card_le_card ?_) Finset.card_biUnion_le
    intro S hS
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hS
    obtain ⟨hSD, hxS, hSx⟩ := hS
    have hvS : v ∈ S.erase x := Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hxv.symm, ((memD S).1 hSD).1⟩
    rw [memD] at hSx
    push_neg at hSx
    obtain ⟨w, hwS, hwadj⟩ := hSx hvS
    have hNw : S ∩ N w = {x} := by
      ext y
      simp only [Finset.mem_inter, hN, Finset.mem_insert, G.mem_neighborFinset,
        Finset.mem_singleton]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨hyS, hy⟩
        by_contra hyx
        have hy' : y ∈ S.erase x := Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hyx, hyS⟩
        rcases hy with rfl | hy
        · exact hwS hy'
        · exact hwadj y hy' hy.symm
      · intro hyx
        rw [hyx]
        refine ⟨hxS, ?_⟩
        rcases ((memD S).1 hSD).2 w with h | ⟨u, hu, h⟩
        · left
          by_contra hne
          exact hwS (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨fun h' => hne h'.symm, h⟩)
        · right
          by_cases hux : u = x
          · rw [← hux]; exact h.symm
          · exact absurd h (hwadj u (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hux, hu⟩))
    have hwU : w ∈ U := by
      rw [hU, Finset.mem_sdiff, Finset.mem_erase, G.mem_neighborFinset]
      refine ⟨⟨fun h => hwS (h ▸ hvS), Finset.mem_univ w⟩, fun h => hwadj v hvS h⟩
    exact Finset.mem_biUnion.2 ⟨w, hwU, Finset.mem_filter.2 ⟨hSD, hNw⟩⟩
  -- at most two thirds of the sets meet `N[w]` in a single vertex
  have hthird : ∀ w, 3 * (D.filter (fun S => (S ∩ N w).card = 1)).card ≤ 2 * D.card := by
    intro w
    obtain ⟨w', hw'⟩ : ∃ w', G.Adj w w' := by
      have := hiso w
      rw [← G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree, Finset.card_pos] at this
      obtain ⟨w', hw'⟩ := this
      exact ⟨w', (G.mem_neighborFinset w w').1 hw'⟩
    have hww' : w ≠ w' := G.ne_of_adj hw'
    have hwN : w ∈ N w := by simp [hN]
    have hw'N : w' ∈ N w := by simp [hN, G.mem_neighborFinset, hw']
    set single := D.filter (fun S => (S ∩ N w).card = 1) with hsingle
    set multi := D.filter (fun S => ¬ (S ∩ N w).card = 1) with hmulti
    have hsm : single.card + multi.card = D.card := Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not _
    let φ : Finset V → Finset V := fun S => if w ∈ S then insert w' S else insert w S
    have hmaps : ∀ S ∈ single, φ S ∈ multi := by
      intro S hS
      rw [hsingle, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.card_eq_one] at hS
      obtain ⟨hSD, z, hz⟩ := hS
      rw [hmulti, Finset.mem_filter]
      by_cases hwS : w ∈ S
      · simp only [φ, if_pos hwS]
        refine ⟨hup S hSD _ (Finset.subset_insert _ _), fun h1 => ?_⟩
        have hw_in : w ∈ insert w' S ∩ N w := Finset.mem_inter.2 ⟨Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hwS, hwN⟩
        have hw'_in : w' ∈ insert w' S ∩ N w := Finset.mem_inter.2 ⟨Finset.mem_insert_self _ _, hw'N⟩
        exact hww' (Finset.card_le_one.1 h1.le w hw_in w' hw'_in)
      · simp only [φ, if_neg hwS]
        refine ⟨hup S hSD _ (Finset.subset_insert _ _), fun h1 => ?_⟩
        have hz_in : z ∈ S ∩ N w := by rw [hz]; exact Finset.mem_singleton_self z
        have hzw : z ≠ w := fun h => hwS (h ▸ (Finset.mem_inter.1 hz_in).1)
        have hw_in : w ∈ insert w S ∩ N w := Finset.mem_inter.2 ⟨Finset.mem_insert_self _ _, hwN⟩
        have hz_in' : z ∈ insert w S ∩ N w :=
          Finset.mem_inter.2 ⟨Finset.mem_insert_of_mem (Finset.mem_inter.1 hz_in).1,
            (Finset.mem_inter.1 hz_in).2⟩
        exact hzw (Finset.card_le_one.1 h1.le z hz_in' w hw_in)
    have hfib : ∀ M, (single.filter (fun S => φ S = M)).card ≤ 2 := by
      intro M
      refine le_trans (Finset.card_le_card (t := {M.erase w', M.erase w}) ?_) Finset.card_le_two
      intro S hS
      rw [Finset.mem_filter, hsingle, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.card_eq_one] at hS
      obtain ⟨⟨_, z, hz⟩, hφ⟩ := hS
      rw [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton]
      by_cases hwS : w ∈ S
      · left
        simp only [φ, if_pos hwS] at hφ
        have hw'S : w' ∉ S := by
          intro h
          have h1 : w ∈ S ∩ N w := Finset.mem_inter.2 ⟨hwS, hwN⟩
          have h2 : w' ∈ S ∩ N w := Finset.mem_inter.2 ⟨h, hw'N⟩
          rw [hz, Finset.mem_singleton] at h1 h2
          exact hww' (h1.trans h2.symm)
        rw [← hφ, Finset.erase_insert hw'S]
      · right
        simp only [φ, if_neg hwS] at hφ
        rw [← hφ, Finset.erase_insert hwS]
    have hle2 : single.card ≤ 2 * multi.card :=
      Finset.card_le_mul_card_image_of_maps_to hmaps 2 (fun M _ => hfib M)
    omega
  have hEsum : ∀ w, ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.erase v, (E w x).card ≤
      (D.filter (fun S => (S ∩ N w).card = 1)).card := by
    intro w
    rw [← Finset.card_biUnion]
    · apply Finset.card_le_card
      intro S hS
      obtain ⟨x, -, hx⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.1 hS
      rw [hE, Finset.mem_filter] at hx
      rw [Finset.mem_filter, hx.2, Finset.card_singleton]
      exact ⟨hx.1, rfl⟩
    · intro x _ y _ hxy
      rw [Function.onFun, Finset.disjoint_left]
      intro S hSx hSy
      rw [hE, Finset.mem_filter] at hSx hSy
      exact hxy (Finset.singleton_injective (hSx.2.symm.trans hSy.2))
  have hcsum : 3 * ∑ x, c x ≤ 3 * D.card + 2 * U.card * D.card := by
    rw [← Finset.add_sum_erase _ _ (Finset.mem_univ v)]
    have hcv : c v ≤ D.card := Finset.card_filter_le _ _
    have h1 : ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.erase v, c x ≤ ∑ w ∈ U, (D.filter (fun S => (S ∩ N w).card = 1)).card := by
      calc ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.erase v, c x
          ≤ ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.erase v, ∑ w ∈ U, (E w x).card :=
            Finset.sum_le_sum fun x hx => hcrit x (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hx)
        _ = ∑ w ∈ U, ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.erase v, (E w x).card := Finset.sum_comm
        _ ≤ _ := Finset.sum_le_sum fun w _ => hEsum w
    have h2 : 3 * ∑ w ∈ U, (D.filter (fun S => (S ∩ N w).card = 1)).card ≤ 2 * U.card * D.card := by
      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
      calc ∑ w ∈ U, 3 * (D.filter (fun S => (S ∩ N w).card = 1)).card
          ≤ ∑ w ∈ U, 2 * D.card := Finset.sum_le_sum fun w _ => hthird w
        _ = 2 * U.card * D.card := by rw [Finset.sum_const, smul_eq_mul]; ring
    omega
  have h2a : 2 * ∑ x, a x = n * D.card + ∑ x, c x := by
    have e1 : ∑ x, (a x + b x) = n * D.card := by
      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => hab x, Finset.sum_const, smul_eq_mul, Finset.card_univ]
    have e2 : ∑ x, a x = ∑ x, b x + ∑ x, c x := by
      rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]; exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => habc x
    rw [← e1, Finset.sum_add_distrib]; omega
  -- conclude
  have hm : U.card + G.degree v + 1 = n := by rw [hUcard]; omega
  have hDpos : (0 : ℚ) < D.card := by exact_mod_cast hDne.card_pos
  have qa : (2 : ℚ) * ((∑ x, a x : ℕ) : ℚ) = n * D.card + ((∑ x, c x : ℕ) : ℚ) := by
    exact_mod_cast h2a
  have qc : (3 : ℚ) * ((∑ x, c x : ℕ) : ℚ) ≤ 3 * D.card + 2 * U.card * D.card := by
    exact_mod_cast hcsum
  have qm : (U.card : ℚ) + G.degree v + 1 = n := by exact_mod_cast hm
  have qs : ∑ S ∈ D, (S.card : ℚ) = ((∑ x, a x : ℕ) : ℚ) := by rw [← hsum, Nat.cast_sum]
  have qnD : (n : ℚ) * D.card = U.card * D.card + G.degree v * D.card + D.card := by
    rw [← qm]; ring
  unfold simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order
  rw [← hD, div_le_div_iff₀ hDpos (by norm_num : (0 : ℚ) < 6), qs]
  linarith

declarations.name: matrix_unit_difference_rows_isTotallyUnimodular
declarations.informal: Every integer matrix whose rows are differences e_u − e_v of two standard basis vectors is totally unimodular: each square minor is 0, 1 or −1.
declarations.statement:
theorem matrix_unit_difference_rows_isTotallyUnimodular {m n : Type*} [DecidableEq n]
    (u v : m → n) :
    (Matrix.of fun (i : m) (j : n) =>
      (Pi.single (u i) (1 : ℤ) : n → ℤ) j - (Pi.single (v i) (1 : ℤ) : n → ℤ) j).IsTotallyUnimodular
declarations.source:
theorem matrix_unit_difference_rows_isTotallyUnimodular {m n : Type*} [DecidableEq n]
    (u v : m → n) :
    (Matrix.of fun (i : m) (j : n) =>
      (Pi.single (u i) (1 : ℤ) : n → ℤ) j - (Pi.single (v i) (1 : ℤ) : n → ℤ) j).IsTotallyUnimodular := by
  -- square matrices whose rows have at most one `1`, at most one `-1`, and zeros elsewhere
  have key : ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ B : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℤ,
      (∀ i j, B i j = 0 ∨ B i j = 1 ∨ B i j = -1) →
      (∀ i j j', B i j = 1 → B i j' = 1 → j = j') →
      (∀ i j j', B i j = -1 → B i j' = -1 → j = j') →
      B.det = 0 ∨ B.det = 1 ∨ B.det = -1 := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero => intro B _ _ _; right; left; exact Matrix.det_isEmpty
    | succ k ih =>
      intro B h0 h1 h2
      by_cases hall : ∀ i, (∃ j, B i j = 1) ∧ (∃ j, B i j = -1)
      · -- every row sums to zero, so the all-ones vector is in the kernel
        left
        rw [← Matrix.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_iff]
        refine ⟨fun _ => 1, fun h => one_ne_zero (congrFun h 0), ?_⟩
        funext i
        obtain ⟨⟨j1, hj1⟩, ⟨j2, hj2⟩⟩ := hall i
        have hne : j1 ≠ j2 := by
          rintro rfl
          rw [hj1] at hj2
          norm_num at hj2
        simp only [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, mul_one, Pi.zero_apply]
        rw [Finset.sum_eq_add j1 j2 hne (fun c _ hc => ?_) (by simp) (by simp), hj1, hj2]
        · norm_num
        · rcases h0 i c with h | h | h
          · exact h
          · exact absurd (h1 i c j1 h hj1) hc.1
          · exact absurd (h2 i c j2 h hj2) hc.2
      · push_neg at hall
        obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hall
        by_cases hz : ∀ j, B i j = 0
        · left; exact Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero i hz
        push_neg at hz
        obtain ⟨j0, hj0⟩ := hz
        -- row `i` has a single nonzero entry, at `j0`
        have honly : ∀ j, j ≠ j0 → B i j = 0 := by
          intro j hj
          by_contra hne
          rcases h0 i j with h | h | h
          · exact hne h
          · rcases h0 i j0 with h' | h' | h'
            · exact hj0 h'
            · exact hj (h1 i j j0 h h')
            · exact hi ⟨j, h⟩ j0 h'
          · rcases h0 i j0 with h' | h' | h'
            · exact hj0 h'
            · exact hi ⟨j0, h'⟩ j h
            · exact hj (h2 i j j0 h h')
        have hB : B i j0 = 1 ∨ B i j0 = -1 := by
          rcases h0 i j0 with h | h | h
          · exact absurd h hj0
          · exact Or.inl h
          · exact Or.inr h
        set B' := B.submatrix i.succAbove j0.succAbove with hB'
        have hminor : B'.det = 0 ∨ B'.det = 1 ∨ B'.det = -1 := by
          refine ih B' (fun a b => h0 _ _) (fun a b b' hb hb' => ?_) (fun a b b' hb hb' => ?_)
          · exact Fin.succAbove_right_injective (h1 _ _ _ hb hb')
          · exact Fin.succAbove_right_injective (h2 _ _ _ hb hb')
        rw [Matrix.det_succ_row B i, Finset.sum_eq_single j0
          (fun j _ hj => by rw [honly j hj]; ring) (by simp)]
        rcases neg_one_pow_eq_or ℤ (i + j0 : ℕ) with hp | hp <;> rcases hB with hb | hb <;>
          rcases hminor with hd | hd | hd <;> simp [hp, hb, ← hB', hd]
  intro k f g _ hg
  set B := (Matrix.of fun (i : m) (j : n) =>
      (Pi.single (u i) (1 : ℤ) : n → ℤ) j - (Pi.single (v i) (1 : ℤ) : n → ℤ) j).submatrix
    f g with hBdef
  have entry : ∀ i j, B i j =
      (if g j = u (f i) then 1 else 0) - (if g j = v (f i) then 1 else 0) := by
    intro i j
    simp [hBdef, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Pi.single_apply]
  have e1 : ∀ i j, B i j = 1 → g j = u (f i) := by
    intro i j h
    by_contra hc
    rw [entry, if_neg hc] at h
    split_ifs at h <;> norm_num at h
  have e2 : ∀ i j, B i j = -1 → g j = v (f i) := by
    intro i j h
    by_contra hc
    rw [entry, if_neg hc] at h
    split_ifs at h <;> norm_num at h
  have h0 : ∀ i j, B i j = 0 ∨ B i j = 1 ∨ B i j = -1 := by
    intro i j; rw [entry]; split_ifs <;> simp
  rcases key k B h0 (fun i j j' hj hj' => hg ((e1 i j hj).trans (e1 i j' hj').symm))
      (fun i j j' hj hj' => hg ((e2 i j hj).trans (e2 i j' hj').symm)) with h | h | h
  · exact ⟨0, by simp [h]⟩
  · exact ⟨1, by simp [h]⟩
  · exact ⟨-1, by simp [h]⟩
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.09349 (A near-quadratic lower bound for sets with no unique sums), Lemma 2.2 (determinants of unit-incidence minors). Stated as total unimodularity (Mathlib's `Matrix.IsTotallyUnimodular`) of the matrix with rows e_{u(i)} − e_{v(i)}; rows with u(i) = v(i) (zero rows) are allowed.

declarations.name: simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_of_degree_eq_card_sub_two
declarations.informal: Let G be a connected graph of order n ≥ 3 and v a vertex of degree n − 2, with u the vertex other than v not adjacent to v. Then the dominating sets containing v have average size (n+1)/2 + (deg u + 1)/(2(2^{deg u + 1} − 1)).
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_of_degree_eq_card_sub_two {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hconn : G.Connected)
    (hn : 3 ≤ Fintype.card V) (v u : V) (huv : u ≠ v) (hnadj : ¬ G.Adj v u)
    (hdeg : G.degree v = Fintype.card V - 2) :
    simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v =
      ((Fintype.card V : ℚ) + 1) / 2 +
        ((G.degree u : ℚ) + 1) / (2 * (2 ^ (G.degree u + 1) - 1))
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_of_degree_eq_card_sub_two {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hconn : G.Connected)
    (hn : 3 ≤ Fintype.card V) (v u : V) (huv : u ≠ v) (hnadj : ¬ G.Adj v u)
    (hdeg : G.degree v = Fintype.card V - 2) :
    simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v =
      ((Fintype.card V : ℚ) + 1) / 2 +
        ((G.degree u : ℚ) + 1) / (2 * (2 ^ (G.degree u + 1) - 1)) := by
  classical
  set n := Fintype.card V with hn'
  set D := simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing G v with hD
  -- sets containing `v` inside `insert v W`: `2^|W|` of them, total size `2^|W| + |W| 2^|W| / 2`
  have count : ∀ W : Finset V, v ∉ W →
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun S : Finset V => v ∈ S ∧ S ⊆ insert v W)).card = 2 ^ W.card ∧
      ∑ S ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun S : Finset V => v ∈ S ∧ S ⊆ insert v W), (S.card : ℚ) =
        2 ^ W.card + W.card * 2 ^ W.card / 2 := by
    intro W hvW
    have himg : Finset.univ.filter (fun S : Finset V => v ∈ S ∧ S ⊆ insert v W) =
        W.powerset.image (insert v) := by
      ext S
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_image,
        Finset.mem_powerset]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨hvS, hSW⟩
        refine ⟨S.erase v, fun x hx => ?_, Finset.insert_erase hvS⟩
        have := hSW (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hx)
        rw [Finset.mem_insert] at this
        rcases this with h | h
        · exact absurd h (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hx)
        · exact h
      · rintro ⟨T, hTW, rfl⟩
        exact ⟨Finset.mem_insert_self v T, Finset.insert_subset_insert v hTW⟩
    have hinj : Set.InjOn (insert v) (W.powerset : Set (Finset V)) := by
      intro S hS T hT h
      simp only [Finset.coe_powerset, Set.mem_preimage, Set.mem_powerset_iff,
        Finset.coe_subset] at hS hT
      have hvS : v ∉ S := fun h' => hvW (hS h')
      have hvT : v ∉ T := fun h' => hvW (hT h')
      rw [← Finset.erase_insert hvS, ← Finset.erase_insert hvT]
      exact congrArg (fun U => Finset.erase U v) h
    -- complements in `W` pair sizes `k` and `|W| - k`
    have hhalf : 2 * ∑ T ∈ W.powerset, (T.card : ℚ) = W.card * 2 ^ W.card := by
      have hc : ∑ T ∈ W.powerset, (T.card : ℚ) = ∑ T ∈ W.powerset, ((W.card : ℚ) - T.card) := by
        refine Finset.sum_nbij' (fun T => W \ T) (fun T => W \ T) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
        · intro T hT; simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_powerset] at hT ⊢; exact Finset.sdiff_subset
        · intro T hT; simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_powerset] at hT ⊢; exact Finset.sdiff_subset
        · intro T hT; simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_powerset] at hT; exact Finset.sdiff_sdiff_eq_self hT
        · intro T hT; simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_powerset] at hT; exact Finset.sdiff_sdiff_eq_self hT
        · intro T hT
          rw [Finset.mem_powerset] at hT
          rw [Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset hT, Nat.cast_sub (Finset.card_le_card hT)]
          ring
      rw [two_mul]
      nth_rewrite 2 [hc]
      rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun T _ =>
        (show (T.card : ℚ) + ((W.card : ℚ) - T.card) = W.card by ring), Finset.sum_const,
        Finset.card_powerset, nsmul_eq_mul]
      push_cast; ring
    rw [himg, Finset.card_image_of_injOn hinj, Finset.card_powerset, Finset.sum_image hinj]
    refine ⟨rfl, ?_⟩
    have : ∀ T ∈ W.powerset, ((insert v T).card : ℚ) = T.card + 1 := by
      intro T hT
      rw [Finset.mem_powerset] at hT
      rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem (fun h => hvW (hT h))]
      push_cast; ring
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl this, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_powerset,
      nsmul_eq_mul]
    push_cast
    linarith
  -- every vertex other than `u` and `v` is a neighbour of `v`
  have hnbr : G.neighborFinset v = (Finset.univ.erase v).erase u := by
    apply Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le
    · intro w hw
      rw [G.mem_neighborFinset] at hw
      rw [Finset.mem_erase, Finset.mem_erase]
      exact ⟨fun h => hnadj (h ▸ hw), (G.ne_of_adj hw).symm, Finset.mem_univ w⟩
    · rw [G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree, hdeg,
        Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨huv, Finset.mem_univ u⟩),
        Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ v)]
      rfl
  have hadj : ∀ w, w ≠ v → w ≠ u → G.Adj v w := by
    intro w hwv hwu
    rw [← G.mem_neighborFinset, hnbr, Finset.mem_erase, Finset.mem_erase]
    exact ⟨hwu, hwv, Finset.mem_univ w⟩
  set Y : Finset V := insert u (G.neighborFinset u) with hY
  have hvY : v ∉ Y := by
    rw [hY, Finset.mem_insert, G.mem_neighborFinset]
    rintro (h | h)
    · exact huv h.symm
    · exact hnadj h.symm
  set X : Finset V := Finset.univ.erase v with hX
  set Z : Finset V := X \ Y with hZ
  have hvX : v ∉ X := Finset.notMem_erase v _
  have hvZ : v ∉ Z := fun h => hvX (Finset.mem_sdiff.1 h).1
  have hYX : Y ⊆ X := fun w hw => Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨fun h => hvY (h ▸ hw), Finset.mem_univ w⟩
  have hXcard : X.card = n - 1 := by rw [hX, Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ v)]; rfl
  have hYcard : Y.card = G.degree u + 1 := by
    rw [hY, Finset.card_insert_of_notMem (by simp), G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
  have hZcard : Z.card + (G.degree u + 1) = n - 1 := by
    rw [hZ, Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset hYX, hXcard, ← hYcard]
    have := Finset.card_le_card hYX
    omega
  -- the dominating sets containing `v` are the sets containing `v` that meet `N[u]`
  set P := Finset.univ.filter (fun S : Finset V => v ∈ S ∧ S ⊆ insert v X) with hP
  set Q := Finset.univ.filter (fun S : Finset V => v ∈ S ∧ S ⊆ insert v Z) with hQ
  have hQP : Q ⊆ P := by
    intro S hS
    rw [hQ, Finset.mem_filter] at hS
    rw [hP, Finset.mem_filter]
    exact ⟨Finset.mem_univ S, hS.2.1,
      hS.2.2.trans (Finset.insert_subset_insert v Finset.sdiff_subset)⟩
  have hDPQ : D = P \ Q := by
    ext S
    rw [hD, Finset.mem_sdiff, hP, hQ]
    unfold simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
    have hSX : v ∈ S → S ⊆ insert v X := fun _ w _ => by
      rw [Finset.mem_insert, hX, Finset.mem_erase]
      by_cases h : w = v
      · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr ⟨h, Finset.mem_univ w⟩
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨hvS, hdom⟩
      refine ⟨⟨hvS, hSX hvS⟩, fun ⟨_, hSZ⟩ => ?_⟩
      rcases hdom u with h | ⟨w, hw, hwu⟩
      · have := hSZ h
        rw [Finset.mem_insert, hZ, Finset.mem_sdiff] at this
        rcases this with h' | h'
        · exact huv h'
        · exact h'.2 (by rw [hY]; exact Finset.mem_insert_self u _)
      · have := hSZ hw
        rw [Finset.mem_insert, hZ, Finset.mem_sdiff] at this
        rcases this with h' | h'
        · exact hnadj (h' ▸ hwu)
        · exact h'.2 (by rw [hY, Finset.mem_insert, G.mem_neighborFinset]; exact Or.inr hwu.symm)
    · rintro ⟨⟨hvS, _⟩, hnot⟩
      refine ⟨hvS, fun w => ?_⟩
      by_cases hwv : w = v
      · exact Or.inl (hwv ▸ hvS)
      by_cases hwu : w = u
      · -- `S` meets `N[u]`
        subst hwu
        by_contra hcon
        push_neg at hcon
        apply hnot
        refine ⟨hvS, fun x hx => ?_⟩
        rw [Finset.mem_insert, hZ, Finset.mem_sdiff, hX, Finset.mem_erase]
        by_cases hxv : x = v
        · exact Or.inl hxv
        · refine Or.inr ⟨⟨hxv, Finset.mem_univ x⟩, ?_⟩
          rw [hY, Finset.mem_insert, G.mem_neighborFinset]
          rintro (h | h)
          · exact hcon.1 (h ▸ hx)
          · exact hcon.2 x hx h.symm
      · exact Or.inr ⟨v, hvS, hadj w hwv hwu⟩
  obtain ⟨hPc, hPs⟩ := count X hvX
  obtain ⟨hQc, hQs⟩ := count Z hvZ
  have hDcard : (D.card : ℚ) = 2 ^ X.card - 2 ^ Z.card := by
    rw [hDPQ, Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset hQP, hPc, hQc,
      Nat.cast_sub (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (Finset.card_le_card (Finset.sdiff_subset)))]
    push_cast; ring
  have hDsum : ∑ S ∈ D, (S.card : ℚ) = (2 ^ X.card + X.card * 2 ^ X.card / 2) -
      (2 ^ Z.card + Z.card * 2 ^ Z.card / 2) := by
    rw [hDPQ, ← hPs, ← hQs, ← Finset.sum_sdiff hQP]; ring
  -- algebra, with `|X| = |Z| + (d + 1)` and `|X| = n - 1`
  set d := G.degree u with hd
  set z := Z.card with hz
  have hXz : X.card = z + (d + 1) := by rw [hXcard]; omega
  have hnq : (n : ℚ) = z + d + 2 := by
    have : n = z + (d + 1) + 1 := by omega
    rw [this]; push_cast; ring
  unfold simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order
  rw [← hD, hDsum, hDcard, hXz, hnq]
  have h2 : (2 : ℚ) ^ (d + 1) - 1 ≠ 0 := by
    have : (1 : ℚ) < 2 ^ (d + 1) := one_lt_pow₀ (by norm_num) (by omega)
    linarith
  have h2z : (0 : ℚ) < 2 ^ z := by positivity
  rw [pow_add]
  push_cast
  field_simp
  ring
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.11446 (On the local average order of dominating sets), Corollary 4.2. The paper's connectivity hypothesis is kept though the proof here does not use it; the proof counts the sets containing v that meet N[u] directly instead of differentiating the domination polynomial.

declarations.name: consecutive_sum_ne_mul_prime_of_two_mul_lt
declarations.informal: If p is a prime with p > 2n and a ≥ 1, then a·p is not a sum of one or more consecutive integers from {1, …, n}.
declarations.statement:
theorem consecutive_sum_ne_mul_prime_of_two_mul_lt (n a p i j : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime)
    (hpn : 2 * n < p) (ha : 0 < a) (hi : 1 ≤ i) (hij : i ≤ j) (hjn : j ≤ n) :
    ∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc i j, x ≠ a * p
declarations.source:
theorem consecutive_sum_ne_mul_prime_of_two_mul_lt (n a p i j : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime)
    (hpn : 2 * n < p) (ha : 0 < a) (hi : 1 ≤ i) (hij : i ≤ j) (hjn : j ≤ n) :
    ∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc i j, x ≠ a * p := by
  intro hS
  obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hij
  -- `2 S = k (2i + k - 1)` with `k = m + 1` terms
  have hsum : ∀ m : ℕ, 2 * ∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc i (i + m), x = (m + 1) * (2 * i + m) := by
    intro m
    induction m with
    | zero => simp
    | succ m ih =>
      rw [show i + (m + 1) = (i + m) + 1 by ring, Finset.sum_Icc_succ_top (by omega), mul_add, ih]
      ring
  have h2 := hsum m
  rw [hS] at h2
  have hsize : ∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc i (i + m), x ≤ (m + 1) * n := by
    have := Finset.sum_le_card_nsmul (Finset.Icc i (i + m)) (fun x => x) n
      (fun x hx => le_trans (Finset.mem_Icc.1 hx).2 hjn)
    rw [Nat.card_Icc, smul_eq_mul] at this
    rwa [show i + m + 1 - i = m + 1 by omega] at this
  rw [hS] at hsize
  have hkn : m + 1 ≤ n := by omega
  -- a positive number below `p` is coprime to `p`
  have hcop : ∀ t, 0 < t → t ≤ n → Nat.Coprime t p := by
    intro t ht htn
    exact Nat.Coprime.symm ((Nat.Prime.coprime_iff_not_dvd hp).2 fun h =>
      absurd (Nat.le_of_dvd ht h) (by omega))
  -- the number of terms is at most `2a`
  have hk : m + 1 ≤ 2 * a := by
    rcases Nat.even_or_odd (m + 1) with ⟨t, ht⟩ | hodd
    · have hS' : a * p = t * (2 * i + m) := by
        have : 2 * (a * p) = 2 * (t * (2 * i + m)) := by rw [h2, ht]; ring
        omega
      have ht0 : 0 < t := by omega
      have htd : t ∣ a := (hcop t ht0 (by omega)).dvd_of_dvd_mul_right ⟨_, hS'⟩
      have := Nat.le_of_dvd ha htd
      omega
    · have hdvd : m + 1 ∣ 2 * (a * p) := ⟨2 * i + m, h2⟩
      have hc2 : Nat.Coprime (m + 1) 2 :=
        Nat.Coprime.symm ((Nat.Prime.coprime_iff_not_dvd Nat.prime_two).2
          (Nat.odd_iff.1 hodd ▸ by omega))
      have h1 : m + 1 ∣ a * p := hc2.dvd_of_dvd_mul_left hdvd
      have h3 : m + 1 ∣ a := (hcop (m + 1) (by omega) hkn).dvd_of_dvd_mul_right h1
      have := Nat.le_of_dvd ha h3
      omega
  -- then the sum is at most `2an < ap`
  have : (m + 1) * n ≤ 2 * a * n := Nat.mul_le_mul_right n hk
  have : 2 * a * n < a * p := by nlinarith
  omega
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.08889 (Consecutive Cycle Sums), Lemma 2, which assumes in addition 2an − T_{2a−1} < ap; that hypothesis is not needed: divisibility forces a run of k consecutive integers with sum ap to have k ≤ 2a, and such a run sums to at most 2an < ap. Serves Theorem 1 (not_cycle_labeling_complete_range_of_ge_eight).

declarations.name: consecutive_sum_ne_mul_prime
declarations.informal: Let a ≥ 1 and p a prime with p > 2n and 2an − T_{2a−1} < ap, where T_m = m(m+1)/2. Then a·p is not a sum of consecutive integers from {1, …, n} (it is not a standard arc sum of the n-cycle).
declarations.statement:
theorem consecutive_sum_ne_mul_prime (n a p i j : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hpn : 2 * n < p)
    (ha : 0 < a) (hap : 2 * a * n < a * p + a * (2 * a - 1)) (hi : 1 ≤ i) (hij : i ≤ j)
    (hjn : j ≤ n) :
    ∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc i j, x ≠ a * p
declarations.source:
theorem consecutive_sum_ne_mul_prime (n a p i j : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hpn : 2 * n < p)
    (ha : 0 < a) (hap : 2 * a * n < a * p + a * (2 * a - 1)) (hi : 1 ≤ i) (hij : i ≤ j)
    (hjn : j ≤ n) :
    ∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc i j, x ≠ a * p :=
  consecutive_sum_ne_mul_prime_of_two_mul_lt n a p i j hp hpn ha hi hij hjn
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.08889 (Consecutive Cycle Sums), Lemma 2 (2an − T_{2a−1} < ap written as 2an < ap + a(2a − 1)); proved here from the stronger consecutive_sum_ne_mul_prime_of_two_mul_lt, which drops that hypothesis.

declarations.name: simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_lt_of_four_le
declarations.informal: For n ≥ 4 the upper bound (5n−1)/6 is never attained: if G has order n ≥ 4 and no isolated vertices, then avd_v(G) < (5n−1)/6 for every vertex v.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_lt_of_four_le {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hn : 4 ≤ Fintype.card V)
    (hiso : ∀ w, 0 < G.degree w) (v : V) :
    simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v < (5 * (Fintype.card V : ℚ) - 1) / 6
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_lt_of_four_le {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hn : 4 ≤ Fintype.card V)
    (hiso : ∀ w, 0 < G.degree w) (v : V) :
    simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v < (5 * (Fintype.card V : ℚ) - 1) / 6 := by
  classical
  set D := simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing G v with hD
  set n := Fintype.card V with hn
  have memD : ∀ S, S ∈ D ↔ v ∈ S ∧ ∀ w, w ∈ S ∨ ∃ u ∈ S, G.Adj u w := by
    intro S; rw [hD]; unfold simple_graph_dominating_sets_containing; simp
  -- `D` is closed under supersets
  have hup : ∀ S ∈ D, ∀ T, S ⊆ T → T ∈ D := by
    intro S hS T hST
    rw [memD] at hS ⊢
    refine ⟨hST hS.1, fun w => ?_⟩
    rcases hS.2 w with h | ⟨u, hu, h⟩
    · exact Or.inl (hST h)
    · exact Or.inr ⟨u, hST hu, h⟩
  have hDne : D.Nonempty :=
    ⟨Finset.univ, (memD _).2 ⟨Finset.mem_univ v, fun w => Or.inl (Finset.mem_univ w)⟩⟩
  -- closed neighbourhoods and the vertices outside `N[v]`
  set N : V → Finset V := fun w => insert w (G.neighborFinset w) with hN
  set U : Finset V := (Finset.univ.erase v) \ G.neighborFinset v with hU
  have hUcard : U.card = n - 1 - G.degree v := by
    rw [hU, Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset, Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ v),
      G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
    · rfl
    · intro w hw
      rw [Finset.mem_erase]
      exact ⟨(G.ne_of_adj ((G.mem_neighborFinset v w).1 hw)).symm, Finset.mem_univ w⟩
  have hdegle : G.degree v ≤ n - 1 := by
    rw [← G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
    have : G.neighborFinset v ⊆ Finset.univ.erase v := by
      intro w hw
      rw [Finset.mem_erase]
      exact ⟨(G.ne_of_adj ((G.mem_neighborFinset v w).1 hw)).symm, Finset.mem_univ w⟩
    calc (G.neighborFinset v).card ≤ (Finset.univ.erase v).card := Finset.card_le_card this
      _ = n - 1 := by rw [Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ v)]; rfl
  have hn1 : 1 ≤ n := Fintype.card_pos_iff.2 ⟨v⟩
  -- counts: `a x` sets containing `x`, `b x` avoiding `x`, `c x` sets in which `x` is critical
  set a : V → ℕ := fun x => (D.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)).card with ha
  set b : V → ℕ := fun x => (D.filter (fun S => x ∉ S)).card with hb
  set c : V → ℕ := fun x => (D.filter (fun S => x ∈ S ∧ S.erase x ∉ D)).card with hc
  have hab : ∀ x, a x + b x = D.card := fun x => Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not _
  have habc : ∀ x, a x = b x + c x := by
    intro x
    simp only [ha, hb, hc]
    have hsplit : (D.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)).card =
        ((D.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)).filter (fun S => S.erase x ∈ D)).card +
        ((D.filter (fun S => x ∈ S)).filter (fun S => ¬ S.erase x ∈ D)).card :=
      (Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not _).symm
    rw [Finset.filter_filter, Finset.filter_filter] at hsplit
    rw [hsplit]
    congr 1
    -- erasing `x` matches the sets with `x` removable with the sets avoiding `x`
    apply le_antisymm
    · have inj : Set.InjOn (fun S : Finset V => S.erase x)
          ↑(D.filter (fun S => x ∈ S ∧ S.erase x ∈ D)) := by
        intro S hS T hT h
        simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_filter] at hS hT
        rw [← Finset.insert_erase hS.2.1, ← Finset.insert_erase hT.2.1]
        exact congrArg (insert x) h
      rw [← Finset.card_image_of_injOn inj]
      apply Finset.card_le_card
      intro T hT
      obtain ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hT
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter] at hS ⊢
      exact ⟨hS.2.2, by simp⟩
    · have inj : Set.InjOn (fun S : Finset V => insert x S) ↑(D.filter (fun S => x ∉ S)) := by
        intro S hS T hT h

    have hvU : v ∉ U := by simp [hU]
    have hyU : y ∉ U := by
      rw [hU, Finset.mem_sdiff, hy]; simp
    have hUcard2 : 2 ≤ U.card := by omega
    have hcase : (∃ w ∈ U, 2 ≤ G.degree w) ∨
        (∃ x, x ≠ v ∧ ∃ w1 ∈ U, ∃ w2 ∈ U, w1 ≠ w2 ∧ ∃ S, S ∈ E w1 x ∧ S ∈ E w2 x) := by
      by_cases hα : ∃ w ∈ U, 2 ≤ G.degree w
      · exact Or.inl hα
      right
      push_neg at hα
      -- every vertex of `U` is a leaf
      have hleaf : ∀ w ∈ U, ∃ z, G.neighborFinset w = {z} := by
        intro w hw
        rw [← Finset.card_eq_one, G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
        have := hiso w; have := hα w hw; omega
      have hNw : ∀ w z, G.neighborFinset w = {z} → N w = {w, z} := by
        intro w z h; simp only [hN, h]
      have hwv : ∀ w ∈ U, ∀ z, G.Adj w z → z ≠ v := by
        intro w hw z hz hzv
        rw [hzv] at hz
        rw [hU, Finset.mem_sdiff, G.mem_neighborFinset] at hw
        exact hw.2 hz.symm
      -- a leaf of `U` whose neighbour is in `U`: a `K₂` component
      have hK2 : ∀ w ∈ U, ∀ z, G.neighborFinset w = {z} → z ∈ U →
          ∃ x, x ≠ v ∧ ∃ w1 ∈ U, ∃ w2 ∈ U, w1 ≠ w2 ∧ ∃ S, S ∈ E w1 x ∧ S ∈ E w2 x := by
        intro w hw z hz hzU
        have hwz : G.Adj w z := (G.mem_neighborFinset w z).1 (by rw [hz]; simp)
        obtain ⟨z', hz'⟩ := hleaf z hzU
        have hzw : G.Adj z w := hwz.symm
        have hz'w : z' = w := by
          have : w ∈ G.neighborFinset z := (G.mem_neighborFinset z w).2 hzw
          rw [hz', Finset.mem_singleton] at this; exact this.symm
        have hne : w ≠ z := G.ne_of_adj hwz
        have hSD : Finset.univ.erase z ∈ D := by
          rw [memD]
          refine ⟨Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨fun h => hvU (h ▸ hzU), Finset.mem_univ v⟩, fun t => ?_⟩
          by_cases htz : t = z
          · exact Or.inr ⟨w, Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨hne, Finset.mem_univ w⟩, htz ▸ hwz⟩
          · exact Or.inl (Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨htz, Finset.mem_univ t⟩)
        refine ⟨w, fun h => hvU (h ▸ hw), w, hw, z, hzU, hne, Finset.univ.erase z, ?_, ?_⟩
        · rw [hE, Finset.mem_filter, hNw w z hz]
          refine ⟨hSD, ?_⟩
          ext t; simp only [Finset.mem_inter, Finset.mem_erase, Finset.mem_univ, and_true,
            Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton]
          constructor
          · rintro ⟨htz, rfl | rfl⟩
            · rfl
            · exact absurd rfl htz
          · rintro rfl; exact ⟨hne, Or.inl rfl⟩
        · rw [hE, Finset.mem_filter, hNw z w (by rw [hz', hz'w])]
          refine ⟨hSD, ?_⟩
          ext t; simp only [Finset.mem_inter, Finset.mem_erase, Finset.mem_univ, and_true,
            Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton]
          constructor
          · rintro ⟨htz, rfl | rfl⟩
            · exact absurd rfl htz
            · rfl
          · rintro rfl; exact ⟨hne, Or.inr rfl⟩
      obtain ⟨w1, hw1⟩ := Finset.card_pos.1 (by omega : 0 < U.card)
      obtain ⟨z1, hz1⟩ := hleaf w1 hw1
      by_cases hz1U : z1 ∈ U
      · exact hK2 w1 hw1 z1 hz1 hz1U
      obtain ⟨w2, hw2, hw21⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_ne (by omega : 1 < U.card) w1
      obtain ⟨z2, hz2⟩ := hleaf w2 hw2
      by_cases hz2U : z2 ∈ U
      · exact hK2 w2 hw2 z2 hz2 hz2U
      have hw1z1 : G.Adj w1 z1 := (G.mem_neighborFinset w1 z1).1 (by rw [hz1]; simp)
      have hw2z2 : G.Adj w2 z2 := (G.mem_neighborFinset w2 z2).1 (by rw [hz2]; simp)
      have hz1y : z1 = y := (hUall z1 hz1U).resolve_left (hwv w1 hw1 z1 hw1z1)
      have hz2y : z2 = y := (hUall z2 hz2U).resolve_left (hwv w2 hw2 z2 hw2z2)
      -- two leaves on `y`: drop both, `y` is critical with both as witnesses
      set S := (Finset.univ.erase w1).erase w2 with hS
      have hw1y : w1 ≠ y := fun h => hyU (h ▸ hw1)
      have hw2y : w2 ≠ y := fun h => hyU (h ▸ hw2)
      have hSD : S ∈ D := by
        rw [memD]
        refine ⟨by simp [hS]; exact ⟨fun h => hvU (h ▸ hw2), fun h => hvU (h ▸ hw1)⟩, fun t => ?_⟩
        by_cases ht1 : t = w1
        · exact Or.inr ⟨y, by simp [hS]; exact ⟨hw2y.symm, hw1y.symm⟩, ht1 ▸ hz1y ▸ hw1z1.symm⟩
        by_cases ht2 : t = w2
        · exact Or.inr ⟨y, by simp [hS]; exact ⟨hw2y.symm, hw1y.symm⟩, ht2 ▸ hz2y ▸ hw2z2.symm⟩
        exact Or.inl (by simp [hS]; exact ⟨ht2, ht1⟩)
      have hmem : ∀ w z, w ∈ U → G.neighborFinset w = {z} → z = y → (w = w1 ∨ w = w2) →
          S ∈ E w y := by
        intro w z _ hz hzy hw
        rw [hE, Finset.mem_filter, hNw w z hz, hzy]
        refine ⟨hSD, ?_⟩
        ext t
        simp only [hS, Finset.mem_inter, Finset.mem_erase, Finset.mem_univ, and_true,
          Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton]
        constructor
        · rintro ⟨⟨ht2, ht1⟩, h | h⟩
          · rcases hw with rfl | rfl
            · exact absurd h ht1
            · exact absurd h ht2
          · exact h
        · rintro rfl; exact ⟨⟨hw2y.symm, hw1y.symm⟩, Or.inr rfl⟩
      exact ⟨y, (G.ne_of_adj ((G.mem_neighborFinset v y).1 (by rw [hy]; simp))).symm, w1, hw1, w2, hw2, hw21.symm, S,
        hmem w1 z1 hw1 hz1 hz1y (Or.inl rfl), hmem w2 z2 hw2 hz2 hz2y (Or.inr rfl)⟩
    have qc : (3 : ℚ) * ((∑ x, c x : ℕ) : ℚ) + 1 ≤ 3 * D.card + 2 * U.card * D.card := by
      exact_mod_cast hcsum_strict hcase
    have q1 : (G.degree v : ℚ) = 1 := by exact_mod_cast hdv1
    have qnD : (n : ℚ) * D.card = U.card * D.card + G.degree v * D.card + D.card := by
      rw [← qm]; ring
    nlinarith
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.11446 (On the local average order of dominating sets), list entry OP-135 (sharpness of the bound (5n−1)/6 of Theorem 3.8 for n ≥ 4); the negation of sharpness. It follows from the conjectured bound (2n+1)/3 (simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_le_two_mul_add_one_div_three), which is below (5n−1)/6 for n ≥ 4.

open.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_lt_ne_loss
open.informal: In Catch-Up played on {1, ..., N} with N(N+1)/2 even, Player 2 does not lose after any opening move x < N by Player 1.
open.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_lt_ne_loss (N : ℕ) (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2))
    (x : ℕ) (hx : x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N) (hlt : x < N) :
    catch_up_value_aux ((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase x) 0 x false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.loss
open.citation: step towards catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_ne_loss (Catch-Up conjecture (Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates, 2015, Sec. 3.1))

open.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_max_ne_loss
open.informal: In Catch-Up played on {1, ..., N} with N(N+1)/2 even and N > 0, Player 2 does not lose after Player 1 opens with the maximum piece N.
open.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_max_ne_loss (N : ℕ) (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2))
    (hN : 0 < N) :
    catch_up_value_aux ((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase N) 0 N false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.loss
open.citation: step towards catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_ne_loss (Catch-Up conjecture (Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates, 2015, Sec. 3.1))

open.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_ne_loss
open.informal: In Catch-Up played on {1, ..., N} with N(N+1)/2 even, Player 2 does not lose after any opening move x ∈ {1, ..., N} by Player 1.
open.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_after_opening_ne_loss (N : ℕ) (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2))
    (x : ℕ) (hx : x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N) :
    catch_up_value_aux ((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase x) 0 x false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.loss
open.citation: step towards catch_up_value_icc_eq_draw_of_even_triangular (Catch-Up conjecture (Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates, 2015, Sec. 3.1))

open.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_initial_ne_loss
open.informal: In Catch-Up played on {1, ..., N} with N(N+1)/2 even, Player 1 does not lose from the initial position with equal scores 0.
open.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_initial_ne_loss (N : ℕ) (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2)) :
    catch_up_value_aux (Finset.Icc 1 N) 0 0 false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.loss
open.citation: step towards catch_up_value_icc_eq_draw_of_even_triangular (Catch-Up conjecture (Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates, 2015, Sec. 3.1))

open.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_ne_win
open.informal: In Catch-Up played on {1, ..., N} with N > 0 and N(N+1)/2 even, Player 2 does not win after Player 1 opens with 1.
open.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_ne_win (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N)
    (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2)) :
    catch_up_value_aux ((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase 1) 0 1 false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.win
open.citation: step towards catch_up_value_aux_icc_initial_ne_loss (Catch-Up conjecture (Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates, 2015, Sec. 3.1))

open.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_response_lt_ne_loss
open.informal: In Catch-Up on {1, ..., N} with even triangular sum, if Player 1 opens with 1 and Player 2 responds with y < N, Player 1 does not lose from the resulting position with scores (1, y).
open.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_response_lt_ne_loss (N : ℕ)
    (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2)) (y : ℕ) (hy : y ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 N).erase 1) (hlt : y < N) :
    catch_up_value_aux (((Finset.Icc 1 N).erase 1).erase y) 1 y false ≠ CatchUpOutcome.loss
open.citation: step towards catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_ne_win (Catch-Up conjecture (Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates, 2015, Sec. 3.1))

open.name: catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_response_max_ne_loss
open.informal: In Catch-Up on {1, ..., N} with even triangular sum and N > 0, if Player 1 opens with 1 and Player 2 responds with N, Player 1 does not lose from the resulting position with scores (1, N).
open.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_response_max_ne_loss (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N)
    (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2)) :

open.citation: step towards catch_up_value_aux_icc_opening_one_ne_win (Catch-Up conjecture (Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates, 2015, Sec. 3.1))

open.name: catch_up_value_icc_eq_draw_of_even_triangular
open.informal: The Catch-Up conjecture (2015, open): for every natural number N such that the triangular number N(N+1)/2 is even, the game Catch-Up played on {1, ..., N} ends in a draw under optimal play by both players. Verified by computer up to N = 20.
open.statement:
theorem catch_up_value_icc_eq_draw_of_even_triangular (N : ℕ) (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2)) :
    catch_up_value (Finset.Icc 1 N) = .draw
open.citation: Catch-Up: A Game in Which the Lead Alternates (2015)

open.name: maxcut_game_optimal_strong_equilibrium_exists
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.04948, Sec. 4, second question): for every finite simple unweighted graph G and every k ≥ 3, some optimal coloring of the Max-k-Cut game on (G, k) is a strong equilibrium. This would imply that every such game has a strong equilibrium.
open.statement:
theorem maxcut_game_optimal_strong_equilibrium_exists :
    ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ),
      3 ≤ k → ∃ σ : V → Fin k, is_maxcut_optimal G σ ∧ is_maxcut_strong_equilibrium G σ
open.citation: second open question of arXiv:2610.04948, Sec. 4 (does every game admit an optimal coloring that is a strong equilibrium?); the paper's Theorem 2 shows not every optimal coloring is one, and Remark 6 notes its counterexample does not rule out another, stable optimum

open.name: maxcut_game_strong_equilibrium_exists
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.04948, Sec. 4): for every finite simple unweighted graph G and every k ≥ 3, the unweighted Max-k-Cut game on (G, k) has a strong equilibrium, i.e. a coloring σ : V → [k] from which no nonempty coalition can deviate so that every member strictly gains.
open.statement:
theorem maxcut_game_strong_equilibrium_exists :
    ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ),
      3 ≤ k → ∃ σ : V → Fin k, is_maxcut_strong_equilibrium G σ
open.citation: open question of arXiv:2610.04948, Sec. 4 (Concluding remarks); that paper shows an optimal coloring need not be a strong equilibrium (Theorem 2), which leaves existence open; known: optimal colorings are strong equilibria when the maximum degree is at most 2k − 1 (Corollary 9) and are 7-strong equilibria in general

open.name: maxcut_optimal_not_strong_degree_66
open.informal: There is a finite simple graph of maximum degree at most 66 with an optimal coloring of the Max-3-Cut game that is not a strong equilibrium; hence Δ*(3) ≤ 65. (The graph G_3 of arXiv:2610.04948, Sec. 2, has 91 vertices and maximum degree 66, attained by the anchor vertices r_{3,1}.)
open.statement: theorem maxcut_optimal_not_strong_degree_66 : ¬ maxcut_optimal_strong_up_to_degree 3 66
open.citation: arXiv:2610.04948, Theorem 2 for k = 3, with the degree bound read off the construction G_3 of Sec. 2.1 (the paper does not state the degree); the upper bound side of the threshold question after Corollary 9

open.name: mms_threshold_monotone_asymptotic
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.06125, Sec. 3): for monotone valuations over goods, μ(n) = n + log₂ n + o(log₂ n) as n → ∞; i.e. (μ(n) − n − log₂ n) / log₂ n → 0.
open.statement:
theorem mms_threshold_monotone_asymptotic :
    (fun n : ℕ => (mms_threshold_monotone n : ℝ) - n - Real.logb 2 n) =o[Filter.atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ => Real.logb 2 n)
open.citation: open question of arXiv:2610.06125 (On MMS allocations with few items), Sec. 3; the paper proves n + 0.93 log₂ n ≤ μ(n) ≤ n + log₂ n + O(log log n) for large n (Theorem 1, Theorem 6, Lemmas 8 and 9)

open.name: condorcet_dimension_le_three
open.informal: Open problem: every election with at least one voter has a Condorcet winning set of at most three candidates, i.e. the Condorcet dimension of every election is at most 3.
open.statement:
theorem condorcet_dimension_le_three :
    ∀ (n m : ℕ) (P : Fin n → Equiv.Perm (Fin m)), 0 < n →
      ∃ S : Finset (Fin m), S.card ≤ 3 ∧ is_condorcet_winning_set P S
open.citation: open question from Condorcet winning sets (Social Choice and Welfare 44(3):493-517, 2015); dimension 3 is attained, and the best upper bound is 5 (arXiv:2506.22133); arXiv:2604.19851 finds no election of dimension above 3 by computer search

open.name: ejr_committee_monotone_chain_exists
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2007.01795, open problems, Q2): every approval profile with at least one voter admits an ordering c_1, ..., c_m of all candidates such that for every k ≤ m the prefix {c_1, ..., c_k} satisfies EJR for committee size k; equivalently, some resolute committee-monotonic approval-based committee rule satisfies EJR.
open.statement:
theorem ejr_committee_monotone_chain_exists :
    ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Finset (Fin m)), 0 < n →
      ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m), ∀ k, k ≤ m →
        is_ejr_committee A k (Finset.univ.filter fun c => (σ c : ℕ) < k)
open.citation: open question of arXiv:2007.01795 (Multi-Winner Voting with Approval Preferences) (committee monotonicity and proportionality); sequential Phragmén is committee monotonic but only satisfies PJR, and the known EJR rules are not committee monotonic; a positive answer is known for party-list profiles (arXiv:1911.08365)

open.name: crystal_components_unique
open.informal: Crystals have unique components (arXiv:1601.03081, open): if n is a crystal with components a, b and also with components c, d, then {a, b} = {c, d}.
open.citation: The Biharmonic Mean (2016), arXiv:1601.03081

open.name: weakly_consecutive_one_at_end
open.informal: Conjecture 5.2 of arXiv:2401.09497 (open): every weakly consecutive sequence of length k begins or ends with the term 1, that is, the position holding the value 1 is the first or the last.
open.statement:
theorem weakly_consecutive_one_at_end {k : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k))
    (hσ : is_weakly_consecutive σ) (i : Fin k) (hi : (σ i : ℕ) = 0) :
    (i : ℕ) = 0 ∨ (i : ℕ) + 1 = k
open.citation: Weakly Consecutive Sequences (2024), arXiv:2401.09497

open.name: matroid_symmetry_gap_lt_eight_seventeenths
open.informal: Open question (arXiv:2610.07387, after Corollary 3.4 and Appendix A): there is a strongly symmetric instance of non-negative submodular maximization over a matroid — a non-negative submodular f on a finite ground set, a matroid M and a permutation group G such that f is G-invariant and independence depends only on the G-symmetrized indicator vector — whose symmetry gap max_{x∈P(M)} F(x̄) / max_{x∈P(M)} F(x) is strictly below 8/17 (F the multilinear extension, P(M) the matroid polytope).
open.statement:
theorem matroid_symmetry_gap_lt_eight_seventeenths :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (M : Matroid (Fin m)) (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ) (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m))),
      (∀ S, 0 ≤ f S) ∧ is_submodular f ∧ is_strongly_symmetric_instance M f G ∧
      sSup ((fun x => multilinear_extension f (perm_group_symmetrize G x)) '' matroid_polytope M) <
        8 / 17 * sSup (multilinear_extension f '' matroid_polytope M)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.07387 (Stronger Hardness for Submodular Maximization Subject to a Matroid Constraint): its gadgets attain symmetry gap 8/17, giving the 8/17 inapproximability bound (Theorem 1.1), and Appendix A shows 8/17 is optimal within the paper's three-parameter family; whether any matroid instance has a smaller gap is left open.

open.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_int_le_22
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 8): there is a bilinear algorithm for 3x3 matrix multiplication with integer coefficients that uses 22 products, i.e. a list of 22 triads over the integers whose evaluation equals A * B for all integer 3x3 matrices A and B. By the paper, such an algorithm is the same as a recursive (block) algorithm with integer constants and 22 multiplications; the paper proves at least 22 are needed and 23 suffice, so the question is whether the rank is exactly 22.
open.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_int_le_22 : matrix3_tensor_rank_le ℤ 22
open.citation: the open problem of arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 8 (a 22-product integer algorithm for 3x3 matrix multiplication), stated as posed

open.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_z_ge_22
open.informal: The tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over the integers is at least 22; that is, every valid decomposition of 3x3 matrix multiplication over ℤ has length at least 22.
open.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_z_ge_22 : matrix3_tensor_rank_ge ℤ 22
open.citation: arXiv:2610.01639, Theorem 1 and Sec. 8 (Lower Bound of 22 for 3x3 Matrix Multiplication over the Integers)

open.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_zmod2_ge_22
open.informal: Every bilinear algorithm (valid triad decomposition) for 3x3 matrix multiplication over the two-element field uses at least 22 products. This is the main lower bound of arXiv:2610.01639 (row 0 of its table), proved there by a large computer-assisted Lean development.
open.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_zmod2_ge_22 : matrix3_tensor_rank_ge (ZMod 2) 22
open.citation: arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 3 and Sec. 7, Table 1, row 0: the paper's main lower bound of 22 over the two-element field

open.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_zmod2_le_22
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 7, Table 1, row 0, interval [22, 23]): the tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over the two-element field is 22, i.e. there are 22 triads over ZMod 2 whose evaluation equals A * B for all 3x3 matrices A, B over ZMod 2. The paper proves the rank is at least 22 and at most 23.
open.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_zmod2_le_22 : matrix3_tensor_rank_le (ZMod 2) 22
open.citation: the open problem of arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 7, Table 1, row 0 (rank over the two-element field in [22, 23]), stated as posed

open.name: tarski_query_complexity_five_le_log_sq
open.informal: Open question (arXiv:2610.07055, the case k = 5 of the gap left by its Theorems 2 and 3): Tarski(n, 5) = O(log² n), i.e. there is a constant C such that for every n ≥ 2 some deterministic query algorithm finds a fixed point of every monotone map [n]^5 → [n]^5 (componentwise order) with at most C·(log₂ n)² queries.
open.statement:
theorem tarski_query_complexity_five_le_log_sq :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n →
      ∃ q : ℕ, tarski_query_complexity_le n 5 q ∧ (q : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.logb 2 n ^ 2
open.citation: arXiv:2610.07055 (Tarski Fixed Points in Quasi-FPT Queries): Theorem 2 gives Tarski(n, 5) = O((log n)^3) and Theorem 3 (with the earlier two-dimensional bound) gives Ω((log n)^2); O(log² n) is known for k = 3 and k = 4. This is the k = 5 instance of the question how the exponent of log n grows with k. The list entry's general form (exponent c·⌈log₂ k⌉ with c < 1 for all k ≥ 3) is already refuted at k = 3 by the known Ω(log² n) lower bound, so only the k = 5 question is stated.

open.name: exists_cycle_labeling_complete
open.informal: Conjecture: for every n there is a placement of 1, …, n around the n-cycle that is complete.
open.statement: theorem exists_cycle_labeling_complete (n : ℕ) : ∃ L : List ℕ, cycle_labeling_complete n L
open.citation: arXiv:2610.08889 (Consecutive Cycle Sums), generalizing list entry OP-121: the paper shows the increasing order fails for every n ≥ 8 (Theorem 1) but there are n(n−1)+1 arcs for n(n+1)/2 targets.

open.name: finset_card_ge_one_add_clog_of_midpoint_balanced
open.informal: For a prime p, every nonempty balanced subset B of Z/pZ has |B| ≥ 1 + ⌈log₂ p⌉.
open.statement:
theorem finset_card_ge_one_add_clog_of_midpoint_balanced {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    (B : Finset (ZMod p)) (hB : finset_is_midpoint_balanced B) : 1 + Nat.clog 2 p ≤ B.card
open.citation: arXiv:2610.09349 (A near-quadratic lower bound for sets with no unique sums), Lemma B.1 (second statement), proved there by a determinant argument on the midpoint-certificate matrix (rows 2e_i − e_{u_i} − e_{v_i}) with the unit-incidence minor lemma (Lemma 2.2).

open.name: matroid_common_list_chromatic_le_add_const
open.informal: Open question (arXiv:2610.07318, Question 3.1): there is an absolute constant C such that χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) ≤ χ(M₁, M₂) + C for every pair of loopless matroids on a common finite ground set. (The paper also asks whether C = 1 works; its Theorem 1.1, matroid_common_list_colorable_two_not_of_colorable_two here, shows C = 0 does not.)
open.statement:
theorem matroid_common_list_chromatic_le_add_const :
    ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ (α : Type) [Finite α] (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α), M₁.Loopless → M₂.Loopless →
      M₁.E = M₂.E →
      matroid_common_list_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ ≤ matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ + C
open.citation: arXiv:2610.07318 (A note on the list chromatic number of two matroids), Question 3.1. Known: χ_ℓ ≤ 2χ for every pair (Combinatorica 45, 2025, Article 46), and the paper's Theorem 1.1 gives a pair with χ = 2, χ_ℓ = 3.

open.name: matroid_sbo_common_list_chromatic_eq
open.informal: Open question (arXiv:2610.07318, Question 3.2): for any two loopless strongly base-orderable matroids M₁, M₂ on a common finite ground set, the common list chromatic number equals the common chromatic number, χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) = χ(M₁, M₂).
open.statement:
theorem matroid_sbo_common_list_chromatic_eq :
    ∀ (α : Type) [Finite α] (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α), M₁.Loopless → M₂.Loopless → M₁.E = M₂.E →
      matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₁ → matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₂ →
      matroid_common_list_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ = matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂
open.citation: arXiv:2610.07318 (A note on the list chromatic number of two matroids), Question 3.2. The paper shows χ_ℓ = χ can fail for general pairs (Theorem 1.1) and proves the strongly base-orderable case when two colors suffice (Corollary 2.3); equality was known for two transversal matroids. The case χ ≥ 3 is open.

open.name: not_cycle_labeling_complete_range_of_ge_eight
open.informal: For every n ≥ 8, the n-cycle labelled 1, …, n in order is not complete.
open.statement:
theorem not_cycle_labeling_complete_range_of_ge_eight (n : ℕ) (hn : 8 ≤ n) :
    ¬ cycle_labeling_complete n (List.range' 1 n)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.08889 (Consecutive Cycle Sums), Theorem 1. The paper's proof uses explicit prime-counting bounds for n ≥ 599 and a computer check for 8 ≤ n ≤ 599.

open.name: nus_min_card_ge_c_log_sq
open.informal: Open question: there is an absolute constant c > 0 such that m(p) ≥ c (log p)² for all sufficiently large primes p.
open.statement:
theorem nus_min_card_ge_c_log_sq :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ p₀ : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, p₀ ≤ p → p.Prime →
      c * Real.log p ^ 2 ≤ (nus_min_card p : ℝ)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.09349 (A near-quadratic lower bound for sets with no unique sums), Question 5.1. The paper proves m(p) ≥ 2^{-80} (log p / log log p)² for p ≥ 64 (Theorem 1.1) and m(p) ≤ (log p)²/(2 (log 3)²) + O((log p)²/log log p) (Theorem 1.2); an affirmative answer would give m(p) = Θ((log p)²).

open.name: nus_min_card_ge_one_add_clog
open.informal: For an odd prime p, m(p) ≥ 1 + ⌈log₂ p⌉: every subset of Z/pZ with no unique sums has at least 1 + ⌈log₂ p⌉ elements.
open.statement:
theorem nus_min_card_ge_one_add_clog {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2) :
    1 + Nat.clog 2 p ≤ nus_min_card p
open.citation: arXiv:2610.09349 (A near-quadratic lower bound for sets with no unique sums), Appendix B (the lower bound 1 + ⌈log₂ p⌉ ≤ m(p), from Lemma B.1).

open.name: simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_le_two_mul_add_one_div_three
open.informal: Conjecture: if the finite graph G of order n has no isolated vertices, then for every vertex v the dominating sets containing v have average size at most (2n+1)/3.
open.statement:
theorem simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_le_two_mul_add_one_div_three {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hiso : ∀ w, 0 < G.degree w) (v : V) :
    simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v ≤ (2 * (Fintype.card V : ℚ) + 1) / 3
open.citation: arXiv:2610.11446 (On the local average order of dominating sets), list entry OP-135 (after Theorem 3.8, which proves avd_v(G) ≤ (5n−1)/6, attained only at n = 3). The conjectured exact maximum answers the entry's second question.

open.name: simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_lt_of_two_le_stem
open.informal: If G is a graph of order n ≥ 2 without isolated vertices and v is an l-stem with l ≥ 2, then avd_v(G) < (4n+1)/6.
open.statement:
theorem simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_lt_of_two_le_stem {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hn : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V)
    (hiso : ∀ w, 0 < G.degree w) (v : V) (hv : 2 ≤ simple_graph_leaf_neighbor_count G v) :
    simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v < (4 * (Fintype.card V : ℚ) + 1) / 6
open.citation: arXiv:2610.11446 (On the local average order of dominating sets), Theorem 5.3.

open.name: simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_stem_le
open.informal: Conjecture: if G is a graph of order n ≥ 2 without isolated vertices and v is an l-stem with l ≥ 1, then avd_v(G) ≤ (4n+1)/6, with equality if and only if l = 1 and G is star-like.
open.statement:
theorem simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order_stem_le {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hn : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V)
    (hiso : ∀ w, 0 < G.degree w) (v : V) (hv : 1 ≤ simple_graph_leaf_neighbor_count G v) :
    simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v ≤ (4 * (Fintype.card V : ℚ) + 1) / 6 ∧
      (simple_graph_local_avg_dominating_order G v = (4 * (Fintype.card V : ℚ) + 1) / 6 ↔
        simple_graph_leaf_neighbor_count G v = 1 ∧ simple_graph_is_star_like G)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.11446 (On the local average order of dominating sets), Conjecture 6.1. The paper proves the bound when every neighbour of v is a leaf or a stem (Theorem 5.2) and the strict bound for l ≥ 2 (Theorem 5.3); the open case is a 1-stem with a neighbour that is neither.

open.name: temporal_path_snapshots_explore_n_log_n
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.06228, Sec. 7): temporal graphs whose snapshots are all spanning paths can always be explored in O(n log n) steps; i.e. there is a constant C such that every such temporal graph on n ≥ 2 vertices can be explored from any start vertex within C·n·log n time steps. (A disproof shows that the exploration time can exceed Θ(n log n).)
open.statement:
theorem temporal_path_snapshots_explore_n_log_n :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∀ G : ℕ → SimpleGraph (Fin n), (∀ t, is_spanning_path_graph (G t)) →
      ∀ s : Fin n, ∃ (w : ℕ → Fin n) (T : ℕ), w 0 = s ∧ is_temporal_walk G w ∧
        temporal_walk_explores_by w T ∧ (T : ℝ) ≤ C * n * Real.log n
open.citation: open question of arXiv:2610.06228 (Hiding a Vertex from the Temporal Explorer), Sec. 7 ('The role of the hub'): the best known lower bound for path snapshots is Ω(n log n) and it is unknown whether it can be improved; the general upper bound is O(n²)

open.name: resolution_fpt_incidence_treewidth
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.02047, abstract and Sec. 8): every unsatisfiable CNF formula has an FPT-sized resolution refutation parameterized by incidence treewidth; that is, there are a computable g : N -> N and a constant c >= 1 such that every unsatisfiable CNF formula F with n variables and m clauses has a resolution refutation (initial clauses, weakening, resolution) of length at most g(tw*(F)) * (n + m)^c.
open.statement: theorem resolution_fpt_incidence_treewidth : ∃ g : ℕ → ℕ, Computable g ∧ ∃ c : ℕ, 1 ≤ c ∧ ∀ F : Finset (Finset (CnfLit ℕ)), ¬ CnfSatisfiable (F.toList.map Finset.toList) → ∃ π, is_resolution_refutation F π ∧ π.length ≤ g (cnf_incidence_treewidth F) * ((cnf_vars F).card + F.card) ^ c
open.citation: the open problem of arXiv:2610.02047, abstract and Sec. 8 (FPT-sized resolution refutations parameterized by incidence treewidth), stated as posed

open.name: ccz_layer_t_count_below_6m_plus_1_with_hadamards
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.01024, abstract and Sec. 1): in general Clifford+T circuits, with Hadamards anywhere and any number of clean ancillas, some layer of m >= 2 disjoint CCZ gates can be implemented with strictly fewer than 6m + 1 T gates (the exact count 6m + 1 is proved only for Hadamard-free circuits).
open.statement: theorem ccz_layer_t_count_below_6m_plus_1_with_hadamards : ∃ m : ℕ, 2 ≤ m ∧ ∃ (a : ℕ) (gs : List (CliffordTGate (3 * m + a))), implements_ccz_layer m a gs ∧ clifford_t_circuit_t_count gs < 6 * m + 1
open.citation: the open problem of arXiv:2610.01024, abstract and Sec. 1 (fewer than 6m + 1 T gates with Hadamards and ancillas), stated as posed; related: its Corollary 83

open.name: gf8_oracle_t_count_ge_24
open.informal: Negation of the premise of Open Problem 10 of arXiv:2610.01024: every set of nonzero parities on nine qubits whose order-1, 2, 3 moments equal the syndrome of the GF(8) multiplication oracle has at least 24 elements, i.e. delta(U_3) > 23, so the T-count is none of 20, 21, 22, 23. Evidence (not a Lean proof): a SAT encoding of the moment equations, which reproduces the known values 7 (CCZ), 17 (GF(4)) and 2n + 1 for the line cubic with n = 5..8, is unsatisfiable for every size up to 26 and satisfiable at 29.
open.statement: theorem gf8_oracle_t_count_ge_24 (S : Finset (Finset (Fin 9))) (hS : is_parity_repr S gf8_oracle_syndrome) : 24 ≤ S.card
open.citation: would refute the premise of Open Problem 10 of arXiv:2610.01024 (T-count in [20, 23]); related: its Proposition 59 floor of 20

open.name: gf8_oracle_t_count_le_23
open.informal: Open Problem 10 of arXiv:2610.01024 presupposes that the T-count delta(U_3) of the GF(8) multiplication oracle (Hadamard-free {CNOT, T} circuits, diagonal Cliffords free) lies in [20, 23] and asks for its value: this is the upper end, that some set of at most 23 nonzero parities on nine qubits has order-1, 2, 3 moments equal to the oracle's syndrome. A SAT search run on 2026-10-05 found no such set of size at most 26 (not a Lean proof).
open.statement: theorem gf8_oracle_t_count_le_23 : ∃ S : Finset (Finset (Fin 9)), is_parity_repr S gf8_oracle_syndrome ∧ S.card ≤ 23
open.citation: the premise of Open Problem 10 of arXiv:2610.01024 (T-count of the GF(8) multiplication oracle in [20, 23]), upper end, stated as posed

open.name: open_problem_line_cubic_t_count
open.informal: For every integer n ≥ 5, there exists a parity representation of the line cubic syndrome of cardinality 2n + 1.
open.statement: theorem open_problem_line_cubic_t_count (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n) : ∃ S : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), is_parity_repr S (line_syndrome n) ∧ S.card = 2 * n + 1
open.citation: arXiv:2610.01024, Appendix K.2, item 1

literature.title: Existence of a 22-multiplication algorithm for 3x3 matrix multiplication over ℤ
literature.statement: Does there exist an algorithm for 3x3 matrix multiplication with integer constants that can be applied recursively (or equivalently, a bilinear decomposition of the 3x3 matrix multiplication tensor over ℤ) using 22 multiplications, or is 23 multiplications the minimum?
literature.source_title: Lower Bound of 22 for 3x3 Matrix Multiplication over the Integers
literature.rationale: The authors prove a lower bound of 22 multiplications for any recursive 3x3 algorithm with integer constants, improving the previous bound of 21. Laderman's 1976 algorithm provides an upper bound of 23. Whether 22 is achievable over the integers remains unresolved.

literature.title: Tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over F2
literature.statement: Is the tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over the finite field F2 equal to 22 or 23? That is, does there exist a set of 22 triad products whose F2-linear combinations compute the product of two arbitrary 3x3 matrices over F2, or is the rank at least 23?
literature.source_title: Lower Bound of 22 for 3x3 Matrix Multiplication over the Integers
literature.rationale: The paper proves in Lean that the tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over F2 is at least 22 (class 495 in Wang's table), improving on the lower bound of 21 from Wang (2026) and Yang et al. (2026). Laderman's 1976 decomposition yields an upper bound of 23 over F2. Thus the exact rank over F2 is either 22 or 23, leaving a gap of exactly one.

literature.title: T-count of parallel CCZ gates in general Clifford+T with Hadamards
literature.statement: Let m ≥ 2 be an integer, and let U_m = ⨂_{j=1}^m CCZ_{3j-2, 3j-1, 3j} be the unitary operator on 3m qubits that acts as the three-qubit Controlled-Controlled-Z gate CCZ = diag(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, -1) on each disjoint triplet of qubits (3j-2, 3j-1, 3j). In a general Clifford+T quantum circuit with an arbitrary number a ≥ 0 of clean ancilla qubits (initialized and returned to |0⟩), where gates may be arbitrary single-qubit Hadamards H, phase gates S = diag(1, i), CNOT gates, and T = diag(1, e^{iπ/4}) gates: can U_m be implemented using strictly fewer than 6m + 1 gates of type T?
literature.source_title: Exact $T$-counts of Toffoli layers from an isotropy bound
literature.rationale: The paper proves that every Hadamard-free Clifford+T circuit with clean ancillas implementing m disjoint CCZ gates requires at least 6m+1 T gates, which matches the Campbell-Howard construction. However, general Clifford+T circuits may place Hadamard gates freely between T gates. For m = 1, it is known that CCZ requires 7 T gates even with Hadamards, but for m ≥ 2 it is unknown whether intermediate Hadamard gates can reduce the T-count below 6m+1.

literature.title: Exact T-count of the line cubic phase gate family
literature.statement: For an integer n ≥ 5, let f_n : (ZMod 2)^n → ZMod 2 be the cubic form f_n(x_1, ..., x_n) = ∑_{i=1}^{n-2} x_i x_{i+1} x_{i+2}, and let U_{f_n} be the diagonal n-qubit gate acting by |x⟩ ↦ (-1)^{f_n(x)} |x⟩. Let δ(U_{f_n}) denote the minimum number of T gates required to implement U_{f_n} in a Hadamard-free {CNOT, T} circuit with diagonal Clifford gates free. By Proposition 65, δ(U_{f_n}) ≥ 2n + 1 for all n ≥ 5, with equality δ(U_{f_n}) = 2n + 1 known to hold for 5 ≤ n ≤ 12. Does δ(U_{f_n}) = 2n + 1 hold for all n ≥ 5?
literature.source_title: Exact $T$-counts of Toffoli layers from an isotropy bound

literature.title: Exact T-count of the GF(8) multiplication oracle
literature.statement: Let U_3 be the reversible multiplication oracle for the finite field GF(8) = GF(2^3) acting on 9 qubits by |a, b, c⟩ ↦ |a, b, c ⊕ (a · b)⟩ for a, b, c ∈ GF(8). Under Clifford equivalence to a diagonal level-three gate, its T-count δ(U_3) in Hadamard-free {CNOT, T} circuits with clean ancillas is known to satisfy 20 ≤ δ(U_3) ≤ 23, where 20 is the slice-rank lower bound (Proposition 59) and 23 is achieved by known compiled circuits. What is the exact T-count δ(U_3) of the GF(8) oracle? Specifically, is it 20, 23, or an intermediate value (21 or 22)?
literature.source_title: Exact $T$-counts of Toffoli layers from an isotropy bound

literature.title: FPT-sized resolution refutations parameterized by incidence treewidth
literature.statement: Does every unsatisfiable CNF formula have an FPT-sized resolution refutation parameterized by its incidence treewidth? Precisely: do there exist a computable function $g: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a constant $c \ge 1$ such that for every unsatisfiable CNF formula $F$ with $n$ variables and $m$ clauses, there exists a resolution refutation of $F$ of length at most $g(\mathrm{tw}^*(F)) (n+m)^c$? Here, a CNF formula $F$ is a finite set of clauses over a finite set of Boolean variables $V$, where each clause is a finite disjunction of literals (variables or their negations); the incidence graph $G^*(F)$ is the bipartite graph with vertex set $V \cup F$ and edges $\{x, C\}$ for every variable $x \in \mathrm{var}(C)$; $\mathrm{tw}^*(F)$ is the treewidth of $G^*(F)$; and a resolution refutation is a sequence of clauses ending in $\bot$ derived by weakening and resolution.
literature.source_title: Short Resolution Refutations for CNFs with Bounded Weighted Incidence Treewidth
literature.rationale: Central open question in parameterized proof complexity, explicitly highlighted in the paper's abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

literature.title: EFX existence for four or more agents with additive goods
literature.statement: There are $n$ agents $N=\{1,\dots,n\}$ and a finite set $M$ of $m$ indivisible goods. Agent $i$ has an additive valuation $v_i(S)=\sum_{g\in S} v_i(g)$ with $v_i(g)\ge 0$. An allocation is an ordered partition $A=(A_1,\dots,A_n)$ of $M$ (every good is allocated; bundles may be empty). The allocation is EFX (envy-free up to any good) if for all agents $i\ne j$ and every good $g\in A_j$ we have $v_i(A_i)\ge v_i(A_j\setminus\{g\})$. Question: for every $n\ge 4$, every $m$ and every additive valuation profile, does an EFX allocation exist? (Some papers quantify only over $g$ with $v_i(g)>0$; for strictly positive values the two versions coincide, and both are open. The smallest open case is $n=4$.)
literature.source_title: Fair Division of Indivisible Goods: Recent Progress and Open Questions
literature.location: Sec. 4.1, Open Problem 2 (EFX itself first proposed in 'The Unreasonable Fairness of Maximum Nash Welfare', ACM TEAC 2019, DOI:10.1145/3355902, which left existence open)
literature.rationale: Widely called the central open problem of discrete fair division. Known: $n=2$ (cut-and-choose, arXiv:1707.04769); $n=3$ with additive valuations ('EFX Exists for Three Agents', arXiv:2002.05119), extended to three agents when at least one valuation is additive/MMS-feasible (arXiv:2205.07638); EFX with at most one unallocated good for $n=4$ (arXiv:2102.10654); EFX with at most $n-2$ unallocated goods in general (arXiv:2102.10654, arXiv:2107.09901); complete EFX when $m\le n+3$ and, for $n=4$, when $m\le 9$ (arXiv:2608.08590, computer-assisted); EFX for up to three valuation types ('EFX Exists for Three Types of Agents', EC 2025); EF2X for four agents (arXiv:2412.00254); EFX on multigraph instances (arXiv:2606.18665). On the negative side, EFX fails for three agents with monotone submodular valuations (arXiv:2604.18216, arXiv:2605.06451) and for $n\ge 4$ additive chores (arXiv:2606.08872), but no additive-goods counterexample is known.

literature.title: EFX for three agents with additive chores
literature.statement: There are $3$ agents and a finite set $M$ of $m$ indivisible chores. Agent $i$ has an additive cost function $c_i(S)=\sum_{e\in S}c_i(e)$ with $c_i(e)\ge 0$. An allocation is a partition $A=(A_1,A_2,A_3)$ of $M$ (all chores assigned). It is EFX for chores if for all agents $i\ne j$ and every chore $e\in A_i$, $c_i(A_i\setminus\{e\})\le c_i(A_j)$. Question: does every such 3-agent instance admit an EFX allocation? (Variant quantifying only over $e$ with $c_i(e)>0$ is equally open; with strictly positive costs they coincide.)
literature.source_title: EFX for Additive Chores: Nonexistence, Pareto Incompatibility, and Bi-Valued Existence
literature.location: Sec. 1 (introduction) and Sec. 6 (open problems); the n=3 gap is also the explicit frontier in arXiv:2609.10585
literature.rationale: After the 2026 counterexample for every $n\ge 4$ (tri-valued costs, two agent types, three chore types; arXiv:2606.08872), three agents is the only remaining number of agents for which EFX existence under additive costs is undecided (two agents is easy by cut-and-choose). Known for $n=3$: all instances with $m\le 8$ chores (arXiv:2609.10585, SMT-verified); personalized bi-valued instances; EFX together with fractional Pareto optimality for bi-valued costs; instances with $m\le 2n$; two chore types. Approximate EFX results exist (e.g. arXiv:2410.18655). A small-$n$ question with a finite search frontier ($m=9$ next), so it is a natural target for computer-assisted search and Lean-checked certificates.

literature.title: Best universal approximation ratio for maximin share with additive goods
literature.statement: There are $n$ agents $N=\{1,\dots,n\}$ and a finite set $M$ of $m$ indivisible goods. Agent $i$ has an additive valuation $v_i(S)=\sum_{g\in S} v_i(g)$ with $v_i(g)\ge 0$. An allocation is an ordered partition $A=(A_1,\dots,A_n)$ of $M$ (every good is allocated; bundles may be empty). The maximin share of agent $i$ is $\mu_i=\max_{(P_1,\dots,P_n)}\min_k v_i(P_k)$, the maximum over all partitions of $M$ into $n$ bundles. For $\alpha\in(0,1]$ an allocation is $\alpha$-MMS if $v_i(A_i)\ge\alpha\,\mu_i$ for every $i$. Let $\alpha^*$ be the supremum of $\alpha$ such that every instance (any $n$, $m$, additive $v$) admits an $\alpha$-MMS allocation. Question: determine $\alpha^*$; currently $7/9\le\alpha^*\le 20/21$.
literature.source_title: Fair Division of Indivisible Goods: Recent Progress and Open Questions
literature.rationale: Exact MMS allocations need not exist for $n\ge 3$, so the right constant is a central question. Lower bounds: $3/4+3/3836$ (arXiv:2307.07304), $10/13$ (arXiv:2510.10423), and $7/9$ with an FPTAS for $7/9-\varepsilon$ (arXiv:2511.13056). Upper bounds: $39/40$ for three agents (arXiv:2104.04977), improved to $20/21$ with four agents and eleven goods, together with an asymptotic bound $1-\Omega((\log n)^{-2})$ (arXiv:2609.15085). The gap $[0.778, 0.952]$ remains wide.

literature.title: Best universal approximation ratio for maximin share with additive chores
literature.statement: There are $n$ agents and a finite set $M$ of indivisible chores; agent $i$ has an additive cost $c_i(S)=\sum_{e\in S}c_i(e)$ with $c_i(e)\ge 0$. An allocation partitions $M$ into $(A_1,\dots,A_n)$. The maximin share (for chores) is $\mu_i=\min_{(P_1,\dots,P_n)}\max_k c_i(P_k)$ over all partitions of $M$ into $n$ bundles. For $\beta\ge 1$ an allocation is $\beta$-MMS if $c_i(A_i)\le\beta\,\mu_i$ for all $i$. Let $\beta^*$ be the infimum of $\beta$ such that every instance admits a $\beta$-MMS allocation. Question: determine $\beta^*$; currently $31/30\le\beta^*\le 13/11$.
literature.source_title: Approximation Algorithms for Max-Min Share Allocations of Indivisible Chores and Goods
literature.rationale: The chores counterpart of OP-9, introduced in arXiv:1604.01435 (which showed exact MMS can fail for chores and gave a 2-approximation). Existence bound $13/11$ through a reduction to the MultiFit job-scheduling algorithm (arXiv:2302.04581), with better bounds for small $n$ ($15/13$ for $n=3$ there; $19/18$ for three agents in arXiv:2205.05363). Impossibility $44/43$ with three agents (arXiv:2104.04977), improved to $31/30$ with four agents and eleven chores, plus asymptotic $1+\Omega((\log n)^{-2})$ (arXiv:2609.15085).

literature.title: Maximin share approximation for three agents with additive goods
literature.statement: Same model as the general MMS problem (see OP-9) with exactly $n=3$ agents: finite goods set $M$, additive $v_i\ge 0$, $\mu_i=\max$ over partitions of $M$ into 3 bundles of the minimum bundle value, and an allocation is $\alpha$-MMS if $v_i(A_i)\ge\alpha\mu_i$ for $i=1,2,3$. Let $\alpha_3^*$ be the largest $\alpha$ such that every 3-agent instance admits an $\alpha$-MMS allocation. Question: determine $\alpha_3^*$; currently $11/12\le\alpha_3^*\le 39/40$.
literature.source_title: Improved maximin fair allocation of indivisible items to three agents
