literature.statement: Let A, B ∈ [0, 1]^{m × n} be rational payoff matrices for a two-player normal-form game. A mixed strategy profile (x, y) ∈ Δ_m × Δ_n is an ε-approximate Nash equilibrium if for all pure strategies i ∈ {1, ..., m}, e_iᵀ A y - xᵀ A y ≤ ε, and for all pure strategies j ∈ {1, ..., n}, xᵀ B e_j - xᵀ B y ≤ ε. Does there exist an absolute constant c < 0.3 and a deterministic or randomized algorithm that, given any such game and any rational δ > 0, outputs a (c + δ)-approximate Nash equilibrium in time polynomial in the game's bit length and 1/δ?
literature.source_title: A Simple Algorithm Breaking the 1/3 Barrier for Approximate Nash Equilibria in Bimatrix Games
literature.rationale: The paper achieves an approximation guarantee of ~0.30954 + δ, breaking the longstanding 1/3 barrier. In Section 6, the authors explicitly identify breaking 0.3 (a constant c < 0.3, typeset as 'c 0' in the text conversion) as the immediate open frontier where proof complexity became the main barrier.

literature.title: Existence of a Polynomial-Time Approximation Scheme for Bimatrix Games
literature.statement: Does there exist a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) for Nash equilibria in bimatrix games? That is, for every fixed rational constant ε > 0, does there exist an algorithm that, given any two-player game with payoff matrices A, B ∈ [0, 1]^{m × n} with rational entries, computes an ε-approximate Nash equilibrium (x, y) ∈ Δ_m × Δ_n in time polynomial in the encoding size of (A, B)?
literature.source_title: A Simple Algorithm Breaking the 1/3 Barrier for Approximate Nash Equilibria in Bimatrix Games
literature.rationale: The paper improves the best known polynomial-time approximation guarantee from 1/3 to 0.30954. A fundamental open question in algorithmic game theory mentioned in Section 1 is determining the infimum error achievable in polynomial time: does there exist a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) for approximate Nash equilibria in bimatrix games, or is there an absolute inapproximability lower bound ε₀ > 0 for polynomial-time algorithms?

literature.title: Complexity of maximizing Nash social welfare with two item types
literature.statement: In the high-multiplicity fair division setting with additive nonnegative utilities and multiplicities encoded in binary, consider instances with q = 2 item types and an arbitrary number of agent types. Is the problem of computing an allocation of indivisible goods that maximizes the Nash social welfare NSW(x) = (∏_{i=1}^n u_i(x_i))^{1/n} solvable in polynomial time, or is the rational-threshold decision problem NP-hard?
literature.source_title: Maximizing $p$-Mean Social Welfare in the High-Multiplicity Setting: Few Agent Types and Few Item Types
literature.rationale: For all finite rational p < 1 with p ≠ 0, the authors prove that computing an optimal allocation is NP-hard with two item types (Theorem 1). For p = -∞ (egalitarian welfare), two item types is solvable in polynomial time (Theorem 8). For Nash welfare (p = 0), NP-hardness is proved for three item types (Theorem 2) and polynomial time for one item type (Theorem 7), leaving the case of two item types open.

literature.title: Tightness of exploration time lower bound for degree-bounded temporal graphs
literature.statement: Let $\mathcal{G} = (G_t)_{t \ge 1}$ be a temporal graph on a finite vertex set $V$ of size $n$, where each snapshot $G_t = (V, E_t)$ is a simple connected undirected graph on $V$, and the underlying graph $U(\mathcal{G}) = (V, \bigcup_{t \ge 1} E_t)$ has maximum degree at most $\Delta$. A temporal walk of length $\ell$ from a start vertex $v^* \in V$ is a sequence $(v_1, \ldots, v_{\ell+1})$ in $V$ with $v_1 = v^*$ such that for every $t \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$, either $v_{t+1} = v_t$ or $\{v_t, v_{t+1}\} \in E_t$. It explores $\mathcal{G}$ if $\{v_1, \ldots, v_{\ell+1}\} = V$. Is the lower bound $\Omega(\Delta n (1 + \log(n/\Delta)))$ tight? That is, does there exist an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that every always-connected temporal graph on $n$ vertices with underlying maximum degree at most $\Delta$ can be explored from any start vertex in at most $C \cdot \Delta n (1 + \ln(n / \Delta))$ time steps? In particular, for constant $\Delta = O(1)$, can every always-connected temporal graph of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ be explored in $O(n \log n)$ time steps?
literature.source_title: Hiding a Vertex from the Temporal Explorer: A Lower Bound for Degree-Bounded Temporal Graphs

literature.title: Exploration time lower bound for temporal graphs with path snapshots
literature.statement: Let $\mathcal{G} = (G_t)_{t \ge 1}$ be a temporal graph on a set $V$ of $n$ vertices such that every snapshot $G_t$ is a path graph spanning $V$ (i.e., a connected graph where two vertices have degree 1 and $n-2$ vertices have degree 2). An agent starts at an arbitrary vertex $v_1 \in V$ and at each time step $t \ge 1$ either stays at its current vertex or traverses an edge of $G_t$. Can the worst-case exploration time of such temporal graphs exceed $\Theta(n \log n)$? Specifically, does there exist a family of temporal graphs on $n$ vertices whose snapshots are all spanning paths requiring $\omega(n \log n)$ steps (e.g., $\Omega(n \log^2 n)$ or $n^{1 + \varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon > 0$) to explore from some start vertex, or does every such temporal graph admit an exploration in $O(n \log n)$ steps?
literature.source_title: Hiding a Vertex from the Temporal Explorer: A Lower Bound for Degree-Bounded Temporal Graphs
literature.location: Sec. 7, under "The role of the hub"

literature.title: Degree-dependent exploration lower bound under two moves per time step
literature.statement: Consider temporal graph exploration in the two-moves-per-step model: at each time step $t \ge 1$, an agent at vertex $v_t$ may traverse a path of length at most 2 in snapshot $G_t$ to reach $v_{t+1}$ (that is, $v_{t+1}$ is at graph distance at most 2 from $v_t$ in $G_t$). An exploration is complete when every vertex in $V$ has been visited at the start or intermediate vertex of some step. For always-connected temporal graphs on $n$ vertices with underlying maximum degree at most $\Delta$, does any lower bound on exploration time with linear (or super-constant) dependence on $\Delta$ survive? That is, does there exist a constant $c > 0$ such that for arbitrarily large $n$ and $\Delta$, some always-connected temporal graph requires $\Omega(\Delta n)$ (or $\Omega(f(\Delta) n)$ for some $f(\Delta) = \omega(1)$) time steps to explore under two moves per step, or can every such temporal graph be explored in $o(\Delta n)$ (or $O(n \log n)$) steps?
literature.source_title: Hiding a Vertex from the Temporal Explorer: A Lower Bound for Degree-Bounded Temporal Graphs
literature.location: Sec. 7, under "Several moves per time step"

literature.title: Explicit polynomial-size robust subspace designs for all dimensions
literature.statement: For positive integers $k \le n$, an operator-norm bounded family of linear maps $Q_1, \ldots, Q_m: \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}^k$ (with $\|Q_i\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le 1$) is a $(k, \eta, \Delta)$-weak robust subspace design if for every $k$-dimensional subspace $W \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n$, at most $\Delta$ indices $i \in [m]$ satisfy $\sigma_{\min}(Q_i|_W) \le \eta$, where $\sigma_{\min}(Q_i|_W) = \inf_{w \in W, \|w\|=1} \|Q_i w\|$. Does there exist an explicit (deterministic polynomial-time or logspace-uniform) construction that, given $n$ and $1 \le k \le n$, outputs a $(k, \eta, \Delta)$-weak robust subspace design $\mathcal{Q}_{n,k} = \{Q_1, \ldots, Q_m\}$ with entries in $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ such that the size $m \le n^{c}$ and the robustness $\eta \ge n^{-c}$ for some universal constant $c > 0$, with $\Delta \le m - 1$?
literature.source_title: Robust subspace designs and the power of a unique small quantum witness
literature.rationale: The paper shows that a random family of $O(k(n-k)\log(nk))$ Gaussian matrices achieves inverse-polynomial robustness $\eta = \Theta(1/\sqrt{nk})$ with high probability. However, its explicit deterministic construction based on sketching and coordinate projections has size $O(n^4 k^{O(k)})$, which is polynomial only when $k = O(\log n / \log \log n)$. Derandomizing this to an explicit polynomial-size construction for all $1 \le k \le n$ would derandomize quantum witness isolation from randomized logspace to deterministic logspace.

literature.title: Truthful polynomial-communication mechanism beating 1/2 for two XOS valuations
literature.statement: Consider a two-bidder combinatorial auction on a set $M$ of $m$ items, where each bidder $i \in \{1, 2\}$ has an XOS valuation $v_i : 2^M \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, meaning $v_i(S) = \max_{k \in K_i} \sum_{e \in S} a_{k, e}^{(i)}$ for a finite collection of nonnegative additive supporting clauses $a_k^{(i)}$. Does there exist a constant $\varepsilon > 0$ and an individually rational, no-negative-transfers truthful (ex-post Nash or dominant-strategy incentive-compatible) mechanism using at most $\operatorname{poly}(m)$ bits of communication that attains expected social welfare at least $(1/2 + \varepsilon) \max_{S \subseteq M} (v_1(S) + v_2(M \setminus S))$ on every pair of XOS valuations $(v_1, v_2)$?
literature.source_title: The Hardness of Dominant Strategy Mechanism Design, Revisited

literature.title: Tight deterministic DSIC approximation ratio for XOS combinatorial auctions
literature.statement: For an auction with $m$ items and parameter $\gamma \in [\log m, m]$, let $\mathsf{DSIC_{XOS}}(m, \gamma)$ denote the best social welfare approximation ratio attainable by a deterministic, individually rational, no-negative-transfers DSIC mechanism using at most $2^\gamma$ communication when bidders have XOS valuations. The paper proves a lower bound $\mathsf{DSIC_{XOS}}(m, \gamma) = \Omega((m/\gamma)^{1/5})$. Is the true optimal approximation ratio $\mathsf{DSIC_{XOS}}(m, \gamma) = \tilde{\Theta}((m/\gamma)^{1/2})$, matching the known bound for maximal-in-range truthful mechanisms, or can deterministic DSIC mechanisms achieve an approximation ratio $o((m/\gamma)^{1/2})$?
literature.source_title: The Hardness of Dominant Strategy Mechanism Design, Revisited
literature.location: Sec. 5, Beyond Reductions to Simultaneous Lower Bounds

literature.title: Existence of a Strong Equilibrium in Unweighted Max-k-Cut Games
literature.statement: Let $G = (V, E)$ be a finite simple unweighted graph and let $k \ge 3$ be an integer. In the unweighted Max-$k$-Cut game on $(G, k)$, each player $v \in V$ chooses a strategy $\sigma(v) \in \{1, \dots, k\}$, and player $v$'s utility is $u_v(\sigma) = |\{w \in N(v) : \sigma(w) \neq \sigma(v)\}|$, where $N(v)$ denotes the open neighborhood of $v$ in $G$. A strong deviation from a strategy profile $\sigma: V \to \{1, \dots, k\}$ is a non-empty coalition $S \subseteq V$ and a profile $\tau: V \to \{1, \dots, k\}$ such that $\tau(v) = \sigma(v)$ for all $v \in V \setminus S$ and $u_v(\tau) > u_v(\sigma)$ for all $v \in S$. A profile $\sigma$ is a strong equilibrium if it admits no strong deviation. Does every finite simple unweighted graph admit a strong equilibrium in the Max-$k$-Cut game for every $k \ge 3$?
literature.source_title: Social Optimality Does Not Imply Coalitional Stability in Unweighted Max-k-Cut Games
literature.rationale: While the paper exhibits an unweighted graph where an optimal coloring admits a profitable coalitional deviation, the coalition deviates to another optimal coloring that may itself be stable, leaving the universal existence of strong equilibria unresolved.

literature.title: Maximum Degree Threshold for Coalitional Stability of Optimal Colorings
literature.statement: For an integer $k \ge 3$, let $\Delta^*(k)$ denote the largest integer $D$ such that for every finite simple unweighted graph $G = (V, E)$ with maximum degree $\Delta(G) \le D$, every cut-maximizing coloring $\sigma: V \to \{1, \dots, k\}$ in the unweighted Max-$k$-Cut game is a strong equilibrium. It is known that $\Delta^*(k) \ge 2k - 1$ (which gives $\Delta^*(3) \ge 5$). What is the exact value of $\Delta^*(k)$ for each $k \ge 3$, and in particular, what is the exact value of $\Delta^*(3)$?
literature.source_title: Social Optimality Does Not Imply Coalitional Stability in Unweighted Max-k-Cut Games
literature.rationale: Corollary 9 shows that every optimal coloring is a strong equilibrium whenever the maximum degree satisfies $\Delta(G) \le 2k - 1$ (recovering a known bound), while Theorem 2 provides a counterexample where $\Delta(G) > 2k - 1$. The paper leaves open the sharp maximum degree threshold separating graphs where all optimal colorings are coalitionally stable from those admitting unstable optima.

literature.title: Tight asymptotic threshold for MMS allocations with monotone goods
literature.statement: Let M be a set of m indivisible items and N = {1, ..., n} a set of n ≥ 2 agents. Each agent i ∈ N has a monotone valuation function v_i : 2^M → ℝ with v_i(∅) = 0 and v_i(S) ≤ v_i(T) whenever S ⊆ T ⊆ M. The maximin share of agent i is MMS(M, v_i, n) = max_{P} min_{j ∈ [n]} v_i(P_j), where the maximum is over all partitions P = (P_1, ..., P_n) of M into n bundles. An allocation A = (A_1, ..., A_n) of M is an MMS allocation if v_i(A_i) ≥ MMS(M, v_i, n) for all i ∈ N. Define μ(n) to be the largest integer m such that every instance with n agents, at most m goods, and monotone valuations has an MMS allocation. Is μ(n) = n + log_2 n + o(log_2 n) as n → ∞?
literature.source_title: On MMS allocations with few items
literature.rationale: The paper establishes that μ(n) = n + Θ(log n), showing the upper bound μ(n) ≤ n + log_2 n + O(log log n) in Theorem 6 and the lower bound μ(n) ≥ n + c log_2 n for c ≈ 0.93 in Lemma 9 and Lemma 8. Closing the gap to determine whether the leading constant is 1 remains open.

literature.title: Universal Constant for General-to-Internal Collage System Conversion
literature.source_title: A Factor-5 Conversion to Internal Collage Systems
literature.rationale: The paper proves an upper bound of $5m$ (and more precisely $4m+a-b$, where $a$ is the number of original truncation rules and $b$ is the breaker count) for converting an arbitrary collage system of size $m$ into an equivalent internal collage system. The proof intentionally allows worst-case helper charges to each lineage, suggesting that a tighter accounting could further reduce the constant.

literature.title: Existence of an optimal coloring that is a strong equilibrium in unweighted Max-k-Cut games
literature.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple unweighted graph and $k\ge 3$. In the unweighted Max-$k$-Cut game each vertex picks a color in $\{1,\dots,k\}$ and its utility is the number of neighbours with a different color; a coloring is optimal if it maximizes the total utility (equivalently, the cut value), and a strong equilibrium if no nonempty coalition can jointly recolor so that every member strictly gains. Does every such game admit an optimal coloring that is a strong equilibrium? (Not every optimal coloring is one: arXiv:2610.04948, Theorem 2.)
literature.rationale: A positive answer implies existence of strong equilibria (OP-85); the paper's counterexample (Remark 6) does not rule out another, stable optimum on its graph. Optimal colorings are strong equilibria when the maximum degree is at most 2k-1.

literature.title: Undirected Multiple-Unicast Coding Advantage over the Binary Field
literature.statement: Does there exist an undirected graph $G = (V, E)$ with edge capacities $c \colon E \to \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ and source-sink pairs $(s_1, t_1), \ldots, (s_k, t_k)$ such that the throughput achievable by deterministic linear network coding over the binary field $\mathbb{F}_2$ strictly exceeds the maximum common rate supported by fractional multicommodity flow?
literature.source_title: The Multiple Unicast Conjecture is False
literature.rationale: The paper refutes the undirected multiple-unicast conjecture by constructing an explicit linear network code over the field with 9 elements on a 182-vertex graph derived from PG(2,9), achieving common throughput 1 where fractional multicommodity flow cannot exceed 147/157. The construction crucially uses the projective geometry of PG(2,9) and degree-4 polynomials over F_9. The paper leaves untouched whether any coding advantage over multicommodity flow is possible using linear (or non-linear) network codes over the binary field F_2.

literature.title: Logarithmic Undirected Multiple-Unicast Coding Gap
literature.statement: Let $g(n)$ denote the maximum ratio of network coding throughput to fractional multicommodity flow throughput among all undirected multiple-unicast instances on $n$-vertex graphs. Is $g(n) = \Theta(\log n)$? Specifically, does there exist an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that $g(n) \ge C \log n$ for all sufficiently large $n$?
literature.source_title: The Multiple Unicast Conjecture is False
literature.rationale: Corollary 1.2 proves that the undirected multiple-unicast coding gap is $\Omega((\log n)^\varepsilon)$ for some constant $\varepsilon > 0$, by combining the 182-vertex counterexample with known graph-product amplification methods. Meanwhile, standard multicommodity flow-cut bounds establish an upper bound of $O(\log n)$. The paper leaves open the exact asymptotic order of the undirected coding gap, and in particular whether it can match the upper bound $\Theta(\log n)$.

literature.title: Linear Dimension Dependence of Fictitious Play Convergence Rates Without Ties
literature.statement: Let n ≥ 2 be an integer. For an n x n payoff matrix A of a two-player zero-sum game, consider simultaneous fictitious play where after an initial move, every subsequent best response for each player is unique. Does there exist a constant c > 0 such that for arbitrarily large n, there exists an n x n matrix A and an initial action with unique subsequent best responses along the trajectory such that the duality gap satisfies Gap_A(x_t/t, y_t/t) = Ω(t^{-c/n}) as t → ∞?
literature.source_title: Arbitrarily Slow Polynomial Convergence of Fictitious Play
literature.rationale: The paper constructs games of dimension n_k = (k+1)^2 - 5 with convergence rate Theta(t^{-1/k}), which gives an exponent of order Theta(1/sqrt(n)) in terms of the number of actions n. On the other hand, the classic upper bound of Shapiro (1958) establishes that the duality gap on any n x n matrix decays as O(t^{-1/(2n-2)}), i.e., with rate exponent at least 1/(2n-2). While an adversarial tie-breaking rule can achieve rate Theta(t^{-1/n}) on the n x n identity matrix (as shown in 2014), it remains open whether this linear dimension dependence Theta(1/n) in the rate exponent can be achieved with unique best responses (or any fixed tie-breaking rule), or whether the Theta(1/sqrt(n)) scaling achieved by the recursive clock construction is optimal.

literature.title: Linear-exponent resolution lower bound for multiplier associativity
literature.statement: Let $\mathsf{Assoc}_n$ be the unsatisfiable CNF formula encoding the associativity of $n$-bit multiplication under a strip-local multiplier encoding (such as the standard array multiplier or Wallace-tree multiplier). Does there exist an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$, every resolution refutation of $\mathsf{Assoc}_n$ requires size at least $2^{c n}$?
literature.source_title: Associativity of Multiplication Is Hard for Resolution
literature.rationale: The paper proves a resolution size lower bound of 2^{Ω((n/log n)^{1/4})} by embedding an m-vertex bipartite expander matching instance into n = O(m^4 log m) bits. A linear exponent 2^{Ω(n)} would match the maximal hardness possible for resolution on formulas with O(n) or O(n^2) variables.

literature.title: Proof complexity of multiplier associativity in Cutting Planes and Polynomial Calculus
literature.statement: Let $\mathsf{Assoc}_n$ be the CNF formula encoding the associativity of $n$-bit multiplication under a strip-local multiplier architecture. Does $\mathsf{Assoc}_n$ require super-polynomial (or exponential) size refutations in Cutting Planes (CP), and in Polynomial Calculus with Resolution (PCR) over any field $\mathbb{F}$?
literature.source_title: Associativity of Multiplication Is Hard for Resolution
literature.rationale: Word-level associativity admits O(n^2)-length polynomial calculus proofs, but extracting bit-level equalities from word-level equalities is known to require exponentially many monomials. The paper's reduction from bipartite expander matching fails to give lower bounds for Cutting Planes or Polynomial Calculus because the matching principle has small proofs in both systems.

literature.title: Tight resolution lower bound for multiplier commutativity and distributivity
literature.statement: Let $\mathsf{Comm}_n$ and $\mathsf{Dist}_n$ be the CNF formulas encoding the negation of commutativity $\mathbf{x}\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{y}\mathbf{x}$ and distributivity $\mathbf{x}(\mathbf{y}+\mathbf{z}) = \mathbf{x}\mathbf{y} + \mathbf{x}\mathbf{z}$ for $n$-bit multipliers, respectively. Does every resolution refutation of $\mathsf{Comm}_n$ (and $\mathsf{Dist}_n$) require size $\Omega(n^6 \log n)$?
literature.source_title: Associativity of Multiplication Is Hard for Resolution
literature.rationale: Upper bounds of size O(n^6 log n) in resolution were previously established for commutativity and distributivity of multiplication. Proving a matching Ω(n^6 log n) lower bound would show that CDCL solvers inherently require high-degree polynomial time even on these degree-two identities.

literature.title: Polynomial-Time (8/17)-Approximation for Submodular Maximization under a Matroid Constraint
literature.statement: Let α* be the supremum of approximation ratios α ∈ [0, 1] for which there exists a randomized polynomial-time algorithm in the value-oracle model that, given an independence oracle for a matroid M = (N, ℐ) and a value oracle for an arbitrary non-negative submodular function f : 2^N → ℝ_{≥ 0}, outputs an independent set S ∈ ℐ such that 𝔼[f(S)] ≥ α · max_{T ∈ ℐ} f(T). Is α* = 8/17? Equivalently, does there exist, for every ε > 0, a polynomial-time value-oracle algorithm achieving an (8/17 - ε)-approximation for non-negative submodular maximization subject to a matroid constraint?
literature.source_title: Stronger Hardness for Submodular Maximization Subject to a Matroid Constraint
literature.rationale: Theorem 1.1 proves that in the value-oracle model, no polynomial-time (or sub-exponential time) algorithm can achieve an approximation ratio exceeding 8/17 for maximizing a non-negative submodular function subject to a matroid constraint (even for cardinality or simplified partition constraints). This improves the 2011 inapproximability bound of approximately 0.478. The current best known polynomial-time algorithm (STOC 2024) achieves an approximation ratio of 0.401. This leaves a gap between 0.401 and 8/17 ≈ 0.471. It is open whether 8/17 is the true approximability threshold, i.e., whether an (8/17 - ε)-approximation can be achieved in polynomial time.

literature.title: Existence of a Strongly Symmetric Matroid Instance with Symmetry Gap Strictly Below 8/17
literature.statement: Consider the symmetry gap framework for submodular maximization: let N be a finite set, ℱ ⊆ 2^N be the collection of independent sets of a matroid on N, and f : 2^N → ℝ_{≥ 0} be a non-negative submodular function. Suppose the problem max {f(S) : S ∈ ℱ} is strongly symmetric with respect to a permutation group 𝒢 on N, meaning f(σ(S)) = f(S) for all S ⊆ N and σ ∈ 𝒢, and S ∈ ℱ ⇔ S' ∈ ℱ whenever 𝔼_{σ ∈ 𝒢}[1_{σ(S)}] = 𝔼_{σ ∈ 𝒢}[1_{σ(S')}]. The symmetry gap of the instance is defined as γ = max_{x ∈ P(ℱ)} F(x̄) / max_{x ∈ P(ℱ)} F(x), where P(ℱ) is the convex hull of indicator vectors of sets in ℱ, F is the multilinear extension of f, and x̄ = 𝔼_{σ ∈ 𝒢}[σ(x)]. Does there exist such an instance (f, ℱ, 𝒢), where ℱ is a matroid constraint (or a simplified partition matroid constraint), with symmetry gap γ < 8/17?
literature.source_title: Stronger Hardness for Submodular Maximization Subject to a Matroid Constraint
literature.rationale: The paper shows that the symmetry gap framework yields an inapproximability bound of 8/17 ≈ 0.471 for submodular maximization subject to a simplified partition matroid or cardinality constraint, improving upon the 2011 bound of 2 e^{-1/2} (1 - e^{-1/2}) ≈ 0.478. In Appendix A, the authors prove that within their 3-parameter family of hyperedge-cut gadgets, the symmetry gap is strictly minimized at 8/17. It remains open whether the symmetry gap framework itself has an intrinsic barrier at 8/17 for matroid constraints, or whether a different gadget or geometry can yield a symmetry gap strictly strictly smaller than 8/17.

literature.title: Objective-switching approximation for weighted 4-set packing
literature.statement: Let an instance of Maximum Weighted $k$-Set Packing consist of a finite collection $\mathcal{S}$ of sets of cardinality at most $k$ on a ground set $U$, together with a positive weight function $w : \mathcal{S} \to \mathbb{Q}_{>0}$. A packing is a subfamily $A \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ of pairwise disjoint sets, with weight $w(A) = \sum_{S \in A} w(S)$. Can the two-phase framework combining squared-weight potential local search with residual linear-objective claw repairs be extended to $k = 4$ to obtain a polynomial-time approximation algorithm for Maximum Weighted $4$-Set Packing with approximation ratio strictly better than the locality gap of squared-weight local search (or strictly less than $2.5$)?
literature.source_title: Breaking the $\sqrt{3}$ Barrier for Maximum Weighted $3$-Set Packing
literature.location: Sec. 5, Extension to weighted k-Set Packing
literature.rationale: The paper breaks the sqrt(3) barrier for k=3 by combining Phase I (squared-weight local search) with Phase II (linear-objective claw repair via auxiliary 9-set packing). For k >= 4, the layered coefficients change and direct claw repairs may occupy up to k^2 ground elements, leaving open whether objective switching yields a net improvement over the squared-weight locality gap.

literature.title: Polynomial-time (4/3 + ε)-approximation for weighted 3-set packing
literature.statement: Let an instance of Maximum Weighted $3$-Set Packing consist of a finite ground set $U$, a family $\mathcal{S}$ of subsets of $U$ with $|S| \le 3$ for each $S \in \mathcal{S}$, and a weight function $w : \mathcal{S} \to \mathbb{Q}_{>0}$. A packing is a collection $A \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ of pairwise disjoint sets, and an optimum packing $O$ maximizes $\sum_{S \in O} w(S)$. Does there exist, for every fixed $\varepsilon > 0$, a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that computes a packing $A$ satisfying $\sum_{S \in O} w(S) \le (4/3 + \varepsilon) \sum_{S \in A} w(S)$?
literature.source_title: Breaking the $\sqrt{3}$ Barrier for Maximum Weighted $3$-Set Packing
literature.rationale: The best polynomial-time approximation ratio for unweighted 3-Set Packing is 4/3 + ε. The present work improves the ratio for weighted 3-Set Packing from sqrt(3) ≈ 1.732 to 1.6908, breaking the squared-weight local search barrier. The known NP-hardness lower bound is only 95/94 ≈ 1.0106. Whether weighted 3-Set Packing can match the 4/3 ratio of the unweighted case remains open.

literature.title: Maximal secant variety order testable by linear flattenings in even dimensions
literature.statement: Let $n \ge 4$ be an even integer. For a nonzero linear map $L : (\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes 3} \to \mathrm{Mat}_{u,v}(\mathbb{C})$ into complex matrices of arbitrary dimensions $u, v \ge 1$, define $\rho(L) = \max_{x,y,z \in \mathbb{C}^n} \mathrm{rank} L(x \otimes y \otimes z)$ and the potency $\mathrm{Pot}(L) = \frac{\max_{T \in (\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes 3}} \mathrm{rank} L(T)}{\rho(L)}$. Let $\Pi(n) = \sup_L \mathrm{Pot}(L)$ be the supremum over all nonzero linear flattenings. For an integer $r \ge 1$, the linear flattening method yields a nontrivial equation for the secant variety $\sigma_r((\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes 3})$ if and only if $\mathrm{Pot}(L) > r$ for some linear flattening $L$, which occurs if and only if $r \le \lceil \Pi(n) \rceil - 1$. Since $2n - 2 \le \Pi(n) \le 2n - 2 + \frac{2}{n+1} < 2n - 1$, the maximum such integer $r$ is either $2n - 3$ (if $\Pi(n) = 2n - 2$) or $2n - 2$ (if $\Pi(n) > 2n - 2$). What is this maximum integer $r$ for each even $n \ge 4$; in particular, is $\Pi(n) > 2n - 2$?
literature.source_title: Explicit tensors beyond the linear flattening barrier

literature.title: Explicit 3-tensors with border rank exceeding 3n
literature.statement: Does there exist a polynomial-time explicit family of tensors $T_n \in (\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes 3}$ whose border rank satisfies $\underline{\mathrm{R}}(T_n) > 3n$ for all sufficiently large $n$, or more generally satisfies $\underline{\mathrm{R}}(T_n) \ge c n$ for some constant $c > 3$? Here, a tensor family $(T_n)_{n \ge 1}$ is polynomial-time explicit if each entry of $T_n$ is an integer computable in binary in time polynomial in $n$.
literature.source_title: Explicit tensors beyond the linear flattening barrier

literature.title: Comb inequality separation at extreme points of the subtour elimination polytope
literature.statement:
Let $n \ge 3$ be an integer, and let $K_n = (V, E)$ be the complete undirected graph on $n$ vertices. The subtour elimination polytope $\operatorname{SEP}(n) \subset \mathbb{R}^E$ is the set of vectors $x = (x_e)_{e \in E}$ satisfying:
(1) $x_e \ge 0$ for all $e \in E$;
(2) $\sum_{e \in \delta(\{v\})} x_e = 2$ for all $v \in V$, where $\delta(S) = \{\{u,w\} \in E : u \in S, w \notin S\}$;
(3) $\sum_{e \in \delta(S)} x_e \ge 2$ for all non-empty proper subsets $S \subsetneq V$.
A point $x^* \in \operatorname{SEP}(n)$ is an extreme point (vertex) of $\operatorname{SEP}(n)$ if it cannot be written as a convex combination $\lambda x_1 + (1 - \lambda) x_2$ of two distinct points $x_1, x_2 \in \operatorname{SEP}(n)$ with $\lambda \in (0, 1)$.
A comb inequality is specified by a handle $H \subsetneq V$ ($H \ne \emptyset$) and an odd integer $s \ge 3$ together with pairwise disjoint subsets $T_1, \dots, T_s \subset V$ (teeth) such that for each $i \in \{1, \dots, s\}$, $T_i \cap H \ne \emptyset$ and $T_i \setminus H \ne \emptyset$. The comb inequality requires
$\sum_{e \in \delta(H)} x_e + \sum_{i=1}^s \sum_{e \in \delta(T_i)} x_e \ge 3s + 1$.
The decision problem asks: given $n$ and an extreme point $x^*$ of $\operatorname{SEP}(n)$ with rational coordinates (encoded in binary), does there exist a comb inequality violated by $x^*$?
Is this decision problem NP-complete (and the corresponding exact separation problem NP-hard), or is it solvable in polynomial time?
literature.source_title: Separating comb inequalities is NP-hard
literature.rationale: The paper resolves the complexity of separating comb inequalities in the general case by showing NP-completeness for half-integral points in SEP(n) with support graph of maximum degree 4. However, in branch-and-cut TSP solvers, separation is called on optimal vertices (extreme points) of the LP relaxation. The construction in the reduction does not guarantee that the constructed fractional point is an extreme point of SEP(n), leaving the complexity on extreme points open.

literature.title: Universal Additive Gap Between List Chromatic Number and Chromatic Number of Two Matroids
literature.statement: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be two loopless matroids on a common finite ground set $E$. A common $k$-coloring is a partition of $E$ into $k$ sets, each independent in both $M_1$ and $M_2$; the common chromatic number $\chi(M_1, M_2)$ is the minimum number of colors in such a coloring. Given an assignment of color lists $L(e)$ of size $k$ for each $e \in E$, a list coloring is a choice of color $c(e) \in L(e)$ for each $e \in E$ such that each monochromatic set is independent in both matroids; the common list chromatic number $\chi_{\ell}(M_1, M_2)$ is the minimum $k$ such that a list coloring exists for every list assignment of size $k$. Is there an absolute constant $C \ge 0$ such that $\chi_{\ell}(M_1, M_2) \le \chi(M_1, M_2) + C$ for every pair of finite loopless matroids $M_1, M_2$ on a common ground set? In particular, does $\chi_{\ell}(M_1, M_2) \le \chi(M_1, M_2) + 1$ always hold?
literature.source_title: A note on the list chromatic number of two matroids
literature.rationale: A multiplicative bound $\chi_{\ell}(M_1, M_2) \le 2\chi(M_1, M_2)$ was previously established for every pair of matroids (Combinatorica 2025). The paper constructs a graphic matroid and a partition matroid with common chromatic number 2 and common list chromatic number 3, demonstrating that an additive gap of 1 is possible. It remains open whether the additive gap $\chi_{\ell} - \chi$ can grow arbitrarily large or is bounded by an absolute constant.

literature.title: Equality of List Chromatic and Chromatic Numbers for Strongly Base-Orderable Matroids
literature.statement: Let $M$ be a finite matroid. Recall that $M$ is strongly base-orderable if for every pair of bases $B_1, B_2$ of $M$, there exists a bijection $\varphi: B_1 \to B_2$ such that $(B_1 \setminus X) \cup \varphi(X)$ is a basis of $M$ for every subset $X \subseteq B_1$. For two loopless strongly base-orderable matroids $M_1, M_2$ on a common finite ground set $E$, does the common list chromatic number always equal the common chromatic number, that is, $\chi_{\ell}(M_1, M_2) = \chi(M_1, M_2)$?
literature.source_title: A note on the list chromatic number of two matroids
literature.rationale: The common chromatic number of two strongly base-orderable matroids equals $\max\{\chi(M_1), \chi(M_2)\}$ by a classical result of 1976. Earlier work proved equality $\chi_\ell = \chi$ for transversal matroids (a subclass of strongly base-orderable matroids). This paper proves that $\chi(M_1, M_2) = 2$ implies $\chi_\ell(M_1, M_2) = 2$ for strongly base-orderable matroids, establishing equality when the common chromatic number is at most 2. The case where $\chi(M_1, M_2) \ge 3$ remains open.

literature.title: Exponent of log n in the Query Complexity of Tarski Fixed Points on the Grid
literature.statement: Let $[n]^k$ denote the grid $\{1, \dots, n\}^k$ with the standard componentwise partial order. Let $\operatorname{Tarski}(n, k)$ denote the deterministic query complexity of finding a fixed point of an unknown monotone function $f: [n]^k \to [n]^k$ accessed via an evaluation oracle. Does there exist a constant $c < 1$ and a function $f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for all $k \ge 3$ and all $n \ge 2$, $\operatorname{Tarski}(n, k) \le f(k) (\log n)^{c \lceil \log_2 k \rceil}$? In particular, for dimension $k = 5$, is $\operatorname{Tarski}(n, 5) = O(\log^2 n)$?
literature.source_title: Tarski Fixed Points in Quasi-FPT Queries
literature.location: after Theorem 2 and Theorem 3 (Abstract and Sec. 1)
literature.rationale: The paper achieves a major breakthrough by showing that $\operatorname{Tarski}(n,k) = (\log n)^{\Theta(\log k)}$ up to the $5^k$ factor, proving an upper bound $O(5^k (\log n)^{\lceil \log_2 k \rceil})$ and a lower bound $\Omega((\log n / \mathrm{polylog}(k))^{\lfloor \log_4(6k+4)\rfloor})$. However, this leaves a factor of 2 gap in the exponent of $\log n$ between $\frac{1}{2}\log_2 k$ and $\log_2 k$. For instance, in dimension $k=5$, the known bounds give $\Omega(\log^2 n) \le \operatorname{Tarski}(n,5) \le O(\log^3 n)$. Determining the exact exponent constant $c \in [1/2, 1]$ is the central remaining open question on the asymptotic query complexity.

literature.title: Universal upper bound of 3 for fractional majority coloring of digraphs
literature.statement: Let $D = (V, E)$ be a finite loopless directed graph. A subset $S \subseteq V$ is called majority-stable if for every vertex $v \in S$, $|N^+_D(v) \cap S| \le \lfloor d^+_D(v) / 2 \rfloor$, where $N^+_D(v) = \{u \in V : (v, u) \in E\}$ and $d^+_D(v) = |N^+_D(v)|$. The fractional majority coloring number $\chi^*_{\mathrm{maj}}(D)$ is the minimum of $\sum_{S \in \mathcal{S}(D)} w_S$ over nonnegative weights $w_S \ge 0$ covering every vertex, i.e., $\sum_{S \in \mathcal{S}(D) : v \in S} w_S \ge 1$ for all $v \in V$, where $\mathcal{S}(D)$ is the family of majority-stable subsets of $V$. Does every finite loopless directed graph $D$ satisfy $\chi^*_{\mathrm{maj}}(D) \le 3$?
literature.source_title: Fractional majority coloring of digraphs: bounds and inapproximability

literature.title: Fractional majority coloring bound of 8/3 for digraphs without terminal directed triangles
literature.statement: Let $D = (V, E)$ be a finite loopless directed graph. A strongly connected component $K \subseteq V$ of $D$ is terminal if there is no arc from $K$ to $V \setminus K$. Suppose $D$ contains no terminal strongly connected component isomorphic to the directed triangle $C_3$ (the directed 3-cycle). Does $D$ satisfy $\chi^*_{\mathrm{maj}}(D) \le 8/3$?
literature.source_title: Fractional majority coloring of digraphs: bounds and inapproximability

literature.title: Universal upper bound of 3 for fractional majority coloring of tournaments
literature.statement: Let $T = (V, E)$ be a finite tournament, meaning a finite loopless directed graph such that for every pair of distinct vertices $u, v \in V$, exactly one of $(u, v) \in E$ or $(v, u) \in E$ holds. Does every finite tournament $T$ satisfy $\chi^*_{\mathrm{maj}}(T) \le 3$?
literature.source_title: Fractional majority coloring of digraphs: bounds and inapproximability
literature.rationale: The paper proves that every tournament has fractional majority coloring number at most 45927/13820 < 3.324 (Theorem 10), improving previous bounds. For general digraphs, the directed triangle achieves value 3, which is also a tournament. Thus 3 is a candidate sharp universal bound for tournaments.

literature.title: Bermond--Thomassen conjecture for disjoint directed cycles
literature.statement: For every positive integer $k$, does every finite simple loopless directed graph $D$ with minimum out-degree at least $2k - 1$ contain $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint directed cycles?
literature.source_title: An asymptotic bound for the Bermond--Thomassen Conjecture
literature.rationale: The Bermond--Thomassen conjecture has been a central open problem in digraph theory since 1981. This paper proves it asymptotically with out-degree 2k + O(k^{3/4} (log k)^{1/2}), but the exact bound 2k - 1 remains open for all k ≥ 4.

literature.title: Bermond--Thomassen conjecture for four disjoint directed cycles
literature.statement: Does every finite simple loopless directed graph $D$ with minimum out-degree at least 7 contain 4 pairwise vertex-disjoint directed cycles?
literature.source_title: An asymptotic bound for the Bermond--Thomassen Conjecture

literature.title: Additive constant gap for disjoint directed cycles
literature.statement: Does there exist an absolute integer constant $C$ such that for every positive integer $k$, every finite simple loopless directed graph $D$ with minimum out-degree at least $2k + C$ contains $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint directed cycles?
literature.source_title: An asymptotic bound for the Bermond--Thomassen Conjecture
literature.rationale: Theorem 1.2 resolves the leading coefficient of the Bermond--Thomassen conjecture by showing that minimum out-degree 2k + O(k^{3/4} (log k)^{1/2}) suffices for all sufficiently large k. However, the paper leaves open whether the sublinear error term can be reduced to an absolute constant C independent of k, which would show f(k) ≤ 2k + C. The authors mention in their discussion that an attempt to obtain an explicit linear bound 2k + C was unsuccessful.

literature.title: Asymptotic Edge Density of 3-Uniform Hypergraphs with Bipartite Links Exceeding 0.251
literature.statement: Let π be the supremum of all α ≥ 0 such that for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large integers n, there exists a 3-uniform hypergraph H on n vertices whose vertex link graphs are all bipartite and whose number of hyperedges satisfies |H| ≥ (α - ε) * (n choose 3). Is π ≥ 0.251?
literature.source_title: A counterexample to the Erdős--Sós bipartite-link conjecture
literature.rationale: The paper disproves the bipartite-link conjecture by constructing a 3-uniform hypergraph family with asymptotic edge density at least 1/4 + 25/70150556 ≈ 0.250000356, strictly surpassing 1/4. On the other hand, the best known upper bound established via flag algebras (doi:10.1017/S0963548312000508) is 0.258295. The true asymptotic maximum edge density is completely open, and closing the gap to 0.251 remains open.

literature.title: Linear Berge saturation for finite families of graphs
literature.statement: Let $k \geq 2$ be an integer, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite nonempty family of finite simple graphs, each having at least one edge. A $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ is a Berge-$F$ (for a graph $F$) if there exists an injection $\psi : E(F) \to E(H)$ such that $e \subseteq \psi(e)$ for every $e \in E(F)$. A $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ is Berge-$\mathcal{F}$-free if it contains no Berge-$F$ as a subhypergraph for any $F \in \mathcal{F}$. A $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ on $n$ vertices is Berge-$\mathcal{F}$-saturated if $H$ is Berge-$\mathcal{F}$-free, but for every hyperedge $e \in \binom{V(H)}{k} \setminus E(H)$, the hypergraph obtained by adding $e$ contains a Berge-$F$ for some $F \in \mathcal{F}$. The saturation number $\mathrm{sat}_k(n, \text{Berge-}\mathcal{F})$ is the minimum number of edges in a Berge-$\mathcal{F}$-saturated $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. Does there exist a constant $C = C(\mathcal{F}, k)$ such that $\mathrm{sat}_k(n, \text{Berge-}\mathcal{F}) \leq C n$ for all $n \geq 1$?
literature.source_title: A linear upper bound for Berge saturation numbers
literature.rationale: The paper proves the single-graph case of this conjecture (Theorem 1.2), but the general case for families of two or more forbidden graphs remains open.

literature.title: Hamilton cycle threshold for digraph connectivity in terms of two-cycle independence number
literature.statement: Let D be a finite simple digraph without loops. Let alpha_2(D) be the maximum size of a vertex set containing no directed 2-cycle in D, and let kappa(D) be the vertex strong-connectivity of D. If kappa(D) >= alpha_2(D) + 1, does D necessarily contain a directed Hamilton cycle? Equivalently, is f_2(a) <= a + 1 for all integers a >= 1, where f_2(a) is the minimum k such that every k-strongly connected digraph with alpha_2(D) <= a has a Hamilton cycle?
literature.source_title: A near-linear Chvátal--Erdős condition for Hamilton cycles in digraphs
literature.rationale: The classical Chvátal--Erdős theorem states that an undirected graph with vertex-connectivity at least its independence number is Hamiltonian. The directed analogue remains open; this paper provides the first near-linear bound but does not settle the linear bound f_2(a) <= a + 1.

literature.title: Classification of graphs H with finitely many vertex-critical (2P3, H)-free graphs
literature.statement: Let $H$ be a simple undirected graph. Characterize all graphs $H$ such that for every integer $k \ge 1$, the class of $(2P_3, H)$-free graphs contains only finitely many non-isomorphic $k$-vertex-critical graphs, where $2P_3$ is the disjoint union of two paths of length 2 (on 3 vertices each), and a graph $G$ is $k$-vertex-critical if its chromatic number is $k$ but every proper induced subgraph has chromatic number strictly less than $k$.
literature.source_title: Obstructions to $k$-colouring $H$-free graphs

literature.title: Finiteness of vertex-critical (2P3, K3)-free graphs
literature.statement: For every integer $k \ge 1$, are there only finitely many non-isomorphic $k$-vertex-critical $(2P_3, K_3)$-free graphs? That is, for each $k \ge 1$, does there exist an upper bound $N(k)$ such that every $k$-vertex-critical graph containing neither an induced $2P_3$ nor an induced triangle $K_3$ has at most $N(k)$ vertices?
literature.source_title: Obstructions to $k$-colouring $H$-free graphs
literature.rationale: Theorem 1.3 establishes that P4 + \ell P1 is the unique maximal forbidden induced subgraph for finiteness of k-vertex-critical H-free graphs for all k >= 5. In Open Problem 4.2, the authors ask to characterize graphs H for which (2P3, H)-free graphs admit only finitely many k-vertex-critical graphs for all k. Excluding triangles K3 is the classic first test case (as in (P7, K3)-free graphs, which were recently shown to have only three 4-vertex-critical graphs). Settling whether H = K3 admits finitely many k-vertex-critical graphs for all k is the natural starting point for Open Problem 4.2.

literature.title: Elementary bound on the order of vertex-critical (P4 + P1)-free graphs
literature.statement: Does there exist an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that for every integer $k \ge 5$, every $k$-vertex-critical $(P_4 + P_1)$-free graph has at most $2^{C k}$ vertices?
literature.source_title: Obstructions to $k$-colouring $H$-free graphs
literature.rationale: The proof of Theorem 1.3 bounds the order of any k-vertex-critical (P4 + \ell P1)-free graph using hypergraph Ramsey numbers R = R^(\ell+1)_{2^{\ell(k-1)}}((k-1)\ell+2). Consequently, the resulting upper bound on the maximum order of such a critical graph is non-elementary (a tower of exponentials). For \ell = 0 (cographs), the only k-vertex-critical graph is K_k of order k. For \ell = 1, it remains open whether the astronomical hypergraph Ramsey bound can be replaced by an elementary (e.g. single exponential) bound in k.

literature.title: Exact value of the maximum oriented diameter for graphs of diameter d
literature.statement: For each integer d >= 2, let f(d) denote the smallest integer such that every finite connected bridgeless simple graph of diameter d admits a strong orientation of directed diameter at most f(d). Is f(d) = ceil(d^2 / 2) + d for all integers d >= 2?
literature.source_title: An asymptotically tight bound on oriented diameter
literature.rationale: The paper proves that ceil(d^2/2) + d <= f(d) <= ceil(d^2/2) + d + 18 for every d >= 2, establishing the exact quadratic coefficient (1/2) and linear coefficient (1). However, it leaves untouched the exact additive constant, leaving a gap of at most 18 between the known lower bound ceil(d^2/2) + d and the new upper bound ceil(d^2/2) + d + 18. Determining whether the lower bound is always tight or finding the exact additive term is the ultimate question left open by this line of work.

literature.title: Exact value of optimal oriented diameter for diameter 4 graphs
literature.statement: Let f(4) be the smallest integer such that every finite connected bridgeless simple graph of diameter 4 admits a strong orientation of directed diameter at most f(4). Determine the exact value of f(4) within the known range {12, 13, 14, 15, 16}, and in particular whether f(4) = 12.
literature.source_title: An asymptotically tight bound on oriented diameter

literature.title: Sublinear Minimum Edge Completion for Consecutive Cycle Sums
literature.statement: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 3$. Let $C_n$ denote the standard cycle graph on vertices $\{1, \ldots, n\}$ with edges $(i, i+1)$ for $1 \le i < n$ and $(n, 1)$. For a graph $G$ on $\{1, \ldots, n\}$ containing $C_n$ as a subgraph, a subset $S \subseteq \{1, \ldots, n\}$ is called connected if the induced subgraph $G[S]$ is connected. Define the sum of $S$ by $S^* = \sum_{v \in S} v$. The graph $G$ is called complete if every integer $k \in \{1, \ldots, n(n+1)/2\}$ can be written as $S^*$ for some connected subset $S$ of $G$. Let $\text{mEC}(n)$ denote the minimum number of additional edges $|E(G) \setminus E(C_n)|$ such that $G$ is complete. For every integer $a \ge 1$, does there exist an integer $N_a$ such that for all $n \ge N_a$, $\text{mEC}(n) \le n / a$? (Equivalently, does $\text{mEC}(n) = o(n)$ as $n \to \infty$?)
literature.source_title: Consecutive Cycle Sums
literature.rationale: The paper proves mEC(n) <= n/2 - 1 for n >= 8 via Proposition 1 and notes that the inductive argument appears extendable to n/a for any integer a >= 1 given an appropriate base case, but leaves open whether mEC(n) is indeed sublinear (o(n)) in n.

literature.title: Existence of a Complete Cycle Permutation for $n \ge 8$
literature.statement: Let $n \ge 8$ be an integer. Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$. Arrange the labels $\sigma(1), \ldots, \sigma(n)$ cyclically around the $n$-cycle $C_n$. An arc is a nonempty proper contiguous subsegment along the cycle, or the entire cycle. The sum of an arc is the sum of the labels of its vertices. We say that the permutation $\sigma$ is complete if every integer $k \in \{1, \ldots, n(n+1)/2\}$ can be represented as the sum of some arc along the cycle. Does there exist any integer $n \ge 8$ and any permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$ such that the cycle labeled by $\sigma$ is complete?
literature.source_title: Consecutive Cycle Sums
literature.rationale: Theorem 1 establishes that the standard consecutive ordering (1, 2, ..., n) around an n-cycle is incomplete for all n >= 8. However, there are n(n-1)+1 distinct arcs on an n-cycle, which strictly exceeds the n(n+1)/2 target sums for every n >= 3. The paper does not investigate whether placing other permutations of {1, ..., n} around the cycle can eliminate duplicate sums and achieve all numbers from 1 to T_n for any n >= 8.

literature.title: Asymptotic Density of Missing Consecutive Cycle Sums
literature.statement: Let $C_n$ be the cycle graph with vertices labeled $1, \ldots, n$ in consecutive clockwise order, and let $T_n = n(n+1)/2$. An arc sum is the sum of vertex labels on a contiguous path in $C_n$. Let $\mathcal{M}_n = \{1, \ldots, T_n\} \setminus \{A^* : A \text{ is an arc of } C_n\}$ be the set of missing sums on the $n$-cycle. Does the asymptotic density of missing sums $\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{|\mathcal{M}_n|}{T_n}$ exist, and if so, what is its value?
literature.source_title: Consecutive Cycle Sums
literature.rationale: The paper proves that the set of missing sums on the standard n-cycle is nonempty for n = 6 and all n >= 8. Lemma 3 establishes an asymptotic lower bound of order (ln 2) T_n on standard-sum non-achievable numbers, showing that missing sums constitute a positive fraction of [1, T_n]. However, the paper leaves open the exact characterization of which sums are missing and the exact asymptotic proportion of missing values.

literature.title: Existence of an 8-regular triangle-distinct graph
literature.statement: Does there exist a finite simple 8-regular triangle-distinct graph? That is, does there exist a finite simple graph $G = (V, E)$ such that every vertex $v \in V$ has degree $\deg_G(v) = 8$, and the triangle-degrees $\operatorname{td}_G(v) = |\{ \{u, w\} \subseteq V \setminus \{v\} : \{u, v\}, \{w, v\}, \{u, w\} \in E \}|$ are pairwise distinct for all $v \in V$?
literature.source_title: Regular $K_3$-Irregular Graphs of Every Regularity at Least Nine
literature.rationale: Hak, Kozerenko, and Serdiuk (arXiv:2507.18776) showed that no r-regular triangle-distinct graph exists for r <= 7, and narrowed the possible orders of an 8-regular triangle-distinct graph to six candidate values. The present paper establishes existence for all regularities r >= 9. Consequently, r = 8 is the sole remaining regularity whose status is open.

literature.title: Minimum order of regular triangle-distinct graphs
literature.statement: For an integer $k \ge 15$, does there exist a finite simple $2k$-regular triangle-distinct graph on strictly fewer than $4k + 2$ vertices? More generally, for each $r \ge 9$, what is the minimum order $N(r)$ of an $r$-regular triangle-distinct graph?
literature.source_title: Regular $K_3$-Irregular Graphs of Every Regularity at Least Nine
literature.rationale: The paper establishes that for every integer k >= 15, there exists a 2k-regular triangle-distinct graph on 4k + 2 vertices (order 2r + 2), and complementation yields a (2k+1)-regular triangle-distinct graph of the same order (order 2r). Trivial degree constraints rule out orders <= r + 3, but the exact minimum order required for an r-regular triangle-distinct graph is unknown.

literature.title: Hajós conjecture on cycle decompositions of Eulerian graphs
literature.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices in which every vertex has even degree (an Eulerian graph). Can the edge set of $G$ always be partitioned into at most $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$ edge-disjoint simple cycles?
literature.source_title: A proof of the Erdős--Gallai cycle decomposition conjecture

literature.title: Gallai path decomposition conjecture for connected graphs
literature.statement: Let $G$ be a connected finite simple graph on $n$ vertices. Can the edge set of $G$ always be partitioned into at most $\lceil n/2\rceil$ edge-disjoint simple paths?
literature.source_title: A proof of the Erdős--Gallai cycle decomposition conjecture

literature.title: Existence of near-closed robust sublinear expanders in light graphs
literature.statement: Let $h(d) = \max\{1, \log_2^2 d\}$ and let $w_G(v) = 1/(d_G(v) h(d_G(v)))$ for any finite graph $G$ without isolated vertices. A graph $G$ is called light if every cycle $C$ satisfies $\sum_{v \in V(C)} w_G(v) < 1$. Does there exist $\delta_0 > 0$ and parameters $\eta > 0, s \ge 0$ such that every light graph $G$ with minimum degree $\delta(G) \ge \delta_0$ contains a nonempty induced subgraph $G[S]$ that is both an $(\eta, s)$-expander (in the sense that $|N_{G[S]-E'}(X)| \ge \eta |X| / \log^2 |S|$ for all $1 \le |X| \le 2|S|/3$ and $|E'| \le s|X|$) and near-closed in $G$ (at least $|S|/50$ vertices of $S$ have at most two neighbors outside $S$ in $G$)?
literature.source_title: A proof of the Erdős--Gallai cycle decomposition conjecture

literature.title: Exact Hilton-Milner bound in (j, p)-norm for k ≥ 4 and n > 2k
literature.statement: Let $k \\ge 4$ and $1 \\le j \\le k-1$ be integers, and let $p > 1$ be a real number. For every integer $n > 2k$ and every nontrivial intersecting family $\\mathcal{F} \\subset \\binom{[n]}{k}$, does the inequality $\\sum_{J \\in \\binom{[n]}{j}} d_{\\mathcal{F}}(J)^p \\le \\sum_{J \\in \\binom{[n]}{j}} d_{\\mathcal{H}(n,k)}(J)^p$ hold, with equality if and only if $\\mathcal{F} \\cong \\mathcal{H}(n,k)$? Here $\\mathcal{H}(n,k) = \\{F \\in \\binom{[n]}{k} : 1 \\in F, \\, F \\cap [2, k+1] \\neq \\emptyset\\} \\cup \\{[2, k+1]\\}$.
literature.source_title: The Hilton-Milner theorem in the $\ell_2$-norm
literature.rationale: The paper proves an exact Hilton-Milner bound in the ℓ₂-norm for all n > 2k (Theorem 5), and an asymptotic Hilton-Milner bound in the (j, p)-norm for n ≥ n₀(k, p, j) (Theorem 6), as well as an exact bound for k=3 for all n ≥ 7 (Proposition 7). However, for k ≥ 4 and general (j, p), it leaves open whether the exact upper bound cojp(F) ≤ cojp(H(n,k)) holds for all n > 2k.

literature.title: Extremal nontrivial intersecting families in (j, p)-norm at n = 2k
literature.statement: Let $k \\ge 4$ and $1 \\le j \\le k-1$ be integers, and let $p > 1$ be a real number. For $n = 2k$, what is the maximum value of $\\sum_{J \\in \\binom{[2k]}{j}} d_{\\mathcal{F}}(J)^p$ among all nontrivial intersecting families $\\mathcal{F} \\subset \\binom{[2k]}{k}$, and is the unique maximizer isomorphic to $\\binom{[2k-1]}{k}$?
literature.source_title: The Hilton-Milner theorem in the $\ell_2$-norm
literature.rationale: Theorem 5 determines that when n = 2k, the codegree squared sum (ℓ₂-norm) of any nontrivial intersecting family is maximized uniquely by the complement of a star, binom([2k-1], k). For the general (j, p)-norm, the paper's techniques establish asymptotic bounds for large n, leaving the boundary case n = 2k completely open.

literature.title: Inclusion of cycle-maximal graphs in edge-extremal graphs at the Turán remainder boundary
literature.statement: Let $r \ge 3$ be an integer. Define the linear coefficient $\gamma_r$ by $\gamma_3 = 5/18$, $\gamma_4 = 7/32$, and $\gamma_r = 2/(2r+1)$ for $r \ge 5$. Let $T_{n,r}$ denote the complete $r$-partite Turán graph on $n$ vertices with $t_r(n) = e(T_{n,r})$ edges. A finite family of graphs $\mathcal{H}$ with chromatic number $\chi(\mathcal{H}) = r+1$ is called a boundary family if its extremal number satisfies $\operatorname{ex}(n, \mathcal{H}) = t_r(n) + \gamma_r n + O(1)$ as $n \to \infty$. Characterize the boundary families $\mathcal{H}$ for which every cycle-maximal $\mathcal{H}$-free graph is edge-extremal for all sufficiently large $n$, that is, $\operatorname{CEX}(n, \mathcal{H}) \subseteq \operatorname{EX}(n, \mathcal{H})$ for all large $n$.
literature.source_title: Sharp linear Turán remainders for cycle and edge extremality

literature.title: Additive Turán remainder threshold for cycle-maximality in 3-chromatic graphs
literature.statement: Let $H$ be a fixed graph with chromatic number $\chi(H) = 3$. Suppose that for all sufficiently large $n$, the extremal number satisfies $\operatorname{ex}(n, H) \le t_2(n) + 1$, where $t_2(n) = \lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$. Must every cycle-maximal $H$-free graph on $n$ vertices be edge-extremal for all sufficiently large $n$, that is, $\operatorname{CEX}(n, H) \subseteq \operatorname{EX}(n, H)$? More generally, what is the maximum integer $c \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ such that $\operatorname{ex}(n, H) \le t_2(n) + c$ implies $\operatorname{CEX}(n, H) \subseteq \operatorname{EX}(n, H)$ for all large $n$?
literature.source_title: Sharp linear Turán remainders for cycle and edge extremality
literature.rationale: The paper proves in Appendix B that for $r=2$, no positive linear coefficient $\gamma > 0$ guarantees $\operatorname{CEX}(n, H) \subseteq \operatorname{EX}(n, H)$, and constructs an explicit 3-chromatic graph $H_2$ on 27 vertices with $\operatorname{ex}(n, H_2) = t_2(n) + 4$ such that $\operatorname{EX}(n, H_2) \cap \operatorname{CEX}(n, H_2) = \varnothing$ for all large odd $n$. However, it leaves open whether the inclusion holds for smaller additive constants $c \in \{1, 2, 3\}$. Determining the discrete additive threshold for 3-chromatic graphs is the natural next step.

literature.title: Worst-Case State-Complexity Blow-up for Bipartite Cactus Automata
literature.statement: Let L be a regular language over a finite alphabet Σ, and let n be the state complexity of L (the number of states of its minimal DFA). What is the optimal upper bound f(n) on the minimum number of states in an ε-free NFA A such that L(A) = L and the transition graph G(A) is a bipartite cactus? In particular, can f(n) be bounded polynomially in n, or is the worst-case blow-up exponential or super-exponential?
literature.source_title: Every Regular Language Has a Bipartite Cactus Automaton

literature.title: Expressiveness of Unambiguous Cactus Automata
literature.statement: Does every regular language admit an unambiguous finite automaton (an ε-free NFA in which every accepted word has a unique accepting run) whose transition graph is a bipartite cactus? If not, which subclass of regular languages is characterized by unambiguous bipartite cactus NFAs?
literature.source_title: Every Regular Language Has a Bipartite Cactus Automaton
literature.rationale: The paper proves that every regular language has an epsilon-free NFA with a bipartite cactus transition graph, heavily exploiting nondeterminism and state duplication. In Section 4, the authors suggest investigating restrictions forced by the cactus property in deterministic, unambiguous, and finitely ambiguous automata. For deterministic automata, planarity is already known to strictly restrict the class of recognizable languages (Book and Chandra, 1976). Whether unambiguous finite automata (where every accepted word has a unique accepting run) can recognize all regular languages with a bipartite cactus transition graph remains untouched and open.

literature.title: Local average order of dominating sets containing a stem
literature.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph of order $n \ge 2$ without isolated vertices. A vertex $u \in V(G)$ is a leaf if $\deg(u) = 1$, and an $l$-stem if it has exactly $l$ leaf neighbors. A graph is star-like if every vertex is either a leaf or an $l$-stem with $l \le 2$. For any vertex $v \in V(G)$, let $\mathcal{D}_v(G)$ be the set of dominating sets of $G$ containing $v$, and let $avd_v(G) = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_v(G)|} \sum_{S \in \mathcal{D}_v(G)} |S|$ be the local average order of dominating sets containing $v$. If $v$ is an $l$-stem with $l \ge 1$, is it always true that $avd_v(G) \le \frac{4n+1}{6}$, with equality if and only if $l = 1$ and $G$ is star-like?
literature.source_title: On the local average order of dominating sets

literature.title: Sharpness of the (5n-1)/6 local average dominating set bound for n at least 4
literature.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph of order $n \ge 4$ without isolated vertices, and let $v \in V(G)$. Theorem 3.8 proves that the local average order of dominating sets containing $v$, $avd_v(G)$, satisfies $avd_v(G) \le \frac{5n-1}{6}$. Is this upper bound sharp for any $n \ge 4$, i.e., does there exist a graph $G$ of order $n \ge 4$ without isolated vertices and a vertex $v \in V(G)$ such that $avd_v(G) = \frac{5n-1}{6}$? If not, what is the exact maximum value of $avd_v(G)$ over all graphs of order $n$ without isolated vertices and all $v \in V(G)$?
literature.source_title: On the local average order of dominating sets
literature.rationale: Theorem 3.8 proves that for every graph G of order n with no isolated vertices and every vertex v, avd_v(G) <= (5n - 2 deg(v) + 1)/6 <= (5n-1)/6. For n = 3, this bound is attained by the path P_3 at an endpoint (avd = 7/3 = (15-1)/6). However, the proof derives (5n-1)/6 by bounding each term (deg(u)+1)/(2^{deg(u)+1}-1) <= 2/3 for all u not in N[v], with equality requiring all such vertices to have degree 1, which cannot all have disjoint closed neighborhoods when n >= 4. It remains open whether the bound (5n-1)/6 is sharp for any n >= 4, or what the exact maximum of avd_v(G) is as a function of n.

literature.title: Polynomial versus Polylogarithmic Word Separation by Permutation Automata
literature.statement: Let \operatorname{Sepp}(n) denote the maximum over all pairs of distinct binary words u, v \in \{0, 1\}^* of length at most n of the minimum number of states in a deterministic finite automaton whose input letters act as permutations on the state set that separates u and v. Does there exist a constant \varepsilon > 0 such that \operatorname{Sepp}(n) = \Omega(n^\varepsilon) as n \to \infty, or is \operatorname{Sepp}(n) = (\log n)^{O(1)}?
literature.source_title: An Improved Lower Bound for Separating Words by Permutation Automata
literature.rationale: Robson (1996) proved an upper bound of O(\sqrt{n}) for separating length-n words by permutation automata. The present paper improves the lower bound from (3/2 - o(1)) log n (Bulatov et al., arXiv:1609.03199) to \Omega(\log n \log \log n). A substantial gap remains between this polylogarithmic lower bound and the O(\sqrt{n}) upper bound, leaving completely open whether the true complexity is polynomial n^{\Omega(1)} or polylogarithmic (\log n)^{O(1)}.

literature.title: Positive Binary Symmetric Group Identities of Maximum Element Order Scale
literature.statement: For each integer k \ge 1, let \mathfrak{S}_k be the symmetric group on k elements, and let \ell_{+,2}(k) be the minimum common length of a pair of distinct words u, v \in \{0, 1\}^* such that u(\sigma_0, \sigma_1) = v(\sigma_0, \sigma_1) for every pair of permutations \sigma_0, \sigma_1 \in \mathfrak{S}_k. Does there exist a constant C > 0 such that \log \ell_{+,2}(k) \le C \sqrt{k \log k} for all sufficiently large k?
literature.source_title: An Improved Lower Bound for Separating Words by Permutation Automata
literature.rationale: Theorem 1.2 constructs positive binary identities of \mathfrak{S}_k of length \exp(O(k / \log k)). In Section 5.1, the authors note that the maximum element order in \mathfrak{S}_k is Landau's function M(k) = \exp((1+o(1))\sqrt{k \log k}), and that any numerical identity has length at least M(k)/2. Constructing positive binary identities of length M(k)^{O(1)} = \exp(O(\sqrt{k \log k})) would achieve the conjectured optimal numerical identity length and yield the improved lower bound \operatorname{Sepp}(n) = \Omega((\log n)^2 / \log \log n).

literature.title: Bounded-depth minimal unique substring certificates for optimal string attractors in uniformly morphic words
literature.statement: Let $\phi \colon \Sigma^* \to \Sigma^*$ be a non-erasing uniform morphism over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ generating an infinite fixed point $w = \phi(w)$, with finite prefixes $w_n = \phi^n(a)$ for $a \in \Sigma$. Let $\gamma(w_n)$ denote the minimum size of a string attractor of $w_n$. For $d \ge 1$, let $\mathcal{C}_n^{[d]} = \bigcup_{j=0}^{d-1} \operatorname{MUS}(w_{n-j})$ denote the candidate certificate of minimal unique substrings of the $d$ most recent generations, where each factor is evaluated by its coverage in the ambient word $w_n$. Does there exist a constant $d \in \mathbb{N}$, depending only on $\phi$, such that for all sufficiently large $n$, every subset $\Gamma \subseteq [1, |w_n|]$ with $|\Gamma| = \gamma(w_n)$ is a string attractor of $w_n$ if and only if $\Gamma \cap \operatorname{Cov}_{w_n}(x) \neq \varnothing$ for every factor $x \in \mathcal{C}_n^{[d]}$?
literature.source_title: Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue--Morse Words
literature.rationale: The paper establishes that for the Thue-Morse words $t_n$, three consecutive source generations of minimal unique substrings ($\operatorname{MUS}(t_n) \cup \operatorname{MUS}(t_{n-1}) \cup \operatorname{MUS}(t_{n-2})$) are necessary and sufficient to certify all minimum-cardinality string attractors for all $n \ge 6$. The authors note that the proof template relies on recognizability and occurrence-transport, raising the question whether a uniform bound on the generation depth $d$ exists for other standard morphic word families.

literature.title: Eventual constancy of the count of minimum string attractors for uniform binary morphisms
literature.statement: Let $\phi \colon \{0,1\}^* \to \{0,1\}^*$ be a non-trivial uniform morphism, and let $w_n = \phi^n(0)$ for $n \ge 1$. Suppose that the minimum string attractor size $\gamma(w_n)$ is eventually constant, i.e., there exist $\gamma_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ and $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\gamma(w_n) = \gamma_0$ for all $n \ge n_0$. Does the number of smallest string attractors $|\mathcal{A}(w_n)| = |\{\Gamma \subseteq [1, |w_n|] : |\Gamma| = \gamma_0 \text{ and } \Gamma \text{ is an attractor of } w_n\}|$ eventually stabilize to a constant value for all sufficiently large $n$?
literature.source_title: Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue--Morse Words
literature.rationale: For Thue-Morse words, the minimum attractor size is known to be 4 for all $n \ge 4$, and this paper shows that the number of smallest attractors $|\mathcal{A}(t_n)|$ is 87 for $n=4$, 40 for $n=5$, and exactly 32 for every $n \ge 6$. The geometric explanation in Section 9.1 is that recursive boundary pairs become separated and scale uniformly without creating new combinatorial choices. A similar stabilization occurs for Fibonacci words and period-doubling words. It is open whether this eventual stabilization of the count of optimal attractors is a universal property of words generated by uniform morphisms with constant attractor size.

literature.title: Balanced Hellinger Conjecture for Boolean Functions
literature.statement: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $X$ be uniform on the Boolean hypercube $\{-1, 1\}^n$. For $\rho \in [0, 1]$, let $Y \in \{-1, 1\}^n$ be the output of sending $X$ through independent binary symmetric channels with crossover probability $(1-\rho)/2$, so $\mathbb{E}[X_i Y_i] = \rho$ for each $i \in [n]$. For any Boolean function $f: \{-1, 1\}^n \to \{-1, 1\}$, let $T_\rho f(y) = \mathbb{E}[f(X) \mid Y = y]$ and $\mathcal{Z}_\rho(f) = \mathbb{E}_Y \sqrt{1 - (T_\rho f(Y))^2}$. Does every balanced Boolean function $f$ (satisfying $\mathbb{E}[f(X)] = 0$) satisfy $\mathcal{Z}_\rho(f) \ge \sqrt{1 - \rho^2}$ for all $\rho \in [0, 1]$?
literature.source_title: The Hellinger Conjecture for Antipodal Boolean Functions
literature.rationale: The paper proves the conjecture under the additional symmetry assumption that f is antipodal (f(-x) = -f(x)), or more generally sign-reversing under an involution, but leaves open the full conjecture for general balanced Boolean functions.

literature.title: Uniqueness of Extremizers for Antipodal Hellinger Inequality
literature.statement: Let $n \ge 1$, $\rho \in (0, 1)$, and let $f: \{-1, 1\}^n \to \{-1, 1\}$ be an antipodal Boolean function (i.e. $f(-x) = -f(x)$ for all $x \in \{-1, 1\}^n$). Suppose $\mathbb{E}_Y \sqrt{1 - (T_\rho f(Y))^2} = \sqrt{1 - \rho^2}$, where $Y$ is obtained from $X$ via coordinatewise BSC($\rho$). Are signed dictators $f(x) = \pm x_i$ (for some $i \in \{1, \ldots, n\}$) the only antipodal functions achieving equality?
literature.source_title: The Hellinger Conjecture for Antipodal Boolean Functions
literature.rationale: The paper establishes that signed dictators attain the minimum affinity bound in the antipodal Hellinger inequality, but points out that classifying all extremizers for 0 < ρ < 1 remains open.

literature.title: Quadratic lower bound for sets with no unique sums in finite fields
literature.statement: For an odd prime $p$, let $m(p)$ denote the minimum size of a subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$ with $|A| \ge 2$ such that every sum in $A + A$ has at least two distinct representations as an unordered pair $\{a, b\}$ with $a, b \in A$, allowing $a = b$. Does there exist an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that $m(p) \ge c (\log p)^2$ for all sufficiently large primes $p$?
literature.source_title: A near-quadratic lower bound for sets with no unique sums

literature.title: Leading asymptotic constant for minimal sets with no unique sums
literature.statement: Let $m(p)$ denote the minimum size of a subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$ with $|A| \ge 2$ such that every element of $A + A$ has at least two representations as an unordered pair of elements of $A$. Does the limit $\lim_{p \to \infty} \frac{m(p)}{(\log p)^2}$ exist along the primes, and if so, is it equal to $\frac{1}{2 (\log 3)^2}$?
literature.source_title: A near-quadratic lower bound for sets with no unique sums
literature.rationale: Theorem 1.2 establishes the upper bound $m(p) \le \frac{1}{2(\log 3)^2} (\log p)^2 + O\left(\frac{(\log p)^2}{\log \log p}\right)$ via weakly ternary-balanced seeds, while Theorem 1.1 provides the lower bound $\Omega((\log p / \log \log p)^2)$. Even if the quadratic lower bound $\Theta((\log p)^2)$ in Question 5.1 holds, the paper leaves untouched whether the base-3 radix construction achieves the optimal asymptotic constant or whether another radix or non-radix construction can achieve a strictly smaller leading constant.

literature.title: Equality of tree stacking number and the tree estimate
literature.statement: Let $T$ be any finite tree. The stacking number $\operatorname{stack}(T)$ is the minimum integer $t \ge 2$ such that every configuration of $t$ pebbles on $T$ can be transformed, by standard pebbling steps (removing 2 pebbles from a vertex and placing 1 on an adjacent vertex), into a configuration supported on a single vertex. For a vertex $r \in V(T)$, let $\operatorname{leaf}_T(r)$ be the number of leaves of $T$ distinct from $r$, and let $\rho_T(r) = \sum_{v \in V(T),\, v = r \text{ or } \deg(v) > 1} \deg(v) \cdot 2^{\operatorname{dist}_T(r, v)}$. Define $\operatorname{estim}(T) = \max\left\{2,\, 1 + \max_{r \in V(T)} (\rho_T(r) + \operatorname{leaf}_T(r))\right\}$. Does the equality $\operatorname{stack}(T) = \operatorname{estim}(T)$ hold unconditionally for every finite tree $T$?
literature.source_title: The Almost Stacked Hypothesis: A Conjectural Analogue of Sjöstrand's Cover Pebbling Theorem
literature.rationale: The paper proves the lower bound unconditionally (Theorem 5.2) and the upper bound assuming the Almost Stacked Hypothesis (Theorem 5.4), but the unconditional equality for arbitrary configurations remains open.

literature.title: The Almost Stacked Hypothesis for graph pebbling
literature.statement: Let $G$ be a finite connected graph. A configuration $c: V(G) \to \mathbb{N}$ is almost stacked if there is at most one vertex $v_0 \in V(G)$ with $c(v_0) > 1$ (so $c(u) \le 1$ for all $u \ne v_0$). (1) Is the stacking number $\operatorname{stack}(G)$ always equal to the least integer $t \ge 2$ such that every almost stacked configuration of size $t$ on $G$ is stackable? (2) If $G$ is non-bipartite, is the clearing number $\operatorname{clear}(G)$ always equal to the least integer $t \ge 2$ such that every almost stacked configuration of size $t$ on $G$ is clearable?
literature.source_title: The Almost Stacked Hypothesis: A Conjectural Analogue of Sjöstrand's Cover Pebbling Theorem
literature.rationale: The Almost Stacked Hypothesis is the central conjectural reduction principle proposed in the paper, generalizing the spirit of cover pebbling theorems to stacking and clearing numbers.

literature.title: Asymptotic Deficit of k-Fold Sumsets in Finite Abelian Groups
literature.statement: Let $k \ge 2$ be an integer. For a finite abelian group $\Gamma$ of order $n$, define the deficit $f_k(\Gamma)$ to be the maximum integer $m \ge 0$ such that every subset $B \subseteq \Gamma$ of size at least $n - m$ can be expressed as a $k$-fold sumset $kA = \{a_1 + \dots + a_k : a_i \in A\}$ for some subset $A \subseteq \Gamma$. If $\Gamma$ contains no non-trivial element whose order divides $k$, does there exist a constant $c_k > 0$ such that $f_k(\Gamma) = \widetilde{\Theta}(n^{1/k})$ as $n \to \infty$?
literature.source_title: Random Cayley sum hypergraphs and $k$-fold sumsets
literature.rationale: The paper proves that the maximum deficit satisfies $f_k(\Gamma) \le \widetilde{O}(n^{(2k-1)/(4k-3)})$ for all finite abelian groups, and $f_k(\Gamma) \ge \widetilde{\Omega}(n^{1/k})$ when $\Gamma$ has no non-trivial element of order dividing $k$. Because the number of representations of an element as a k-fold sum grows with $k$, the deficit exponent is conjectured to match the lower bound $1/k$.

literature.title: Tight Hole Number Exponent in Random Cayley Sum Graphs
literature.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, let $k \ge 2$ be an integer, and let $p \in (0, 1/2]$. For a $p$-random subset $S \subseteq \Gamma$, let $\alpha_k(\mathrm{Cay}_k^+(\Gamma; S))$ be the $k$-partite hole number of the Cayley sum $k$-hypergraph, defined as the maximum integer $m$ such that there exist subsets $U_1, \dots, U_k \subseteq \Gamma$ each of size $m$ with $(U_1 + \dots + U_k) \cap S = \emptyset$. In particular for $k = 2$, is the bound $\alpha_2(\mathrm{Cay}_2^+(\Gamma; S)) \le \widetilde{O}(p^{-3/2})$ tight, or does there exist an upper bound $\alpha_2(\mathrm{Cay}_2^+(\Gamma; S)) \le \widetilde{O}(p^{-c})$ with high probability for some exponent $c < 3/2$ (such as $c = 1$)?
literature.source_title: Random Cayley sum hypergraphs and $k$-fold sumsets
literature.rationale: The paper proves in Theorem 1.5 that the k-partite hole number of a random Cayley sum k-hypergraph satisfies $\alpha_k(\mathrm{Cay}_k^+(\Gamma; p)) \le \widetilde{O}(p^{-(2k-1)/(2k-2)})$ with high probability, recovering the bound $\widetilde{O}(p^{-3/2})$ for $k = 2$ from arXiv:2509.02561. However, no matching lower bounds are established for either the independence number or the hole number. Improving the exponent from $(2k-1)/(2k-2)$ toward $1$ is the principal barrier to closing the polynomial gap in the deficit exponent.

literature.title: Optimal Asymptotic Base Constant for Ambiguity of Finitely Ambiguous NFAs
literature.statement: Let M(n) denote the maximum degree of ambiguity (the maximum number of accepting runs on any word) over all trim finitely ambiguous nondeterministic finite automata with n states. What is the value of the asymptotic base constant c = lim_{n -> infty} M(n)^{1/n}? In particular, is c = 1 + Real.sqrt 2, or does there exist an infinite family of finitely ambiguous NFAs with base constant strictly greater than 1 + Real.sqrt 2?
literature.source_title: Stronger bounds on the degree of ambiguity of finite automata
literature.rationale: The paper proves that every n-state finitely ambiguous NFA has degree of ambiguity at most 2^{O(n)}, improving the long-standing 2^{O(n log n)} bound, and constructs a family of NFAs with ambiguity at least 2 P_{n-2} = Omega((1+sqrt(2))^n), where log_2(1+sqrt(2)) ≈ 1.27155. The upper bound constant in the exponent is of the order of 12-14. The exact optimal base constant c = lim_{n -> infty} M(n)^{1/n} remains unknown and is the central quantitative question left open.

literature.title: Order of Growth of the Turán Coefficient in Uniformity for Trace 4-Cycles
literature.statement: For each integer $r \ge 3$, let $\operatorname{ex}_r(m, \operatorname{Tr}(C_4))$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $r$-uniform hypergraph on $m$ vertices containing no 4-cycle trace, and let $a_r := \limsup_{m \to \infty} \frac{\operatorname{ex}_r(m, \operatorname{Tr}(C_4))}{m^{3/2}}$. What is the asymptotic order of growth of $a_r$ as $r \to \infty$? In particular, does there exist a constant $\beta \in [1/2, 3/2]$ such that $\lim_{r \to \infty} \frac{\log a_r}{\log r} = \beta$, and does $a_r = \Theta(r^{1/2})$?
literature.source_title: Polynomial-in-$r$ bounds for forbidden traces of uniform hypergraphs
literature.rationale: The paper proves an upper bound of $O_\varepsilon(r^{3/2+\varepsilon} m^{3/2})$ for trace-$C_4$-free $r$-graphs, and constructs a family showing a lower bound of $\Omega(r^{1/2} m^{3/2})$. This leaves a polynomial gap in the uniformity $r$ for the asymptotic coefficient $a_r$.

literature.title: Elimination of Epsilon Loss in Forbidden Trace Turán Bounds
literature.statement: Let $H$ be a fixed hypergraph on $h \ge 1$ vertices, and let $\alpha \ge 0$. Suppose that for every fixed integer $j \ge 1$, there exists a constant $D_j > 0$ such that every trace-$H$-free $j$-uniform hypergraph on $s$ vertices has at most $D_j s^\alpha$ edges. Does there exist a constant $C_{H,\alpha} > 0$ such that for all integers $m \ge r \ge 2$, every trace-$H$-free $r$-uniform hypergraph on $m$ vertices has at most $C_{H,\alpha} r^{h-1-\alpha} m^\alpha$ edges (that is, with no $r^\varepsilon$ overhead)?
literature.source_title: Polynomial-in-$r$ bounds for forbidden traces of uniform hypergraphs
literature.rationale: Theorem 1 establishes that if $\operatorname{ex}_j(s, \operatorname{Tr}(H)) \le D_j s^\alpha$ for all fixed $j$, then $\operatorname{ex}_r(m, \operatorname{Tr}(H)) \le C_{H,\alpha,\varepsilon} r^{h-1-\alpha+\varepsilon} m^\alpha$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$. The factor $r^\varepsilon$ is introduced by setting the restriction size $s = \lfloor m / r^{1+\delta} \rfloor$ with $\delta > 0$ so that the probability of large trace sizes decays as $r^{-\delta L}$. It remains open whether this loss can be removed to give $\operatorname{ex}_r(m, \operatorname{Tr}(H)) \le C_{H,\alpha} r^{h-1-\alpha} m^\alpha$, or at least with polylogarithmic dependence $r^{h-1-\alpha} (\log r)^c$.

literature.title: Tightness of the n^2 edge bound for simple solid bricks of order 2n
literature.statement: Let $n \\ge 4$ be an integer. A connected graph $G$ is matching covered if every edge belongs to a perfect matching.
