A matching covered graph is a brick if it is nonbipartite and has no nontrivial tight cuts (equivalently, 3-connected and bicritical). A brick is solid if it has no two vertex-disjoint odd cycles $C_1, C_2$ such that $G - (V(C_1) \\cup V(C_2))$ has a perfect matching. Does there exist, for every integer $n \\ge 4$ (or for any integer $n \\ge 4$), a simple solid brick of order $2n$ with exactly $n^2$ edges? What is the maximum number of edges in a simple solid brick of order $2n$, and what are the extremal graphs?
literature.source_title: The maximum size of simple solid matching covered graphs
literature.rationale: Theorem 1.2 establishes that every simple solid brick of order 2n has at most n^2 edges for n >= 4. However, the authors do not determine whether this bound is tight for any or all n >= 4, nor do they characterize the extremal simple solid bricks. The extremal graphs A_n, B_n, D_n that achieve n^2 + 2 edges in Theorem 1.3 are not bricks because each contains a nontrivial tight cut for n >= 3, and complete bipartite graphs K_{n,n} are bipartite and thus not bricks. Hence, the sharpness of the n^2 bound for simple solid bricks remains open.

literature.title: Polynomial upper bound for square-difference-free sets
literature.statement: Does there exist an absolute constant $\epsilon > 0$ and a constant $C > 0$ such that for every positive integer $N$, every subset $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ satisfying $(A - A) \cap \{n^2 : n \in \mathbb{N}_{\ge 1}\} = \emptyset$ has cardinality $|A| \le C N^{1 - \epsilon}$?
literature.source_title: A new bound for the Furstenberg--Sárközy theorem using the van der Corput property
literature.rationale: The paper proves the upper bound $|A| \ll N \exp(-c \sqrt{\log N \log \log N})$ for sets without square differences using a quantitative van der Corput method with signed coefficients. It also proves in Theorem 1.3 that any van der Corput witness trigonometric polynomial $P(\theta) = a_0 + \sum_{n \le \sqrt{N}} a_n \cos(2\pi n^2 \theta)$ with $P \ge 0$ and $P(0) = 1$ must have constant coefficient $a_0 \ge \exp(-C \sqrt{\log N \log \log N})$, demonstrating that this method cannot yield a polynomial power-saving bound $N^{1-\epsilon}$. Meanwhile, the best known lower-bound constructions give subsets of size $\gg N^{0.752796...}$. Whether square-difference-free sets satisfy a polynomial upper bound $|A| \ll N^{1-\epsilon}$ remains wide open and is beyond the reach of both the van der Corput method and existing density-increment techniques.

literature.title: Sub-exponential difference bounds for general quadratic intersective polynomials
literature.statement: Let $h \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be an intersective polynomial of degree 2, meaning that for every positive integer $m$, there exists $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ such that $h(n) \equiv 0 \pmod m$. Do there exist constants $c > 0$ and $C > 0$ depending only on $h$ such that for all integers $N \ge 3$, every subset $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ satisfying $(A - A) \cap \{h(n) : n \in \mathbb{N}_{\ge 1}\} \subseteq \{0\}$ satisfies $|A| \le C N \exp(-c \sqrt{\log N \log \log N})$?
literature.source_title: A new bound for the Furstenberg--Sárközy theorem using the van der Corput property
literature.rationale: The paper obtains the bound $N \exp(-c \sqrt{\log N \log \log N})$ for difference sets avoiding $h(n) = n^2$. For general intersective polynomials of degree at least 2, the best known bound from density-increment methods is $N \exp(-c_h (\log N)^\mu)$ for any fixed $\mu \in (0, 1/2)$. The paper's signed van der Corput construction relies on the explicit structure of quadratic Gauss sums $G_q(a v^2)$ for pure squares. Extending this signed coefficient averaging to arbitrary quadratic intersective polynomials $h(X) \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ remains open.

literature.title: Approximation ratio strictly below 6 for metric heterogeneous TSP
literature.statement: Let $(V, d)$ be a finite metric space with a designated depot vertex $r \in V$ and client set $V^\circ = V \setminus \{r\}$. Given $k \in \mathbb{N}_{\ge 1}$ vehicles with positive speeds $s_1, \dots, s_k \in \mathbb{Q}_{>0}$, a feasible solution to the heterogeneous traveling salesman problem (HetTSP) is a tuple of $k$ closed walks $(T_1, \dots, T_k)$ each starting and ending at $r$ (possibly empty) such that every client $v \in V^\circ$ is visited by at least one tour $T_i$. The makespan of the solution is $\max_{1 \le i \le k} \ell(T_i) / s_i$, where $\ell(T_i) = \sum_{j=1}^m d(u_{j-1}, u_j)$ for a walk $T_i = (u_0, u_1, \dots, u_m)$ with $u_0 = u_m = r$. Let $\mathrm{OPT}_{\mathrm{HetTSP}}$ denote the infimum makespan over all feasible solutions. Does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm for HetTSP that, on every finite metric instance, outputs a feasible solution with makespan at most $\rho \cdot \mathrm{OPT}_{\mathrm{HetTSP}}$ for a constant factor $\rho < 6$?
literature.source_title: Improved Approximations for Vehicle Routing with Nonuniform Speeds
literature.rationale: Theorem 1.1 establishes the first single-digit constant-factor approximation algorithm for HetTSP with nonuniform vehicle speeds, achieving a ratio of 6 and improving upon the previous guarantee of 90(1+δ) from 2016. When all vehicle speeds are identical, the classical 1978 tour-splitting method combined with Christofides' algorithm yields an approximation ratio of 5/2. For nonuniform speeds, APX-hardness inherited from metric TSP and makespan scheduling leaves a significant gap between known lower bounds (at least 2 under standard complexity assumptions) and the upper bound of 6. Whether the layered decomposition technique or an alternative relaxation can bridge this gap to achieve an approximation ratio strictly below 6—or match the equal-speed ratio of 5/2—remains open.

literature.title: Anti-Ramsey Numbers of Spanning Forests of 4-Vertex Paths
literature.statement: Let $k \ge 2$ be an integer, and let $n = 4k$. Let $F = k P_4$ be the spanning linear forest on $n$ vertices consisting of $k$ vertex-disjoint paths on 4 vertices (and hence having no isolated edges $P_2$). What is the exact value of the anti-Ramsey number $\mathrm{AR}(4k, k P_4)$? In particular, is $\mathrm{AR}(4k, k P_4) = \binom{4k-2}{2} + 1$, or is it strictly larger? For the base case $k = 2$ on $n = 8$ vertices, what is $\mathrm{AR}(8, 2 P_4)$? (The general coloring with a monochromatic 2-star shows $\mathrm{AR}(8, 2P_4) \ge \binom{6}{2} + 1 = 16 > 14 = \mathrm{AR}(8, 4 P_2)$.)
literature.source_title: Spanning Even Linear Forests with Isolated Edges Share the Anti-Ramsey Numbers of Perfect Matchings
literature.rationale: Theorem 3.3 establishes that every spanning even linear forest on $n \ge 6$ vertices with at least one component isomorphic to $P_2$ satisfies $\mathrm{AR}(n, F) = \mathrm{AR}(n, (n/2)P_2)$. The proof relies fundamentally on embedding $F$ as a subgraph of $P_{n-2} \cup P_2$. However, when all path components have length at least 3 (i.e. at least 4 vertices), such as $k P_4$ with $k \ge 2$, $F$ has no $P_2$ component and cannot be embedded in $P_{n-2} \cup P_2$. Moreover, assigning a single color to all edges incident to a fixed pair of vertices $\{x, y\}$ and distinct colors to all other $\binom{n-2}{2}$ edges of $K_n$ yields a coloring with $\binom{n-2}{2} + 1$ colors that contains no rainbow copy of any spanning forest without isolated edges (since every copy must use at least two edges incident to $\{x, y\}$). This demonstrates that $\mathrm{AR}(n, F) \ge \binom{n-2}{2} + 1 > \mathrm{AR}(n, (n/2)P_2)$ whenever $F$ has no isolated edges, so the equality from Theorem 3.3 fails and the exact value of $\mathrm{AR}(4k, k P_4)$ remains undetermined.

literature.title: Tightness of conjectured worst-case efficiency bounds for public project redistribution with n >= 6
literature.statement: Consider the public project problem with $n \ge 6$ agents and cost normalized to $1$. Agent $i$ reports $\theta_i \in [0, 1]$, and the social surplus under the efficient decision is $S(\theta) = \max\{s, 1\}$, where $s = \sum_{i=1}^n \theta_i$. In an anonymous Groves redistribution mechanism, agent $i$ receives a payment determined by a symmetric function $h: [0, 1]^{n-1} \to \mathbb{R}$ of the other agents' reports $\theta_{-i}$. The mechanism satisfies ex-post weak budget balance (non-deficit) if the retained revenue $L(\theta) = \sum_{i=1}^n h(\theta_{-i}) - (n-1)S(\theta) \ge 0$ for all $\theta \in [0, 1]^n$. The worst-case efficiency ratio is defined by $\alpha(M) = \inf_{\theta \in [0, 1]^n} \frac{S(\theta) - L(\theta)}{S(\theta)} = 1 - \sup_{\theta \in [0, 1]^n} \frac{L(\theta)}{S(\theta)}$. What is the exact optimal worst-case efficiency ratio $\alpha_n^* = \sup_h \alpha(M_h)$ for $n = 6$ (and for general $n \ge 6$), and do the upper bounds on $\alpha_n^*$ conjectured in 2012 match the optimal ratio for all $n \ge 6$?
literature.source_title: Asymptotically Optimal Public Project Redistribution without Bounded Precision: A Complex-Analytic Proof
literature.rationale: The paper settles the asymptotic question as n approaches infinity without bounded precision, but highlights that exact optimal mechanisms remain open for all fixed n >= 6.

literature.title: Polynomial convergence rate for public project redistribution without bounded precision
literature.statement: For each integer $n \ge 3$, let $\alpha_n^*$ denote the supremum of the worst-case efficiency ratio $\alpha(M)$ over all deterministic, anonymous, strategy-proof, and ex-post weakly budget-balanced mechanisms $M$ for the public project problem with $n$ agents having arbitrary real valuations in $[0, 1]$. Does there exist a constant $c > 0$ such that $1 - \alpha_n^* = O(n^{-c})$ as $n \to \infty$? If not, what is the optimal convergence rate of $1 - \alpha_n^*$ (for instance, is it $\Theta(1/\log n)$ or $\Theta(1/\log\log n)$)?
literature.source_title: Asymptotically Optimal Public Project Redistribution without Bounded Precision: A Complex-Analytic Proof
literature.rationale: Theorem 1.4 establishes a deterministic, anonymous, dominant-strategy incentive compatible, and non-deficit mechanism achieving worst-case efficiency ratio $1 - O(1/\log\log n)$ for arbitrary real valuations in $[0, 1]^n$. Under the restrictive bounded precision assumption, earlier work achieved $1 - O(1/n)$. The author explicitly states in Section 7 that no claim is made that $1 - O(1/\log\log n)$ is optimal. Whether the optimal convergence rate without bounded precision is polynomial, e.g. $1 - O(n^{-c})$ for some constant $c > 0$, is completely open.

literature.title: Tightness of the harmonic residual error bound for iterated trade operations
literature.statement: Let $G: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be defined by $G(t) = \max\{1-t, 0\}$. For $n \ge 3$ and $\theta = (\theta_1, \dots, \theta_n) \in [0, 1]^n$ with $s = \sum_{i=1}^n \theta_i$, let $\mathsf{T}$ be the averaging operator defined by $(\mathsf{T}f)(t) = \frac{1}{n^2} \sum_{j=1}^n \sum_{k=1}^n f(t - \theta_j + \theta_k)$, and let $E_m = (\mathrm{I} - \mathsf{T})^m G$. Lemma 4.2 shows that for all $m \ge 1$, $|E_m(s)| \le \frac{s}{n H_m} = O(\frac{s}{n \log m})$. Is this harmonic/logarithmic upper bound on $|E_m(s)|$ tight for the iterated trade operator on $G$? That is, does there exist a sequence of profiles $\theta^{(m)}$ such that $|E_m(s)| = \Omega(\frac{s}{n \log m})$, or does $\sup_{\theta \in [0, 1]^n, s > 0} \frac{n |E_m(s)|}{s}$ decay at a faster rate in $m$, such as $O(m^{-c})$ for some $c > 0$?
literature.source_title: Asymptotically Optimal Public Project Redistribution without Bounded Precision: A Complex-Analytic Proof
literature.rationale: Lemma 4.2 proves that the aggregate residual error $|(\mathrm{I} - \mathsf{T})^m G(s)|$ is at most $s / (n H_m) \le s / (n \ln m)$. The author notes that it is unknown whether this logarithmic decay is tight or if the residual error decays faster as a function of the number of rounds m.

literature.title: Existence of CSS codes with three logical qubits and quasi-transversal CCZ for block lengths 39 to 46
literature.source_title: Building codes with transversal CCZ using projective geometry and SAT solvers
literature.rationale: Theorem 4.5 proves that no CSS code with k = 3, d_Z >= 3 and quasi-transversal CCZ exists for n <= 38, while Jacinto et al. constructed a [[47,3,3]] code. The paper isolates the remaining gap 39 <= n <= 46 as open.

literature.title: Diameter and finiteness of graphs whose powers are all well-covered
literature.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple connected graph such that for every positive integer $d \geq 1$, the power graph $G^d$ is well-covered (every maximal independent set of $G^d$ has the same cardinality). Is the diameter of $G$ at most 3? Furthermore, if $\operatorname{diam}(G) = 3$, are there only finitely many such graphs up to isomorphism that contain no true twins (pairs of adjacent vertices $u, v$ such that $N[u] = N[v]$)?
literature.source_title: On graphs whose powers are well-covered

literature.title: Classification of planar graphs whose powers are all well-covered
literature.statement: Let $G$ be a finite connected simple planar graph with at least two vertices. Characterize all such graphs $G$ with the property that for every integer $d \geq 1$, the power graph $G^d$ is well-covered. In particular, is every such planar graph either a complete graph ($K_3$ or $K_4$), or an induced cycle $C_5$, or a clique blow-up thereof?
literature.source_title: On graphs whose powers are well-covered
literature.rationale: The paper completely classifies connected chordal graphs whose powers are all well-covered (Theorem 1.2: only complete graphs), connected very well-covered graphs (Theorem 1.3: complete bipartite graphs), and connected cochordal graphs (Theorem 1.4: well-covered with diameter at most 2). A previous result by Deniz (2022) established that bipartite graphs whose powers are well-covered are disjoint unions of $K_{n,n}$ and $K_1$. Planar graphs are another fundamental graph class for which well-coveredness has been extensively studied, yet the classification of planar graphs all of whose powers are well-covered remains open.

literature.title: Characterization of Periodic Firing Words in Fixed-Priority Chip-Firing
literature.statement: Let $D=(V,E)$ be a finite strongly connected digraph, and let $\prec$ be a total order on $V$. Let $\Delta_D$ be the Laplacian matrix of $D$, and let $\rho \in \mathbb{N}^V$ be the primitive generator of the integer left kernel of $\Delta_D$, with $\ell_D = \sum_{v \in V} \rho_v$. Under the fixed-priority chip-firing map $\Phi$, which at each step fires the $\prec$-least vertex with at least as many chips as its out-degree, every active periodic orbit has period $\ell_D$ and vertex firing count vector $\rho$. What is the characterization of the words in $V^{\ell_D}$, up to cyclic rotation, that can occur as the firing sequence of an active periodic orbit of $\Phi$?
literature.source_title: Primitive periods in greedy chip-firing games
literature.rationale: Theorem 4.1 proves that every active periodic orbit has least period equal to the sum of coordinates of the primitive kernel vector and fires each vertex with that exact frequency. The specific sequential orderings of these firings that can actually appear remain uncharacterized.

literature.title: Polynomial Transient Bound for the Rational Hunger Game
literature.statement: Let $(V, P, F)$ be an irreducible rational hunger game on $n$ states with stationary distribution $\pi$ and minimal period $T$ such that $T\pi$ is integral. For an initial hunger vector $h \in \mathbb{Q}^n$ with $\sum_{i=1}^n h_i = 0$, let $\tau(h) = \min \{t \ge 0 : F^t(h) \in B\}$ denote the transient time to reach the recurrent basin $B$. Is $\tau(h)$ bounded by a polynomial in $n$, $T$, $\|h\|_\infty$, and the least common denominator of the entries of $P$?
literature.source_title: Primitive periods in greedy chip-firing games
literature.rationale: The paper proves that every rational hunger game trajectory on the zero-sum hyperplane is eventually periodic and converges to a unique recurrent state tiling the hyperplane by lattice shifts, but provides no quantitative bounds on the number of steps required to reach this recurrent basin as a function of the initial state or transition matrix.
